artigo.texto: The 50-Gigawatt Test: SemiAnalysis Sees a Historic Data Center Surge in 2027 Key Highlights - SemiAnalysis forecasts 51.2 GW of net data center IT capacity additions outside China in 2027, more than double its estimate for 2026. - The research firm identifies over 60 GW under construction and more than 24 GW in advanced development across 40 major campuses, although nearly 12 GW of its 2027 forecast involves projects still classified as planned. - Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner has questioned the pace of deployment, suggesting approximately 25 GW is more realistic, while recent forecasts from Goldman Sachs and JLL provide additional perspectives. - October earnings from Vertiv, ABB, Meta and Microsoft demonstrate extraordinary investment momentum alongside continuing project delivery constraints. - The report raises a potentially consequential question: Could shortages of GPUs, memory and semiconductor manufacturing capacity eventually constrain AI expansion more than data center buildings and power? The global data center industry is approaching a potentially historic test of its ability to turn artificial intelligence investment into operational infrastructure. In a provocative new forecast, semiconductor and AI infrastructure research firm SemiAnalysis predicts that approximately 51.2 gigawatts of net data center IT capacity will be added globally, excluding China, during 2027. That would represent more than double the 25 GW the firm expects to be added in 2026. Published October 19, the report, Datacenters 2027: The Year of Acceleration, +50GW in a Single Year, makes a forceful argument that much of this unprecedented expansion is already visible in the industry's construction pipeline. Authored by Jeremie Eliahou Ontiveros, Reyk Knuhtsen and Dylan Patel, the analysis draws on SemiAnalysis' proprietary tracking of construction starts, individual buildings, hyperscale leasing commitments, equipment procurement and project financing. Its researchers identify more than 60 GW of data center capacity under construction. Among the 40 largest campuses they examined, more than 24 GW is reportedly in advanced stages of development, with much of that capacity expected to be delivered in 2027. The forecast is not entirely composed of projects already under construction, however. SemiAnalysis' capacity chart includes approximately 11.9 GW of 2027 additions associated with projects still classified as planned. The remainder is associated with facilities already operating or under construction, according to the model's building-status categories. SemiAnalysis argues that the volume and maturity of projects already underway make a dramatic acceleration increasingly likely, despite well-documented constraints involving electricity, construction labor, equipment and capital. But the prediction has also become the subject of a revealing industry debate, with competing forecasts and new corporate disclosures raising questions about how much infrastructure can actually be delivered on schedule. The disagreement is no longer principally about whether AI infrastructure demand is real. It is about whether the industrial systems supporting that demand can expand quickly enough to satisfy it. The 50-Gigawatt Forecast Meets Its Skeptics One of the most prominent public challenges came from Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner, who questioned an earlier SemiAnalysis estimate of approximately 43 GW of capacity additions in 2027. Speaking on the September 17 episode of the All-In podcast, Gerstner suggested that approximately 25 GW was a more realistic expectation. "Atoms and energy are hard," Gerstner observed, pointing to permitting delays, local opposition, grid interconnection requirements, skilled labor shortages and backlogs for power equipment. His skepticism was directed at the physical limitations of the buildout, not necessarily at the underlying growth of AI demand. There is also a geographic distinction worth recognizing. Gerstner discussed SemiAnalysis' earlier projection in the context of U.S. computing capacity, while the firm's latest published forecast covers global additions outside China. Those are not interchangeable measurements, and the precise geographic scope of Gerstner's 25-GW counterestimate was not established in his remarks. Nevertheless, the central disagreement is clear: Gerstner doubts that the industry can deliver computing infrastructure at the pace SemiAnalysis anticipates. The researchers responded by increasing their forecast rather than reducing it. Their October report emphasizes the distinction between broad infrastructure forecasts and models built from individual construction projects. SemiAnalysis contends that its forecasts already incorporate expected delays, financing difficulties and the gradual commissioning of new facilities. In an October 20 episode of the SemiAnalysis Weekly podcast, the researchers elaborated on their methodology, describing building-level tracking of construction progress, power allocations, permits and delivery schedules. Their argument is that applying another blanket discount to the resulting estimates risks counting execution delays that the underlying model has already incorporated. This is a consequential methodological distinction. A campus under construction may represent substantial committed capital and a high probability of eventual completion. But its physical progress does not automatically establish when each phase will have permanent power, commissioned cooling infrastructure, installed computing equipment and operational capacity. Whether those milestones can converge during 2027 is central to evaluating the forecast. A Trillion-Dollar Leasing Boom Underwrites the Forecast The financial foundation of SemiAnalysis' projection is nearly as remarkable as its construction forecast. artigo.texto: Industrial Manufacturing Power Transmission, Data Centers a Driving Force Behind U.S. Wire & Cable Manufacturing New power transmission and the medium- and low-voltage wiring used for power connections are a driving force behind construction investments in the U.S. wire and cable sector Released Thursday, October 29, 2026 Reports related to this article: Written by Eric Funderburk for IIR News Intelligence (Sugar Land, Texas) Summary New power transmission and the medium- and low-voltage wiring used for power connections are a driving force behind construction investments in the U.S. wire and cable sector. A Growing Need Utilities are scrambling to meet new power transmission needs as renewable energy projects come online, natural gas power plants see a resurgence in U.S. construction, and hyperscale data centers and other large-load consumers remain a driving force behind the need to move new power to new places. Both between and within those generation facilities, data centers and other large-load projects, electrical wiring is needed for in-plant connections and power distribution. Behind all this stand the companies that manufacture the wire and cable used for these connections, be it overhead, underground or subsea transmission power cables or lower voltage wiring for in-plant uses. Current Construction One of the largest power cable projects underway in the U.S. was recently expanded in scope and comes from Hellenic Cable, a Greece-based cable manufacturer that is a subsidiary of a Belgian holding company Cenergy, which is itself part of Belgian industrial group Viohalco, which has holdings in cable-manufacturing and other metals-related businesses. The European corporate chain aside, since late 2024, Hellenic has been at work on a new grassroot manufacturing plant in Baltimore, Maryland, geared toward power cable production. Land-based transmission cables are in the cards for Hellenic's new plant, and while the company had originally scoped the potential manufacture of subsea cables from the facility down the road, the systematic dismantlement of the U.S. offshore wind industry seems to have caused the company to change its tune, and Hellenic recently announced that it will expand the scope of the plant to include cable-insulation lines, allowing it to substantially increase the plant's land cable output. Hellenic is targeting an initial completion date next year. Subscribers can access details of the project, including construction timelines, key contact details, and equipment and service needs, by clicking here. The distribution and interconnections needed between and within facilities are driving multiple U.S. projects geared toward the manufacture of low- and medium-voltage cabling. One company, LS Cable & System USA Incorporated, is actually expanding the scope of a line addition planned toward lower voltage cables into a broader project for overhead power transmission, although details are only just being confirmed regarding LS Cable's exact plans. In the meantime, at its manufacturing plant in Tarboro, North Carolina, LS Cable is very much underway with its line addition adding capacity for the medium-voltage cable used extensively within the artificial intelligence (AI) data center sector. Work is expected to finish up next summer, when the company will broaden its focus on high-voltage transmission cable. Wire and cable company Southwire is taking aim specifically at medium-voltage cables used primarily for power distribution from substations to communications or facilities with the expansion of its plant in Heflin, Alabama, including a new 340,000-square-foot building addition equipped and ready to begin production by the end of 2027. Southwire also is just getting started on another construction project in the southern U.S. at its Starkville, Mississippi, plant, where a groundbreaking ceremony took place earlier this month for a planned 380,000-square-foot building addition. While Southwire hasn't elaborated on the voltage ratings and types of cabling that the new construction is targeting, the plant currently produces a range of cable products. Future Construction Projects While cable and wiring company Viakable hasn't specifically elaborated on what products an expansion of its plant in LaSalle, Illinois, is aiming for, electricity transmission and distribution are very much in the company's product offerings and will probably feature in the new equipment and systems planned for installation in 22,000 of new building space. Construction is expected to kick off next year and be wrapped up before the year is out. Another company is preparing for the future of large-load power transmission and distribution: MetOx aims to manufacture its Xeus high-temperature superconducting (HTS) wire at a new plant in Chatham County, North Carolina. HTS wire can be incorporated into cables capable of carrying large loads of electricity of more than five than 10 times larger than conventional copper cables depending on the design specs, according the company, which is taking clear aim at both large-load transmission and hyperscale data centers sitting within a confined footprint. While MetOx's Xeus HTS wire represents the future of power transmission and distribution to some degree, it's not without its own headwinds as it must be cooled to extremely low temperatures to maintain its superconductivity. About Fiber Optic Cabling Fiber optic cable, a key component of data centers not covered in this article, represents a substantial amount of U.S. construction related to nonferrous wire and cable production that's not directly tied to large-load power transmission. Projects related to fiber optic cable were recently discussed in October 16 article - U.S. Fiber Optic Cable Construction Progresses Alongside Data Centers. Key Takeaways - Power transmission and the large-load power needs of hyperscale data scale centers are leading U.S. wire and cable manufacturers to invest in capacity growth

artigo.texto: Geral Aneel aprova editais para a contratação inédita de baterias em dezembro de 2026 Novas regras para leilões de armazenamento de energia visam garantir mais segurança ao sistema elétrico brasileiro. A Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) aprovou nesta terça-feira, 27, os editais dos leilões para a inédita contratação de baterias, que irão contribuir para a segurança do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). Para o certame com conteúdo local, o preço-teto foi fixado em R$ 1.760.000,00/MW ao ano, enquanto o certame sem a restrição terá preço-teto de R$ 1.580.000,00/MW ao ano. O relator é o diretor Gentil Nogueira. Conforme a lei de 2025, os sistemas de armazenamento de energia, na forma de baterias, terão custos de contratação rateados apenas entre os geradores de energia. Isso gerou críticas do setor, e um dos argumentos é a falta de tratamento isonômico. No início de outubro, a Câmara dos Deputados aprovou o requerimento de urgência do projeto de lei que abre margem para o custo da contratação de baterias ser arcado pelos usuários finais de energia elétrica do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), incluídos os consumidores. A votação do mérito do texto (PL 3716/2026) deve ocorrer em breve. Tendo em vista eventual mudança, o Diretor-Geral da Aneel, Sandoval Feitosa, reforçou que eventual mudança legislativa será recepcionada "com a maior agilidade possível". Nos processos de hoje, a Aneel faz um ajuste de redação para substituir a expressão "gerador de energia" por "usuário de reserva de capacidade", tanto no edital quanto no Contrato de Reserva de Capacidade na forma de Potência (CRCAP). A nova redação permite melhor adequação à proposta de regulamentação do rateio dos custos dos Leilões de Reserva de Capacidade na forma de Potência (LRCAPs) de baterias. A norma está em discussão na consulta pública, com prazo de contribuição até 6 de novembro. O titular do empreendimento fará jus à receita fixa (em R$/ano), a ser paga em 12 parcelas mensais. Em geral, os contratos terão 15 anos de duração, com início de suprimento em 1º de agosto de 2028. A área técnica da Aneel propôs uma mudança nos editais dos leilões para a contratação de baterias, que pode levar à inclusão dos consumidores no rateio do custo de contratação. Os certames estão previstos para 2 e 4 de dezembro. As baterias serão contratadas na modalidade de "reserva de capacidade". Em geral, os custos administrativos e financeiros e os encargos tributários precisam ser rateados entre todos os usuários finais de energia elétrica do SIN, incluídos os consumidores. A exceção, contudo, foi dada aos sistemas de armazenamento de energia. Daí a alegação de falta de isonomia. artigo.texto: Gerando resumo ENVIADO ESPECIAL A COLUMBUS, OHIO, E PITTSBURGH, PENSILVÂNIA- Mal o pequeno avião da companhia aérea American Eagle tinha pousado em Columbus, capital do Estado americano de Ohio, um burburinho tomou conta da cabine. Passageiros animados conversavam sobre a transformação da cidade. O otimismo era palpável “Columbus está em sua melhor fase, se você não tiver sucesso aqui, o problema é seu”. Uma breve caminhada pelo aeroporto confirmou a tese dos passageiros. Por todo terminal, banners exaltam o fato de a cidade estar entre as que mais crescem nos Estados Unidos. Os terminais estão sendo ampliados para aumentar a capacidade de Columbus receber voos internacionais e áreas consideradas suburbanas ou rurais estão mudando com a chegada de novos moradores e a construção de prédios em tempo recorde. A transformação de Columbus ressalta uma mudança na região do Meio-Oeste americano que vem acontecendo aos poucos. A área conhecida como Cinturão da Ferrugem por conta do declínio industrial e de decadência econômica está vivendo um renascimento gradativo, impulsionado pelo setor de tecnologia. Na capital de Ohio, ainda existem memórias relacionadas a usinas siderúrgicas e minas de carvão, mas os galpões e armazéns que ficaram pelo caminho se transformaram em charmosos ateliês e galerias de arte. A zona metropolitana da cidade conta com escritórios de empresas como Amazon, Intel e Google e a região de Downtown está cheia de jovens profissionais. “A economia está muito forte aqui em Columbus. Todos estão aproveitando o boom da tecnologia”, destaca Dorsey Hager, secretário executivo do Sindicato de Ofícios da Construção Civil de Columbus em entrevista ao Estadão. “Vamos construir prédios de grande porte e a densidade populacional vai aumentar especialmente porque os mais jovens querem morar na cidade”. Crescimento respaldado em números A capital de Ohio se tornou a segunda maior cidade do Meio-Oeste americano em 2017, atrás apenas de Chicago. Columbus também está entre as 15 maiores cidades dos EUA em população e sua região metropolitana poderá ganhar até 600 mil moradores até 2050, segundo dados da Comissão de Planejamento Regional do Centro de Ohio. O desenvolvimento econômico da cidade ocorreu por conta de políticas estaduais de subsídios, impostos baixos e regulamentação flexível. Columbus também conta com uma grande infraestrutura estudantil devido ao campus da Ohio State University, uma das maiores instituições de ensino superior dos EUA em número de estudantes. “Estamos vendo o surgimento de uma manufatura de alta tecnologia e maior valor agregado, como aeroespacial, robótica e defesa”, avalia Mark Muro, economista do Instituto Brookings, um think-tank americano. “O histórico industrial, aliado a uma forte presença universitária na área de tecnologia, provou ser a fórmula de sucesso para Columbus.” De acordo com Muro, Columbus ocupa a 46ª posição entre 100 regiões metropolitanas em termos de crescimento de empregos no setor de manufatura em um estudo feito pelo Instituto Brookings. A cidade ocupava a 70ª posição em 2022. O boom de Columbus está relacionado ao investimento da Intel de mais de US$ 28 bilhões para a construção de duas novas fábricas de semicondutores para a construção de chips na região metropolitana da cidade. A expectativa é que o projeto crie 3 mil empregos na Intel e 7 mil empregos na construção civil ao longo da obra, que está prevista para terminar em 2030. A empresa afirma que poderá construir outras seis fábricas, o que tornaria o complexo um dos maiores centros de produção de chips do mundo. Outra companhia que está contribuindo para as notícias positivas para Columbus é a Anduril, empresa americana do setor de defesa que está em estágio avançado na construção de seu complexo de manufatura e tecnologia. Coração de Silício A expansão do polo tecnológico na região central de Ohio levou à criação do apelido Coração de Silício (Silicon Heartland em inglês) para caracterizar a área. O termo se refere à transformação do Cinturão da Ferrugem em um polo de manufatura avançada, semicondutores, inteligência artificial e data centers. Silício (Silicon) faz referência ao Vale do Silício, principal polo global de tecnologia do mundo, enquanto a palavra Coração (Heartland) se refere ao Meio-Oeste americano. O novo hub tecnológico teve uma grande parcela de investimentos federais, que começaram no primeiro governo Trump e foram expandidos durante a administração do democrata Joe Biden. A Lei CHIPS e Ciência (CHIPS and Science Act), que foi aprovada no governo Biden em 2022, destinou US$ 7,8 bilhões em subsídios diretos e empréstimos para a Intel impulsionar a fabricação de semicondutores nos EUA, incluindo cerca de US$ 1,5 bilhão em financiamento direto voltado para o complexo que está sendo construído em Columbus. O objetivo principal do projeto de lei era reduzir a dependência de Washington em relação à fabricação estrangeira de semicondutores. O financiamento também fez parte de uma promessa de campanha de Trump e Biden de investir em áreas que haviam sido prejudicadas com o fechamento de fábricas e usinas no final do século 20. “A eleição de Trump em 2016 ressaltou as necessidades e a frustração de comunidades do Cinturão da Ferrugem que sofreram duros golpes durante 30 anos”, diz Muro. “Apesar disso, foi Biden quem deu passos importantes para investir nessas áreas. A boa notícia é que Trump não retirou esse investimento em seu segundo mandato”. O novo momento da cidade anima o líder sindical por conta do aumento dos trabalhos no setor de construção. “Eu diria que 60% das nossas horas de trabalho atualmente são dedicadas a data centers e fábricas de chips. 4 mil empregos foram gerados por conta dessas instalações”, diz Dorsey Hagey. Ele ainda avalia que a região de Columbus não pode mais ser considerada como parte do Cinturão da Ferrugem. “Agora estamos na era do Coração do Silício. artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich- XPENG Vice President Gu Jie revealed on October 28 at the China Society of Automotive Engineers (SAECCE) conference that the company has completed small-scale production of a solid-state battery designed specifically for its IRON humanoid robot. The robot itself is now in the final stages before formal mass production (SOP). According to Gu, the battery features high energy density and extreme safety. It weighs about 30% less and offers roughly 30% more capacity than conventional liquid lithium batteries. Its design prevents thermal runaway, allowing it to withstand rigorous tests including impact and nail penetration. Image source: XPENG Motors This marks XPENG's first public release of a solid-state battery dedicated to robotics. As the group's second-largest business unit after new energy vehicles, the robotics division has accelerated its production timeline recently. On September 22, XPENG held its first supply chain partner conference, attended by leading companies in core components such as actuators, dexterous hands, sensors, and AI chips. The company has completed supplier audits and finalized selections for key parts. Under XPENG's previously announced roadmap, the IRON humanoid robot will enter mass production by the end of 2026. Sales and deliveries are set to begin in 2027, with the robots deployed in global stores and commercial settings to handle services like guidance and product demonstrations. Notably, XPENG had already built up its solid-state battery capabilities for its automotive business. In February 2026, the company announced the completion of all-weather road testing, achieving a pack volume utilization rate of 78%—23 percentage points higher than traditional liquid battery packs—while reducing weight by 35%. Chairman He Xiaopeng also stated in September that XPENG has invested in three battery cell manufacturers and will bring battery production in-house starting in 2026.

artigo.texto: ContactExisting Customer SupportLogin Discussions at the conference centered on how policymakers could manage increasingly tight carbon markets with appropriate flexibility while preserving a credible investment signal. A major focus was the UK ETS and its impact on market regulation and investment strategies. Meanwhile, speakers viewed the prospect of linking the EU and UK ETS as increasingly achievable. The EUA-UKA spread is increasingly dependent on when the market expects fungibility between the two. The EEX EUA December 2026 futures contract settled at €85.42 ($95.99) per tCO2e on October 16. The EEX UKA December 2026 futures contract settled at £63.36 ($84.41) per tCO2e, leaving the EUA-UKA spread at $11.58 per tCO2e. The spread widened slightly from just under $11 per tCO2e on October 12. This followed confirmation that the EU-UK summit would take place on November 20. Since October 12, EUAs have settled €2.91 per tCO2e lower, from €88.33 ($98.57) per tCO2e. UKAs have softened by £2.98 per tCO2e from £66.34 ($87.63) per tCO2e. A dedicated UK ETS session named ‘UK ETS playing catch-up’ examined cap design and the alignment of free-allocation rules. The discussion highlighted that linking the UK and EU systems would require broader regulatory convergence. This applies particularly to the rules governing each market and allowance allocation. Grant Opperman, portfolio manager at Molecule Ventures, suggested that linkage could be established relatively quickly once the necessary political and technical conditions were in place. Panellists said mutual exemptions from the UK and EU carbon border adjustment mechanisms (CBAM) would provide a further incentive to conclude negotiations. This applies particularly to the UK, as the EU has so far been reluctant to grant CBAM waivers. Fungibility would be the practical test of any agreement. Regulated companies would need confidence that they could surrender an allowance issued under either system seamlessly for compliance in the other. This would require alignment across registry infrastructure, auction rules and the use of carbon-market revenues. Steve Freeman of the Confederation of Paper Industries said EU member states must direct auction revenues toward industrial decarbonization. He added that the UK will have to look at similar interventions to support its industry in a linked scenario. Linkage would give UK participants access to a much larger and more liquid market, fundamentally expanding the liquidity available to UK participants. The UK ETS is only around one-eleventh the size of the EU market. Participants characterized the standalone UK market as tight. They raised the prospect of UK allowances developing a premium from 2028 if linkage does not occur. Linkage would also require closer alignment on cap ambition, sectoral coverage and market-stability rules. One such technical hurdle is the difference between the two systems’ existing safeguards. The UK relies on price-based interventions, while the EU’s Market Stability Reserve adjusts allowance supply according to market volumes. The UK’s planned supply-adjustment mechanism, or SAM, would bring its approach closer to the EU model. Negotiators would nevertheless need to determine how the two mechanisms would interact within a linked market. Charlie Lewis, deputy director for trading at the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), said several UK ETS developments remain in the pipeline. These include the integration of engineered greenhouse-gas removals from 2029 and a possible expansion of maritime coverage to include international voyages. The framework for non-pipeline CO₂ transport is also evolving, allowing installations to deduct captured emissions transported to geological storage from their reportable ETS emissions. Panellists at a session called ‘Policymakers’ vision for the future of European carbon pricing’ said efforts to shield the EU ETS from extreme price moves risk weakening the stable carbon-price signal needed to unlock industrial investment. This places the balance between market intervention and long-term certainty at the heart of the post-2030 reform debate. That tension framed the policy session on the European Commission’s ETS revision proposal. The proposal spans changes to the Market Stability Reserve, free allocation, CBAM and aviation, as well as the possible roles of international credits and removals. Krzysztof Bolesta, secretary of state at Poland’s Ministry of Climate and Environment, spoke on the panel. He said securing a Council agreement on the wider ETS review by December would be difficult. “We have just started looking at the proposed reforms,” he said, adding that a Council agreement “by December looks difficult.” Attendees noted that a delay in the Council’s December position risks stalling crucial climate policy. This would leave it vulnerable to a shifting political landscape, as France conducts elections in April 2027. The immediate fault line highlighted during the session was the proposed reform of Article 29a, the mechanism that releases allowances when prices rise excessively. Changes discussed included shortening the period used to assess a price spike from six months to two and releasing 25 million allowances. A 25% guardrail is intended to limit the scale of intervention. The Article 29a changes debated at the conference form part of a wider reform package put forward by Peter Liese, the European Parliament’s rapporteur on the EU ETS review. His broader proposals would slow the near-term tightening of the emissions cap and allow permanent removals into the system earlier. These measures aim to ease supply pressure while preserving the EU ETS decarbonization signal. artigo.texto: Notícias MERCADO DE CARBONO PGFN debate estratégias para reduzir litígios no mercado regulado de carbono A secretária extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono, Cristina Reis, apresentou o funcionamento e o cronograma de implementação do Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE) durante o 3º Encontro Nacional da Consultoria da Procuradoria-Geral da Fazenda Nacional (PGFN). O evento reuniu procuradores de todo o país no auditório da Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC), em Brasília (DF), na quarta-feira (21/10). A palestra da secretária integrou a programação técnica do encontro. O objetivo central foi atualizar os quadros jurídicos da Fazenda e demais participantes sobre o andamento da regulamentação do SBCE e alinhar a elaboração dos futuros atos normativos. “Apresentei na PGFN a implementação do mercado regulado de carbono brasileiro, explicando sua sistemática e os passos da implementação. É muito importante travar esse diálogo com procuradores e advogados que prestam consultorias. O SBCE é um instrumento novo, de financiamento climático e de descarbonização, que tem contado bastante com o suporte de algumas áreas e vai precisar de mais e mais suporte à medida que normas infralegais sejam publicadas”, afirmou Cristina Reis. A articulação preventiva com a consultoria jurídica busca mitigar riscos regulatórios e conferir previsibilidade ao setor produtivo durante a transição para a economia de baixo carbono. Segundo a secretária extraordinária, a solidez dos decretos e das portarias em elaboração é o principal instrumento para evitar a judicialização do sistema. “Uma das intenções da Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono (SEMC) é reduzir os contenciosos judiciais e, para isso, contamos com a excelência do trabalho jurídico da PGFN”, destacou Cristina Reis. A implementação do SBCE é gradual e está estruturada em cinco fases sucessivas, nos termos do artigo 50 da Lei 15.042/2024. A Fase I, voltada à governança institucional e à regulamentação infralegal, está em andamento, enquanto a entrada em operação plena do mercado regulado (Fase IV) está prevista para 2030. Durante a apresentação, a secretária também apontou que a complexidade técnica das regras de mensuração, relato e verificação (MRV) e a conciliação de metas exigirão suporte especializado permanente, tanto para os setores regulados quanto para os proponentes de projetos de mitigação. O alinhamento contínuo entre os corpos técnico e jurídico visa assegurar integridade ambiental, transparência operacional e segurança institucional ao mercado brasileiro.

artigo.texto: The APEC Business Advisory Council Hong Kong, China, announced the launch of a major research initiative titled “Mobilising Capital for Nature: An APEC Roadmap for Nature Finance and Carbon Market Connectivity”on Thursday, with Standard Chartered (2888) acting as the lead authoring institution. The project, supported by knowledge partners Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero and Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing, aims to mobilize private capital for nature-positive activities while enhancing carbon market connectivity across APEC economies. The announcement was made during a side event organized by ABAC Hong Kong alongside the 2026 APEC Finance Ministers’ Meeting held in Hong Kong. The research will examine the policy, market, and financing conditions needed to unlock private capital, focusing on three areas: developing investable nature-related projects; embedding nature considerations into capital-allocation decisions; and using blended finance and catalytic capital to improve project bankability. Mobilizing private capital Mary Schapiro, vice chair and head of the GFANZ Secretariat, emphasized the critical role of market incentives in addressing environmental challenges. There is no sustainable future without nature, Schapiro said. "Carbon markets have the potential to play an important role in creating financial incentives for emissions reductions and nature-positive investment. GFANZ looks forward to supporting this research, which will help inform pathways for creating the enabling conditions for private capital to mobilise at scale." Mary Huen Wai-yi, ABAC Hong Kong representative and chief executive officer for Hong Kong, Greater China, and North Asia at Standard Chartered, noted the significance of the collaboration. "Standard Chartered is pleased to serve as lead author of this ABAC Hong Kong, China research, with GFANZ and HKEX contributing as knowledge partners," Huen said. "Bringing together public- and private-sector perspectives, the research will examine opportunities for greater cooperation across APEC and develop practical recommendations to strengthen nature finance, carbon market connectivity and the enabling conditions for private capital to support nature-positive investment." Supporting APEC agenda The initiative will support ABAC's sustainable-finance agenda and promote cross-border investment and collaboration on blended finance and carbon markets across APEC economies. The research findings are expected to be released in the third quarter of 2027.

artigo.texto: CHESTERFIELD COUNTY, Va. — Dozens of families gathered at Brightpoint Community College Tuesday to hear from representatives from companies including Google and Dominion Energy about data center projects in Chesterfield County, with some residents calling for greater transparency, community involvement and accountability as development continues. “My question is, will you commit to coming to the table as community partners and do an actual community benefits agreement?” one attendee asked during the forum. County officials said the decision to pursue data centers was driven in part by pressure to reduce the tax burden on residents. But some people who attended Tuesday’s forum said they want to see the numbers behind those projects and know what protections will be put in place for surrounding communities. Ben Nelson, who attended the forum, said he wants Chesterfield County to strengthen its zoning rules and give residents a larger role in decisions involving data centers. “I would like the county to rewrite the zoning rules so that community benefit agreements have to be considered and then enforced,” Nelson said. “I'd like the county to set up a citizen advisory board, so that people from the community can have meaningful real-time interactions with representatives from the tech companies.” According to Chesterfield County’s website, the county lists nine ongoing data center projects and currently has three data center campuses in operation. Environmental concerns also surfaced during the forum. A Google representative addressed recent environmental violations involving the company after the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality sent a letter citing seven violations connected to the Project Peanut data center. “We understand that trust is earned, and that is something that we will continue to try and earn with the community regarding the recent violations,” the Google representative said. “We've worked with DEQ to mitigate the impacts, to make corrective actions to ensure that those do not happen again.” Still, some residents said they want stronger assurances from the companies developing data center campuses and mechanisms to hold them accountable. “They really didn't give a clear answer,” Nelson said. County officials said the forum was organized in response to hundreds of questions and comments about data centers. Nelson said the meeting was a positive step, but believes county leaders could do more to create opportunities for residents to have a meaningful voice in the process. “The board can do a lot more to create mechanisms for actual meaningful community involvement,” Nelson said. “This is a great first step, but it's tiny compared to what they could be doing for us.” CBS 6 is committed to sharing community voices on this important topic. artigo.texto: Município será reconhecido em São Paulo por iniciativa que pretende transformar a chegada de grandes centros de processamento de dados em um novo ciclo de desenvolvimento econômico, inovação e empregos qualificados. Projeto é uma das apostas da gestão do prefeito Naumi Amorim Caucaia, na Região Metropolitana de Fortaleza, receberá o IA Honors – Governos Inteligentes 2026, prêmio nacional concedido pela concepção e pelo desenvolvimento do Parque Tecnológico de Caucaia (Partec). A cerimônia ocorrerá em 6 de novembro, no Cubo Itaú, em São Paulo, durante o Fórum Brasileiro de Governança em Inteligência Artificial, evento associado ao Fórum Mundial de Inteligência Artificial. O reconhecimento destaca a estratégia da administração do prefeito Naumi Amorim, executada pela Secretaria Municipal de Ciência, Inovação e Desenvolvimento Tecnológico (Setec), comandada por Machidovel Trigueiro Filho. direitoce+1 O que está em jogo O Parque Tecnológico foi concebido para aproveitar a expansão dos investimentos em data centers na região do Complexo Industrial e Portuário do Pecém. A proposta vai além de receber grandes instalações de processamento e armazenamento de dados. Pretende criar um ambiente capaz de atrair empresas de tecnologia, instituições de pesquisa, startups e profissionais especializados. Com uma área projetada de 124,68 hectares, o Partec já possui delimitação territorial estabelecida por decreto municipal. A iniciativa busca conectar infraestrutura digital, conhecimento e novos negócios. Jornal dos Municípios+1 Por que importa: Caucaia tenta dar um passo estratégico na economia digital. Em vez de funcionar apenas como território de instalação de grandes empreendimentos tecnológicos, o município pretende participar da cadeia de valor que se desenvolve ao redor deles. A diferença é relevante. Data centers exigem investimentos bilionários, mas não necessariamente geram grandes volumes de empregos permanentes. O desafio é transformar a infraestrutura instalada em oportunidades de formação profissional, empreendedorismo e inovação para a população local. Os investimentos que impulsionam a estratégia O município já está no centro de grandes projetos ligados à infraestrutura digital. Entre eles está o empreendimento associado à ByteDance, controladora do TikTok, na ZPE Ceará, com investimentos anunciados que podem alcançar R$ 200 bilhões ao longo de suas etapas. Outro projeto, ligado à Voltalia Energia do Brasil, recebeu aprovação do Conselho Nacional das Zonas de Processamento de Exportações em agosto, com investimento previsto de R$ 181,7 bilhões. Os valores anunciados não representam recursos já integralmente executados. Prefeitura de Caucaia+1 É nesse ambiente que a Prefeitura pretende inserir o Parque Tecnológico. O protagonismo de Naumi e Machidovel O prefeito Naumi Amorim tem colocado o desenvolvimento tecnológico entre as apostas estratégicas de sua administração. À frente da Setec, Machidovel Trigueiro Filho conduz a estruturação institucional do Partec e deverá representar o município na cerimônia de premiação. O secretário resume a ambição do projeto ao defender que Caucaia não seja apenas endereço de grandes data centers, mas também o lugar onde surjam empresas, conhecimento e empregos qualificados associados a esses investimentos. A premiação, de natureza exclusivamente honorífica, reconhece a concepção e o desenvolvimento da iniciativa. Não significa que o parque esteja integralmente implantado ou em operação. direitoce Vá mais fundo O reconhecimento nacional fortalece a visibilidade de Caucaia em um momento de expansão dos investimentos em inteligência artificial e infraestrutura digital. Mas o verdadeiro indicador de sucesso não será a premiação. Será a capacidade de transformar projetos e investimentos anunciados em empresas instaladas, pesquisa aplicada, qualificação profissional e renda para a população. O desafio de Caucaia é deixar de ser apenas o endereço da infraestrutura digital para se tornar protagonista da economia que nascerá ao redor dela. Se conseguir, o Parque Tecnológico poderá representar uma mudança estrutural no perfil econômico do município — e não apenas mais um grande empreendimento em seu território. artigo.texto: With India’s energy storage market poised for significant growth, the focus is shifting beyond capacity to grid stability, efficiency and advanced technologies. William Gui, General Manager of Sineng Electric Asia-Pacific, discusses how grid-forming PCS technology is shaping the future of utility-scale BESS, shares insights from Sineng Electric’s 1.44 GWh project in Gujarat, and outlines the company’s long-term vision for India’s evolving energy storage landscape. 1. How do you see India’s energy storage market evolving over the next 3–5 years? We expect strong growth in India’s energy storage market over the next three to five years, driven by the expansion of solar and wind power and the need for a more flexible electricity system. Storage will become increasingly important for balancing renewable generation, meeting peak demand and maintaining a stable power supply. We see significant opportunities in both standalone BESS and storage co-located with renewable energy projects. As the market develops, customers will increasingly look beyond how much energy a system can store to how effectively it responds to grid needs. Efficiency, operational flexibility and grid-forming capability will therefore become more important, together with reliability and lifecycle costs. The pace of deployment will depend on how quickly awarded projects progress through financing, grid connection and commissioning. Close coordination between developers, utilities and technology providers will be essential to bringing these projects into operation and meeting performance expectations. 2. What are the key technology requirements for utility-scale BESS projects in India? System design and equipment selection should be guided by the project’s operating requirements, including how often the system will charge and discharge, the grid services it needs to provide and the conditions in which it will operate. Safety and reliability are fundamental. In India, high ambient temperatures make effective thermal management essential to maintaining system performance and availability over time. Our 1.725 MW central PCS, for example, uses composite temperature control technology to keep the core cabinet temperature rise below 10 K. Additionally, it features IP65-rated protection and C5-rated corrosion to support reliable operation in harsh environments. Grid integration is equally important. The PCS must work reliably with the batteries and plant control systems and respond effectively to changing grid conditions. As renewable energy penetration increases, grid-forming capabilities will play a greater role in supporting voltage and frequency stability. 3. How can grid-forming PCS technology support India’s growing renewable energy grid? As solar and wind account for a larger share of India’s electricity supply, the grid will need additional resources to maintain stable voltage and frequency. Grid-forming PCS allows battery storage to contribute directly by establishing a voltage and frequency reference and responding to changes in the power system. This is particularly valuable in areas with weak grid connections. Our experience in Gujarat provides a practical example. At a 1.44 GWh BESS project, we have validated the black-start capability of our PCS through a series of tests. - Grid-forming (Virtual Synchronous Generator, VSG) commissioning and control parameter optimization to enhance system stability and dynamic response; - Seamless transition from on-grid operation to islanded operation following utility grid separation; - Black start capability and progressive restoration of the electrical network using a single grid-forming 2 MW Central PCS unit; - Parallel operation and power sharing between grid-forming and grid-following PCS units to ensure coordinated system operation; - Dynamic voltage and frequency regulation under varying load conditions to validate the system’s adaptability and resilience. These results show how grid-forming storage can contribute to both stable operation and power restoration. 4. What lessons from Sineng Electric’s global energy storage experience can be applied to India’s large-scale BESS deployment? Our global experience has shown that a successful storage project starts with understanding where and how it will operate. Climate, grid conditions and daily operating demands vary from market to market, and system design needs to reflect those differences. For India, this means drawing on international experience while adapting solutions to local project requirements. Another lesson is the importance of delivering value throughout the project lifecycle. At Sineng, this means improving efficiency, maintaining high availability and simplifying maintenance. These priorities guide our approach to India’s large-scale BESS projects, helping customers achieve reliable operation and long-term value from their investment. 5. What is Sineng Electric’s long-term strategy for India’s energy storage market? India is a key market for Sineng Electric. Our long-term strategy is to build on our established local presence and apply our global expertise in PCS technology and energy storage projects to support the sector’s growth in India. We already have a strong foundation in India: an 8,900 m² manufacturing facility with an annual production capacity of 20 GW, more than 280 local employees, seven service centers, seven spare-parts centers and two regional marketing centers. This network brings us closer to customers and supports project delivery, technical service and ongoing maintenance. On the technology side, we will continue to develop our offering across central and string PCS, with a focus on efficient power conversion, reliability and advanced grid-forming capabilities. Working closely with developers, utilities and system integrators will help us align these solutions with India’s evolving grid and project requirements. artigo.texto: [DigitalToday reporter Seok Dae-geon (석대건)] Posco Future M is expanding the scope of its battery materials cooperation with LG Energy Solution. Posco Future M said on Thursday it signed a “future cooperation” memorandum of understanding with LG Energy Solution. The two companies agreed to strengthen a cooperative framework to jointly respond to the electric vehicle and energy storage system markets and changes in the global trade environment. The scope of the cooperation includes LFP cathode materials that use lithium, phosphate and iron, and synthetic graphite anode materials. It also includes supply and technology development cooperation for next-generation products such as ultra high-nickel cathode materials that maximize nickel content, sodium-ion batteries and silicon anode materials. The two companies plan to diversify cathode and anode products and specify a supply roadmap to sign a formal contract within the year. Under the agreement, Posco Future M plans to supply a total of 720,000 tonnes of cathode and anode materials over seven years from 2027 to 2033. For NCM cathode materials, an existing supply item, it will increase over the medium to long term the use of recovered metals extracted from used batteries. As a step to boost cost competitiveness, it plans to broaden cooperation targets to include LFP cathode materials, for which demand has surged due to expansion of AI data centres and increased sales of entry-level electric vehicles. LFP cathode materials will be produced by converting a high-nickel ternary cathode production line at the Pohang plant. Posco Future M will push ahead with the conversion work so it can begin full-scale supply to LG Energy Solution from early next year. It also plans to develop a new process using Argentine salt-lake lithium held by the Posco Group to supply next-generation LFP cathode materials with improved cost competitiveness and quality. Demand for synthetic graphite anode materials has been steadily rising because they are advantageous for fast-charging performance and longer lifespan. Posco Future M will produce the anode materials in South Korea and Vietnam and supply them to LG Energy Solution. The two companies will also cooperate on technology development and supply of materials for sodium-ion batteries, ultra high-nickel cathode materials and silicon anode materials. They also agreed to seek joint response measures if supply chain issues arise, such as the introduction of U.S. prohibited foreign entity requirements or the announcement of the European Industry Acceleration Act. The Posco Group presented in July a vision to build a “triple core” system spanning industrial resources, strategic resources and energy resources and leap to become a “national representative core resource supplier”. Posco Future M plans to strengthen competitiveness in its cathode and anode materials business based on the group’s value chain, including lithium salt lakes and graphite mines, and cement its position as a strategic resources key company.

artigo.texto: From e-commerce to cloud computing, artificial intelligence to remote work, the modern world is increasingly digital and dependent on data centers, the physical foundation of the 21st Century economy. As communities grapple with building out this vital infrastructure, a coalition of organizations dedicated to limited government and protecting the free market has issued a statement of principles to ensure that the United States continues to lead the world on data center infrastructure. The coalition of the Goldwater Institute, the Abundance Institute, the Pacific Legal Foundation, and the Taxpayers Protection Alliance—with foundational research input from the James Madison Institute—is urging legislators to enact policies that ensure technological growth is driven by free markets rather than bureaucratic mandates, while preserving individual rights, rewarding private initiative, and protecting ratepayers. The following seven principles start from a default policy posture of enabling data center infrastructure to grow: - Data centers are critical technology infrastructure that support an ecosystem of economic activity. We reject arbitrary bans, emergency moratoria, and discriminatory prohibitions on data center development, which raise costs and harm American technological leadership and national security. - Data centers are already essential infrastructure for AI, cloud computing, and the modern world. As demand grows, US firms must be free to expand capacity to host the infrastructure underpinning the next generation of services. - Property rights must be respected and the policy environment must be predictable. Data centers should be afforded the same legal certainties as traditional commerce. They should also be classified and treated consistently with comparable industrial or commercial uses, and governed by objective standards rather than retroactive or discriminatory permitting imposed under pressure. - Energy abundance and market access to power must be prioritized. AI and the digital economy require the nation’s energy capacity to grow, which is why we support a framework that values energy abundance, empowers consumer choice, protects property rights, and allows market forces to shape the energy landscape. - Fiscal integrity must be maintained and general ratepayers must be protected. Data centers should be neither privileged nor punished by the communities that host them. They should operate under rules that ensure their extraordinary new electric load is not shifted to households and existing businesses. - Water stewardship must be prioritized through evidence-based permitting. Responsible water use is fully compatible with data center growth. Under existing permitting processes, applicants can be required to demonstrate no harm to the watershed or to neighboring wells before a permit is issued. - The right to innovate and to cloud compute must be respected. With the rapid evolution of AI and high-performance computing, policy frameworks should favor experimentation over prohibition and flexibility over static assumptions about how data centers operate today. Data centers are as important today as previous innovations in telephones, broadband, and power plants were to prior generations. The builders of this modern-day infrastructure deserve the same freedom to respond to market signals to enable broad economic participation and national competitiveness. The digital future is going to be built somewhere. By sticking to a free-market framework that rewards private initiative and protects individual rights and ratepayers, U.S. leaders can ensure it is built right here. artigo.texto: The APEC Business Advisory Council Hong Kong, China, announced the launch of a major research initiative titled “Mobilising Capital for Nature: An APEC Roadmap for Nature Finance and Carbon Market Connectivity”on Thursday, with Standard Chartered (2888) acting as the lead authoring institution. The project, supported by knowledge partners Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero and Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing, aims to mobilize private capital for nature-positive activities while enhancing carbon market connectivity across APEC economies. The announcement was made during a side event organized by ABAC Hong Kong alongside the 2026 APEC Finance Ministers’ Meeting held in Hong Kong. The research will examine the policy, market, and financing conditions needed to unlock private capital, focusing on three areas: developing investable nature-related projects; embedding nature considerations into capital-allocation decisions; and using blended finance and catalytic capital to improve project bankability. Mobilizing private capital Mary Schapiro, vice chair and head of the GFANZ Secretariat, emphasized the critical role of market incentives in addressing environmental challenges. There is no sustainable future without nature, Schapiro said. "Carbon markets have the potential to play an important role in creating financial incentives for emissions reductions and nature-positive investment. GFANZ looks forward to supporting this research, which will help inform pathways for creating the enabling conditions for private capital to mobilise at scale." Mary Huen Wai-yi, ABAC Hong Kong representative and chief executive officer for Hong Kong, Greater China, and North Asia at Standard Chartered, noted the significance of the collaboration. "Standard Chartered is pleased to serve as lead author of this ABAC Hong Kong, China research, with GFANZ and HKEX contributing as knowledge partners," Huen said. "Bringing together public- and private-sector perspectives, the research will examine opportunities for greater cooperation across APEC and develop practical recommendations to strengthen nature finance, carbon market connectivity and the enabling conditions for private capital to support nature-positive investment." Supporting APEC agenda The initiative will support ABAC's sustainable-finance agenda and promote cross-border investment and collaboration on blended finance and carbon markets across APEC economies. The research findings are expected to be released in the third quarter of 2027.

Amazon, Tata Motors to Deploy 3,000 E-Trucks Across Indian Transportation Network Amazon and Tata collaborated to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon’s transportation network in India. In a press release, Tata Motors explained that the deployment marks a step towards extending fleet electrification beyond last-mile delivery in India’s e-commerce sector. The trucks will support the movement of customer shipments between facilities, across cities and along national freight corridors. The first batch of Tata electric trucks was flagged off by dignitaries in Delhi. CATL’s Australia Play Offers Lessons for India’s Battery Storage Sector Battery maker CATL has launched its 9 MWh TENER+ energy storage system at All-Energy Australia in Melbourne which its claims would require 40% fewer containers and has a 35% smaller footprint than conventional designs. artigo.texto: Portugal has introduced new technical regulations for large-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS), requiring advanced grid-forming capabilities and synthetic inertia to strengthen electricity grid stability and security. The new ministerial order, signed by Jean Paulo Gil Barroca, Secretary of State for Energy, came into effect on October 23, 2026. The regulations establish technical requirements for battery storage projects connecting to the country’s national electricity transmission network. Under the new framework, battery energy storage installations with a capacity of 45 MW or above, as well as facilities directly connected to the primary transmission grid, must incorporate grid-forming capabilities and synthetic inertia. These technologies are designed to help battery systems support the electricity network by maintaining stable voltage and frequency during fluctuations in power supply and demand. The introduction of these requirements comes as Portugal continues to increase the share of renewable energy in its electricity mix. Solar and wind power generation can vary depending on weather conditions, creating challenges for grid operators in maintaining a continuous and reliable electricity supply. Battery storage systems are expected to play an important role in balancing these variations and supporting the integration of additional renewable energy capacity. The regulations also introduce operational requirements for smaller battery installations. Battery energy storage plants with a rated capacity of 500 kW or higher must automatically switch from charging to discharging whenever grid frequency falls. This requirement is intended to enable storage facilities to respond quickly to changes in grid conditions and provide additional electricity when the system experiences a supply imbalance. Portugal’s new technical framework also places the country ahead of upcoming European Union developments concerning generator connection requirements. The national regulations are expected to be aligned with broader European grid connection standards as the EU updates its technical framework for electricity generation and storage facilities. The requirements will primarily apply to new connection applications submitted after the regulations came into force. Existing operational battery storage installations will generally remain exempt. However, facilities undergoing substantial modernization, capacity expansion or major equipment replacement may become subject to the updated technical requirements. The regulatory changes come at a time when Portugal is preparing to significantly expand its battery storage capacity. According to data from the Portuguese renewable energy association APREN, the country’s operational battery storage fleet currently stands at approximately 20 MW. This remains relatively small compared with the anticipated growth in electricity storage demand as renewable energy deployment increases. Government funding programmes and recent financial allocations for several battery storage projects are expected to support the expansion of the country’s storage infrastructure. These initiatives are aimed at improving flexibility in the electricity system, managing renewable energy generation and strengthening energy security. By introducing advanced technical requirements at an early stage of market development, Portugal aims to ensure that future battery storage installations contribute directly to grid stability. The regulations are also expected to establish clearer technical standards for developers and investors planning large-scale storage projects. As renewable energy capacity continues to grow, battery storage is expected to become increasingly important in maintaining electricity supply reliability. Portugal’s new framework represents a regulatory step towards building a more flexible, resilient and renewable energy-based power system. artigo.texto: No dia 28 de outubro, o Sr. Tran Chi Hung, Vice-Presidente do Comitê Popular da cidade de Can Tho , recebeu e trabalhou com uma delegação da Embaixada do Canadá e da organização CARE, liderada pela Sra. Francesca Bellone, Conselheira e Chefe de Cooperação para o Desenvolvimento da Embaixada do Canadá, a respeito do projeto C4G Carbon e do potencial dos projetos de carbono em manguezais na cidade de Can Tho. Cenas da sessão de trabalho. O Projeto de Assistência Técnica, cujo objetivo é capacitar a implementação de planos de mitigação das mudanças climáticas e mobilizar financiamento sustentável para a proteção e o desenvolvimento florestal, incluindo um mercado de carbono florestal de alta qualidade – abreviado como Projeto C4G – foi aprovado pelo Comitê Popular da Cidade de Can Tho na Decisão nº 965/QD-UBND, de 25 de agosto de 2025. O projeto é financiado pelo Governo do Canadá e pela CARE Canadá, por meio da CARE EUA , com um orçamento total superior a 16,4 bilhões de VND, e é implementado nas comunas de Cu Lao Dung, Lai Hoa e Vinh Hai, e nos distritos de Vinh Phuoc e Vinh Chau. Sra. Francesca Bellone, Conselheira e Chefe de Cooperação para o Desenvolvimento da Embaixada do Canadá, Discussão sobre o projeto C4G. Até o momento, o projeto organizou dois cursos básicos de capacitação sobre o mercado de créditos de carbono para 30 pessoas-chave e realizou um levantamento sobre os meios de subsistência em 16 comunidades em Vinh Chau, Vinh Hai e Cu Lao Dung. Os resultados iniciais identificaram diversas direções potenciais de geração de renda ligadas à proteção florestal: aquicultura sob a copa das árvores (criação de camarão em manguezais), mecanização adequada e utilização de subprodutos agrícolas para reduzir custos e aumentar a eficiência econômica . Com base na plataforma do projeto C4G, ambas as partes discutiram o potencial dos projetos de carbono em manguezais na cidade de Can Tho. De acordo com o Comitê Popular da cidade de Can Tho, as reservas de carbono dos manguezais dentro das áreas de proteção florestal da cidade totalizam 351.746,2 toneladas, concentradas principalmente ao longo da costa de Vinh Chau, Vinh Hai, Cu Lao Dung e Lai Hoa. As intervenções potenciais para o carbono em manguezais incluem reflorestamento e restauração, melhoria da eficiência da gestão florestal e limitação do desmatamento e da degradação florestal. A cidade de Can Tho espera que o Governo Canadense e a Embaixada do Canadá continuem a conectar a cidade com organizações, parceiros e investidores experientes no mercado de carbono de manguezais, a fim de buscar recursos para levantamentos detalhados, estudos de viabilidade, conclusão da documentação e desenvolvimento de projetos de acordo com os padrões apropriados. O Sr. Tran Chi Hung, Vice-Presidente do Comitê Popular da cidade de Can Tho , discursou na sessão de trabalho. Em seu discurso na reunião, o Sr. Tran Chi Hung expressou sua gratidão ao Governo Canadense, à Embaixada do Canadá e à organização CARE pelo financiamento e apoio na implementação do projeto C4G. A cidade está empenhada em utilizar a ajuda de forma eficaz, explorando racionalmente o potencial de carbono dos manguezais, criando recursos adicionais para a proteção e o desenvolvimento florestal e contribuindo para o compromisso do Vietnã de alcançar emissões líquidas zero até 2050. Além disso, a cidade espera participar mais ativamente da cadeia de valor do carbono florestal, não apenas vendendo créditos de carbono brutos, mas também desenvolvendo produtos de baixa emissão, ecoturismo e aquicultura sustentável com certificação de carbono, contribuindo para a melhoria da qualidade de vida da população, especialmente das mulheres e dos grupos vulneráveis. O Sr. Tran Chi Hung, Vice-Presidente do Comitê Popular da cidade de Can Tho , entregou um presente comemorativo à delegação. Texto e fotos: MEU THANH

artigo.texto: The monthly report published by APPA Renovables , corresponding to December 2025, confirms a trend that is beginning to consolidate in the Spanish energy system: storage is no longer a future promise, but an active and growing reality . During that month, 37371.93 MW were registered in requests for grid access for storage facilities , positioning itself as the largest volume among all categories of new connection demands. These requests far exceed other modalities such as grid-connected self-consumption with almost 25.6 GW and conventional consumption with 23.34 GW, reflecting the acceleration of the deployment of storage systems , both independent and hybridized with renewable generation. In total, the set of demand requests reached 90.42 GW in December , spread across 122 requests. This surge responds to the need to integrate increasing volumes of renewable energy into an increasingly electrified system. In December alone, renewables generated 11,359 GWh , which is equivalent to 48.9% of the Spanish electricity mix . Solar photovoltaics, however, continues to face challenges: its point-index stood at 0.83 , with an average capture price of 64.53/MWh , while wind power achieved a point-index of 0.90 with 68.89/MWh. This context of high renewable generation has also brought with it technical restrictions , evidenced in the adjustment services. During December, 5,188 GWh of renewable energy were recorded as going down , compared to just 42.2 GWh of energy going up. In real time, the figures were also compelling: 1,822 GWh of renewable energy "down" and only 59.8 GWh "up" , confirming the imbalance in the operation and the urgency of tools such as storage. In this context, the electricity market recorded an average daily price of 58.29/MWh , with the lowest values at 14:00 and peaks of 105.25/MWh at 20:00 . These price fluctuations present an opportunity for storage systems, which enable energy arbitrage and grid stabilization. On the other hand, the network access system remains under strain. As of December 2025, there are 16.54 GW of access capacity reserved for tenders and nodes of special interest , distributed across 386 nodes throughout the country . Communities such as Andalusia, Castile and León and Catalonia concentrate the largest volumes, both for generation and storage. Meanwhile, national demand reached 22,582 GWh in December, an increase of 4.2% compared to the same month in 2024 , which reinforces the need for backup infrastructure that can cover variations in supply. In line with this trend, Red Eléctrica de España is also moving forward with the development of specific demand access tenders , which will allow for the channeling of new installations in strategic areas of the grid. As highlighted in a recent analysis by Energía Estratégica , 80 demand nodes have been identified in 14 autonomous communities, with a particular concentration in regions such as Andalusia, Castile and León, and Aragon . This type of competition will allow for the organization and optimization of the deployment of storage and flexible consumption projects , facilitating the use of existing infrastructure and promoting territorial balance in access. As the system becomes more dependent on intermittent sources, the role of storage becomes unavoidable. The APPA Renovables report makes it clear that this technology already occupies a central place in the country's energy planning . If the application figures materialize, Spain will have tens of GW of additional storage capacity in the coming years, a transformation that will have a major impact on the flexibility, stability and efficiency of its energy mix. It is worth remembering that these topics will be at the center of the debate during the Future Energy Summit Iberia , which will be held on February 12 in Madrid . The event will bring together representatives from IDAE, leaders of energy communities and CEOs from the sector , who will analyze the progress of storage, the management of access nodes and the new regulatory scenario to accelerate the energy transition in Spain.

artigo.texto: Finlândia investiga dano ambiental em obras de data center do Google A polícia finlandesa informou nesta quinta-feira que iniciou uma investigação criminal sobre supostas violações da legislação ambiental no canteiro de obras de um data center do Google que está sendo planejado no norte da Finlândia. O projeto faz parte de um plano anunciado no mês passado pelo Google, subsidiária da Alphabet, de investir US$ 15 bilhões em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial na Finlândia — o que a empresa norte-americana descreveu como seu maior investimento na Europa. Autoridades afirmam que a Tuike Finland, uma subsidiária do Google, realizou o desmatamento e a drenagem em um local planejado em Muhos antes que as avaliações de impacto ambiental exigidas pela legislação finlandesa tivessem sido concluídas. "Com base em informações preliminares, houve ambiguidades e falhas na drenagem e na gestão da água no canteiro de obras do projeto do data center da Tuike Finland Oy", afirmou a polícia em comunicado. "A investigação criminal examinará, entre outras coisas, as circunstâncias relacionadas a essas questões", acrescentou. A Agência de Supervisão da Finlândia, responsável pelo controle de licenças e avaliações ambientais, ordenou, em 6 de outubro, que o Google suspendesse as medidas preparatórias que alteravam o meio ambiente em Muhos, bem como em um local separado. A empresa iniciou os trabalhos preparatórios com base em seu entendimento das aprovações exigidas pela legislação pertinente, conforme já havia informado anteriormente o Google. artigo.texto: To strengthen domestic battery storage manufacturing capabilities, Mecpower Solutions and Navitas Solar have collaborated to establish a 5 GWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing facility in Karjan, Gujarat. In a release, Navitas Solar stated that the facility is expected to commence operations in the first quarter of FY2027-28. The facility is expected to support the growing demand for integrated energy storage solutions across India’s renewable energy sector. The collaboration brings together Mecpower Solutions’ expertise in renewable energy project development, engineering, and execution with Navitas Solar’s integrated manufacturing capabilities. The proposed facility is envisioned as a platform integrating manufacturing, project deployment, and system integration capabilities. By leveraging their respective strengths, Mecpower Solutions and Navitas Solar aim to develop scalable battery storage solutions tailored to utility-scale, commercial, and industrial renewable energy applications. Developing Battery Storage Capacity Battery Energy Storage Systems are increasingly becoming a critical component of renewable energy infrastructure, helping address intermittency challenges, improve grid stability, and enable more efficient utilisation of renewable power. Through this collaboration, both companies aim to strengthen indigenous energy storage capabilities in line with India’s long-term renewable energy ambitions. The facility’s output is expected to support the project requirements of both companies, including EPC deployments and utility-scale renewable energy projects, while addressing the growing market demand for advanced energy storage solutions. Commenting on the development, Setul Shah, Director of Mecpower Solutions Limited, said,“As India continues to scale its renewable energy capacity, Battery Energy Storage Systems will be critical in addressing the intermittency of solar and wind power, improving grid flexibility, and enabling more predictable energy delivery. Our proposed 5 GWh manufacturing facility in Karjan represents a strategic step towards strengthening our capabilities across the energy storage value chain. By integrating battery storage manufacturing with our EPC and IPP businesses, we aim to develop scalable solutions that address the evolving needs of utility-scale renewable energy projects and support India's transition towards a more flexible and reliable power ecosystem.” Ankit Singhania, Director of Navitas Solar, said, “As India accelerates its transition towards renewable energy, Battery Energy Storage Systems are emerging as a critical component of the power sector, enabling better management of renewable intermittency, greater grid flexibility, and more efficient energy utilisation. Building domestic manufacturing capabilities in this segment will be an important step towards strengthening India’s clean-energy supply chain and supporting the evolving requirements of utility-scale storage projects. Through this collaboration, we aim to extend our manufacturing capabilities into a strategically important segment of the energy transition and contribute to the development of scalable storage solutions for India’s power sector.”

artigo.texto: The City of San Antonio on Thursday passed its first significant restrictions on data center development, requiring each of the computing facilities to seek City Council approval on a case-by-case basis before construction can begin. City Council approved the amendment to the city’s Unified Development Code (UDC) on a 9-2 vote, with District 9’s Misty Spears and District 10’s Mark Whyte — the council’s two conservatives — casting the dissenting votes. In addition to requiring council approval for each data center, the code amendment also limits the development of such facilities to the city’s heavy industrial and commercial zones. Additionally, the amendment gives council flexibility to require increased setbacks for certain facilities, depending on the surrounding area. An alternate proposal by Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones requiring a minimum setback of 1,000 feet was shot down during the session. In her remarks, Jones described her visit to a data center this week, when she reflected on the homes surrounding it. “Does anyone think that those homeowners’ property values increased when that data center showed up? It’s not likely,” Jones said. “It’s not likely that Redfin or Zillow will start advertising the distance to a data center as a selling point.” With her proposed amendment, Jones suggested offering public hearings in order to address a common complaint community members have voiced at town halls and permit hearings — that they didn’t have a say before a data center was built in their backyard. At a town hall hosted by Public Citizen and the Great Edwards Aquifer Alliance at Northwest Vista College earlier this month, one woman said she initially thought a warehouse was being constructed across the street from her home in Westover Hills. In impassioned public comments, she spoke of the “perpetual daylight” that flooded through her windows from the center and lamented that she was no longer able to see the stars at night. Like many others who live next to data centers, she got her first chance to vocalize her opposition after the facility was already built, she added. Instead of Jones’ proposed separate public hearings, the public will now have a chance to voice their opinion on each data center when facility representatives seek approval at city council sessions. Representing a win for environmentalists, the approved UDC amendment forbids data center development over the Edwards Aquifer Recharge Zone. Rachel Hanes, Policy Director of Greater Edwards Aquifer Alliance, had advocated for such protections relentlessly over the past year. In her public comments Thursday, Hanes stated that requiring data centers to seek Specific Use Authorization (or Special Use Permit) was standard practice in a number of cities around the country including Phoenix, Tucson, Atlanta, and Minneapolis as well as Lone Star State cities like El Paso, La Grange, Tyler and San Antonio’s Hill Country neighbor New Braunfels. Randy Neuman, representing the Scenic Loop Helotes Alliance, cautioned City Council during public comment to consider the cumulative effect of the proliferation of data centers on the area’s environment, comparing it to trucks going over a bridge. “Every truck might comply. Every truck might be perfectly legal. But as the number of trucks increases and the traffic patterns change, the question changes,” Neuman said. “It’s no longer simply, ‘Does this truck comply?’ It becomes, ‘Can the bridge carry the cumulative load?'” Council considered two separate data center proposals originally offered up by San Antonio’s Development Services Department at Thursday’s meeting before Jones had offered up her own last week. The plan council approved wasn’t the one favored by the data center industry. Business lobbyists at the meeting insisted that their preferred proposal was already a compromise, and any further restrictions would slow development or prompt tech companies to build their data centers in nearby Medina County instead. Both original proposals would limit data centers to certain industrial and commercial-zoned neighborhoods in the city. However, the option with looser regulations would have allowed data center operators to build “by right” in such neighborhoods, meaning they wouldn’t be required to seek community or council approval before starting construction. Until Thursday, data center operators have been able to build largely unfettered in San Antonio. The centers were zoned like any other commercial development, though environmental and neighborhood groups argue their potential environmental harms surpass those of many other commercial properties. That relative lack of oversight has allowed data centers to proliferate throughout the city as the San Antonio-Austin corridor experiences the largest data center boom in the country. Meanwhile, opposition to data centers grows in Texas. An October 2026 survey by the University of Houston Hobby School of Public Affairs shows that over 80% of Texas voters are concerned about data center impacts on resources and power, and 99% believe they should cover any required electrical grid expansion. San Antonio currently has roughly 40 data centers, 19 of which are in Councilman Ric Galvan’s District 6 on the West Side. Galvan has led the charge for stricter regulations since filing a formal request last October that council deliberate on the issue. Exactly a year later, this represents his first major regulatory victory as a council freshman. Though Galvan initially called for a 180-day moratorium on the facilities, that motion was shot down at an August City Council meeting. Members of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers Local 60 union who spoke at the meeting cautioned against adopting stringent rules for data center development, warning the regulations could kill high-paying jobs.
