artigo.texto: New Research Shows Scandium Doping Can Boost Sodium-Ion Battery Life A new report from Tokyo University of Science in Japan reveals how new materials can dramatically improve the durability and performance of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) through two distinct mechanisms—bulk doping and surface coating. A research team led by Professor Shinichi Komaba and Associate Professor Shinichi Kumakura from the Department of Applied Chemistry at Tokyo University of Science investigated how incorporating scandium, specifically Sc3+ , into cathodes based on a sodium-ion chemistry called NNMO. The study showed scandium doping can stabilize the battery's bulk crystal structure, while scandium coating can suppress surface degradation, offering two complementary strategies for boosting battery life and performance (Fig. 1). Tests revealed that scandium modification dramatically improved capacity retention after 100 charge-discharge cycles from 18.6% for undoped electrodes to 67.8% with scandium doping and 75.4% with scandium coating. The other highlight is that, in full sodium-ion cells, the scandium-coated cathode retained 91.2% of its initial capacity after 300 cycles, representing a substantial improvement in long-term battery durability, the team said. The research could be a boon to battery manufacturers, giving them a way to supply lower-cost, longer-lived SIB cells. Part of SIB's rising popularity is due to the much greater abundance of sodium compared to lithium. As a result, SIBs offer the potential to provide much lower cost per kW/h of capacity relative to today's lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries. In addition, SIBs could also offer better safety and low-temperature performance. While it’s still early, SIBs are already being commercialized in stationary, grid-connected battery energy storage systems (BESSs) and backup power applications, where they probably have the best of chance of beating Li-ion batteries. They are also breaking through in applications ranging from portable electronics to electric vehicles (EVs). The report, titled "Scandium doping and coating for improving O3-NaNi1/2Mn1/2O2 electrode in sodium battery,” was published in “Small”. a journal for micro/nano-technology, which can be accessed at this link: 10.1002/smll.75049. About the Author Lee Goldberg Contributing Editor Lee is the author of the popular PowerBites series. Lee Goldberg is a self-identified “Recovering Engineer,” Maker/Hacker, Green-Tech Maven, Aviator, Gadfly, and Geek Dad. He spent the first 18 years of his career helping design microprocessors, embedded systems, renewable energy applications, and the occasional interplanetary spacecraft. After trading his ‘scope and soldering iron for a keyboard and a second career as a tech journalist, he’s spent the next two decades at several print and online engineering publications. Lee’s current focus is power electronics, especially the technologies involved with energy efficiency, energy management, and renewable energy. This dovetails with his coverage of sustainable technologies and various environmental and social issues within the engineering community that he began in 1996. Lee also covers 3D printers, open-source hardware, and other Maker/Hacker technologies. Lee holds a BSEE in Electrical Engineering from Thomas Edison College, and participated in a colloquium on technology, society, and the environment at Goddard College’s Institute for Social Ecology. His book, “Green Electronics/Green Bottom Line - A Commonsense Guide To Environmentally Responsible Engineering and Management,” was published by Newnes Press. Lee, his wife Catherine, and his daughter Anwyn currently reside in the outskirts of Princeton N.J., where they masquerade as a typical suburban family. artigo.texto: Demanda por data centers está vindo, mas em velocidade menor que a desejada, diz CEO da CPFL Gustavo Estrella afirmou ainda que, só nos últimos 12 meses, a companhia negou pedidos de conexão que somam 8 GW de capacidade de data centers, e disse que parte destas solicitações era especulativa O presidente da CPFL Energia, Gustavo Estrella, avalia que ainda que a indústria de data centers esteja vindo de forma relevante para o Brasil, estando concentrada entre 60% e 70% nas áreas de concessão da companhia, a demanda esperada está vindo em velocidade menor que o projetado. “A gente segue com expectativa grande para atrair essa indústria”, afirmou durante painel do Brazil Wind Power, evento sobre energia eólica que está sendo realizado em São Paulo. Para ele, isso ocorre por conta de dois principais gargalos, sendo o primeiro a carga tributária, que deverá ser endereçada com a regulamentação do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata), afirmou. O segundo gargalo é a velocidade de expansão da rede de transmissão, que não acompanha a necessidade de mais rapidez na implantação característica dos data centers. “Existe uma demanda enorme de expansão e, se a gente pegar o tempo médio entre a identificação de necessidade de expansão da rede para que ela realmente aconteça e entre em operação, esse prazo médio é de sete anos”, apontou. Ele afirmou que, só nos últimos 12 meses, a companhia negou pedidos de conexão que somam 8 gigawatts (GW) de capacidade de data centers. O executivo explicou que parte deste montante é especulativo e que há, de fato, um desafio de identificar qual demanda efetivamente é real para justificar o aumento da infraestrutura, mas defendeu algum regime especial para que a indústria de data centers não deixe o país por conta desse gargalo.

artigo.texto: CATL's Australian Battery Push Comes With a Catch: Profit Is Trailing Revenue Published on 10/29/2026 at 11:21 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL used Sydney's All Energy Australia stage to roll out TENER+, a grid-scale storage system it says can trim a project's footprint by 12% and cut container requirements by as much as 40%. The launch came with memoranda of understanding signed alongside Hitachi Energy and EPEC Group covering project integration, validation and training — pairing the product debut with partners meant to help deploy it. The Australian angle runs deeper than hardware. Bloomberg reported, citing the company's regional chief, that CATL wants to turn Australian interest in sodium-ion batteries into firm project investments. That is an opening, not a booked outcome: whether interest hardens into investment decisions is the question that matters. A Big Top Line, a Smaller Bottom Line The stakes became clearer with the October 20 third-quarter 2026 results. Revenue climbed 58.58% year on year to RMB 165.221 billion. Net profit attributable to shareholders reached RMB 21.246 billion, up 14.54% from a year earlier — but down 5.77% from the prior quarter. That gap is the crux. Top-line growth is running far ahead of earnings growth, and the sequential decline sharpens scrutiny of profitability. The figures themselves neither explain the cause nor tie it to the Australian initiative; they simply set a yardstick. Growth, in other words, should eventually show up on the bottom line. Both headline numbers also fell short of analyst expectations, with Reuters pointing to intensifying competition in the battery market and cooling Chinese car sales as drags. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Citi responded on October 21 by cutting its target price for CATL's A-shares to 479 yuan from 500, citing a weaker-than-expected gross margin, higher expenses and larger impairments. The bank also trimmed its earnings forecasts for 2026–2028. Swap Networks and a Joint Venture Alongside the storage push, CATL is building out battery swapping on several fronts. An October 22 cooperation agreement with BAIC Group targets one million swap-compatible vehicles, with BAIC adapting models across several brands to CATL's Chocolate swap system. The tie-up spans vehicle development, battery supply, network build-out and new business models, and BAIC is expected to help fund swap stations through its dealers, according to media reports. Heavy trucks get their own play. On October 20 CATL presented the Tianxing II battery platform and the Qiji swap system, with signed orders for 13,000 units in the first batch. By year-end the company aims for 900 heavy-truck swap stations in China. The most binding commitment came on October 19, when CATL and Chery Automobile established the joint venture CATL Chery (Wuhu) New Energy Technology. Registered capital is CNY 1 billion, with CATL holding 51% and Chery 49%. A completed JV is a firmer step than a memorandum — yet it, too, does not by itself translate into an earnings contribution. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. What Would Prove the Bull Case The projects carry different degrees of commitment. Investment interest is not a formed joint venture; an agreed target volume says nothing about actual progress or eventual profit. Keeping those distinctions intact matters. The near-term catalyst would be tangible progress on Australian project investments. A longer-dated marker is the small-series production of solid-state batteries in 2027 that CATL told investors on Tuesday to expect — an expectation, not a started line. The bear case is straightforward: activity expands while profit keeps lagging revenue, a risk the latest quarter makes relevant without yet confirming. Should investment decisions materialize and new activity feed through to earnings, the optimistic reading gains support; if the weaker profit trend takes hold, ambitious project targets lose their pull. artigo.texto: Daelim Belefic Group has announced that its 1,000-kVA dry-type transformer has received UL and cUL certification for the U.S. and Canadian markets, expanding the company's portfolio of certified power distribution equipment. The three-phase, vacuum pressure encapsulated (VPE) transformer, designated model SGB-1000/0.48-0.48, is intended for integration into a mobile microgrid application in the United States. The company did not identify the project or provide a deployment schedule. Dry-type transformers use solid insulation and air cooling rather than liquid insulation systems. These characteristics make them suitable for a range of commercial and industrial applications, including data centers where electrical safety, maintenance requirements and installation flexibility are important considerations. In data center environments, dry-type transformers can support power distribution infrastructure serving IT equipment, cooling systems and other critical facility loads. The certification announcement comes as Daelim Belefic continues expanding its manufacturing operations in Jiangsu, China. The second phase of that expansion, initiated in 2025, is intended to strengthen production capabilities and improve manufacturing flexibility and delivery efficiency. Founded in April 2010, Daelim Belefic manufactures power and distribution transformers for commercial and industrial applications. The company reports serving customers in more than 40 countries and identifies manufacturing facilities in China and Houston, Texas, supporting its international power distribution business. For more information, visit www.daelimtransformer.com, www.daelim-electric.com Media Contact: Isabella Chen Marketing Department, DAELIM BELEFIC Group Email: [email protected]

artigo.texto: Lucro da BYD salta no 3º trimestre com exportações robustas, mas fica abaixo das estimativas Companhia exportou mais de 550,7 mil veículos de nova energia — categoria que inclui veículos totalmente elétricos e híbridos “plug-in” — durante o período, mais que o dobro do volume registrado um ano antes O lucro líquido da BYD cresceu 28% no terceiro trimestre, à medida que a maior vendedora de veículos elétricos do mundo avançou em sua expansão internacional para compensar a desaceleração da demanda em seu mercado doméstico, a China. A montadora, com sede em Shenzhen, informou nesta quinta-feira (29) que o lucro líquido somou 10,02 bilhões de yuans, equivalentes a US$ 1,50 bilhão, ante 7,82 bilhões de yuans no mesmo período do ano anterior. A receita aumentou 14%, para 221,49 bilhões de yuans (aproximadamente US$ 33,2 bilhões). Os resultados ficaram abaixo das expectativas do mercado. Analistas consultados pela Visible Alpha estimavam lucro líquido de 11,10 bilhões de yuans e receita de 240,83 bilhões de yuans para o trimestre. Nos nove meses encerrados em setembro, o lucro líquido recuou ligeiramente, de 23,33 bilhões de yuans para 22,34 bilhões de yuans, enquanto a receita permaneceu estável em 566,30 bilhões de yuans, informou a companhia. Os resultados da BYD evidenciam os desafios enfrentados pelas montadoras chinesas no maior mercado automotivo do mundo. Assim como muitas de suas concorrentes, a principal fabricante de veículos elétricos da China tem buscado crescimento no exterior, diante da desaceleração das vendas e do aumento da concorrência doméstica. As vendas internacionais continuaram impulsionando o crescimento da BYD no último trimestre, respondendo por mais de 40% do total. A companhia exportou mais de 550,7 mil veículos de nova energia — categoria que inclui veículos totalmente elétricos e híbridos “plug-in” — durante o período, mais que o dobro do volume registrado um ano antes. As vendas totais de veículos, por sua vez, cresceram em ritmo bem mais lento, de 19%, para 1,3 milhão de unidades.

artigo.texto: California-based company Coulomb Solutions Inc (CSI) has launched a dedicated mobile energy storage business to support the commercial vehicle market. On 1 November, CSI will transer all of its mobile battery energy storage system (BESS) activities to the new company, ReadyGrid. ReadyGrid will take on the engineering, product development, purchasing, manufacturing, sales, distribution, service and warranty formerly wrapped into CSI’s work as a provider of electrification components for the North American commercial vehicle market. ReadyGrid will develop, deliver and support rapidly deployable power solutions to get around infrastructure problems faced by fleet operators in electrifying their vehicles. Through a partnership with OEM CATL, CSI provides advanced high-voltage battery systems, low-voltage batteries and electrification components. It said that in recent years, it has had to place an increasingly significant amount of focus on delivering capacity where permanent grid capacity is unavailable. Related:Allye Energy launches ESS-integrated EV charger using repurposed EV battery packs As such, it has created the dedicated business to address those areas. ReadyGrid now has a portfolio of mobile energy storage systems ranging in capacity from 233kWh to 5MWh. These can support high-power commercial EV charging, demand response, grid resiliency and high-load facilities like data centres. Operating as a wholly-owned subsidiary of CSI, ReadyGrid’s flagship product is a 2.3MWh mobile BESS using CATL’s LFP battery technology, with an integrated 1MW power conversion system (PCS), providing 480V AC power and up to 1 MW bidirectional Megawatt Charging System (MCS) capability for high-power commercial vehicle and equipment charging. Increased electrification in the move away from fossil fuels is putting an increasing strain on electricity grids globally, as the infrastructure struggles with the additional load. While infrastructure upgrades will be an inevitable (and expensive) part of the energy transition, there are solutions to get around the constraint. In many cases, energy storage is used to maximise grid connection capacity, or increase the power that an EV charger can deliver without the need for a large grid connection. The portability element of the BESS products ReadyGrid offers offer faster deployment and off-grid use. These are some of the use cases of mobile BESS units by Allye Energy, which yesterday launched its first second-life EV battery-powered portable EV charger.

artigo.texto: The Bulloch County Data Center Committee officially began its work Tuesday, October 27, 2026, establishing its leadership, meeting schedule, and priorities as the county moves toward developing regulations for potential data center developments. During the approximately 80-minute organizational meeting at the North Main Annex Community Room, the 15-member committee unanimously elected retired trauma surgeon Frank Davis as chairman and businessman Glenn Womack as vice chairman. Members also agreed to meet on the first and third Mondays of each month at 5:30pm, beginning Monday, November 2. The committee's next meeting will focus on organizing its areas of study and discussing a possible request to extend the county's existing data center moratorium. The committee was established by the Bulloch County Board of Commissioners following its September decision to deny a proposed data center zoning amendment. Each of five commissioners appointed three members to the group, bringing together residents with backgrounds in business, agriculture, environmental protection, planning and zoning, education, and other fields. County Commission Chairman David Bennett opened Tuesday's meeting by outlining the committee's responsibilities and emphasizing that members would not be pressured to reach a conclusion before completing their research. "I'm not going to rush you to come to a conclusion," Bennett told members. Bennett acknowledged concerns about the county's current data center moratorium, which is scheduled to expire at the end of the year. He said he had already discussed the possibility of an extension with county staff and believed an additional 180 days could be legally justified. However, Bennett emphasized that extending the moratorium would ultimately require action by the full Board of Commissioners, not the committee itself. "I don't want y'all to worry about the length of the moratorium," Bennett said, encouraging members to focus on developing recommendations that would serve the county's long-term interests. Toward the end of the meeting, members voted to place a proposed request for a moratorium extension on their November 2 agenda. The motion did not specify how long an extension should last, instead focusing on allowing sufficient time for the committee to complete its work. View the BOC Data Center Committee Agenda Here View the meeting below: Committee tasked with reviewing proposed regulations The committee's central responsibility is to evaluate the technical and community impacts of data centers and deliver a comprehensive report with actionable recommendations concerning the county's draft data center zoning resolution and related policies. The county has already prepared a draft ordinance, which committee members will use as the starting point for their review rather than developing regulations entirely from scratch. Bennett explained that the goal is to establish clear expectations for developers considering building data centers in Bulloch County. Under that approach, the county would have regulations addressing matters such as available utilities, environmental standards, property requirements, and infrastructure responsibilities before a developer submits a proposal. The committee received 14 primary areas for consideration, including location and site selection, electricity demands, water usage, wastewater infrastructure, noise, lighting, emergency services, traffic, stormwater management, decommissioning requirements, and infrastructure costs. Members can also recommend additional topics for review. One proposed addition came from committee member Ben Watkins, who argued that the economic benefits and potential costs of data center developments should receive specific consideration. Watkins said the committee should evaluate whether data centers would provide meaningful financial benefits to the county and its residents rather than simply bringing new buildings to the area. Other members suggested examining state tax incentives and abatements, including potentially inviting representatives of the local legislative delegation to explain existing policies and possible changes. Members discuss whether their role is to determine how, or whether, data centers should come One of the meeting's most significant discussions centered on the committee's authority and whether its recommendations should focus exclusively on regulating data centers or also consider whether they are appropriate for Bulloch County. Alana Olson, a committee member associated with Coastal Communities United, questioned whether the group could ultimately recommend against accommodating data centers if its research identified infrastructure limitations or unacceptable impacts. Olson specifically raised concerns about wastewater treatment capacity, noting that Bulloch County does not operate its own sewage treatment facility and would need to consider the availability of municipal infrastructure and potential intergovernmental agreements. She encouraged members to remain open to the findings of their research rather than begin with a predetermined conclusion. Watkins offered a different interpretation of the committee's responsibilities, arguing that its primary task is to determine what standards would be necessary if data centers are permitted. "I'm coming here with not a no, not a yes, but a how," Watkins said. Bennett reinforced that the committee's assignment is to examine the existing draft regulations and recommend what requirements should be included. Decisions about whether to approve particular developments would remain with the county's elected officials under the applicable zoning process. The discussion underscored the different perspectives represented on the committee, although members generally agreed that their recommendations should be based on research and technical information. artigo.texto: Editais Nº 05/2026 e Nº 06/2026 dos leilões de Armazenamento de Energia são aprovados pela ANEEL Os certames serão realizados em 2 e 4 de dezembro de 2026 exclusivamente via Internet. A Diretoria da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (ANEEL) aprovou nesta terça-feira (27), durante Reunião Pública Extraordinária, os editais nº 05/2026-ANEEL e 06/2026-ANEEL, desnados à contratação de potência elétrica proveniente de novo Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia (SAE), denominado “Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade na forma de Potência de 2026”. De acordo com os editais aprovados, os certames serão realizados exclusivamente via internet em 2 e 4 de dezembro de 2026. Os produtos a serem negociados serão por disponibilidade de potência (MW), com início em 1º de agosto de 2028 e período de suprimento de 15 anos. O edital Nº 05/2026prevê critérios de nacionalização dos equipamentos e requisitos técnicos mínimos, já o edital nº 06/2026-ANEEL não tem essa previsão. A ANEEL atualizou os custos com base no PDE 2035 (referência oficial mais recente). O investimento de referência foi reduzido de R$ 9,8 milhões/MW para R$ 6,0 milhões/MW. Consequentemente, os valores da Garantia de Proposta (R$ 60 mil/MW), da Garantia de Fiel Cumprimento (R$ 600 mil/MW) e do Patrimônio Líquido mínimo exigido também foram reduzidos, diminuindo a barreira de entrada e aumentando a competitividade. Os custos da contratação de reserva de capacidade com baterias serão rateados apenas entre os geradores de energia, conforme regulamentação da ANEEL. O compromisso de entrega é por disponibilidade de potência máxima por 4 horas/ciclo, até 2 ciclos diários, limitado a 366 ciclos/ano. O pagamento será por receita fixa anual, ajustada conforme desempenho. Os SAEs deverão possuir capacidade para realizar recarga completa, de 0% a 100% da disponibilidade contratada, em um intervalo máximo de seis horas. O pagamento pela disponibilidade contratada será realizado por receita fixa, em R$/ano, a ser paga em doze parcelas mensais, as quais poderão ser reduzidas conforme a apuração do desempenho operativo em meses anteriores. Para consórcios de empresas do mesmo grupo, a comprovação do patrimônio líquido mínimo será feita apenas pela controladora, não computando o das controladas. O SAE pode compartilhar infraestrutura física com outros empreendimentos, desde que mantenha contratos e medições individualizados, evitando a caracterização de associação. O cálculo das garantias financeiras será feito com base na disponibilidade de potência contratada, reduzindo o valor exigido e tornando o certame mais competitivo. Os editais ficaram em Consulta Pública e, somados, receberam quase 2.500 sugestões de agentes e interessados no assunto. Os leilões seguem diretrizes da Lei nº 9.427/1996, Lei nº 10.848/2004 e Portarias do Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME), especialmente a Portaria Normativa GM/MME nº 136/2026.

artigo.texto: Finlândia investiga dano ambiental em obras de data center do Google A polícia finlandesa informou nesta quinta-feira que iniciou uma investigação criminal sobre supostas violações da legislação ambiental no canteiro de obras de um data center do Google que está sendo planejado no norte da Finlândia. O projeto faz parte de um plano anunciado no mês passado pelo Google, subsidiária da Alphabet, de investir US$ 15 bilhões em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial na Finlândia — o que a empresa norte-americana descreveu como seu maior investimento na Europa. Autoridades afirmam que a Tuike Finland, uma subsidiária do Google, realizou o desmatamento e a drenagem em um local planejado em Muhos antes que as avaliações de impacto ambiental exigidas pela legislação finlandesa tivessem sido concluídas. "Com base em informações preliminares, houve ambiguidades e falhas na drenagem e na gestão da água no canteiro de obras do projeto do data center da Tuike Finland Oy", afirmou a polícia em comunicado. "A investigação criminal examinará, entre outras coisas, as circunstâncias relacionadas a essas questões", acrescentou. A Agência de Supervisão da Finlândia, responsável pelo controle de licenças e avaliações ambientais, ordenou, em 6 de outubro, que o Google suspendesse as medidas preparatórias que alteravam o meio ambiente em Muhos, bem como em um local separado. A empresa iniciou os trabalhos preparatórios com base em seu entendimento das aprovações exigidas pela legislação pertinente, conforme já havia informado anteriormente o Google.

artigo.texto: Electrent Unveils Lithium Energy Storage Portfolio at REI 2026 28 Oct 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Haryana-based Electrent unveiled a new portfolio of lithium energy storage systems (ESS) and solar hybrid inverters at Renewable Energy India Expo (REI) 2026 in Greater Noida. The products are intended for residential, commercial and industrial applications, covering routine backup needs and higher-capacity power management. The launch comprises four product categories: universal lithium battery banks, in-built lithium ESS, online lithium ESS and solar hybrid inverters. The expanded range is designed to support different power backup and solar integration requirements across homes, businesses and industrial facilities. The universal battery banks use lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) chemistry and are available in 12.8 V, 25.6 V, 51.2 V and 128 V configurations. The in-built ESS range combines lithium batteries with inverters and includes the ESS 2350-60/25.6 V and ESS 5500-100/51.2 V models. Electrent’s online ESS range includes systems rated at 5 kVA and 30 kVA, aimed at applications requiring higher-capacity power backup. The company has also introduced four solar hybrid inverter models with different power ratings, phase configurations and ingress protection ratings. The inverter portfolio includes the 3 kW Solar Hybrid 4000/24 V with an IP21 rating, the 6.2 kW Solar Hybrid 7500/48 V with IP54 protection, the single-phase Pure Solar Hybrid 6.6 kW/48 V with IP66 protection and the three-phase Pure Solar Hybrid 12 kW/48 V, also rated IP66. These configurations provide options for varied installation environments and power requirements in residential and commercial settings. The products were displayed at India Expo Mart during the 2026 edition of REI, where the company presented its broader energy storage and solar integration offering. artigo.texto: MELBOURNE, Australia, Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HiTHIUM is showcasing the ARKVOLT F8S and HeroEE 16 at All Energy Australia 2026 on 28-29 October, offering distinct residential storage configurations. The F8S focuses on flexible high-voltage expansion, while the 16 kWh HeroEE 16 offers greater starting capacity for compatible low-voltage systems. Australia installed 276,011 home batteries in the first half of 2026, an increase of 52% compared with the preceding six months, according to the Clean Energy Council. The country also added 1.89 GW of rooftop solar capacity, with the federal Cheaper Home Batteries Program supporting battery uptake. The modular high-voltage F8S uses DC-BOOST technology to manage battery modules independently, allowing new and existing modules to work together. Its 8-32 kWh configurations enable households to expand storage in stages while retaining installed modules. It is rated for at least 11,000 cycles under specified test conditions, supporting long-term use. The HeroEE 16 combines a 16 kWh low-voltage lithium iron phosphate (LFP) design with a cycle-life rating of up to 11,000 cycles. Parallel connections allow expansion, while individual modules can be checked or replaced without dismantling the battery. It is designed for households seeking higher initial capacity and integration with compatible low-voltage inverters. With compatible inverters, both products can store rooftop solar power for later use. Backup functions require additional equipment. Ratel, General Manager at HiTHIUM Hero Energy, said: "As the global home energy transition deepens, the residential storage market is evolving to meet increasingly diverse and sophisticated customer needs. Leveraging HiTHIUM's deep expertise in cell R&D and smart manufacturing, we integrate inherent safety at the cell level into our system designs to deliver reliable, market-specific solutions for Australia. For us, global expansion is about more than geographic reach. We are dedicated to building long-term, sustainable value with our regional partners." HiTHIUM draws on its battery cell and system engineering expertise for residential storage. Cumulative global shipments exceeded 200 GWh as of October 2026. Its Australian utility-scale work includes its role in supplying 640 MWh of batteries for Lightsource bp's Woolooga BESS in Queensland, currently undergoing commissioning, and the supply of 500 MWh of batteries for FRV's Gnarwarre BESS in Victoria, under construction since August 2025. HiTHIUM aims to build ties with local installers, distributors and industry partners. Contact: Neil, Neil.chai@hithium.com

artigo.texto: A CATL lança globalmente sistema de armazenamento de energia de capacidade ultr elevada na All Energy 2026 e assina três memorandos de entendimento (MoUs) de parceria na Austrália AGÊNCIA DE COMUNICAÇÃO Conteúdo de responsabilidade da empresa 29 de outubro de 2026 MELBOURNE, Austrália, 29 de outubro de 2026 /PRNewswire/ — A Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL) apresentou hoje o TENER+ em seu lançamento global na All Energy Australia 2026, onde também exibiu o TENER Sodium. A empresa assinou memorandos de entendimento (MoUs) com a Hitachi Energy, o EPEC Group e a UNSW Sydney para reforçar a execução e a conexão à rede elétrica de projetos de baterias de grande escala na Austrália. TENER: projetado para oferecer desempenho de longo prazo e atender aos rigorosos requisitos de conexão à rede elétrica da Austrália Os sistemas de armazenamento de energia TENER+ e TENER Sodium da CATL foram projetados para oferecer a confiabilidade e o desempenho de longo prazo exigidos pelos projetos australianos de armazenamento de energia em escala de serviços públicos. Projetados para condições climáticas extremas, elas visam atender aos rigorosos requisitos de conexão à rede elétrica da Austrália e dar aos financiadores do projeto a confiança necessária na confiabilidade e no desempenho a longo prazo que sustentam as receitas das baterias. O TENER+ é um sistema de armazenamento de energia de capacidade ultr elevada, com 9 MWh, que ajuda os desenvolvedores a gerar valor para os projetos no longo prazo e maximizar sua capacidade de armazenamento. O TENER+ reduz em até 40% o número de contêineres necessários e em 12% a área ocupada pelo projeto, sendo ideal para empreendimentos com restrições de espaço. Seu sistema inteligente de gerenciamento térmico proporciona maior eficiência de ciclo e menor consumo de energia auxiliar. Várias baterias TENER+ podem ser comissionadas simultaneamente com um único clique para agilizar a implantação do projeto. Projetado para uma vida útil de 25 anos, o TENER+ oferece resfriamento a líquido e proteção para ambientes úmidos e costeiros. Os níveis de ruído permanecem abaixo de 65 dBA a 1 metro de distância. Seu design de exaustão superior com tecnologia “sem ilha de calor” direciona o ar quente verticalmente para cima, afastando-o das unidades adjacentes. Isso evita a dissipação horizontal do calor e minimiza o impacto térmico sobre as unidades PCS adjacentes, permitindo que operem à potência nominal máxima mesmo nas condições extremas do verão. O TENER Sodium é o primeiro sistema de armazenamento de energia com baterias de íons de sódio produzido em massa e validado em campo do mundo. Ele fornece mais de 30 MWh através de sua arquitetura de gabinete modular. Projetado para o calor da Austrália, ele opera em temperaturas de até 55 °C e oferece mais de 10.000 ciclos a 45 °C. Oferece 95% de eficiência de ida e volta, com uma vida útil de mais de 20 anos. Em conjunto, esses sistemas de armazenamento de energia oferecem aos desenvolvedores e proprietários de ativos a possibilidade de escolher entre as tecnologias de íons de lítio e de sódio. O sódio é muito mais abundante e está distribuído geograficamente de forma mais ampla do que o lítio, oferecendo uma alternativa para diversificar as cadeias de suprimentos de baterias. “O valor de uma bateria é medido ao longo de toda a sua vida útil de um projeto e não apenas no dia em que ela é colocada em funcionamento”, disse Zane Zhou, gerente-geral da CATL Austrália e Nova Zelândia. “Os desenvolvedores precisam ter confiança de que suas baterias suportarão os ciclos de operação previstos para comercialização no Mercado Nacional de Eletricidade e manterão um bom desempenho durante toda a vida útil dos sistemas instalados em projetos de grande escala. É para isso que o TENER+ e o TENER Sódio foram desenvolvidos. Estamos oferecendo tecnologias de íon-sódio e íon-lítio para dar aos proprietários e desenvolvedores de ativos a flexibilidade de escolher a tecnologia certa para o seu sucesso.” Parcerias da CATL com a indústria local para acelerar a transição energética da Austrália para fontes de energia limpa Os sistemas de armazenamento de energia TENER ajudam a superar os desafios da rede elétrica australiana diante da crescente participação das fontes renováveis na matriz energética. As fontes renováveis responderam por um recorde de 44,3% da geração de eletricidade do Mercado Nacional de Eletricidade (NEM) no trimestre encerrado em setembro de 2026. As baterias em escala de rede responderam por 8% da geração de eletricidade no pico da demanda noturna, superando pela primeira vez as usinas a gás, segundo o Operador do Mercado de Energia Australiano (AEMO). Com a desativação das usinas a carvão, a rede elétrica necessita cada vez mais de sistemas de armazenamento de energia com capacidade de formação de rede para garantir suporte de tensão e frequência. Para ajudar a fornecer mais armazenamento na Austrália, os três memorandos de entendimento da CATL visam abordar os desafios de uma rede elétrica movida a fontes renováveis usando a experiência e a inovação australianas. Os produtos de baterias CC da CATL e os sistemas de conversão de energia da Hitachi Energy formarão a base de uma oferta integrada proposta para a Austrália e para a região da Ásia-Pacífico. Por meio dessa parceria, a empresa busca ampliar a compatibilidade entre os sistemas, padronizar a implementação dos projetos e reduzir os riscos de integração. Na Austrália, a CATL colaborará com o EPEC Group e o Instituto de Pesquisa e Validação de Armazenamento de Energia de Xiamen (ESVL) para combinar sua tecnologia de armazenamento de energia com a experiência do EPEC em integração à rede elétrica e execução de projetos de engenharia, além de aproveitar a capacidade do ESVL de validar sistemas em escala real. As partes buscam fortalecer a validação técnica e acelerar a implementação de projetos de armazenamento de energia confiáveis, economicamente viáveis e compatívei

artigo.texto: Where Containment Meets Compliance: How a Life-Safety Ban Reshaped Data Center Containment For years, data center containment relied on "fallout panels"— horizontal roof panels that helped to seal roof systems in cold aisle containment, vital for cooling efficiency. In the case of fire, these panels were designed to drop from the horizontal roof system, allowing suppression systems or sprinklers to operate. The design worked as intended but also created an unintended consequence in some jurisdictions. Since the panels drop out of the horizontal roof system and fall to the floor, some AHJs (Authorities Having Jurisdiction) have flagged this as a life-safety issue rather than a minor compliance footnote, banning fallout panels in all new builds and retrofits. This left data centers in these jurisdictions with no compliant means of sealing containment roofs. For years, facilities were left with two options: leave the gap or install sprinklers in every aisle. Most operators took the simpler route, leaving the aisle never truly sealed. What was required was an alternative material to solve the problem in these locations. Something that wouldn't fall, wouldn't burn, and would disappear cleanly when hit with sprinkler water. Surprisingly, the fix came from outside the industry, found in a material already used in food production and nuclear facilities. It was EPA-safe, non-combustible, and able to dissolve almost instantly on water contact. This article details DAB panels' origin story to help us understand why this material exists and why it's now effectively the de facto standard for compliant containment in markets where fire code enforcement is strictest. Where Containment Meets Compliance: How a Life-Safety Ban Reshaped Data Center Containment Containment has long been considered the standard for cooling efficiency. Sealing the aisle and properly regulating airflow are relatively straightforward measures based on well-established principles of physics that consistently deliver proven energy savings and lower cooling costs. But full containment only works if the aisle is completely sealed. So why has the roof never been fully sealed in all data center locations? For many years, the ceiling panel has been closed with what the industry refers to as fallout panels. As per fire regulations, these lightweight roof panels were designed and engineered to do exactly what their name suggests; in a fire event, they dropped out of the horizontal roof containment grid, clearing the way for sprinklers to reach the aisle below. It was a clever piece of dual-purpose design: seal the space for cooling, then drop out of the way for safety. The trouble exists in some jurisdictions with "dropping out of the way". When the Fix Became the Problem Fallout panels worked in exactly the way they were built. However, in a fire event, as the panels were released from the horizontal containment ceiling grid, they landed, and in a working aisle, they drop into the very space that first responders and evacuating personnel needed to move through. Unfortunately, what had been designed as a life-safety feature was, in practice, generating debris in the exact corridor people needed clear. While not an issue everywhere, AHJs didn't just treat the situation as a minor code infringement. It was flagged as a safety issue, and the response was decisive. Fallout panels were banned outright across an increasing number of jurisdictions. That left the data center industry with a real design quandary. Containment still needed a sealed roof to deliver its cooling efficiency. Fire code still needed suppression systems to reach the aisle unobstructed, and the one option that reconciled those two demands was no longer allowed. Two Poor Options With fallout panels no longer a choice in certain jurisdictions, this left new and legacy data centers with no compliant means of sealing containment roofs. Data center operators were left picking between two compromises: - Leave the roof gap. Skip a sealed roof system of the cold aisle entirely, accepting the air mixing between the hot and cold aisles and absorbing the efficiency loss. This was, and still is, the path most operators in these locations defaulted to, simply because it required no new engineering. It also meant a large share of "contained" data halls were never truly sealed. - Sprinkler every aisle. Rather than relying on panels to clear the way for fire suppression, install pipe sprinkler heads inside every contained aisle. While this option solved the code problem, it adds cost, complexity, and a maintenance burden most facilities aren't designed or prepared for. Neither option solves the underlying problem. So how do you seal a contained cold aisle for cooling purposes while guaranteeing, with certainty, that it will not become an obstruction or a hazard the moment fire suppression is activated? Looking Outside the Industry The eventual answer didn't come from a cooling engineer or a fire protection specialist. It came from re-examining the material itself. The specification was narrow and demanding. The panel required was one that would not fall as rigid debris, would not burn or add fuel to the fire, and would immediately remove itself from the aisle the instant it contacted sprinkler water. It needed to do this automatically without manual removal or contribute to post-incident cleanup. It was discovered that this combination of properties did already exist, just not near any data center. A water-soluble, non-combustible sheet material had been used for years in food production environments, and in nuclear facility applications. This solution is suitable for all contexts where a barrier needs to hold its shape under normal conditions and then disappear instantly and safely on contact with water. By virtue of its existing applications, this material has already been certified EPA-safe, is already non-combustible, and already proven to dissolve almost immediately on water contact

artigo.texto: Exclusivo: Governo publicará portaria que define cobertura setorial do mercado regulado de carbono As regras começam a valer a partir de 2027 para empresas com emissões anuais acima de 10 mil toneladas O Ministério da Fazenda publicará nesta quinta-feira (28) portaria que define a cobertura setorial do mercado regulado de carbono brasileiro. A norma estabelece os segmentos enquadrados nas obrigações de Monitoramento, Relato e Verificação (MRV) de emissões de gases de efeito estufa e o cronograma para implementação gradual. As regras começam a valer a partir de 2027 para empresas com emissões anuais acima de 10 mil toneladas. A Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono estima que menos de 600 grandes empresas terão de iniciar os processos de relato de emissões, ou seja, informar de forma precisa a quantidade de CO2 emitida. O objetivo do governo é construir uma base oficial de dados antes do início do mercado regulado de carbono. O texto final traz mudanças em relação à proposta submetida à consulta pública em 28 de julho, após diferentes setores pedirem alterações na distribuição das atividades entre as três etapas de implementação. Em entrevista ao Valor, a secretária extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono, Cristina Reis, avaliou o resultado da consulta pública como positivo. Sem a inclusão de novos segmentos, o plano mantém o total de 17 setores, mas redistribui algumas atividades entre as etapas do cronograma. Para Reis, a manutenção do escopo confirma o acerto da proposta original do governo federal. Sobre a antecipação de alguns segmentos para a primeira fase, a secretária afirmou que o movimento demonstra que “os setores já se consideram maduros, preparados e entendem o valor da regulamentação”. A publicação da portaria não exige a apresentação imediata de relatórios nem estabelece limites de emissão ou custos para as empresas. O teto de emissões e a distribuição gratuita de cotas brasileiras de emissão (CBEs) estão previstos para 2030, com o início do Plano Nacional de Alocação (PNA). Até lá, a Fazenda recomenda que as empresas acompanhem a regulamentação e se familiarizem com o mercado de carbono. A qualificação dos setores dependerá da definição das metodologias específicas, ainda em elaboração. Para o secretário-adjunto da Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono, José Pedro Bastos Neves, a regulamentação também pode abrir oportunidades para soluções nacionais de descarbonização. “Em geral, essa pauta da descarbonização, diferentemente de outros países do mundo, em que é vista muito como um aumento de custos, no Brasil traz em si uma oportunidade de certa forma valorizar soluções tecnológicas, rotas de descarbonização que já são desenvolvidas no Brasil”, disse Neves. A primeira etapa de MRV começa em 2027 e abrange as indústrias de alumínio, ferro e aço em usinas integradas, cimento, exploração e produção de petróleo e gás natural, papel e celulose, vidro, além de alguns segmentos da indústria química e da mineração de minério de ferro e de bauxita. Em relação ao desenho preliminar, foram antecipados para a primeira etapa o vidro, a mineração de minério de ferro e bauxita e alguns segmentos da indústria química. Já o refino de petróleo e o transporte aéreo deixaram de integrar essa fase. A segunda etapa, prevista para começar até 2029, abrangerá cerâmica, ferro e aço em usinas semi-integradas, atividades da indústria química não incluídas na primeira etapa, indústria de alimentos e bebidas, mineração das demais substâncias minerais, refino de petróleo e setor elétrico. Deixam a segunda fase os segmentos de alumínio reciclado, vidro, resíduos sólidos e tratamento de esgoto. A terceira etapa permanece prevista para 2031 e inclui os transportes rodoviário, ferroviário e aquaviário, sem alterações em relação à proposta original. Cada etapa prevê um período de preparação e adaptação de quatro anos antes da consolidação dos dados. No primeiro ano, as empresas devem elaborar o plano de monitoramento e submetê-lo à aprovação do órgão gestor do Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE). No segundo e no terceiro anos, começa o monitoramento efetivo, com a medição e a coleta de dados sobre emissões e remoções de gases de efeito estufa. No quarto ano, ocorre a consolidação dos dados e o envio do relato de emissões no âmbito do PNA. A retirada dos setores de resíduos sólidos e tratamento de esgoto do cronograma geral decorre, segundo Reis, do entendimento de que a própria legislação afasta obrigações diretas para atividades que comprovadamente apresentam atributos de produção sustentáveis. A equipe técnica decidiu tratar o setor separadamente. “Isso significa que, para incentivar a descarbonização, e aqui a gente está falando principalmente da emissão de metano no setor de resíduos, o melhor é que eles atuem pelo lado do voluntário, gerando crédito de carbono, e caso tenham alta integridade e metodologia credenciada, esses créditos de carbono podem se tornar CRVE, que é o Certificado de Remoção Verificada de Emissões”, explicou a secretária. Segundo Reis, o mecanismo também pode contribuir para ampliar o tratamento de resíduos em instalações sanitárias e estimular o encerramento de lixões no país. A Fazenda também atendeu a um pedido do setor aéreo para alinhar o cronograma de monitoramento, relato e verificação à implementação do ProBioQAV, programa voltado ao mercado de combustível sustentável de aviação (SAF). “Simplificando: ao invés de fixar o transporte aéreo na etapa 1, definimos que a exigência ocorrerá no momento em que o ProBioQAV for regulamentado”, resumiu ela. O MRV e a fiscalização do cumprimento das metas regulatórias de redução de emissões de voos domésticos estão sob responsabilidade da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac), que terminou consulta pública sobre o assunto no início de outubro.

artigo.texto: Australian Vanadium (ASX:AVL) AVL (ASX:AVL) unveiled its Lumina vanadium flow battery (VFB) energy storage system (BESS) design and local content approach at the All Energy Australia conference held in Melbourne in October 2026, highlighting the current landscape of global VFB deployments and AVL's strategic position in the Australian market. Key Highlights - AVL’s Lumina VFB BESS design is optimized to maximize Australian local content across pumps, tanks, pipework, civil construction, EPCM, and electrolyte manufacturing. - Globally, over 8 GWh of vanadium flow batteries are operational, with an additional 44 GWh of projects either under construction or announced. - AVL has launched commercial electrolyte production and identified opportunities for local manufacturing of cell stack technology within Australia. - Three notable VFB projects planned for 2026 include the Flexbase Technology Centre (2.1 GWh, Switzerland), Hunter VFB (864 MWh, Australia), and Kalgoorlie VBESS (500 MWh, Australia, aiming for 2029 operation). Lumina BESS Architecture and Local Content Potential Designed to maximize Australian local content, AVL’s Lumina vanadium flow battery BESS architecture incorporates off-the-shelf pumps, tanks, and pipework that leverage the local supply chain. Civil works and EPCM services are sourced from Western Australia-based EPC partners and local contractors. AVL has established commercial electrolyte production and identified potential for cell stack technology manufacturing in Australia. However, inverter and power control systems currently require offshore procurement due to limited domestic manufacturing capabilities. Local content percentages are indicative and vary depending on specific project requirements. Global Deployment of Vanadium Flow Batteries According to the filing, over 8 GWh of vanadium flow batteries are operational worldwide, with an additional 44 GWh of projects either under construction or announced as of 2025. Data from Vanitec indicates that individual VFB projects now exceed 1 GWh in capacity. The filing notes that full deployment of the Flexbase, Hunter VFB, and Kalgoorlie VBESS projects would account for nearly 12% of the estimated annual global vanadium oxide supply in new vanadium demand. This underscores the evolution of the technology from bespoke solutions to scalable Australian projects. Vanadium Flow Battery Features Highlighted in Filing The filing emphasizes several key features of vanadium flow battery systems supporting AVL’s Lumina product, including minimal degradation with full depth of discharge, absence of thermal runaway risk, suitability for installation near critical infrastructure such as data centers and in hot climates, and a design lifespan exceeding 30 years. Additionally, the electrolyte is not consumed during operation and retains value over time, facilitating recycling and reuse. These attributes are detailed in an AVL filing dated 9 May 2025 titled "Project Lumina confirms improved competitiveness," as referenced in the presentation.

artigo.texto: Oshtemo Township considers extending moratoriums on energy projects, data centers OSHTEMO TWP, Mich. — Oshtemo Township leaders are proposing to align several moratoriums on energy projects and data centers through Dec. 31, 2027, as they continue developing regulations. "We'll just make them all uniform, all the same," Township Attorney James Porter said during Tuesday's meeting. Board members also received an update on NewEdge Power, a company that could pursue an energy project in the township. According to an email shared with officials, the earliest the company expects to meet with the township is September or October 2027, with a permit application potentially following in early 2028. Before moving forward, the project would need to go through the MISO queue, a regional process for evaluating proposed electricity projects, and demonstrate its proposed location is suitable. “They’re going to have to show, whether here or in Lansing, that their proposed location is suitable,” Porter said. Township Supervisor Cheri Bell said NewEdge’s plans have not changed because of the township’s work on the ordinance. “Their plans are not altered based on the activity of the planning commission and the creation of the ordinance,” Bell said. The proposed moratorium changes have not yet been approved by the board.

artigo.texto: Company highlights application-specific battery packs, BESS solutions and energy management technologies for electric mobility, telecom and energy storage applications. NASH Energy, an Indian manufacturer of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells and integrated energy storage solutions, showcased its portfolio of battery packs, energy storage systems and battery management technologies at The Battery Show India 2026, held from October 22–24, 2026, at the India Expo Centre & Mart, Greater Noida, NCR. At the exhibition, NASH Energy presented its Made-in-India NE32140 LFP cells alongside solutions spanning battery packs, battery enclosures, electric mobility applications, telecom energy systems and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). NASH Energy is part of the NASH Group, an engineering-led technology and manufacturing company with exports to more than 25 countries and an R&D centre in Japan. The company’s participation highlighted the Group’s ability to integrate product engineering, electronics, battery management capabilities and advanced manufacturing to develop application-specific energy solutions. The showcase featured multiple battery pack configurations and enclosure designs developed for different application requirements. These included 5kWh battery packs with cylindrical and prismatic cells, along with a 16kWh battery pack in a single-enclosure design. NASH Energy also displayed a 5kWh E-Rickshaw battery pack and a two-wheeler battery solution comprising two 51.2V, 45Ah packs. For telecom and distributed energy applications, the company demonstrated a 48V, 45Ah telecom enclosure, a 5kWh wall-mounted enclosure with NASH Energy branding and an integrated 1kWh battery solution with an inverter. An enclosure featuring a 6kWh battery pack was also presented to demonstrate battery enclosure design and pack architecture. The exhibition also highlighted NASH Energy’s capabilities in larger-scale energy storage through showcase models of 261kWh and 500kWh Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). These displays provided an overview of the Group’s capabilities in developing scalable energy storage solutions to address emerging energy infrastructure requirements. NASH Group has developed an integrated engineering ecosystem with the capability to manufacture 90% of a battery pack. According to the company, this enables it to support customers throughout the product lifecycle, from product development and engineering to manufacturing and deployment. Its energy technology capabilities include hardware and Smart Battery Management Systems (BMS) supporting LFP and NMC battery chemistries across applications such as electric mobility, renewable energy storage, UPS and telecom. The Group’s energy technology portfolio is further supported by software and battery management solutions, including Battmonx, BMS Automation and EVolt. These technologies bring together battery monitoring, management and energy management capabilities. NASH Group’s integrated approach combines engineering, technology and manufacturing expertise to develop customised solutions aligned with specific industry and application requirements. With more than 175 R&D engineers, over 15 manufacturing facilities, exports to more than 25 countries and over five decades of manufacturing experience, NASH Group continues to strengthen its capabilities as an engineering and technology partner for global customers. Through its group companies, NASH Industries, NASH Tech Labs and NASH Energy, the Group brings together expertise across precision manufacturing, electronics, embedded computing, intelligent vision, automation and energy technologies. Founded in 1971, NASH Group has evolved from a manufacturing company into an engineering-led technology and manufacturing enterprise. Its capabilities span product design and development, electronics engineering, embedded systems, AIoT, Smart Vision, industrial computing, automation, energy technologies and advanced manufacturing, supporting the development and production of technology solutions for customers across global markets. NASH Energy’s participation at The Battery Show India 2026 highlighted its expanding portfolio of domestically manufactured LFP cells, application-specific battery packs and scalable energy storage solutions, reflecting the growing importance of integrated battery technologies in India’s electric mobility and energy storage sectors. artigo.texto: Tesla, Sungrow, Fluence, Wartsila and BYD are competing for a larger share of the global battery energy storage system (BESS) market as utilities, renewable energy developers and investors accelerate spending on energy storage infrastructure. Their offerings differ significantly in battery capacity, system efficiency, software capabilities, safety technologies, operating costs and long-term investment returns. Selecting the best BESS integrator in 2026 requires more than comparing battery prices. Developers must evaluate installed costs, guaranteed electricity delivery, degradation, round-trip efficiency, warranties, maintenance and revenue optimisation capabilities. According to Wood Mackenzie’s 2026 global BESS integrator ranking, global battery storage capacity exceeded 100 GW in 2025. Sungrow ranked first in the comprehensive assessment, followed by Tesla and CATL, while BYD secured fourth position. Fluence and Wärtsilä also featured among the top ten. Chinese BESS integrators accounted for 76 percent of global market share in 2025, demonstrating their growing influence over battery storage supply chains and project economics. However, supplier rankings do not necessarily indicate which integrator offers the highest returns for individual projects. Tesla Megapack: Integrated Battery Storage and AI-Driven Energy Trading Tesla has established a strong position in utility-scale energy storage through its Megapack platform, combining battery modules, power electronics, thermal management and software. The company’s Megapack energy storage system is designed for large-scale renewable energy integration, grid balancing and electricity trading. Examples of Tesla’s offerings include: Megapack utility-scale battery storage systems with integrated power conversion and thermal management. Autobidder software for automated electricity trading and revenue optimisation. Powerhub software for monitoring and controlling distributed energy resources. Integrated project engineering, commissioning and maintenance services, depending on contract scope. Tesla’s Autobidder platform is particularly relevant to merchant battery storage projects that earn revenue from electricity price fluctuations and ancillary services. For example, a 100 MW battery project may charge during periods of low electricity prices and discharge when wholesale prices increase. Automated trading software can help determine dispatch schedules, although profitability depends on market access, charging costs, battery degradation and trading fees. Tesla’s integrated approach may reduce coordination requirements between equipment suppliers and software providers. However, developers should evaluate Megapack pricing, guaranteed AC output, warranty exclusions, software charges and local service availability. Sungrow PowerTitan: Competitive Storage Systems and Power Electronics Sungrow combines battery storage integration with established expertise in solar inverters, power conversion and grid-connected energy systems. Its PowerTitan portfolio targets utility-scale battery projects requiring integrated equipment, thermal management and grid support. Examples of Sungrow’s offerings include: PowerTitan 2.0 liquid-cooled battery energy storage systems. PowerTitan 3.0 utility-scale energy storage platform. Power conversion systems and grid-support technologies. Integrated monitoring, energy management and lifecycle services. PowerTitan 2.0 incorporates a liquid-cooled design and integrated AC architecture intended to simplify installation and improve thermal management. Efficient cooling is important because elevated battery temperatures can accelerate degradation and increase maintenance requirements. Sungrow’s power electronics expertise may also benefit projects requiring grid-forming capabilities, voltage regulation and renewable energy integration. For developers, Sungrow’s competitiveness should be measured through guaranteed AC efficiency, usable battery capacity, installation costs and service response times. Its manufacturing scale may support competitive equipment pricing, but buyers should compare complete project quotations rather than battery hardware prices alone. Fluence: Battery Storage Software and Revenue Optimisation Fluence competes through integrated battery storage systems, digital controls, asset management and electricity market optimisation. Its energy storage technology portfolio targets utilities, renewable developers and independent power producers. Examples of Fluence’s offerings include: Gridstack Pro utility-scale battery energy storage systems. Fluence OS for battery storage control and management. Mosaic software for automated bidding and revenue optimisation. Nispera software for renewable energy and storage asset-performance monitoring. Lifecycle services covering operations, maintenance and performance management. Fluence’s software offerings can be particularly valuable for storage projects participating in multiple electricity markets. For example, a battery may earn revenue from energy arbitrage, frequency regulation and capacity services, subject to market regulations. Mosaic can support trading decisions, while Nispera provides performance monitoring and operational insights. However, developers should request independently verifiable results demonstrating additional revenue after software fees, electricity losses and operating expenses. A projected improvement in trading revenue should not be confused with guaranteed investment returns. Wartsila: Battery Storage Integration and Lifecycle Services Wartsila offers battery storage integration, energy management software and power-system engineering capabilities. Its energy storage business is particularly relevant to renewable energy integration, hybrid power plants, island grids and complex electricity systems. artigo.texto: Bondada Engineering Bags LOI for 120 MWh Battery Storage Project 28 Oct 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Bondada Engineering has received a Letter of Intent (LOI) from Gujarat Industries Power Company (GIPCL) to develop a 20 MW/120 MWh Vanadium Redox Flow Battery Energy Storage System (VRFB BESS) in Vadodara, Gujarat. The project will be located at GIPCL’s 165 MW natural gas power plant complex and includes a 10-year operations and maintenance (O&M) contract. The Hyderabad-based engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company said the project would support its expansion into advanced energy storage technologies. It described the installation as India’s largest grid-scale Vanadium Redox Flow Battery Energy Storage System, positioning the project within the country’s growing battery energy storage market. Bondada Engineering’s scope covers the engineering, procurement and construction of the 120 MWh VRFB-based system. It will also provide operations and maintenance services for 10 years. The project is scheduled for completion within 18 months of the receipt of the Notice of Award (NOA). The company’s chairman and managing director, Dr Bondada Raghavendra Rao, said the project represented an important step in its expansion into advanced energy storage solutions. He noted that the increasing deployment of renewable energy in India would raise the importance of storage systems in maintaining reliable and efficient power supply. Vanadium Redox Flow Battery technology is being considered for long-duration energy storage because it can store and discharge electricity over extended periods. The technology uses liquid electrolytes and is suited to applications requiring repeated charging and discharge cycles. The Government of India has set a target of deploying approximately 236 GWh of battery energy storage systems by 2030, indicating the scale of infrastructure required to support the country’s energy transition. Bondada Engineering’s project adds to the development of grid-scale storage capacity in Gujarat and broadens the company’s role beyond conventional EPC activities. artigo.texto: Technology and Scienceupdated 4h ago2 min read EnergyFluo Orchestrates Grid, Storage, And On-Site Generation For U.S. Data Centers 7 Other3 Western Mainstream This article is an automated aggregation of coverage from news outlets. Our editorials offer in-depth analysis curated by the NewsCord team. AI-driven data centers spur microgrid and on-site generation investments to meet power demand. Utilities face substantial costs and planning for connecting data centers to expanding grids. AI drives power rethink Artificial intelligence is reshaping the energy demands of data centers, as computing equipment becomes more power-intensive and operators face a dual challenge of securing electricity while managing interactions between power supply, storage, cooling, and backup generation. U.S. data centers accounted for approximately 4.7% of the nation’s electricity consumption in 2024, a share projected to reach 11.8% by 2030 in Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory’s reference case. The International Energy Agency projected that a single advanced server rack could have peak power demand equivalent to that of 65 U.S. households by 2027. TransGrid Energy CEO Dr. Youngchoon Park said EnergyFluo “orchestrates grid, storage and on-site generation as one system and optimizes the load behind them, so operators can put more megawatts to work for IT and run their entire fleet from one intelligent view.” EnergyFluo was among the first AI-enabled products globally to receive certification from UL Solutions under UL 3115 in March 2026. Community trust becomes key 7x24 Exchange Chairman Bob Cassiliano said community opposition has overtaken several of the industry’s other longstanding concerns as the conference opened its technical program in San Antonio under the themeThe Intersection of AI & Traditional Data Centers. Cassiliano said, “Last year it was artificial intelligence, sustainability, the labor shortage,” and he added, “they have been superseded by community opposition to data centers.” AI futurist and former Google DeepMind executive Steve Brown told attendees, “We're using data centers to turn energy into intelligence,” as he described physical infrastructure required for an increasingly AI-driven economy. Brown said, “There may be a financial bubble, there may be a debt bubble, but I do not believe there is a demand bubble,” while he argued agentic computing could sustain expansion. Google power systems engineer Ashish Upreti and Cummins technical advisor Rich Scroggins described layered approaches to mitigating power swings, including software-level controls and supercapacitors for extremely short-duration spikes. Microgrids and grid costs Soaring demand from data center developers, widespread integration of clean power, and dwindling grid capacity on regional networks have spurred investment and development in microgrid solutions. The U.S. microgrid market is forecast to rise from $8 billion in 2025 to $21.2 billion by 2030, and a $2.6 billion acquisition in September of Utility Innovation Group by Vertiv was cited. Scale Microgrids General Manager of Data Centers Mike Grunow told Reuters Events that Scale is working on multiple new data center projects ranging from 200 to 500 MW, with several expected to exceed 1 GW. WTTW News said records filed by ComEd in an ongoing regulatory matter show that new infrastructure and system upgrades needed to connect 30 data centers to the grid will cost $3.1 billion. ComEd director of economic and workforce development Max Leichtman said, “The deposits that today stand at $721 million may continue to increase as these projects move forward and become more mature and more well-defined,” while consumer advocates warned ratepayers could face shortfalls.

artigo.texto: Residents Question if Firefighters Can Handle Issues at Proposed Battery Storage Plant near Saugerties, NY SAUGERTIES, N.Y. — Councilperson Mike Ivino took issue with several people during a Town Board meeting after hearing remarks he considered to be an affront to his credibility on whether fires at a proposed Key Capture Energy lithium-ion battery facility could be properly contained. During the Wednesday, Oct. 21, session, Ivino said comments made by a couple — apparently between themselves — required him to respond with a forceful defense of the Centerville Fire District, which he oversees as chief. “I’m gonna bring you up to speed on the fire district that will oversee this project if it comes to fruition,” he said. “We are the best fire district in this town, OK? We have 60 members that provide service to the largest district in the town, OK?” Ivino questioned the couple, who left the meeting without identifying themselves, about where they live and then said they need to study details of the district. One of the two people said they felt the questions were inappropriate. “My question to you is: If you don’t live in the Centerville Fire District, I think you should start doing your homework on the fire districts that you might live in and see what their response times are, see what their membership is, what they respond to versus what we respond to,” he said. “I’m speaking to everybody, not just you,” Ivino added. “You kind of gave me a snide attitude when we were discussing or (a consultant) was discussing some facts about fire districts.” Key Capture Energy is seeking to construct a 100-megawatt lithium-ion energy storage system on 11 acres of a 59.8-acre parcel owned by KMP Realty Holdings adjacent to the village. The project continues to be controversial, with Ivino forcefully responding to criticism at several meetings since the 629-page application was filed last December. The Oct. 21 meeting included a discussion over how well the district could cover a battery fire. After mentioning that the Key Capture plan calls for 2.5 million gallons of water to be available at the site, Ivino said, “We’re not up here (on the Town Board) to be treated like a punching bag.” Resident Josepha Gutelius drew Ivino’s ire when she responded with statistics from the state Division of Homeland Security that stated that up to five million gallons of water would be needed for a major fire event at a lithium-ion battery facility. “That’s if every box is on fire and it’s catastrophic,” Ivino responded. “I recommend that you set up an appointment with me or one of my other officers and we can give you a rundown of … our equipment,” he said. After the meeting, resident Gaetana Ciarlante said Ivino’s approach to comments he perceived as adversarial was not reassuring. “We are not reassured that the current fire chief, who is also on the Town Board is taking a mature, unemotional, sensible look at this project, leaving many of us residents wondering why he is behaving in such a way,” she said. © 2026 Daily Freeman, Kingston, N.Y.. artigo.texto: Douglas County seeking community feedback on battery energy storage systems at upcoming event photo by: Journal-World Douglas County Zoning and Codes will be hosting a community drop-in session about battery energy storage systems next week. The BESS session will be held from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 6 at the Douglas County Public Works building, 3755 E. 25th St., according to a press release from the county. Planner Karl Bauer will provide 15-minute presentations at 2 p.m., 4 p.m. and 5:30 p.m. covering what a BESS system is and the regulations process. A battery energy system, also referred to as a BESS, stores electrical energy in rechargeable batteries and releases it when needed. The systems range in size from small units commonly found in garages and basements to large installations resembling rows of shipping containers that can span many acres. These systems are becoming increasingly important as utilities integrate more renewable energy into the grid and as electricity demand grows from data centers and other large energy users. As the Journal-World reported, Douglas County commissioners initiated a text amendment to zoning and land use regulations in 2024 to add data centers, battery storage facilities and cryptocurrency mining operations as potential conditional uses in certain zoning districts and develop standards. County commissioners received an update on the process in May, as the Journal-World reported, and decided for staff to begin working on regulations for BESS first. They wanted to save more detailed conversations about data centers and digital asset retrieval until after the county’s zoning diagnostic review was completed. According to the release, Douglas County has not received any applications for a BESS installation. During the event next week, staff will be available to gather community input on a walk-in basis. The feedback will help inform staff’s ongoing work to develop regulations, and a draft is scheduled to be shared with Lawrence-Douglas County Planning commissioners during their meeting on Dec. 16. The proposed regulations would then require final approval from the Douglas County commissioners, which is anticipated in 2027, the release said. Individuals unable to attend the community drop-in session can contact Zoning and Codes staff by filling out a form on the county’s website at https://www.dgcoks.gov/zoning-and-codes/contact.
