artigo.texto: The Cap Times is an independent newsroom serving Madison and Wisconsin. Sign up for the Morning Update to receive news in your inbox each morning. With Madison’s one-year moratorium on data center construction set to expire in January, Madison residents pressed city staff this week on draft regulations aimed at restricting so-called “hyperscale” facilities. The proposed framework would divide allowed data centers into three categories: buildings under 10,000 square feet, or about twice the size of a fast food restaurant; buildings up to 50,000 square feet, or about the size of an average bowling alley; and buildings up to 100,000 square feet, or around the size of a grocery or department store. Data centers over 100,000 square feet would be banned. Potential locations for new data centers — facilities that house computer or network equipment used for storing, managing, processing and transmitting digital data — would be narrowed down as the size of a building increases. Smaller data centers, which are often tenants or sub-uses within larger facilities, would be permitted in a variety of nonresidential zones, including mixed-use, downtown, industrial, employment and “campus institutional” districts like the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Mid-sized data centers would be allowed in most employment and industrial zonings, along with campus-institutional districts. Larger data centers would be restricted to industrial areas. Other regulations would also increase with size, with fewer restrictions on smaller data centers. One potential limit would see smaller data centers banned on the ground floor in certain areas where planners prefer more public uses, for example. “If we're going to potentially allow data centers downtown — (where) there are already some in existence — we want to be preserving the ground floor for active uses like shops and bars and things that are creating that kind of vibrant downtown,” city planner Lisa Ernest said. Noise mitigation plans would be instituted only for mid-sized and larger facilities, with required inspection by a sound engineer. The proposal would set up 1,000-foot buffer zones between mid-sized and larger data centers to avoid creating “data center campuses” in certain areas of town. Larger data centers would need to be built at least 300 feet from residential buildings to reduce impacts like noise. Mid- and larger-sized data centers would be prohibited in areas planned for transit-intensive development. Regulation of data centers has drawn interest in and around Madison. Dane County and Sun Prairie also have moratoriums on new construction, and fierce public debate followed a proposed data center in DeForest. At Madison’s virtual meeting Oct. 27 about data center regulations, the number of residents registered for the meeting exceeded its allowed capacity. Residents asked around 70 questions, many of which fell into six broader themes. 1. Does Madison even need to allow data centers? City leaders said the draft regulations are meant to strike a balance between the needs of local businesses and public concern over the potential impacts of so-called “hyperscale” data centers, like Meta’s $1 billion project in Beaver Dam. “We're trying to move through this moratorium to come up with the rules that aim to restrict all types and sizes of data centers in the city, while meeting the data needs of local entities like hospitals and research centers,” Deputy Mayor Christie Baumel said. City staff noted at least six standalone data centers exist in Madison, ranging from 1,200 to 17,000 square feet. Those data centers have not caused issues for the city or produced public complaints, Planning Director Meagan Tuttle said. “We have had smaller data centers operating in the city without many people even knowing that they were there,” Tuttle said. “We anticipate that we could adopt rules that would allow for those types of facilities to continue to operate in the city successfully.” A complete ban on data centers could land the city in legal hot water, Tuttle added. “We do have to be mindful of our requirements and limitations of using zoning to discriminate against certain types of businesses under state law and under Wisconsin case law,” she said. “While we can allow or disallow different types of businesses in our community, we have to be careful not to single out a specific type of business when the way that it operates isn't significantly different from other types of businesses or uses in our community already.” For the same reason, the city cannot extend its 12-month moratorium to give others like state lawmakers time to develop regulations, Tuttle added. 2. Can the city limit data centers’ water or energy usage? Local governments are limited under state law in their ability to regulate water or energy usage. For instance, cities must allow users to connect to the municipal water system and cannot restrict the flow of water to facilities. The state Public Service Commission regulates energy providers in Wisconsin. But regulating the size of data centers could be an indirect vehicle for limiting potential strain on infrastructure, as well as other concerns like noise, city officials said. Data centers under 40,000 square feet generally require 500 kilowatts to 3 megawatts of electricity, or enough to power around 500 to 2,900 houses. The largest facilities can require nearly 2 gigawatts of electricity, or roughly equal to the power requirements of 100,000 homes. “Size alone, which is one of the main things that's within our purview to regulate, is a proxy,” Tuttle said at a Plan Commission meeting on data centers last month. 3. Why 100,000 square feet as a potential max? City planners said they drew from research on other places in Wisconsin and across the country for the proposed upper limit. artigo.texto: AIKEN — Rare is the day that data centers don’t pop up in headlines or conversations. There’s been a fistfight in Memphis, Tenn. Protests and arrests across the country. Even in nearby McCormick, sheriff’s office deputies had to step in between council members and angry citizens. Data centers are facilities for “housing computer systems and related equipment used for the storage and processing of large amounts of data,” as defined by Merriam-Webster. They prompt a lot of discussion, ironically, on the social media platforms that require their very existence. And they are a political football with candidates from both major parties lining up in support, or opposition, of them. Many data centers are located in Republican-leaning states such as South Carolina, but they are also in states such as Virginia and Oregon that vote blue. A growing number of community governments in the Palmetto State have imposed moratoriums or bans on data centers. That hasn’t happened in Aiken County, but there has been discussion about the matter in surrounding communities. “Data centers get a bad rap, and some of them deserve it,” said Will Williams, president and CEO of the Western SC Economic Development Partnership. “The technology has changed. But calling something a data center is like comparing Meta to a bitcoin miner. It’s kind of like calling a Mercedes-Benz a Yugo. Not a fair comparison.” Aiken County data centers There are three data centers that have been approved in Aiken County: Meta, DC BLOX and Oppidan. Together, they will bring an investment of nearly $1 billion. Meta is under construction at Sage Mill Industrial Park in the Graniteville area and is scheduled to be complete in 2027. The parent company of Facebook and Instagram, with headquarters in California, features a local investment of $800 million and around 100 employees. DC BLOX is located in the North Augusta area between U.S. 1 and Atomic Road. Its headquarters are in Georgia, and its initial investment in the area is around $22.5 million with one employee. Oppidan, based in Minnesota, is building its facility on 13 acres adjacent to Sage Mill Industrial Park. It features an investment of $32 million and will have six employees when operational. All three data centers received economic incentives from Aiken County Council. To date, there has been no discussion of a moratorium or ban from county council, Aiken City Council or North Augusta City Council. “I have not had any feedback from either the planning commission or fellow members of county council to move in that direction,” said Gary Bunker, chairman of Aiken County Council. He added that there are no more data centers “in the pipeline” for Aiken County. “The state of South Carolina may or may not put down statewide rules,” Bunker said. “Why would Aiken County want to put countywide rules if the state is considering something? “… My understanding is neither Dominion nor Santee Cooper through the co-ops has additional mega wattage to do something as large as the Meta center.” Earlier this year, there was a concern that a gas-fired power plant developer would build in Aiken County’s rural equestrian area to feed the energy need for data centers. “That prompted us to take a harder look on where we allow power generation in the various zones in Aiken County,” Bunker said. But in September, Aiken County Council unanimously approved an ordinance that would restrict power generation plants that use fossil fuels to areas with an Industrial Development zoning designation. Aiken City Council has not had any data center discussions either. “It really hasn’t been a city issue. We have not had anyone come to talk to council about a data center within our utility service area,” City Manager Stuart Bedenbaugh said. “Of course, obviously, where we would come into play would be providing water and sewer. There’s been no interest to date.” Ditto for North Augusta City Council. “I can confirm that the City Council has not formally debated a data center moratorium, nor have I been directed to draft a Council document for their consideration in regards to data centers,” City Administrator Jim Clifford wrote in an email. “I can also say that I'm not in dialog with any data center providers at this time.” Myth vs. reality As director of the economic development partnership that serves Aiken, Edgefield, McCormick and Saluda counties, it’s Williams’ job to attract new businesses and industries. That includes data centers. He’s used to setting the record straight on several misconceptions surrounding them. “I call it ‘STP.’ The same ten people,” Williams said. “They complain about growth, complain about they’re not that many jobs associated with data centers. They would also complain if a 3,000 job automotive facility showed up.” With more than three decades in economic development, Williams knows that a lot goes into a major investment from a company. “Companies look at multiple sites,” he said. “If the power requirement, water/sewer requirement, and they may have some other requirements, if all those boxes weren’t checked, they didn’t come.” Water demands, power usage and noise pollution are frequent talking points against data centers. According to Data Center Watch, which tracks opposition to data centers, the facilities are the new version of NIMBY: not in my backyard. “Where communities once rallied against factories, warehouses, or retail sprawl, they’re now opposing data centers,” the site said. “… Server farms have become a new target in the broader backlash against large-scale development. The landscape of local resistance is shifting — and data centers are squarely in the crosshairs.” Williams said it might be a moot point about any more data centers coming to this area. “Power is not there. Dominion will tell you in their entire system they have 100 megawatts,” he said. “Their whole system, being our area to Charleston, is 100 megawatts. “I also think industry is getting better. artigo.texto: Europe is accelerating the launch of new auctions linked to energy storage , with Portugal and Italy making progress in their respective competitive procedures during October. While the Portuguese government will auction 1,050 MVA of grid access capacity and the Italian operator Terna opens registrations for its 2028 capacity market, Spain is still awaiting the first calls for its own mechanism. These moves come against a backdrop of growing need for flexibility, reliability, and the integration of renewable energy into European electricity systems. However, the instruments differ: Portugal will allocate grid access rights for storage projects, while Italy will remunerate available capacity to ensure security of supply. In the Spanish case, the approval of Order TED/966/2026 , published on September 17 in the Official State Gazette (BOE), finally establishes the regulatory framework for its capacity market. However, this regulation still needs to be translated into the auctions that will define the contracting conditions for companies in the sector. Portugal to tender 1 GW for batteries: access conditions and operational restrictions On October 22nd, the Government of Portugal formalized the opening of two competitive procedures for a maximum of 1,050 MVA , aimed at facilitating the incorporation of storage systems through the allocation of reserve titles for injection capacity into the electricity grid. The tenders were approved through provisions 12924-B/2026 and 12924-C/2026 , published in the Diário da República, and will be managed by the General Directorate of Energy and Geology (DGEG). Of the total volume, 750 MVA correspond to independent storage facilities, known as standalone , while the remaining 300 MVA will be reserved for renewable generation centers with batteries located on the same site. Both procedures will be carried out through electronic auctions, with capacity distributed among the connection points established in the documentation of each call. The initiative opens up new possibilities for battery developers, although the allocation of injection capacity does not guarantee having an equivalent power to charge energy from the grid . In this regard, access limits for demand are a determining factor for project operation. Load capacity will depend on the conditions of each node, with particularly relevant restrictions in certain locations, such as Sines, according to sector information published by Optimize Energy. Furthermore, the shared technical terms regarding the upcoming tenders contemplate the possibility that the network operator may limit the operation of storage systems during certain periods of the year. Specifically, the industry documentation indicates up to 500 hours per year of combined charging and discharging restrictions for stand-alone batteries and up to 750 hours of grid charging restrictions for hybrid projects . These limits should be verified against the final specifications applicable to each installation. Therefore, the allocated capacity does not necessarily imply unrestricted availability for all 8,760 hours of the year. For developers, access conditions, location, and operational limitations must be incorporated into the technical design and economic model. This aspect is especially relevant for projects that depend on energy arbitrage, whose profitability is linked to the possibility of charging electricity during periods of reduced prices and unloading during the hours of highest market value . Italy opens its call for proposals for 2028 and reduces the recognized power output of batteries. For its part, Terna, the Italian operator, confirmed that the main auction of the capacity market for the 2028 delivery period will be held on December 21, 2026 , starting at 10:00 a.m. The operator opened the application period on October 20 , while interested companies will have until November 3, at 12:00 pm , to submit their applications. Subsequently, the schedule sets November 23 as the deadline for incorporating certain technical documentation and completing specific guarantees, while December 14 will be the deadline for submitting the deposits corresponding to the participation. The call is accompanied by modifications to the power accreditation coefficients for storage systems , known as derating factors, which determine what proportion of the installed power is recognized as firm capacity within the mechanism. The new technical provisions were approved on October 16 by the Ministry of Environment and Energy Security , following the regulatory review by the Energy, Networks and Environment Regulatory Authority (ARERA). The change particularly affects four-hour battery projects, whose recognized power decreases in all Italian electric zones, although with significant differences depending on the location. In the North and North Central regions , the coefficient falls from 51% to 40%, while in the South Central region it drops from 54% to 51%. The largest reductions are in the South and Calabria, where the percentage falls from 40% to 21% , and in Sicily and Sardinia, with a reduction from 31% to 21%. In practical terms, a 100 MW battery with four hours of storage will be able to provide 40 MW of capacity in the North, 51 MW in the Central South and only 21 MW in the South, Calabria, Sicily and Sardinia. This means that, for an installation located in the South and Calabria, the recognized power is reduced by 47.5% compared to the previous parameters , which directly modifies the volume of capacity that it will be able to offer in the auction. The revision responds to the increased forecasts for the integration of batteries into the Italian electricity system. A greater presence of storage capacity modifies the contribution of each additional installation to meeting peak demand periods. artigo.texto: CHEYENNE — The University of Wyoming released its 2026 Wyoming Election Year Survey on Thursday, gauging the opinions of Equality State residents on abortion, cost of living, data centers and election security, among other topics. The survey provides a picture of where Wyoming residents stand on those issues, broken down by gender, age, county, party affiliation and education to accurately reflect Wyoming’s population. It was conducted from Sept. 29-Oct. 25, and included 660 responses from randomly selected Wyoming adults. The margin of error is plus or minus 4.7 percentage points for all questions. Cost of living Wyoming residents identified cost of living and the economy as the biggest issue the state is facing in 2026. When asked to pick just one issue, the economy and cost of living — including inflation, jobs, wages and taxes — was the top concern of 40% of respondents. Republicans, Democrats and independents of every age group all agreed that cost of living was their top concern. Ryan Williamson, associate professor of political science in UW’s School of Politics, Public Affairs and International studies, explained why. “Whatever their politics, Wyomingites are telling us the same thing: Day-to-day costs are what concern them most,” he said. The other top issues were healthcare access and affordability, and government leadership or political dysfunction, with both at 14%. The other issues to receive more than 5% were public lands, natural resources and the environment at 6%, and immigration and workforce issues at 5%. Based on those responses, it is no surprise that their view of the state economy is not favorable, with 52% saying Wyoming’s economy has worsened over the past year, 37% stating it has stayed the same, and only 11% saying it has improved. The results are indistinguishable from 2024, however. The percentage saying the economy was worse was identical, and there was only a 1 percentage point difference between the two surveys in the “stayed the same” and “improved” categories. Residents are also less optimistic about the state’s economy improving in the next year, as only 26% expect the economy to improve, 38% expect it to stay the same and 36% expect it to get worse. Similar to the 2024 results, respondents’ views on the national economy remained more negative than the state’s economy, with 64% answering that the nation’s economy has declined over the past year, though that percentage is down from 71% in 2024. They are also more pessimistic about the nation’s economy for the future, with 52% stating their belief that the national economy will worsen over the next year, 22% expecting it to remain the same and 26% expecting it to improve. Public lands and data centers Wyoming residents staunchly oppose selling public lands, according to their responses, as 96% object to selling public lands to private buyers, leaving only 4% who are in support of selling public lands. Nine out of 10 Republicans, Democrats and independents, of all age groups, oppose the selloff of public lands. Williamson explained how unique this result is. “Opposition to selling public lands is about as close to unanimous as survey results get,” he said. Seventy percent of respondents also expressed their opposition to allowing more large data center projects into Wyoming to support artificial intelligence, with only 30% expressing support for those projects. The level of opposition varied depending on political party, though, with Democrats at 90%, Republicans at 61% and independents at 76%, and among age groups, with opposition peaking at 80% from residents aged 18-34, compared to 69% of those 55 and older and 65% for those age 35-54. Cheyenne LEADS CEO Betsy Hale argued that much of the conversation surrounding data centers in Wyoming has not provided the entire picture. “I just think there hasn’t been a healthy dialogue,” she said. “I think that there’s been more fear-mongering than there’ve been people with bonafide factual information at the podium.” She also said that including AI in the question was incorrect, due to many of the data centers around Cheyenne contributing to the United States’ strategic defense system or the cloud. Hale asked people to do their own research and determine for themselves their position on data centers. “I would just ask people to do their homework to look for facts, don’t look for the loudest person online,” she said. Election security Wyoming residents remained confident in both their county and their state’s ability to accurately count votes, with 86% and 84% confidence, respectively, compared to 89% and 88% in 2024. Confidence peaked for those who have already voted or say they will vote, at 92%, with the lowest reported confidence coming from residents aged 18-34, who have 77% confidence in statewide counts. Williamson touched on how this confidence is shared across the board. “That confidence has held steady across two election cycles and across party lines,” he said. Republicans and independents were much more supportive of requiring hand-count audits of a sample of ballots to verify machine counts at 92% and 78%, respectively, compared to Democrats at only 61%. That was also true concerning allowing poll watchers to observe all aspects of elections and remain at polling places after polls close with Republicans at 88% and independents at 75%, whereas Democrats were only at 43%. Support for voting by mail increased slightly from 38% in 2024 to 45% today. Another 42% expressed support for limiting mail-in voting to people whose special circumstances prevent them from voting in person, down from 45% in 2024. Only 12% of respondents believe all voting should be done in person, down from 16% in 2024. Less than 1% favor conducting Wyoming’s elections entirely by mail. artigo.texto: Por dentro dos data centers que movem a IA e os desafios do Brasil para recebÃª-los O Diario foi ao Data Center World Brasil 2026, onde grandes players do mercado se encontraram para discutir o presente e o futuro do ramo no paÃs. Já estamos vivendo na era das inteligências artificiais, as IAs. A participação dos chatbots já é uma realidade e, por isso, sua presença já não é mais uma perspectiva futura, mas um fato consolidado. Dessa forma, não só aprender a usá-las, mas entender o processo que faz com que elas cheguem até nós é cada vez mais determinante em como podemos encarar essa novidade. Além do debate extensivo e mais óbvio sobre o que a tecnologia pode nos oferecer, há uma discussão ainda mais palpável e que confronta diretamente o Brasil: a vinda dos Data Centers. Para debater sobre o assunto, o Diario foi ao Data Center World Brasil 2026, neste mês de outubro, onde grandes players do mercado se encontraram para discutir o presente e o futuro do ramo no país. Um data center é como uma grande fábrica, mas tudo o que ele produz é digital. Nesta grande fábrica, que pode ocupar milhares de metros quadrados, estão servidores formados por gavetas cheias de peças, ligadas por um grande circuito que cria e armazena dados, funcionando como a parte física da internet. Atualmente, existem dois tipos de data center: para nuvem ou para IA, que, do lado de fora, podem parecer os mesmos, mas suas peças e estruturas diferem em capacidade e complexidade de tarefas. De acordo com a IBM, multinacional norte-americana de tecnologia, os data centers típicos contêm uma infraestrutura que seria rapidamente sobrecarregada pelas cargas de trabalho da IA. Ao usar unidades de processamento central (CPUs), o foco maior é controlar o fluxo de dados e executar instruções que fazem o sistema funcionar. Porém, um data center voltado à IA requer o uso de unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs), que lidam com cargas de processamento muito mais intensas. Uma GPU é um circuito eletrônico que divide problemas complicados em partes menores que podem ser resolvidas simultaneamente devido aos milhares (ou até milhões) de processadores, o que torna essas peças mais rápidas e eficientes, como um cérebro extremamente potente. Os modelos de IA são treinados e executados em GPUs de data centers, alimentando muitas das principais aplicações de IA, indo de uma receita simples até a escrita de um livro, passando pela criação de códigos de programação ou de um vídeo meme do momento. Claro, nem só de peças de processamento vivem os data centers, mas também de componentes de armazenamento — como SSDs e HDDs — e de infraestrutura de rede, com roteadores, switches e cabeamento de fibra óptica e cobre, que interligam todas as máquinas. Com todos esses aparelhos funcionando ao mesmo tempo, começam a aparecer os desafios. Se o nosso celular ou laptop já esquenta funcionando algumas horas por dia, imagine um sistema complexo desses, que permanece ligado vinte e quatro horas por dia, sete dias por semana. É aí que entra o uso da água como principal meio de resfriamento dessas peças. A questão é que esses componentes são sensíveis a impurezas e variações químicas, exigindo água completamente limpa e potável para evitar danos. Além disso, a questão do uso de energia também assusta os investidores, que chegam a pôr bilhões de dólares em projetos como esses. Com o aumento exponencial da necessidade de IAs, o setor de data centers cresceu para atender à demanda. Atualmente, as regiões da Ásia-Pacífico e da América do Norte têm a maior proliferação de data centers, especialmente em cidades como Pequim e Xangai, na Ásia, e em regiões como o norte da Virgínia e a Baía de São Francisco, nos Estados Unidos. Porém, as grandes empresas que investem na tecnologia querem muito mais e exploram outros mercados, especialmente os que oferecem mão de obra barata, oferta de energia renovável, água abundante e geografia adequada, tudo o que o Brasil tem de sobra. Por isso, o país virou um dos principais alvos da corrida pelos data centers e tem seu território disputado por big techs, as grandes empresas que detêm a maior parcela da conexão do mundo, como Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, entre outras. Mas se, por um lado, a geografia natural e a disponibilidade de mão de obra favorecem a vinda dessas organizações, outros fatores podem contar para o estabelecimento desses empreendimentos, como explica Iuri Santos, gerente de tecnologia da Kingston, durante visita do Diario ao evento. “O Brasil é um país atrativo porque não tem terremoto ou furacão, conta com matriz energética e tem um mercado consumidor gigantesco. No entanto, a lógica econômica brasileira assusta investidores estrangeiros. Empresas de fora fazem o planejamento contando com determinado benefício fiscal e, quando vão implementar o projeto, a regra do jogo mudou ou o benefício caiu. Essa falta de segurança jurídica faz o investidor recuar”, avalia. Para além das questões nacionais, em que o governo federal busca alternativas para facilitar a vinda dos data centers, como o Redata — incentivo tributário para a vinda de infraestruturas de tecnologia —, a perspectiva global também gera debates e questionamentos. Segundo a Gartner, empresa de pesquisa e consultoria de tecnologia, os gastos globais com IA já chegaram à casa dos trilhões de dólares em 2026, com mais da metade desse valor sendo destinado à infraestrutura. Porém, em qualquer lugar do mundo, para aumentar a capacidade de IA são necessários os data centers que, por sua vez, fazem necessárias as peças, que não existem sem os semicondutores, materiais “ideais para tecnologias como chips de computador, chips de inteligência artificial (IA) e dispositivos da Internet das coisas (IoT) que dependem da condução de uma grande quantidade de energia através de uma pequena área”, como explica a IBM. É essa cadeia frágil e cara a base de toda a infraestrutura de IA que chega ao usuário final. A questão dos semicondutores ainda é um ponto sensível n

artigo.texto: Election Preview November's midterm election will have wide-ranging impacts on communities across Ohio. Not only are state-wide seats like governor to be decided on, but municipalities across the state will be voting on issues that deal with school funding, property taxes and even data centers. Several Ideastream reporters join the "Sound of Ideas" with Stephanie Haney on Thursday to discuss some of the issues they're following ahead of the midterms. That includes everything from using income taxes to fund school systems, to paying for county boards of developmental disabilities. Guests: - Sean McDonnell, Cleveland Government Reporter, Ideastream Public Media - Conor Morris, Education Reporter, Ideastream Public Media - Amanda Pirani, Regional Reporter, Ideastream Public Media High school students create election podcasts For the past few weeks, as part of our Listen, Engage, Vote election initiative, Ideastream has reported on how consequential this midterm election is, especially for Ohioans — from deciding who will lead the state as the next governor, to statewide and federal races that could determine the balance of power in Congress, to the makeup of our state Supreme Court, to how our local schools and social services are funded. But what do young people think of the midterms? Is it on their radar? As of the voter registration deadline a few weeks ago, only 35% of 18-year-olds were registered to vote in Ohio, which is 10% below the national average. What will it take to get more young people to the polls? And for those who can't vote yet, how engaged are they in what's happening this election cycle? Our team got a chance to sit down with a group of passionate high school students from Hawken Schools in Gates Mills, in Cuyahoga County, who were tasked with covering the election in the elective course called "Campaign Headquarters." Groups of students created podcasts that focused on competitive races in Ohio and elsewhere. Guests: - Birk Farinacci, Senior, Hawken School - Maya Wadhawan, Senior, Hawken School - Grayson Rezaee, Senior, Hawken School "The Menu: All City Candy" Halloween is Saturday, and with the cost of just about everything going up, some folks are getting creative with their costumes — maybe DIY-ing a look at home, or repurposing clothes already in their closets. Other families are rethinking how much candy they can afford to hand out, if at all. Candy prices are up more than 15% for consumers this year, according to an analysis from progressive think tanks the Groundwork Collaborative and the Century Foundation. But Halloween is still a big moment for the candy business, including right here in Northeast Ohio. Thursday on “The Menu,” our biweekly segment in collaboration with Cleveland Magazine, we’re checking in with All City Candy, a small business serving up sweet treats on Halloween and all year round. Guests: - Yuta Hsu, e-Commerce & Customer Service representative, All City Candy

artigo.texto: Para evitar processos de moradores contra seus data centers, trilionário Elon Musk adota solução original: comprar todas as casas da região As vantagens de ser um trilionário: moradores dizem que a xAI, de Elon Musk, se ofereceu para comprar suas casas em troca da desistência de processos judiciais motivados pelo ruído de um data center Atualizado Moradores de um bairro do Mississipi relatam que a xAI, de Musk, se ofereceu para comprar suas casas em troca da desistência de processos judiciais motivados pelo ruído de um data center. Diversas residências próximas a data centers no Mississippi foram compradas; um morador relatou que um corretor de imóveis mencionou uma meta de adquirir mais de 400 casas, segudo o The Guardian. Corretores de imóveis têm batido de porta em porta em Southaven, no Mississippi, em nome da xAI, oferecendo a compra de residências sob a condição de que os proprietários concordem em não participar de um processo judicial contra a empresa por conta do ruído gerado pela instalação. (A empresa de IA de Musk passou a se chamar, oficialmente, SpaceXAI em julho, e mais recentemente foi renomeada como SpaceXSI; contudo, para os vizinhos do data center no Mississippi, ela continua sendo a xAI.) Esse plano pode acabar absorvendo praticamente todo o bairro de Colonial Hills, na zona oeste de Southaven. Segundo uma gravação de conversa a que o The Guardian teve acesso, um corretor informou a um morador que existe uma meta de adquirir 418 casas — 18 proprietários já concordaram com a venda. A xAI não respondeu a perguntas sobre esses números ou sobre seus planos para o bairro. Anteriormente, a empresa afirmou que pretende ser uma "boa vizinha" e negou todas as alegações apresentadas no processo judicial referente ao ruído. Segundo o corretor e o prefeito local, os imóveis servirão para acomodar funcionários da xAI, à medida que a empresa segue sua expansão acelerada na região — nos últimos dois anos, três de seus data centers foram construídos em Southaven e na vizinha Memphis, no Tennessee. Esse ritmo frenético, somado ao ruído constante — dia e noite — proveniente de turbinas a gás instaladas sem as devidas licenças para alimentar os data centers, tem causado grande descontentamento entre moradores locais. “Parece um motor de avião, mas é um ruído contínuo; é incrivelmente alto”, disse Elizabeth Rose, professora de piano, referindo-se à instalação da xAI que fica a cerca de três quilômetros (duas milhas) de sua casa. “Já fui acordada às 2h da manhã por causa disso. Às vezes, preciso simplesmente sair de perto, porque o barulho me deixa muito irritada.” Rose conta que ficou chocada quando a central de energia — uma antiga unidade da Duke Energy que agora abriga 69 turbinas a gás temporárias para abastecer os novos data centers — começou a emitir um ronco constante em agosto do ano passado. “De repente, surgiu uma usina ali”, disse ela. “E agora tenho a impressão de que estão tentando expandir as ofertas de compra para todo o bairro. Basicamente, vai virar o parquinho particular de Elon Musk. ‘Elonville’”, afirmou As ofertas para esses imóveis, baseadas no valor de mercado — em uma região onde o preço médio de uma casa é de cerca de US$ 180 mil —, representam um gasto relativamente pequeno para a criação do maior conjunto de supercomputadores de IA do mundo, como planeja Musk. Ainda mais se levarmos em conta que o empresário é a pessoa mais rica do planeta e um importante doador do Partido Republicano. Desde julho de 2024, a xAI construiu três enormes data centers — chamados Colossus I, Colossus II e Macrohardrr — na intersecção entre Memphis e Southaven, que se estende pela fronteira entre o Tennessee e o Mississippi. Atualmente, Musk passa até quatro noites por semana em um trailer na região de Memphis, supervisionando pessoalmente a construção dos data centers para continuar o desenvolvimento do chatbot Grok. “Estamos presenciando o crescimento mais rápido que já vi na vida com o bot Grok”, afirmou Musk durante uma teleconferência sobre os resultados financeiros da SpaceX, este mês. “Nunca vi nada crescer tão rápido.” Musk gastou cerca de meio bilhão de dólares ajudando a eleger republicanos nos dois últimos ciclos eleitorais, e seu entusiasmo por centros de dados é compartilhado por Donald Trump, que afirmou que qualquer um que se oponha a tal desenvolvimento acabará “atrasado e pobre”. Contudo, como tem sido cada vez mais comum, os moradores disseram ter sido atropelados por essa “corrida do ouro”. Três residentes locais, angustiados com o barulho da expansão, entraram com uma ação judicial em junho, queixando-se de “ruído quase constante, vibrações e outros transtornos” causados pela instalação da xAI nas proximidades. Jason Haley, um dos três autores da ação, afirmou que nunca se considerou um ativista nem alguém politizado, mas que o ruído das turbinas a gás — localizadas a cerca de 800 metros de sua casa, imóvel que ele possui há 20 anos — tornou-se insuportável. “Há um zumbido agudo e, depois, um som que lembra um avião passando sobre a sua casa”, disse ele. “É algo tão torturante que não consigo dormir; acabo saindo de casa ou ligando um som até cair no sono, completamente exausto. Isso te deixa louco. Você também perde a esperança, porque é ignorado ou menosprezado. Não há saída.” Exasperado com as conversas infrutíferas com o prefeito de Southaven e enfurecido com Tate Reeves — o governador republicano do Mississippi, defensor da inteligência artificial, que declarou que impor restrições aos centros de dados seria “entregar o futuro da tecnologia à China” — Haley abriu um processo judicial e começou a publicar vídeos nas redes sociais nos quais ele monitora os níveis de ruído. “Pensei em fazer um pouco de barulho por conta própria por causa dessa palhaçada”, disse Haley. “Eu não sabia nada sobre o Elon; ainda não conheço o homem. artigo.texto: [Digital Today intern reporter Seung-a Yoo] The U.S. Department of Energy has launched BattMan, a programme to support the development and commercialisation of next-generation battery manufacturing technologies. The focus is to cut battery production costs and connect new technologies developed in laboratories to actual factory production. On Oct. 29, EV outlet CleanTechnica reported that the department announced the BattMan battery manufacturing accelerator on Oct. 28. The department set out a goal of completing a U.S. battery supply chain by 2030 and securing leadership in battery technology and manufacturing by 2035. BattMan focuses on reducing battery manufacturing costs and speeding up the commercialisation of next-generation batteries. The department forecast that U.S. demand for batteries for transportation and energy storage will rise to 707 GWh in 2035 from 179 GWh in 2025. That would be close to a fourfold increase in about 10 years. Pacific Northwest National Laboratory will lead the project, with Argonne National Laboratory, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the University of Washington, Binghamton University, the University of Alabama, Arizona State University and the University of Michigan-Dearborn taking part. Rocky Mountain National Laboratory will also support battery materials analysis and electrode design technologies. Rocky Mountain National Laboratory plans to use artificial intelligence to analyse how small defects inside batteries or differences in materials affect long-term performance. It will help more accurately predict quality and performance from the early stages of battery development and support manufacturers so they can use the information without equipping separate expensive devices. It will also test manufacturing processes that can be applied to actual production with U.S. battery and materials companies. It also plans to develop a system in which manufacturing equipment identifies problems on its own and improves production methods, using real-time data collected during production and a virtual factory model. In the United States, investment is continuing not only in batteries but also in EV production facilities. A conditional loan guarantee initially pursued for a Rivian plant in Georgia was for $6.57 billion, and was later adjusted to $4.5 billion and proceeded to a groundbreaking ceremony. Georgia estimated that it has attracted more than $31 billion in investment and created more than 38,000 jobs in EV and battery manufacturing since 2015. Audi also announced a plan to invest about $4 billion to build its first U.S. production plant in Georgia. Final approval from parent Volkswagen's supervisory board is still pending. The United States is putting weight behind strengthening battery research and development and its production base even as growth in the EV market has slowed. BattMan is drawing attention as a key project to raise the competitiveness of the U.S. battery industry by having research institutions and companies verify manufacturing processes and link them to actual production.

artigo.texto: Receita da Caterpillar desacelera no 3º trimestre apesar de salto em negócios ligados a data centers Fabricante de equipamentos industriais informou que sua receita avançou 17% no período, para US$ 20,6 bilhões A Caterpillar segue crescendo, mas num ritmo insuficiente para satisfazer Wall Street. A fabricante de equipamentos industriais informou que sua receita avançou 17% no terceiro trimestre, para US$ 20,6 bilhões, ficando abaixo das estimativas de analistas e sinalizando uma desaceleração sequencial frente à alta de 24% registrada três meses antes. Grande parte da expansão da Caterpillar nos últimos anos decorre de sua divisão de energia e motores, que fabrica grupos geradores de grande porte e turbinas voltadas a atender data centers, altamente intensivos no consumo de eletricidade. As vendas dessa unidade cresceram 18% no trimestre recente, atingindo US$ 8,78 bilhões. O “boom” da inteligência artificial segue impulsionando a demanda pelos produtos do segmento, afirmou o diretor-presidente da companhia, Joe Creed. A Caterpillar já está aceitando pedidos de grandes motores alternativos com entregas previstas para 2029 e encomendas de turbinas para 2030. A empresa também vem investindo na unidade com o objetivo de ampliar a produção e expandir a capacidade instalada para suprir a demanda. “A equipe está gerenciando com eficácia os desafios operacionais decorrentes desse crescimento acelerado”, afirmou Creed, em teleconferência com analistas. “A entrada em operação de capacidade adicional continua sendo o principal fator delimitador para o ritmo de expansão em energia e motores.” Nesta quinta-feira (29), por volta das 15h30, as ações da companhia caíam 9,38%, cotadas em US$ 646,46, na Bolsa de Nova York (Nyse). No acumulado do ano, os papéis sobem cerca de 10%. Além da área de energia e motores, a Caterpillar destacou que o ritmo saudável na atividade de construção, tanto no segmento residencial quanto no não residencial, deu suporte à sua divisão de indústrias de construção, amplamente reconhecida por seus tratores e caminhões fora de estrada amarelos. A divisão registrou faturamento de US$ 7,98 bilhões, alta de 18% na base anual. Em paralelo, a divisão de indústrias de recursos naturais contabilizou vendas de US$ 4,62 bilhões, avanço de 15% na comparação com o terceiro trimestre do ano passado. “O forte ritmo de captação de pedidos em nossos três principais segmentos elevou a carteira de pedidos ao patamar recorde de US$ 78 bilhões”, afirmou Creed, destacando que o “backlog” em 30 de setembro praticamente dobrou em relação ao nível de um ano antes. Em suas projeções para o ano, a Caterpillar reiterou a previsão de crescimento de vendas totais e receitas na faixa intermediária a superior de dois dígitos. A companhia também manteve a estimativa de custos com tarifas alfandegárias em torno de US$ 2,2 bilhões. O balanço revelou ainda um lucro líquido consolidado de US$ 3,29 bilhões no período, ou US$ 7,13 por ação, superando os US$ 2,3 bilhões de um ano antes. Desconsiderando itens não recorrentes, o lucro por ação ajustado de US$ 7,20 superou os US$ 7,06 projetados pelo consenso de analistas consultados pela FactSet.

artigo.texto: {KXLG, Watertown, SD} Area residents will have an opportunity this week to learn more about a major commercial energy storage project proposed for the region. The Local Review Committee (LRC), established by the South Dakota Public Utilities Commission, will host a public informational meeting regarding Crowned Ridge Energy Storage I, LLC’s proposed Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project. The meeting is scheduled for Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. at the First District Association of Local Governments Office, located at 418 18th Avenue NE in Watertown. The session is free and open to all members of the public. During the meeting, committee members will receive a preliminary report on a required Social and Economic Effect/Impact Study. This evaluation assesses how the addition of large-scale energy storage infrastructure could impact local public services, tax revenues, employment, and community resources throughout the area. Members of the public are encouraged to attend to review the preliminary findings and learn more about the proposed development. The committee appointed by the South Dakota Public Utilities Commission to review the project includes Codington County Commission Chair Troy VanDusen, Grant County Commission Chair William Tostenson, City of South Shore Mayor Jamie Dolen, Waverly 14-5 School District Board President Penny Thyen, and Milbank 25-4 School District Board President Richard Schwandt.

artigo.texto: $25.5 Million Deal Sparks Rally as Energy Storage Firm Expands Global Reach Developing battery technology is one challenge. Getting products into customers’ hands is another. For energy storage companies seeking international growth, distribution partnerships can provide access to new markets without the expense of building additional manufacturing capacity. Shares of Elong Power Holding Limited (NASDAQ: ELPW) are climbing Wednesday after the company announced that its Hong Kong subsidiary entered into a one-year omnichannel cooperation agreement valued at $25.5 million. The company has already completed delivery of an initial shipment worth about $840,000. The agreement, signed by Elong Power (Hong Kong) Holding Limited, took effect on signing and includes an automatic renewal provision that activates in the absence of objection. It covers distribution of smart consumer electronic products, and the subsidiary plans to build a business-to-business network serving enterprise customers across a range of commercial applications. Elong Power did not identify the counterparty or disclose a delivery schedule for the remaining contract value. The deal follows an asset-light strategic transformation completed in the first half of 2026. Elong Power, incorporated in the Cayman Islands and headquartered in Beijing, specializes in lithium battery energy storage systems for portable, residential, commercial, industrial and utility-scale applications. The company plans to use Hong Kong’s trade infrastructure and financial system to strengthen its cross-border supply chain and develop new commercial channels for its smart hardware business. It also intends to use the expanded distribution network to support international sales of its energy storage products. “With the asset-light strategic transformation completed in the first half of 2026 and our robust cash reserves, we possess strong risk resilience and a solid foundation for business expansion,” management said. Management added that the agreement establishes the company’s overseas distribution gateway for enterprise customers. Going forward, Elong Power plans to integrate resources along its industrial chain and accelerate adoption of its energy storage solutions in the Asia-Pacific region, developing the trading business alongside its core lithium battery operations. artigo.texto: Newswise — The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory is joining DOE’s Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) in a new national consortium aimed at accelerating the transition of energy storage innovations from discovery to domestic manufacturing. Called the Battery Manufacturing (BattMan) Accelerator, the consortium will tackle key challenges in scaling emerging battery technologies, with a focus on lowering manufacturing costs, shortening development timelines and strengthening U.S. leadership in advanced energy storage. “Breakthroughs in battery science must be matched by our ability to manufacture them at scale. BattMan brings together the tools, data and partnerships needed to design manufacturable solutions from the start and accelerate their transition into industry,” said Jie Xiao, Battelle Fellow at PNNL with a joint appointment as Boeing Martin professor of mechanical engineering at the University of Washington in Seattle. The four laboratories contribute complementary strengths to bridge gaps between lab discovery and commercial production. PNNL will apply manufacturing science to show that new materials and processes can scale. Argonne will expand this work by validating feasibility and increasing production using its pilot lines. Both labs will provide materials — such as powders and electrodes — to ORNL for smart coating process development. NLR will lead the integration of advanced characterization, physics-guided quality control and digital materials design for rapid feedback to project partners. “Argonne brings materials synthesis and process scale-up capabilities that can shorten the time required for new technologies to reach commercialization,” said Jianlin Li, director of the Energy Storage and Conversion department at Argonne, who serves as the lab’s lead on the project. “Demonstrating technical and economic feasibility at larger production volumes is essential for validating new technologies efficiently.” BattMan will also strengthen critical mineral supply chains by advancing battery materials made from more abundant domestic elements. In addition to Argonne, PNNL, ORNL and NLR, the BattMan Accelerator includes the University of Washington, Binghamton University, University of Alabama, Arizona State University and University of Michigan-Dearborn as founding partners. The accelerator is actively establishing collaborations with companies across the battery and materials manufacturing sector. The laboratories will work closely with these university partners and industry to test and validate manufacturing processes at increasing scales and toward commercially viable production. “To advance the next generation of battery technologies, we must reduce the risks associated with scaling innovations from laboratory discovery to commercial production,” said Claus Daniel, associate laboratory director for Argonne’s Advanced Energy Technologies directorate. “Processes that work at small scale can behave very differently at larger volumes. Addressing those uncertainties earlier with better science, reliable data and rigorous validation gives companies greater confidence to invest.” SI-driven manufacturing Super intelligence (SI) is expected to play a central role in the initiative. “SI-driven methods that use processing and manufacturing data have the potential to speed up discovery of new materials, improve efficiency of laboratory processes and support predictive, cost-effective design,” Xiao said. “Beyond enabling high throughput, SI has the potential to optimize workflows to reduce cost and accelerate technology maturation,” Li said. “The Argonne team will begin by applying SI to individual processes and later integrate SI models across full production line.” As part of BattMan, Argonne will generate synthesis and scale-up data, train machine learning models and identify optimal processing conditions through active learning. Scientific goals In the near term, BattMan will deploy high-throughput experimentation, automated synthesis and characterization, and digital manufacturing tools to improve data quality, reproducibility and process consistency across partner institutions. Longer term, the consortium aims to develop self-optimizing manufacturing systems using real-time data, digital twins and tight closed-loop control. BattMan will build on the autonomous laboratory concepts by advancing autonomous pilot lines designed to reduce scale-up time and costs, accelerate commercialization and reinforce domestic supply chains. BattMan is currently forming industry partnerships in battery and battery-materials manufacturing. For institutions and companies interested in participating, visit pnnl.gov/projects/battman. Supported by DOE’s Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Technologies Office within the Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation Office, the BattMan Accelerator integrates SI, materials science and advanced manufacturing into a coordinated, data-driven innovation ecosystem. Argonne National Laboratory seeks solutions to pressing national problems in science and technology by conducting leading-edge basic and applied research in virtually every scientific discipline. Argonne is managed by UChicago Argonne, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Science. The U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Science is the single largest supporter of basic research in the physical sciences in the United States and is working to address some of the most pressing challenges of our time. For more information, visit https://energy.gov/science.

artigo.texto: Chinesa Envision Energy estuda fábrica no Brasil para baterias e turbinas eólicas A chinesa Envision Energy estuda abrir uma fábrica no Brasil para produzir baterias e turbinas eólicas, condicionando o aporte a incentivos fiscais do governo. Em expansão no país após fechar contrato com a Casa dos Ventos em meio à crise da indústria eólica local, a empresa busca atender ao futuro leilão de armazenamento de energia (BESS), que exigirá conteúdo nacional. O movimento reflete a ofensiva de fabricantes chinesas no mercado verde brasileiro, setor que atrai rivais como BYD e CATL. A chinesa Envision Energy está avaliando a possibilidade de instalar uma fábrica no Brasil para produzir baterias e turbinas eólicas, dois negócios de seu portfólio de soluções para o setor de energia que estão no foco dos planos de crescimento para o país, disse um executivo da companhia à Reuters. A decisão de um eventual investimento para fabricação local dependeria de uma demonstração de "interesse" do governo brasileiro, segundo Marcello Trombelli, diretor de soluções e de relações institucionais e governamentais da Envision no Brasil. "Nós estamos em constante contato com os governos, estaduais e federal, no intuito de demonstrar as soluções que nossas tecnologias podem trazer para o sistema elétrico brasileiro. Já seria possível termos nossas fábricas aqui, mas também é preciso que demonstrem interesse", afirmou ele à Reuters, à margem do evento Brazil Windpower, na terça-feira. Questionado sobre o que seria esse "interesse", o executivo mencionou medidas como incentivos fiscais e ex-tarifários, que ajudariam a empresa a trazer gradualmente sua produção de tecnologias consideradas inéditas para o mercado brasileiro. Uma das maiores fornecedoras mundiais de soluções de tecnologia "verde", a Envision ainda é relativamente nova no Brasil. No ano passado, anunciou suas primeiras intenções para o país, incluindo uma planta de combustível sustentável de aviação (SAF), após uma visita do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e outros integrantes do governo à China. Em janeiro deste ano, a Envision divulgou seu primeiro grande negócio local, um acordo com a geradora renovável Casa dos Ventos para o fornecimento de 630 megawatts (MW) de turbinas eólicas e outros serviços. O contrato com a Casa dos Ventos, que será atendido com máquinas importadas, ganhou projeção por ser um dos únicos anunciados em meio a uma crise prolongada da indústria eólica doméstica, enquanto o segmento ainda luta por uma retomada a partir de 2027. Multinacionais como GE e Siemens paralisaram suas atividades no país nos últimos anos, devido à falta de encomendas para novos parques. Ao mesmo tempo, outras fabricantes desembarcaram no Brasil, vindas especialmente da China, como Goldwind, Sinoma e Windey. Além de aerogeradores, a Envision Energy também está interessada no segmento de baterias e já tem ofertado seus produtos a empresas que pretendem participar do primeiro leilão do Brasil para contratar essa tecnologia para o sistema elétrico. "Estamos seguindo a cartilha definida para o BESS (sistema de bateria), ou seja, é esperado que para participar do leilão de BESS tenha-se conteúdo nacional, estamos nessa estratégia, trabalhando para isso, com parcerias locais", explicou Trombelli. Algumas fabricantes chinesas de sistemas de armazenamento de energia, como Jinko ESS e CATL, já fecharam parcerias com empresas brasileiras do segmento para nacionalizar projetos e garantir uma participação maior no leilão inédito para a tecnologia, marcado para dezembro. Já a BYD anunciou um investimento de até R$500 milhões para produção de BESS no Brasil.

artigo.texto: 'Lord Farquuad' addresses 'massive' 400-megawatt data center at city hall meeting SAN DIEGO, Calif. (WKRC) - Two unusual appearances were made during a city council meeting Tuesday. According to KSWB, City Council members and people from around the San Diego area gathered to give input on a moratorium regarding the development and expansion of artificial intelligence data centers across the city. The meeting was also attended by two individuals in character as “Lord Farquaad” from the hit animated comedy “Shrek” and “Sesame Street’s” Elmo. When addressing the gathering, "Lord Farquaad" issued the following statement: "I would like to begin my comments today by advising the rest of this room to please put off their foul stench, it smells like too many poors, and too many working class in this room. And that is not the interest that we are interested in serving in my town of Duloc, and we should not be interested in serving those interests here in San Diego either. We should be interested in representing the business community, that represents the AI data centers, that represents the ability to monitor our constituents with our Flock cameras and we know these two things go hand in hand, of course." "What will the AI data centers be used for, but to store the technology, to store the information of all our civilians in a massive, in a massive center, where all of us can be further studied, including the ogre and including any of the other undesirable fairy tale trash that is poisoning my perfect world." The report states that the moratorium was an effort by the city of San Diego to pause a potential federal plan that would see the Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR) site converted into a 400-megawatt AI data center. According to KSWB, the moratorium was passed unanimously and will pause the project for 45 days. After that, San Diego city leaders can vote to extend the moratorium for an additional 10 months and 15 days, per the report, which notes that the developer originally proposed converting the site into a development with an emphasis on Navy military housing.

artigo.texto: Exclusivo: Governo publicará portaria que define cobertura setorial do mercado regulado de carbono As regras começam a valer a partir de 2027 para empresas com emissões anuais acima de 10 mil toneladas O Ministério da Fazenda publicará nesta quinta-feira (28) portaria que define a cobertura setorial do mercado regulado de carbono brasileiro. A norma estabelece os segmentos enquadrados nas obrigações de Monitoramento, Relato e Verificação (MRV) de emissões de gases de efeito estufa e o cronograma para implementação gradual. As regras começam a valer a partir de 2027 para empresas com emissões anuais acima de 10 mil toneladas. A Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono estima que menos de 600 grandes empresas terão de iniciar os processos de relato de emissões, ou seja, informar de forma precisa a quantidade de CO2 emitida. O objetivo do governo é construir uma base oficial de dados antes do início do mercado regulado de carbono. O texto final traz mudanças em relação à proposta submetida à consulta pública em 28 de julho, após diferentes setores pedirem alterações na distribuição das atividades entre as três etapas de implementação. Em entrevista ao Valor, a secretária extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono, Cristina Reis, avaliou o resultado da consulta pública como positivo. Sem a inclusão de novos segmentos, o plano mantém o total de 17 setores, mas redistribui algumas atividades entre as etapas do cronograma. Para Reis, a manutenção do escopo confirma o acerto da proposta original do governo federal. Sobre a antecipação de alguns segmentos para a primeira fase, a secretária afirmou que o movimento demonstra que “os setores já se consideram maduros, preparados e entendem o valor da regulamentação”. A publicação da portaria não exige a apresentação imediata de relatórios nem estabelece limites de emissão ou custos para as empresas. O teto de emissões e a distribuição gratuita de cotas brasileiras de emissão (CBEs) estão previstos para 2030, com o início do Plano Nacional de Alocação (PNA). Até lá, a Fazenda recomenda que as empresas acompanhem a regulamentação e se familiarizem com o mercado de carbono. A qualificação dos setores dependerá da definição das metodologias específicas, ainda em elaboração. Para o secretário-adjunto da Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono, José Pedro Bastos Neves, a regulamentação também pode abrir oportunidades para soluções nacionais de descarbonização. “Em geral, essa pauta da descarbonização, diferentemente de outros países do mundo, em que é vista muito como um aumento de custos, no Brasil traz em si uma oportunidade de certa forma valorizar soluções tecnológicas, rotas de descarbonização que já são desenvolvidas no Brasil”, disse Neves. A primeira etapa de MRV começa em 2027 e abrange as indústrias de alumínio, ferro e aço em usinas integradas, cimento, exploração e produção de petróleo e gás natural, papel e celulose, vidro, além de alguns segmentos da indústria química e da mineração de minério de ferro e de bauxita. Em relação ao desenho preliminar, foram antecipados para a primeira etapa o vidro, a mineração de minério de ferro e bauxita e alguns segmentos da indústria química. Já o refino de petróleo e o transporte aéreo deixaram de integrar essa fase. A segunda etapa, prevista para começar até 2029, abrangerá cerâmica, ferro e aço em usinas semi-integradas, atividades da indústria química não incluídas na primeira etapa, indústria de alimentos e bebidas, mineração das demais substâncias minerais, refino de petróleo e setor elétrico. Deixam a segunda fase os segmentos de alumínio reciclado, vidro, resíduos sólidos e tratamento de esgoto. A terceira etapa permanece prevista para 2031 e inclui os transportes rodoviário, ferroviário e aquaviário, sem alterações em relação à proposta original. Cada etapa prevê um período de preparação e adaptação de quatro anos antes da consolidação dos dados. No primeiro ano, as empresas devem elaborar o plano de monitoramento e submetê-lo à aprovação do órgão gestor do Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE). No segundo e no terceiro anos, começa o monitoramento efetivo, com a medição e a coleta de dados sobre emissões e remoções de gases de efeito estufa. No quarto ano, ocorre a consolidação dos dados e o envio do relato de emissões no âmbito do PNA. A retirada dos setores de resíduos sólidos e tratamento de esgoto do cronograma geral decorre, segundo Reis, do entendimento de que a própria legislação afasta obrigações diretas para atividades que comprovadamente apresentam atributos de produção sustentáveis. A equipe técnica decidiu tratar o setor separadamente. “Isso significa que, para incentivar a descarbonização, e aqui a gente está falando principalmente da emissão de metano no setor de resíduos, o melhor é que eles atuem pelo lado do voluntário, gerando crédito de carbono, e caso tenham alta integridade e metodologia credenciada, esses créditos de carbono podem se tornar CRVE, que é o Certificado de Remoção Verificada de Emissões”, explicou a secretária. Segundo Reis, o mecanismo também pode contribuir para ampliar o tratamento de resíduos em instalações sanitárias e estimular o encerramento de lixões no país. A Fazenda também atendeu a um pedido do setor aéreo para alinhar o cronograma de monitoramento, relato e verificação à implementação do ProBioQAV, programa voltado ao mercado de combustível sustentável de aviação (SAF). “Simplificando: ao invés de fixar o transporte aéreo na etapa 1, definimos que a exigência ocorrerá no momento em que o ProBioQAV for regulamentado”, resumiu ela. O MRV e a fiscalização do cumprimento das metas regulatórias de redução de emissões de voos domésticos estão sob responsabilidade da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac), que terminou consulta pública sobre o assunto no início de outubro.

artigo.texto: Global Renewables M&A Hits $80 Billion in First Nine Months of 2026 as Battery Storage Deals Surge, Enerdatics Reports The data from the period points to a more selective market, with private equity leading large acquisitions and buyers paying a premium for contracted revenue. The Renewables M&A Outlook & Analysis Q3 2026 Report finds that transaction activity increased approximately 7%, trailing growth in reported value. Buyers increasingly favored storage platforms, projects with secured grid access and assets backed by predictable revenues. "The headline growth masks a more selective market," said Kshitij N R (Kay), Partner at Enerdatics. "Buyers are looking closely at what makes a portfolio deliverable: grid access, development capability and a credible route to contracted revenues. Those factors are shaping both acquisition appetite and the value sellers can realize." North America: Private equity and storage drive $61 billion in deal value North America recorded approximately $61 billion in reported deal value, with private equity driving around half of acquisitions. Battery energy storage system (BESS) deal activity increased 75%, while solar-plus-storage activity rose 65%. Standalone solar activity remained broadly steady. Storage featured in 95% of corporate and platform power deals tracked in the region, up from 71% a year earlier. "Storage has become central to North American platform acquisitions," said Mohammad Thousif, Lead Analyst at Enerdatics. "Buyers are acquiring development teams, grid positions and pipelines that can respond to growing power demand. The opportunity is substantial, but converting those pipelines into contracted, operating assets remains the critical test." Europe: Contracted wind commands a premium as buyers link payments to project milestones European BESS activity nearly doubled year on year to 109 deals, with the UK and Germany leading by transacted capacity. Solar activity declined approximately 20%, while wind activity remained broadly steady. Enerdatics' analysis of transactions since January 2025 estimates that contracted operating onshore wind assets commanded a valuation premium of approximately 45% over merchant-exposed assets. Buyers also increasingly used contingent payments to manage development risk. These arrangements featured in 16 of 24 European development-stage deals with disclosed terms in the first nine months of 2026, equivalent to 67%, compared with 35% a year earlier. "Revenue certainty affects both the price an asset attracts and the terms on which a buyer will transact," said Priyanka Khot, Senior Analyst at Enerdatics. "For development-stage sellers, securing a headline valuation is only part of the outcome. The milestones attached to payment determine how much execution risk they retain and when they receive the proceeds." Asia-Pacific and Latin America: Activity diverges as curtailment increases buyer scrutiny Asia-Pacific transaction activity increased approximately 20%, led by India, with Australian wind and storage also contributing. Latin American activity declined approximately 55% as curtailment in Brazil and Chile made buyers more selective. The report's 2027 outlook identifies storage as a major driver of future acquisitions across regions. It highlights contracted European batteries, North American storage platforms and project stake sales to fund construction in India and Australia. In Latin America, it expects storage contracts to support deals, starting with Brazil's first battery storage auctions in December 2026. The report includes regional transaction analysis, precedent deals, developer premium insights and valuation benchmarks. Request for a free copy of the report: https://www.enerdatics.com/renewables-m-a-outlook-analysis-q3-2026 Mohit Kaul (Founder and CEO, Enerdatics) and Kay also presented the reportâs key findings and the outlook for 2027 in an exclusive webinar session. Watch the live webinar session on the report: https://www.enerdatics.com/m-a-outlook-2027-webinar-recording About Enerdatics Founded in 2021, Enerdatics provides renewable energy market intelligence covering M&A, projects, power purchase agreements and financing. Its data and analytics support corporate strategy and M&A teams, advisors, investment banks and private equity firms. Reported deal values include disclosed values only. The European onshore wind valuation analysis covers transactions from January 2025 through September 2026. The contingent-payment percentages apply only to development-stage deals with disclosed terms. artigo.texto: Longer drone flights, full-shift humanoid robots, lighter and faster race cars, and data centers that don't burden the grid. IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Engineers building drones, humanoid robots, race cars, data center power systems, and electric aircraft want more energy in less weight and space, plus the power to use it. Enevate Technologies today introduced Trifecta, a licensable cell technology designed so they no longer have to choose between energy density, power, and cycle life. Battery engineers live by an unwritten rule: energy, power, or cycle life, pick two. At the cutting edge, they often get just one, paying for it with oversized packs, shorter missions, and lost payload. Trifecta designs match or exceed the energy density of leading lithium-metal and solid-state cells without their usual safety and charge-rate problems, and long-life configurations reach 1,000 cycles. "Engineers have spent years designing around their batteries," said Benjamin Park, CEO of Enevate Technologies. "Trifecta flips that. We want to have open conversations about how our technology can change how you design things." Trifecta comes in five modeled configurations: Figures are for modeled designs that build on a successful proof of concept with earlier prototype cells. Enevate Technologies works with each customer to match or tailor a configuration, then helps get cells built by a licensee, through a custom build, or by the customer's existing supplier. Battery manufacturers interested in licensing Trifecta to produce cells for their own customers are invited to reach out. To book a technical briefing or discuss licensing, email [email protected]. About Enevate Technologies Enevate Technologies develops and licenses high-energy, high-power battery cell technology. It builds on technology and team members from Enevate Corporation, whose 20 years of battery innovation was validated by global automakers and cell manufacturers and produced more than 700 patents issued and pending. Its open, cooperative culture gives customers a direct path to its experts. Learn more at enevate.com. artigo.texto: Notícias MERCADO DE CARBONO Mercado Regulado de Carbono define cronograma para que setores da indústria comecem a medir emissões O Ministério da Fazenda, por meio da Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono (SEMC), publicou a Portaria nº 3.199 nesta quinta-feira (29/10), que estabelece o cronograma oficial de implementação das obrigações de Mensuração, Relato e Verificação (MRV) de emissões e remoções de gases de efeito estufa (GEE) para o Mercado Regulado de Carbono no Brasil. O novo sistema, que está gradualmente sendo implementado até 2030, estabelece que grandes empresas comecem a medir anualmente suas emissões de carbono equivalente. A obrigação de MRV é aplicada aos operadores com emissões a partir de 10 mil tCO₂e ao ano, atingindo menos de 1% dos CNPJs do país. Depois de 2030, empresas que emitem mais de 25 mil tCO2e deverão cumprir as obrigações estabelecidas no Plano Nacional de Alocação. O Brasil se comprometeu internacionalmente a ser neutro em emissões até 2050. As regras do novo mercado regulado estão determinadas na Lei 15.042/2024. A Portaria foi precedida de consulta pública realizada no portal Brasil Participativo entre 28 de julho e 28 de agosto de 2026, contabilizando 938 contribuições – entre comentários sobre a minuta e documentos e relatórios anexados, com diversas sugestões. A construção do regulamento contou com a participação de empresas, associações setoriais, comunidade acadêmica e organizações da sociedade civil. Os resultados da consulta pública estão disponibilizados na plataforma Brasil Participativo. “Nos próximos quatro anos, o foco é aprender a medir e reportar as emissões de GEE de maneira padronizada e com rigor metodológico, entendendo que o país vive uma curva de aprendizado. O setor produtivo pode enxergar o Ministério da Fazenda como parceiro comprometido com os setores econômicos visando o estímulo à inovação, ao aumento da competitividade e à sustentabilidade da indústria nacional. O Mercado Regulado de Carbono, além de um instrumento de política climática, é uma política industrial de desenvolvimento e modernização e uma grande oportunidade para o país dar um salto tecnológico e econômico”, destacou a secretária extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono, Cristina Reis. Cronograma e etapas setoriais A portaria estabelece a entrada gradual no sistema dos setores econômicos regulados em três etapas: Etapa 1, com início em 2027: alumínio, usinas integradas de ferro e aço, cimento, exploração e produção de petróleo e gás natural, alguns segmentos da indústria química, mineração de minério de ferro e de bauxita, papel e celulose e vidro. Etapa 2, com início até 2029: cerâmica, usinas semi-integradas de ferro e aço, atividades da indústria química não incluídas na etapa 1, indústria de alimentos e bebidas, mineração das demais substâncias minerais, refino de petróleo e setor elétrico. Etapa 3, com início até 2031: contempla transportes rodoviário, ferroviário e aquaviário. Cada etapa setorial prevê um ciclo de preparação de quatro anos. O primeiro ano é dedicado à elaboração do plano de monitoramento; o segundo e o terceiro anos ao acompanhamento das emissões; e o quarto ano à consolidação de dados para o Plano Nacional de Alocação (PNA). A publicação da portaria não exige a apresentação imediata de relatórios e nem impõe limites de emissão ou custos nesta fase inicial. A definição do teto global de emissões e a alocação de Cotas Brasileiras de Emissões (CBEs) ocorrerão no Plano Nacional de Alocação (PNA), cuja vigência está prevista a partir de 2030, com distribuição 100% gratuita de cotas na largada. Próximos passos A partir da decisão tomada, o governo pretende, ainda em 2026, estruturar a Câmara de Assuntos Regulatórios (CAREG) com os setores da Etapa 1, que se inicia em 2027. A função da Caregé opinar e contribuir para que todas as normas e metodologias relativas ao processo de mensuração sejam adequadas e tenham o melhor desenho para os setores, garantindo um processo previsível e harmonioso para os atores econômicos. A SEMC trabalha agora na estruturação do Programa Brasileiro de Mensuração, Relato e Verificação (PB-MRV) por meio de um decreto e de um conjunto de portarias normativas temáticas. O programa estabelecerá diretrizes gerais para o MRV no âmbito do SBCE, metodologias de mensuração e regras para a acreditação de auditores de inspeção credenciados responsáveis pela verificação independente dos relatos, conhecidos no mercado como Organismos de Validação e Verificação (OVVs). Uma consulta pública sobre o decreto do programa está prevista para novembro de 2026, antes da sua publicação ainda neste ano. Está prevista, também para novembro, uma consulta pública sobre o decreto que institui o Programa Brasileiro de Compensação de Emissões (PBCE), que estabelecerá as diretrizes e disciplinará as bases para os processos e critérios para o credenciamento de metodologias para a originação de Certificados de Remoção ou Redução Verificadas de Emissões (CRVEs). Isso garantirá que, em 2027, as primeiras metodologias aprovadas pelo SBCE sejam credenciadas. No início de 2027, estão previstas turmas de capacitação para apoio dos setores.
