artigo.texto: CATL globally launches ultra-high capacity energy storage system at All Energy 2026 and signs three Australian partnership MoUs MELBOURNE, Australia, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL) today unveiled TENER+ in a global launch at All Energy Australia 2026, where it also showcased TENER Sodium. The company signed memorandums of understanding (MoU) with Hitachi Energy, EPEC Group and UNSW Sydney to strengthen the delivery and grid connection of utility-scale battery projects in Australia. TENER: Engineered for long-term performance and Australia's demanding grid connection requirements CATL's TENER+ and TENER Sodium energy storage systems are designed to deliver the reliability and long-term performance Australian utility-scale energy projects need. Engineered for harsh weather conditions, they are designed to support compliance with Australia's demanding grid connection requirements and give project financiers confidence in the reliability and long-term performance that underpin battery revenues. TENER+ is a 9MWh ultra-high capacity energy storage system that helps developers to achieve a longer-term project value and to maximise the storage capacity of their project, TENER+ reduces the number of containers needed by up to 40% and the project footprint by 12%, making this ideal for projects that are facing land constraints. Its intelligent thermal management system supports a higher round-trip efficiency and lower auxiliary power consumption. Multiple TENER+ batteries can be simultaneously commissioned with a single click to streamline project deployment. Designed for a 25-year lifespan, TENER+ features liquid cooling and protection for humid and coastal environments. Noise levels remain below 65 dBA at 1 metre. Its "no heat island" top-exhaust design directs hot air vertically upwards, away from adjacent units. This prevents horizontal heat discharge and minimises thermal impact on neighbouring PCS units, allowing them to operate at full rated power even in extreme summer conditions. TENER Sodium is the world's first mass-produced, field-validated sodium-ion battery energy storage system. It delivers more than 30MWh through its modular cabinet architecture. Built for Australia's heat, it operates in temperatures of up to 55°C and delivers more than 10,000 cycles at 45°C. It delivers 95% round-trip efficiency with an operating lifespan of more than 20 years. Together, these energy storage systems give developers and asset owners a choice of lithium-ion and sodium-ion chemistries. Sodium is far more abundant and geographically widespread than lithium and it delivers an additional pathway for battery supply chains. "A battery's value is measured over the entire lifespan of a project and not just on the day it's commissioned," said Zane Zhou, General Manager of CATL Australia and New Zealand. "Developers need confidence that their batteries can handle the expected cycling to trade in the National Electricity Market and to perform throughout the lifespan of batteries installed in a utility-scale project. That is what TENER+ and TENER Sodium are designed to deliver. We're offering both sodium-ion and lithium-ion technologies to give asset owners and developers the flexibility to choose the right technology for their success." CATL's local industry partnerships to advance Australia's clean energy transition TENER energy storage systems solve the challenges the Australia's grid is facing as more renewable energy powers the grid. Renewables supplied a record 44.3% of the National Electricity Market's (NEM) generation in the September quarter of 2026. Grid-scale batteries supplied 8% of evening peak generation, overtaking gas-powered generation for the first time according to the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO). As coal-fired power stations retire, the grid increasingly needs energy storage systems with grid-forming capability to provide voltage and frequency support. To help deliver more storage in Australia, CATL's three MoUs aim to address the challenges of a renewables-driven grid through Australian expertise and innovation. CATL's DC battery products and Hitachi Energy's power conversion systems will form the basis of a proposed integrated offering in Australia and the Asia Pacific region. Through this partnership, the company's aim to improve compatibility, standardise project delivery and to reduce integration risk. In Australia, CATL will collaborate with EPEC Group and the Xiamen Energy Storage Validation Research Institute (ESVL) to combine its energy storage technology, with EPEC's grid integration and engineering delivery expertise, and ESVL's full-scale system validation. The parties aim to strengthen technical validation and accelerate the delivery of reliable, bankable and grid-compliant energy storage projects in Australia. CATL and UNSW Sydney will also jointly develop the Centre for Integrated Renewable Energy Training and Innovation in Western Sydney, NSW. This renewable energy training and innovation centre will advance the skills and capabilities needed for Australia's clean energy transition. Zhou added, "CATL is working with Hitachi Energy, EPEC Group, ESVL and UNSW Sydney to give our Australian customers greater confidence in how our technology is integrated, validated and supported throughout a project's life. Together, we're building the local expertise needed to deliver reliable battery projects in the long-term." The MoUs build on CATL's work with Australian customers, including Birdwood Energy, which has selected CATL as the technology partner for the Baranduda Electrical Energy Reserve, a 400MW/1,860MWh battery near Wodonga in Victoria. artigo.texto: Sexta-feira, 30 de outubro de 2026 Por Henrique Casanova | 29 de outubro de 2026 Esta coluna reflete a opinião de quem a assina e não do Jornal O Sul. O Jornal O Sul adota os princípios editoriais de pluralismo, apartidarismo, jornalismo crítico e independência. Data centers são infraestruturas industriais que armazenam e processam dados das corporações digitais, como redes sociais e inteligências artificiais. Na comunidade de Sterling, Virgínia, Estados Unidos, a chegada de um data center mudou drasticamente a vida dos moradores. O ruído constante é debilitante. Dentro ou fora de casa, os moradores ouvem, sem interrupção, um barulho que descrevem como uma cigarra elétrica infernal. Além disso, a alta demanda por energia elétrica do empreendimento pressiona a rede elétrica da cidade e ocasiona o uso também de motores a diesel e a gás natural, que têm sido associados a um surto de problemas respiratórios na comunidade. Já em Fayetteville, Geórgia, Estados Unidos, além da poluição sonora e do ar, a comunidade tem problemas de abastecimento de água desde a implementação de um data center na região. Os moradores logo perceberam a perda de pressão da água nas torneiras e nos chuveiros da comunidade. A mesma coisa aconteceu perto de outros data centers no Arizona, na Carolina do Norte e em Utah. Em todos os casos, as comunidades sofrem também com a desvalorização imobiliária, já que ninguém quer viver perto dos famigerados data centers. Brasil está importando um problema? A resposta curta parece ser sim. Corporações norte-americanas já começaram a estabelecer seus data centers no Brasil, e muito tem se falado das altas cifras de investimento direto no mercado brasileiro. A maior parte desse dinheiro, porém, se destina à compra de equipamentos de empresas estrangeiras. Para piorar o quadro, os data centers geram menos empregos permanentes que outras iniciativas industriais, como, por exemplo, as fábricas de automóveis. Após a construção dos data centers, a manutenção requer uma mão de obra especializada que poderá vir, em parte, de fora do país. Tudo isso é agravado pela falta de planejamento para construir uma indústria nacional em torno desse investimento, com a produção de peças e equipamentos, por exemplo. O interesse das corporações é obter o máximo de vantagens fiscais e estruturais possíveis, e os passivos ambientais ficam no nosso território. Outra grande preocupação é a pressão dos empreendimentos sobre o sistema energético brasileiro. Com as privatizações no país inteiro no setor de distribuição de energia elétrica, temos visto tanto a qualidade dos serviços cair quanto os preços das contas de luz subirem, e a grande demanda dos data centers por energia elétrica poderá agravar esse quadro. Henrique Casanova Jornalista e geógrafo

artigo.texto: Want an Energy-Efficient Data Center? Build It Underwater Microsoft wants to submerge data centers to keep them cool and to harvest energy from the sea When Sean James, who works on data-center technology for Microsoft, suggested that the company put server farms entirely underwater, his colleagues were a bit dubious. But for James, who had earlier served on board a submarine for the U.S. Navy, submerging whole data centers beneath the waves made perfect sense. This tactic, he argued, would not only limit the cost of cooling the machines—an enormous expense for many data-center operators—but it could also reduce construction costs, make it easier to power these facilities with renewable energy, and even improve their performance. Together with Todd Rawlings, another Microsoft engineer, James circulated an internal white paper promoting the concept. It explained how building data centers underwater could help Microsoft and other cloud providers manage today’s phenomenal growth in an environmentally sustainable way. At many large companies, such outlandish ideas might have died a quiet death. But Microsoft researchers have a history of tackling challenges of vital importance to the company in innovative ways, even if the required work is far outside of Microsoft’s core expertise. The key is to assemble engineering teams by uniting Microsoft employees with colleagues from partner companies. The four of us formed the core of just such a team, one charged with testing James’s far-out idea. So in August of 2014, we started to organize what soon came to be called Project Natick, dubbed that for no particular reason other than that our research group likes to name projects after cities in Massachusetts. And just 12 months later, we had a prototype serving up data from beneath the Pacific Ocean. Project Natick had no shortage of hurdles to overcome. The first, of course, was keeping the inside of its big steel container dry. Another was figuring out the best way to use the surrounding seawater to cool the servers inside. And finally there was the matter of how to deal with the barnacles and other forms of sea life that would inevitably cover a submerged vessel—a phenomenon that should be familiar to anyone who has ever kept a boat in the water for an extended period. Clingy crustaceans and such would be a challenge because they could interfere with the transfer of heat from the servers to the surrounding water. These issues daunted us at first, but we solved them one by one, often drawing on time-tested solutions from the marine industry. But why go to all this trouble? Sure, cooling computers with seawater would lower the air-conditioning bill and could improve operations in other ways, too, but submerging a data center comes with some obvious costs and inconveniences. Does trying to put thousands of computers beneath the sea really make sense? We think it does, for several reasons. For one, it would offer a company like ours the ability to quickly target capacity where and when it is needed. Corporate planners would be freed from the burden of having to build these facilities long before they are actually required in anticipation of later demand. For an industry that spends billions of dollars a year constructing ever-increasing numbers of data centers, quick response time could provide enormous cost savings. The reason underwater data centers could be built more quickly than land-based ones is easy enough to understand. Today, the construction of each such installation is unique. The equipment might be the same, but building codes, taxes, climate, workforce, electricity supply, and network connectivity are different everywhere. And those variables affect how long construction takes. We also observe their effects in the performance of our facilities, where otherwise identical equipment exhibits different levels of reliability depending on where it is located. As we see it, a Natick site would be made up of a collection of “pods”—steel cylinders that would each contain possibly several thousand servers. Together they’d make up an underwater data center, which would be located within a few kilometers of the coast and placed between 50 and 200 meters below the surface. The pods could either float above the seabed at some intermediate depth, moored by cables to the ocean floor, or they could rest on the seabed itself. Once we deploy a data-center pod, it would stay in place until it’s time to retire the set of servers it contains. Or perhaps market conditions would change, and we’d decide to move it somewhere else. This is a true “lights out” environment, meaning that the system’s managers would work remotely, with no one to fix things or change out parts for the operational life of the pod. Now imagine applying just-in-time manufacturing to this concept. The pods could be constructed in a factory, provisioned with servers, and made ready to ship anywhere in the world. Unlike the case on land, the ocean provides a very uniform environment wherever you are. So no customization of the pods would be needed, and we could install them quickly anywhere that computing capacity was in short supply, incrementally increasing the size of an underwater installation to meet capacity requirements as they grew. Our goal for Natick is to be able to get data centers up and running, at coastal sites anywhere in the world, within 90 days from the decision to deploy. Most new data centers are built in locations where electricity is inexpensive, the climate is reasonably cool, the land is cheap, and the facility doesn’t impose on the people living nearby. The problem with this approach is that it often puts data centers far from population centers, which limits how fast the servers can respond to requests. For interactive experiences online, these delays can be problematic. We want Web pages to load quickly and video games such as Minecraft or Halo to be snappy and lag free. artigo.texto: Missoulians Urge Data Center Controls, But Also Ideas Missoula County residents tell county leaders they're still concerned about the impacts of data centers, even without an active proposal now. Some are also suggesting it could be time for the community to innovate, coming up with parameters that could control the big computing centers, but also ensure some benefits. Those comments last night, as the county held a question and answer center around the first draft of new zoning regulations. Opposition, but also ideas A few speakers floated the idea of the county using the opportunity to ask, and ensure impacts are paid for, even it involves billions of dollars. "Those sorts of penalties sound like a lot to us but don't necessarily impact," the centers, noted House District 97 Representative Melody Cunningham. "Nobody wants us in our backyard. So we need to look harder for solutions and say, if we want a data center, maybe we need to own it. Maybe we need to figure out how to build that big, better mousetrap," offered another woman. Where the county is looking for ideas County Climate Action Program Manager Svien Newman explained that it would be up to commissioners, since planners have been focused on regulations and not on how other states are handling the debate, because of the difference in laws. "We've mostly looked at counties and cities and towns today," explained Newman. "Just kind of what's the most comparable kind of apples to apples, because states have such vastly different regulatory authorities than we do." artigo.texto: EAF investirá em conversores de TV 3.0 e data center com saldo do 5G Propostas de R$ 1,66 bilhão destinam recursos a 910.000 famílias de baixa renda e a um data center público operado pela Telebras. O Grupo de Acompanhamento da Implantação das Soluções para os Problemas de Interferência (Gaispi) aprovou nesta terça-feira (27) dois projetos que poderão receber recursos economizados na execução das obrigações do leilão do 5G. As propostas apresentadas pela Entidade Administradora da Faixa (EAF) ainda precisam ser aprovadas pelo Conselho Diretor da Anatel. As iniciativas preveem R$ 1,28 bilhão para distribuir conversores de TV 3.0 a famílias de baixa renda e R$ 375 milhões para implantar um data center público voltado a aplicações de inteligência artificial (IA), por meio de uma reserva de aproximadamente R$ 2 bilhões para garantir a conclusão dos compromissos originais, incluindo uma margem de segurança de 10%. Segundo os estudos da EAF, há cerca de R$ 1,69 bilhão disponível para investimentos adicionais. Conversores de TV 3.0 A maior parte do investimento, estimada em R$ 1,28 bilhão, será destinada à distribuição de conversores de TV 3.0 para aproximadamente 910.000 famílias de baixa renda em São Paulo, no Rio de Janeiro e no Distrito Federal, inicialmente. A prioridade será para beneficiários do Bolsa Família inscritos no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico). O custo médio estimado é de R$ 1.407,36 por família, incluindo equipamentos, logística, distribuição, comunicação, atendimento e despesas operacionais do projeto piloto de São Paulo. A implementação poderá levar até 24 meses. Os conversores permitirão que televisores compatíveis com a recepção digital atual tenham acesso à nova geração da televisão aberta, que promete melhorias de imagem e som, além de recursos de interatividade e integração com serviços digitais. Data center da Telebras O segundo projeto prevê investimento de R$ 375 milhões em um data center da União, com operação pela Telebras, que deverá atender órgãos federais, com capacidade para processar dados sensíveis, hospedar serviços governamentais críticos e executar aplicações de inteligência artificial. O projeto prevê uma área de aproximadamente 5.000 metros quadrados, com infraestrutura para aplicações de IA e serviços tradicionais de tecnologia da informação. O módulo dedicado à inteligência artificial contará com 20 racks e seis servidores equipados com um total de 48 GPUs, além de servidores e sistemas de armazenamento. A instalação também terá sistemas redundantes de energia, conectividade e resfriamento para processamento de alto desempenho. A implantação está estimada em 12 meses, condicionada à disponibilidade de energia, aos licenciamentos e ao fornecimento e à integração dos equipamentos. A EAF será responsável pela execução do projeto, seguindo um modelo semelhante ao utilizado na implantação da Rede Privativa de Comunicação da Administração Pública Federal.

artigo.texto: The surge in construction of fossil-fueled power plants to run AI data centers is set to undo 15 years’ worth of greenhouse gas reductions from U.S. electricity generation, according to an internal analysis by the Sierra Club. The U.S. power sector would emit 2.1 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide by 2030, after factoring in planned AI projects. That’s 618 million tons more than 2025 levels, by the Sierra Club’s calculations, or about a 42% increase. A year and a half ago, researchers at the nonprofit environmental group would have estimated that the buildout and its impact would have been a quarter or half of current projections, said Jeremy Fisher, the Sierra Club’s principal advisor for climate and energy. “The numbers continue to sort of boggle our minds,” he said. Related: Insurer Rolls Out Policy to Protect Data Centers Against Growing Backlash Many data center developers are turning to natural gas to meet the immense electricity demand, relying on power sources that are both on and off the grid. The bulk of the expected emissions by 2030 would come from sources that are not directly linked to the grid, often built by tech companies to avoid the long wait for a connection. These could exceed 460 million tons, Fisher said, roughly the same as the annual emissions of Mexico. Helen Kou, a BloombergNEF analyst, said if there’s significant growth in gas power for new facilities, “you would presume emissions would increase from year to date.” But how much is a difficult question to answer. There’s so much uncertainty in the projections for power emissions that the lowest and highest estimates differ by more electricity than the combined demand of California and Florida. The Sierra Club’s estimate of the climate impacts of the data center buildout is higher than others released so far. The wide range of projections is due to questions around how many facilities will actually be built, what technologies they will ultimately use and how much renewable energy capacity comes online over the next few years. The environmental nonprofit Union of Concerned Scientists in January projected that fossil-fuel-powered electricity for data centers could increase U.S. power-sector emissions by 19% to 29%, or as much as 342 million tons a year by 2035. U.S. and Canadian researchers in June published a journal article projecting a 28% rise in the sector’s emissions. Other forecasts see U.S. electricity continuing to decarbonize as economically competitive renewables outperform fossil fuels, despite the data center boom. Rhodium Group, a research firm that projects energy use and CO2, finds that in its highest-emission scenario for 2040 that the sector’s greenhouse gas emissions fall 24% below their 2025 level. If the rush to build AI data centers leads to the upper bounds of the emissions projected by these researchers, it represents a reversal of a two-decade economic and policy trend toward less U.S. power-sector climate pollution. Electricity emissions peaked in 2007. In 2009, thanks to advances in hydraulic fracturing, the U.S. became the world’s largest natural gas producer. The fracking boom in turn drove down the price of natural gas, displacing dirtier coal plants across the U.S. Meanwhile, the Environmental Protection Agency wrote regulations to dial down carbon from power plants, and former President Joe Biden aimed to decarbonize the grid completely by 2035. Today, natural gas prices are historically low and President Donald Trump has undertaken a dramatic rollback of climate rules. That helped nudge U.S. power-sector emissions back up in 2025. The Sierra Club analysis draws on public filings and other groups’ data center projections, including the Environmental Integrity Project’s count of expected plants and emissions by 2030. Grid-connected generators alone would increase 2030 baseline emissions by 10%, or 154 million tons of CO2. Then there are the bring-your-own-power projects. Four-fifths of the energy for those could come from natural gas, according to a separate analysis by Earthjustice and Better Data Center Project. The increased local air and climate pollution from such plants has already helped stoke opposition to data centers across the country. If all the projected data centers do end up being built on time, and with new natural gas fueling inefficient turbines 24/7 at some facilities, that could drive power emissions up, said Brendan Pierpont, director of electricity at Energy Innovation, a non-partisan energy and climate policy think tank. “There’s certainly a risk that that’s enough emissions to push us back many years of our progress on reducing power-sector emissions,” he said. “But it’s not a foregone conclusion that that’s going to happen.” But Pierpont said it’s challenging to model data-center emissions when little is known about factors like backlogs of gas turbine orders, wait times for grid connections or myriad other things that can slow or halt projects. “There’s just enormous uncertainty, both around the scale of data center demand that ultimately gets built and gets added as well as the power supply strategy,” Pierpont said. Many projects could be delayed or canceled. Just last month Oracle Corp. submitted a force majeure notice to the developer of its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico, saying there is a risk that it won’t come online by 2028 as planned due to regulatory setbacks and community opposition. “The big question of the day is trying to create an accurate forecast of project demand,” BloombergNEF’s Kou said. Top photo: An Amazon Web Services (AWS) data center, left, and Microsoft data center in Aldie, Virginia, on Tuesday, Oct. 28, 2025. Microsoft Corp. is scheduled to release earnings figures on October 29. Bloomberg. Was this article valuable? Here are more articles you may enjoy.

artigo.texto: POSCO Future M said Friday that it has expanded its cooperation scope with LG Energy Solution to include LFP (lithium iron phosphate) cathode materials, artificial graphite anode materials, and others. The two companies signed a "Future Cooperation MOU" on the same day, agreeing to strengthen their cooperative framework to jointly respond to the rapidly changing EV (electric vehicle) and ESS (energy storage system) markets as well as the global trade environment. POSCO Future M will supply a total of 720,000 tons of cathode and anode materials, including LFP and ternary cathode materials and artificial graphite anode materials, to LG Energy Solution from 2027 through 2033. The two companies plan to sign a definitive contract within the year. First, the company will swiftly advance the conversion of its high-nickel ternary cathode material production line at the Pohang cathode material plant into an LFP cathode material production line. It plans to begin full-scale supply of LFP cathode materials to LG Energy Solution from early next year. Going forward, the company aims to develop a new process utilizing the POSCO Group's salt lake lithium in Argentina to enhance cost competitiveness and improve quality, thereby supplying next-generation LFP cathode materials. For the ternary NCM (nickel cobalt manganese) cathode materials previously supplied to LG Energy Solution, the two companies agreed to pursue measures to further boost cost competitiveness by expanding the use of recovered metals extracted from spent batteries in the medium to long term. The agreement also includes cooperation on the supply and technology development of next-generation products such as sodium-ion batteries and silicon anode materials. First, POSCO Future M will produce artificial graphite anode materials, which are advantageous for improving fast-charging performance and battery lifespan and have seen steadily growing demand, in Korea and Vietnam to supply LG Energy Solution. The two companies also agreed to cooperate on technology development and supply of future battery materials, including materials for sodium-ion batteries (SIB), ultra high-nickel cathode materials, and silicon anode materials. In addition, they committed to proactively responding to changes in the trade environment by seeking joint response measures in cases where variables related to global supply chains arise or are anticipated, such as the introduction of the U.S. PFE (Prohibited Foreign Entity) requirements and the announcement of the European IAA (Industrial Acceleration Act).

artigo.texto: Douglas County staff members will host a drop-in session for the community to come share input on battery energy storage systems and regulations that are in development. A BESS “stores electrical energy in rechargeable batteries and releases it when needed,” according to a county news release. “Systems range in size from small units commonly found in garages and basements to large installations resembling rows of shipping containers that can cover several acres.” They are not data centers. The drop-in event is set for 2 to 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6 at the Public Works building, 3755 E. 25th St. in Lawrence. “Planner Karl Bauer will provide 15-minute presentations at 2 p.m., 4 p.m. and 5:30 p.m. covering what a BESS entails and the regulations process,” according to the release. “Staff will seek community input on topics such as location, notification areas, setbacks and size limitations.” Don’t miss a beat … Click here to sign up for our email newsletters Click here to learn more about our newsletters first Staff members will gather input on a walk-in basis throughout the event. Folks who can’t make it to the event can provide their input via this form on the county’s website. During a county commission work session in May, Bauer mentioned BESS fire risks such as thermal runaway — a rapid increase in temperature that can lead to a fire. The county’s regulations would aim to mitigate potential risks. See the video of that meeting at this link. The Lawrence-Douglas County Planning Commission will consider draft regulations for BESS during a meeting set for Wednesday, Dec. 16. Proposed regulations would then go to the Douglas County Commission for consideration in early 2027. Planning commissioners heard more about BESS research Bauer has been working on during their midmonth meeting on Sept. 9. That meeting video is available via YouTube at this link, and audio is available via the city’s Soundcloud at this link. The county has not received any applications seeking to install a BESS. Note: YouTube was down for part of the day Wednesday. Linked videos may be temporarily unavailable. If local news matters to you, please help us keep doing this work. artigo.texto: Resultados da American Tower no 3T26: Crescimento de Data Centers Eleva Projeção de Receita Imobiliária No terceiro trimestre de 2026, a American Tower registrou receita total de US$ 2,785 bilhões, alta de 2,5% na comparação anual, impulsionada pelo avanço de 16,3% em Data Centers. Contudo, o lucro líquido GAAP recuou 14,4%, pressionado por perdas não realizadas em participações acionárias e variações negativas na receita linearizada. O AFFO por ação cresceu 3,2%, atingindo US$ 2,87, e o fluxo de caixa livre manteve-se estável em US$ 986 milhões. A empresa elevou a projeção de receita de propriedades para o ano, mas enfrenta riscos como alta alavancagem financeira, de 4,9 vezes o EBITDA ajustado, e crescimento orgânico modesto no segmento de torres. A American Tower (NYSE: AMT) registrou uma receita total de US$ 2,785 bilhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, uma alta de 2,5% na comparação anual, enquanto o LPA GAAP diluído caiu 9,9%, para US$ 1,64. A receita de propriedades subiu 4,5%, para US$ 2,734 bilhões, impulsionada pelo crescimento de 16,3% na receita de caixa no segmento de Data Centers, mas o lucro líquido GAAP recuou, já que perdas não realizadas em investimentos em participações acionárias substituíram os ganhos do ano anterior. O AFFO por ação aumentou 3,2%, o fluxo de caixa livre ficou praticamente estável e a empresa elevou sua projeção de receita de propriedades para o ano todo. Dados dos Principais Resultados O trimestre apresentou um crescimento moderado da receita, com o faturamento total de inquilinos aumentando 1,7% e o faturamento orgânico de inquilinos subindo 1,1%. A receita reportada também absorveu uma contribuição não caixa de receita linearizada negativa de US$ 24,0 milhões, em comparação com os US$ 27,7 milhões positivos registrados um ano antes. Os lucros GAAP enfraqueceram, embora diversas métricas não GAAP tenham apresentado alta. O lucro líquido caiu 14,4%, enquanto o AFFO atribuível aos acionistas ordinários subiu 2,4% e o AFFO por ação cresceu 3,2%. EBITDA ajustado, AFFO e fluxo de caixa livre são métricas não GAAP ou definidas pela empresa e devem ser analisadas em conjunto com os resultados GAAP. Desempenho Operacional e por Segmento O segmento de Data Centers foi o principal motor de crescimento operacional, entregando um avanço de 16,3% na receita de caixa. A administração atribuiu o desempenho ao forte resultado contínuo da CoreSite, citando também a demanda constante por locação em todo o portfólio global de torres. O crescimento relacionado a torres foi mais moderado. O faturamento total de inquilinos aumentou US$ 34 milhões, ou 1,7%, enquanto o faturamento orgânico de inquilinos subiu US$ 22 milhões, ou 1,1%. A diferença entre o crescimento de data centers e o faturamento orgânico de inquilinos indica que as duas plataformas de infraestrutura entraram no último trimestre com ritmos de expansão distintos. Itens Não Caixa Pressionaram o Lucro GAAP, Enquanto o AFFO Se Manteve Firme Dois fatores não caixa ajudam a explicar a divergência entre receita, lucros GAAP e AFFO. A receita linearizada passou de US$ 27,7 milhões positivos no 3T 2025 para US$ 24,0 milhões negativos no 3T 2026, uma variação anual adversa de aproximadamente US$ 51,7 milhões. Em termos líquidos, a receita linearizada menos a despesa linearizada ficou negativa em US$ 31,7 milhões, em comparação a US$ 18,3 milhões positivos no ano anterior, o que também limitou o crescimento do EBITDA ajustado. Paralelamente, a American Tower registrou cerca de US$ 71,5 milhões em perdas não realizadas em investimentos em participações acionárias, em comparação a US$ 10,9 milhões em ganhos não realizados no mesmo trimestre do ano anterior. Essa reversão contribuiu para as quedas no lucro líquido GAAP e no LPA, mesmo com o avanço da receita de propriedades. As métricas orientadas pelo caixa mostraram maior estabilidade. O AFFO atribuível aos acionistas ordinários subiu para US$ 1,335 bilhão, enquanto o fluxo de caixa livre avançou ligeiramente para US$ 986 milhões. No entanto, o crescimento de 0,9% do EBITDA ajustado continuou num ritmo mais lento do que o aumento da receita, mostrando que nem toda a expansão da receita se traduziu em um ganho proporcional no lucro operacional. Lucratividade, Fluxo de Caixa e Balanço Patrimonial O valor absoluto da margem bruta de propriedades subiu 2,5%, num ritmo inferior à alta de 4,5% da receita de propriedades, com a margem bruta de propriedades em 73,5%. O EBITDA ajustado aumentou 0,9%, para US$ 1,832 bilhão, gerando uma margem de 65,8%. O fluxo de caixa operacional recuou 4,6%, para US$ 1,393 bilhão. Os investimentos de capital (Capex) totais em caixa diminuíram 14,6%, para US$ 407 milhões, o que ajudou o fluxo de caixa livre a se manter praticamente estável em US$ 986 milhões, apesar da menor geração operacional de caixa. A American Tower encerrou o trimestre com uma dívida total de US$ 37,579 bilhões e US$ 1,872 bilhão em caixa e equivalentes de caixa, resultando em uma dívida líquida de US$ 35,707 bilhões. Seu índice de alavancagem líquida ficou em 4,9 vezes o EBITDA ajustado anualizado do 3T, enquanto a liquidez total atingiu aproximadamente US$ 10,6 bilhões. Durante o trimestre, a empresa emitiu US$ 1,6 bilhão em títulos seniores não garantidos com vencimento entre 2031 e 2036. Os recursos foram utilizados para quitar US$ 600 milhões em títulos a vencer, reduzir empréstimos na linha de crédito rotativo e financiar fins corporativos gerais. Outro montante de US$ 1,0 bilhão em títulos foi quitado no vencimento em outubro. A American Tower recomprou aproximadamente 1,8 milhão de ações por US$ 315 milhões durante o 3T. Posteriormente, recomprou outros 0,4 milhão de ações por US$ 68 milhões até 20 de outubro, e o conselho de administração autorizou um valor adicional de US$ 2,0 bilhões para futuras recompras. artigo.texto: Women have been at the forefront of a fast-growing, bipartisan backlash to data centers, packing local meetings, organizing protests and even running for office. Now, less than a week from Election Day, some are saying it’s reshaping how they plan to vote. Half of Americans think data centers are affecting home energy costs, a perception that is adding to voters’ concerns around affordability ahead of the elections, according to a September survey by the nonpartisan Pew Research Center. In addition, more than half think data centers are bad for the environment, up from 39 percent in January. It’s one of the few issues that has bypassed partisan polarization, and broken down by gender, the opposition is strongest among women. According to a Gallup poll from May, 55 percent of women said they strongly opposed data centers compared with 43 percent of men. The 19th spoke with five women — both Republicans and Democrats — about what has driven their opposition and how that has informed their vote. Cheryl Shadden | Texas In 2023, when a data center that hosts a bitcoin mining operation set up shop across the street from her home, Cheryl Shadden became involved in a battle to find peace again in the rural community she’s lived in for 41 years. The operation, which runs 24 hours a day and houses 60,000 computers, has inundated residents like Shadden with nonstop noise, leading to health issues — such as vertigo, hearing loss and migraines — and negatively impacted property values. “This is akin to being tortured,” she said. Residents are blasted with bright lights and incessant noise, and they can’t sleep, she said. “That is an absolute assault.” She spends all of her free time fighting the bitcoin operation and is now worried about a proposal for two other hyperscale data centers that could go up near her home. “It’s so unpleasant riding horses on my property right now because of this horrific noise; it’s no longer a hobby of peace that you can enjoy quietly,” she said. “It’s like trying to ride a horse on an airport runway because literally that’s how bad the noise is.” As a result of how she feels her community has been treated, she says her politics “have absolutely changed.” “I’ve been a conservative Republican my entire life,” she said. But when she asked her congressman, Rep. Roger Williams, for help, she said his staff responded that he supports the data center industry. “He’s pushing that in Washington, D.C., not decreasing the impact on the community,” she said. “That sent a clear message to me.” On the other hand, when she reached out to Williams’ challenger, Democrat Dione Sims, her campaign manager put Shadden in touch with the candidate. After Shadden connected with Sims, Democratic gubernatorial hopeful Gina Hinojosa reached out and arranged to visit the community to hear from residents. Shadden has since appeared in a campaign commercial for Hinojosa. “Why would I vote for any of the Republicans that haven’t done anything to decrease the harm to my community? Why would I give them another shot at raking my community over the coals and harming my neighbors?” she said. She said her decision to vote for Democrats this election is far from an anomaly in her county: “The rural rebellion is in full swing, and if you aren’t going to protect your constituents, then it’s time to give somebody else a shot.” Maranda Edwards | Southwest Virginia Over the summer, Maranda Edwards was devastated to learn that one of the largest data centers planned in Virginia would be built in Wythe County where she lives. It was the second data center announced in a year in the county and would span 1,000 acres. To visualize how big that is, an acre is a little smaller than a football field. “We’re losing farmland, and that’s really devastating. The piece of land is absolutely beautiful,” she said. She also worries about the wildlife. “It has deer. It has birds. It has endangered species.” Edwards has been involved in the local fight to stop the planned data centers, organizing with others in the community through a Facebook page with 1,500 members and by attending public meetings. While Edwards grew up in a Republican household and voted for President Donald Trump in the last election, the 25-year-old said that in the past two years her views have shifted. As someone with a master’s in public health, she’s found herself more aligned with Democrats on some issues, including access to healthcare. “I wouldn’t say that I identify with a specific political group,” she said. “I think it just makes more sense to be more open-minded, be a good person.” But this year, she said, “I’m voting for whatever candidate is against data centers.” Before the data center issue, she said she wasn’t that involved in politics and doesn’t think she would have voted in the midterms. But now she’s invested and has been researching the candidates. “It boils down to politics, and who you elect, because they make a lot of those final decisions,” she said. As a result, she said she’s voting for Joy Powers, a Democrat and fourth-generation cattle farmer who is running to represent the 9th Congressional District, which Cook Political Report rates as solidly Republican. Rachel St. James | Wisconsin Rachel St. James was aware of the data center issue long before it became national news. She remembers reading a Greenpeace report about a decade ago describing the energy that data centers needed to power our increasingly online lives back during the initial uptick in television streaming. Now, with artificial intelligence requiring vast amounts of both energy and water, St. James fears the environmental and human repercussions from a new wave of data center construction. “I really do not want to see something happen where the costs of AI are borne by the public … and all profits go to the companies and the data centers,” she said. “I’m not OK with that. artigo.texto: Comunidades americanas intensificam protestos contra a expansão de data centers, tornando o tema central nas eleições de 2026. Fato: Oposição a data centers se intensifica nos EUA Em 2026, a construção acelerada de data centers tem despertado resistência em diversas cidades dos Estados Unidos. O investimento em instalações de armazenamento massivo de servidores, aliado ao custo de infraestrutura necessária – como linhas de transmissão e estradas de acesso – está gerando controvérsia nas campanhas eleitorais de nível federal, estadual e municipal. Eleitores de diferentes espectros políticos têm usado a questão como ponto de ataque contra candidatos que apoiam a expansão, enquanto opositores apontam impactos ambientais, aumento de tarifas de energia e perda de qualidade de vida nas áreas afetadas. Contexto: por que isso importa Os data centers são a espinha dorsal da economia digital contemporânea: eles hospedam serviços de nuvem, streaming, jogos online e plataformas de redes sociais. A demanda por capacidade de processamento cresceu exponencialmente nos últimos anos, impulsionada por IA generativa, realidade aumentada e o boom de dispositivos conectados. Entretanto, a expansão física desses centros traz desafios reais: - Consumo energético: Grandes instalações podem absorver megawatts de energia, pressionando redes elétricas já sobrecarregadas. - Impacto ambiental: O uso intensivo de ar‑condicionado e sistemas de refrigeração gera emissão de gases de efeito estufa, além de exigir grandes áreas de terreno. - Deslocamento de comunidades: Projetos de infraestrutura associados – como novas rodovias e linhas de transmissão – podem gerar desapropriações e mudar o perfil urbano. Esses fatores convergem em um ponto sensível para eleitores que priorizam sustentabilidade e qualidade de vida, explicando por que o tema tem se tornado arma política nas disputas de 2026. Reação da população e do mercado Nas cidades onde os projetos foram anunciados, grupos de moradores organizaram assembleias, petições online e manifestações presenciais. Em estados como Califórnia e Texas, as protestas ganharam cobertura nacional, forçando candidatos a incluir propostas de regulação mais rígida nos seus programas. Do lado empresarial, as gigantes de tecnologia – como Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure e Google Cloud – têm buscado mitigar a crise de imagem. Estratégias recentes incluem: - Investimento em energia renovável para alimentar os novos data centers. - Desenvolvimento de projetos de “data centers verdes”, com sistemas de refrigeração por água de mar ou ar externo. - Parcerias com governos locais para criar incentivos fiscais condicionados a metas de redução de carbono. Apesar desses esforços, a percepção pública ainda está em formação. A oposição não se limita a questões ambientais; há também preocupações sobre concentração de poder tecnológico e vulnerabilidade a falhas de infraestrutura. O que esperar Nos próximos meses, a pauta deve ganhar ainda mais força nas primárias e nas eleições gerais. Analistas preveem três cenários principais: - Regulamentação mais rígida: Estados podem aprovar leis que exigem avaliações de impacto ambiental detalhadas antes de autorizar novos projetos. - Descentralização da capacidade: Empresas podem investir em micro‑data centers distribuídos, reduzindo a necessidade de mega‑estruturas. - Conflitos judiciais: Processos de desapropriação e disputas sobre licenças podem atrasar ou cancelar projetos em andamento. Para os eleitores, o tema pode ser decisivo na escolha de representantes que prometam equilibrar desenvolvimento tecnológico e responsabilidade ambiental. Para o setor, a pressão pode acelerar a adoção de soluções mais sustentáveis e abrir espaço para novos modelos de negócios, como serviços de computação na borda (edge computing). Datas e o que vem depois As próximas rodadas de debates eleitorais, previstas para o segundo semestre de 2026, deverão incluir perguntas específicas sobre políticas de data centers. Além disso, a Comissão Federal de Energia (FERC) anunciou que publicará diretrizes preliminares sobre consumo energético de data centers ainda neste trimestre, o que pode influenciar tanto a agenda legislativa quanto as estratégias corporativas. Enquanto isso, organizações de defesa ambiental estão preparando relatórios detalhados para pressionar legisladores em nível estadual. O acompanhamento desses documentos será crucial para entender como a pressão popular pode transformar o panorama da infraestrutura digital nos Estados Unidos. Em síntese, a disputa pelos data centers está longe de ser apenas um detalhe técnico; ela se tornou um ponto de convergência entre tecnologia, política e sociedade, com repercussões que podem redefinir o futuro da nuvem nos próximos anos.

artigo.texto: Lucro da Seagate no 1º Tri Fiscal de 2027 Atinge Recorde com Demanda por Data Centers A Seagate Technology registrou no primeiro trimestre fiscal de 2027 receita recorde de US$ 4,23 bilhões, alta de 61% na comparação anual, impulsionada pela forte demanda do segmento de Data Centers. A margem bruta não-GAAP atingiu 57,8% e o LPA diluído não-GAAP alcançou o recorde de US$ 7,68. O fluxo de caixa livre saltou para US$ 1,48 bilhão, permitindo expressiva redução da dívida bruta. Para o segundo trimestre, a empresa projeta receita de US$ 4,8 bilhões e LPA não-GAAP de US$ 9,20, embora persista o risco de incertezas macroeconômicas, tarifas e restrições comerciais globais. A Seagate Technology Holdings plc (NASDAQ: STX) registrou rentabilidade e fluxo de caixa livre recordes no primeiro trimestre fiscal de 2027, à medida que a demanda sustentada por data centers, os preços favoráveis e a execução operacional impulsionaram a receita em 61% na comparação anual. A empresa de armazenamento também projetou novo crescimento sequencial no segundo trimestre, com previsão de que o lucro diluído por ação não-GAAP atinja US$ 9,20 no ponto médio de sua projeção. A receita do trimestre encerrado no primeiro trimestre fiscal subiu para US$ 4,23 bilhões, ante US$ 2,63 bilhões no mesmo período do ano anterior, representando um avanço de 17% na comparação sequencial. A receita do segmento de Data Center, que respondeu por 81% do total, saltou 63% na comparação anual, para US$ 3,45 bilhões, impulsionada pela demanda contínua de nuvem e de empresas/OEM. A margem bruta não-GAAP atingiu o recorde de 57,8%, um aumento de 17,7 pontos percentuais na comparação anual e de 5,1 pontos em relação ao trimestre anterior. A margem operacional não-GAAP subiu para o recorde de 50,7%, em comparação com 29,0% um ano antes e 44,6% no quarto trimestre fiscal. As despesas operacionais na mesma base foram de US$ 300 milhões, alta de 3% na comparação anual. O lucro líquido não-GAAP mais que triplicou, passando de US$ 583 milhões para US$ 1,78 bilhão. O LPA diluído não-GAAP aumentou 194%, alcançando o recorde de US$ 7,68, valor que a empresa afirmou ter ficado acima de suas projeções. Em base GAAP, o lucro líquido foi de US$ 1,76 bilhão, o LPA diluído foi de US$ 7,59, a margem bruta ficou em 57,3% e a margem operacional em 48,8%. Demanda por Data Centers impulsiona mix de remessas A Seagate entregou 220 exabytes de capacidade em HDDs durante o trimestre, uma alta de 21% na comparação anual. As remessas de unidades nearline subiram 24%, para 198 exabytes, representando 90% do total de exabytes entregues, enquanto o volume não-nearline foi de 22 exabytes. O segmento de nuvem permaneceu como o principal motor da demanda e registrou seu 12º trimestre consecutivo de crescimento de receita, de acordo com a apresentação. A receita de empresas/OEM cresceu pelo sexto trimestre consecutivo, registrando altas de dois dígitos tanto na comparação sequencial quanto na anual, à medida que a demanda se fortaleceu em ambientes de nuvem híbrida. A empresa informou que a grande maioria de sua oferta nearline para data centers está alocada até o ano civil de 2028, com alguns contratos de fornecimento em nuvem estendendo-se até 2030. A receita de Edge IoT também aumentou, subindo 52% na comparação anual e 13% na sequencial, para US$ 784 milhões, embora sua fatia na receita total tenha permanecido em 19%. A Seagate está utilizando seu roteiro tecnológico baseado em HAMR para aumentar a capacidade por disco em vez de expandir a produção física de unidades. Seus produtos Mozaic 4 estão em fase de ramp-up em dois grandes provedores de serviços de nuvem, enquanto qualificações adicionais para nuvem e empresas/OEM devem ser concluídas nos próximos meses. As remessas de qualificação para o Mozaic 5 continuam programadas para começar no final do ano civil de 2027. A empresa também relatou ter demonstrado 8 terabytes por disco em testes de laboratório. Geração de caixa sustenta redução da dívida O fluxo de caixa operacional atingiu o recorde de US$ 1,69 bilhão, alta de 218% na comparação anual, enquanto o fluxo de caixa livre subiu 246%, para o recorde de US$ 1,48 bilhão, após US$ 211 milhões em despesas de capital. A Seagate encerrou o trimestre com US$ 1,26 bilhão em caixa e equivalentes de caixa. O principal da dívida bruta diminuiu 53% na comparação anual, para US$ 2,35 bilhões, enquanto a dívida líquida caiu de US$ 3,93 bilhões para US$ 1,13 bilhão. O índice de alavancagem total baseado na dívida líquida e no EBITDA ajustado dos últimos 12 meses caiu de 1,5 vez para 0,2 vez. O EBITDA ajustado dos últimos 12 meses foi de US$ 6,09 bilhões, e as despesas com juros em dinheiro no período caíram para US$ 272 milhões. A Seagate relatou liquidez total de US$ 2,6 bilhões, composta por aproximadamente US$ 1,3 bilhão em caixa e uma linha de crédito rotativo de US$ 1,3 bilhão. A empresa também resgatou outros US$ 750 milhões em notas sênior de alto rendimento após o fechamento do primeiro trimestre fiscal. Perspectivas para o segundo trimestre fiscal Para o segundo trimestre fiscal de 2027, a Seagate projeta receita de US$ 4,8 bilhões, com variação de mais ou menos US$ 100 milhões. A margem operacional não-GAAP deve se situar na faixa média dos 50%, enquanto o LPA diluído não-GAAP está estimado em US$ 9,20, mais ou menos US$ 0,20. No ponto médio da projeção, espera-se que as despesas operacionais não-GAAP fiquem em aproximadamente US$ 300 milhões, a alíquota de imposto não-GAAP é estimada em cerca de 16% do lucro antes dos impostos e o número de ações diluídas usado no cálculo do LPA deve ser de cerca de 233 milhões. A projeção de LPA exclui despesas estimadas com remuneração baseada em ações de US$ 0,30 por ação. As perspectivas permanecem sujeitas às condições de demanda, execução de produção e ritmo de qualificação de produtos. artigo.texto: Bob Foos Mayor Lynn Ragsdale began the regular City Council meeting on Monday with an open discussion about data centers. Gina Monson (2nd Ward) initially raised awareness of the issue when she learned that a firm that owns property in the Joplin/Webb City Industrial Park has reportedly inquired with Joplin city staff about possibly rezoning the property for use as a data center. The 2.85-acre tract in question is on the west side of Industrial Park Road, two lots north of Kennedy Lane. According to Beacon, it is owned by AIDataCenter Inc., of Hollywood, Fla. Discussion topics included harmful effects of data centers, including excessive noise. City Administrator Carl Francis said he has recently researched ways other cities have adopted methods of regulating data centers. He said he knows of five Missouri cities that have regulations in place. At the end of discussion, the council approved an ordinance authorizing Ragsdale to hire a sound acoustics engineer, if complaints of noise or vibrations are brought to the council. « » Also on Monday, the council approved Ragsdale’s appointment of Tyler Burgess (1st Ward) to succeed Jerry Fisher (3rd Ward) on the Centennial Railroad Transportation Development District. Burgess will begin a new three-year term. Fisher has attempted to resign from his city council seat for medical reasons, but his resignation letter was refused by the mayor and council. He continues to attend council meetings by phone from his home. A Planning and Zoning Commission meeting that had been rescheduled for Monday, Nov. 10, has now been canceled. The request on the agenda was for permission to use the north side of the White Oak Station at 2587 N. Range Line Road as a bus stop. It has since been learned that the property has a new owner, which will require a new application. The original owner was Navroz Ali, of Overland Park, Kan. The new owner is Hisham Alqammaz. artigo.texto: American Tower eleva projeções de receita e AFFO para 2026 impulsionada pelo crescimento de data centers A American Tower elevou suas projeções para 2026 de receita imobiliária e AFFO por ação, impulsionada pelo forte desempenho em data centers, que compensou a pressão do churn da DISH e fraqueza nos serviços dos EUA. No terceiro trimestre, a receita imobiliária subiu 4,5% para US$ 2,73 bilhões e o AFFO por ação avançou 3,2% para US$ 2,87. A alavancagem encerrou em 4,9 vezes e a liquidez atingiu US$ 10,6 bilhões. Os riscos futuros incluem volatilidade cambial, taxas de juros, inflação e a dinâmica de crédito e consolidação dos clientes. American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT) elevou suas projeções para o ano todo de 2026 para a receita imobiliária e o AFFO por ação atribuível, após o crescimento no segmento de data centers ajudar a compensar a pressão contínua do cancelamento de contratos (churn) relacionado à DISH. A empresa manteve sua previsão para o EBITDA ajustado, com o desempenho superior dos data centers sendo equilibrado por uma atividade mais fraca no segmento de serviços nos EUA. No terceiro trimestre, a receita imobiliária aumentou 4,5% na comparação anual, para US$ 2,73 bilhões. O EBITDA ajustado subiu 0,9%, para US$ 1,83 bilhão, enquanto a margem EBITDA ajustada em caixa reduziu de 66,8% para 66,3%. O AFFO atribuível aos acionistas ordinários subiu 2,4%, para US$ 1,34 bilhão, e o AFFO atribuível por ação avançou 3,2%, para US$ 2,87. Em base neutra em termos cambiais (FX-neutral), a receita imobiliária cresceu 2,9%, o EBITDA ajustado recuou 0,5% e o AFFO atribuível por ação aumentou 1,4%. Excluindo os efeitos lineares líquidos (straight-line), o EBITDA ajustado em caixa e neutro em relação ao câmbio cresceu 2,3%. A apresentação também mostrou um crescimento de cerca de 5% em caixa e neutro em relação ao câmbio no EBITDA ajustado e no AFFO atribuível por ação quando o churn da DISH foi excluído. O lucro líquido GAAP caiu de US$ 913 milhões no mesmo trimestre do ano anterior para US$ 781 milhões. As despesas com juros aumentaram de US$ 347 milhões para US$ 366 milhões, enquanto as despesas com imposto de renda subiram de US$ 37 milhões para US$ 118 milhões. Data centers sustentam o crescimento enquanto o churn da DISH pesa sobre as torres O faturamento orgânico de inquilinos cresceu cerca de 4% excluindo a DISH, refletindo os investimentos contínuos nas redes 4G e 5G. Incluindo o churn relacionado à DISH, o crescimento do faturamento orgânico consolidado de inquilinos foi de 1,1%. O desempenho regional variou. O faturamento orgânico de inquilinos ficou estável nos EUA e no Canadá após remover as contribuições da DISH, enquanto África e Ásia-Pacífico cresceram 8,2% e a Europa avançou 4,2%. A América Latina registrou queda de 2,1%. A receita de data centers subiu 17,4%, passando de US$ 267 milhões para US$ 313 milhões, com um crescimento da receita em caixa de 16,3%. A American Tower informou que a demanda associada a casos de uso de nuvem híbrida e inteligência artificial sustentou a atividade em seus ativos de data center focados em interconexão. Projeções de receita e AFFO para o ano todo são elevadas A American Tower elevou o ponto médio de sua projeção de receita imobiliária para 2026 de US$ 10,77 bilhões para US$ 10,83 bilhões. O aumento de aproximadamente 1% reflete principalmente cerca de US$ 10 milhões decorrentes do desempenho superior dos data centers e US$ 45 milhões de outros itens, incluindo receitas repassadas (pass-through) e lineares (straight-line). O ponto médio atualizado sugere um crescimento da receita imobiliária de cerca de 5%, ou aproximadamente 4% excluindo os efeitos de taxa de câmbio e os efeitos lineares não caixa. A projeção continua assumindo um crescimento orgânico do faturamento de inquilinos de cerca de 1%, ou aproximadamente 4% excluindo o churn da DISH. O crescimento esperado para data centers é agora de cerca de 16%, aproximadamente 100 pontos-base acima do plano anterior. A empresa manteve o ponto médio do EBITDA ajustado em US$ 7,28 bilhões, o que representa um crescimento de aproximadamente 2% na comparação anual. Espera-se que cerca de US$ 10 milhões em desempenho superior dos data centers e US$ 5 milhões de outros itens sejam compensados por cerca de US$ 15 milhões a menos na contribuição dos serviços nos EUA. A faixa atual para o EBITDA ajustado é de US$ 7,25 bilhões a US$ 7,30 bilhões. A American Tower também elevou o ponto médio de sua projeção de AFFO atribuível por ação de US$ 11,08 para US$ 11,10, principalmente devido à recompra de ações. A faixa atual situa-se entre US$ 11,04 e US$ 11,16, com o ponto médio implicando um crescimento de cerca de 3%, ou aproximadamente 2% excluindo os efeitos cambiais e os custos de refinanciamento. A projeção para o AFFO por ação incorpora um impacto negativo (headwind) de aproximadamente 4% decorrente do churn da DISH, cerca de 3% de impostos em caixa e juros líquidos, e aproximadamente 1% de serviços. Capital permanece focado em mercados desenvolvidos A alavancagem líquida permaneceu em 4,9 vezes o EBITDA ajustado anualizado do último trimestre em 30 de setembro, sem alterações em relação a 30 de junho. A liquidez aumentou de US$ 9,9 bilhões para US$ 10,6 bilhões, enquanto a dívida a taxa fixa representou 94% do total de empréstimos, ante 93%. O prazo médio ponderado remanescente da dívida foi de 5,1 anos. O plano de capital da American Tower para 2026 inclui US$ 1,6 bilhão para projetos discricionários, US$ 200 milhões para despesas de capital (capex) não discricionárias e US$ 200 milhões para fusões e aquisições. Os data centers nos EUA representam 40% dos gastos com projetos discricionários, seguidos pela Europa com 25%, torres nos EUA e Canadá com 20% e mercados emergentes com 15%. artigo.texto: This New Study Shows If Data Centers Are Actually Creating New Jobs As more and more data centers pop up to accommodate increased AI use, there have been a lot of questions regarding who benefits from them. Though the facilities themselves don't employ many people once open, proponents claim that data centers can boost the local economy by creating lots of new jobs. A study from the MIT Center for Real Estate provides some useful insight, revealing that the truth is, unsurprisingly, more complicated. While it does link data centers to "a gradual increase in local employment following data center entry," the research shows that modest success doesn't transfer across the board. Before getting into the details, it's worth mentioning that this study was not peer reviewed and was published for "discussion and comment purposes." The researchers looked at 1,584 active data centers in the United States that opened and operated between 2000 and 2023 to examine their impact on things like employment and income in the surrounding area. Since counting data centers can be tricky, the study focused on those listed in the Aterio database with clear activation dates. The study found that, after a small increase in the first couple of years, job growth picks up a bit after approximately three to five years and ends up equaling around 2.74 jobs per megawatt of capacity. However, these jobs are primarily in the transportation/warehousing and professional/technical services industries, showing little impact on things like retail and restaurants. Given that the data ends in 2023, it doesn't account for massive investment in new data centers over the last couple of years. Still, it's a useful glimpse at the economic impact of data centers, which can help determine whether the benefits justify the costs. Data centers don't help local economies as promised While data centers are connected to some job creation, the MIT Center for Real Estate's study indicates that this isn't happening on a scale that could transform struggling communities. In fact, most would say their negative impacts outweigh the positives. There are common problems associated with living near a data center, including increased utility prices and pollution, which have an outsized impact on the rural areas where they tend to crop up. Data centers are power-intensive, requiring lots of electricity to power their supercomputers and clean water to cool equipment. That puts further strain on already stretched resources, having a frustrating impact on power bills that looks like it'll get worse as more data centers get built. Even if data centers do create jobs, their benefits seem minimal to nonexistent when weighed against the economic and environmental harm they cause, the burden of which falls on the average American rather than those running the data centers. That's why a lot of communities are fighting back against new data centers. According to Data Center Watch, pushback from local residents has blocked or delayed nearly $200 billion worth of data center projects in the first two quarters of 2026 alone, and that's led to increased scrutiny from politicians. The governors of New York and Texas have implemented moratoriums on new projects, joining local ones in places like Oklahoma City and Seattle in showing that opposition to data centers is one of the few things Americans across the political spectrum can agree on.

artigo.texto: A first of its kind for the region, the new battery energy storage system at Darwin’s Channel Island power station presented a unique engineering challenge. But it soon proved it could provide essential grid services traditionally supplied by a gas turbine. Soon after the Channel Island Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) was commissioned, an external network event caused two of the power station’s largest generators to trip offline. The event provided a significant real-world demonstration of the capability of the first grid-forming battery in the Darwin-Katherine Interconnected System (DKIS), the Northern Territory’s largest electricity network. The battery responded to the trip immediately, injecting power to stabilise it and prevent extended blackouts. “It responded exactly as it was expected to,” Boyd Hillebrand MIEAust CPEng, Principal Electrical Engineer at Territory Generation, explained. “In response to a major system event, the battery saved the day. So that was a very good test case.” This was a particularly important outcome as the DKIS is an island network, meaning it exists and operates independently of the national electricity grid. As an island network, the DKIS must maintain system stability without support from the national electricity grid. The BESS provides a new way of supporting essential grid services. Replicating essential grid services with batteries The Channel Island BESS project, delivered by Territory Generation in partnership with principal contractor Hitachi Energy, was awarded the Northern Project of the Year at the 2026 Engineers Australia Excellence Awards. Its main engineering objective was to provide essential grid services traditionally completed by an ageing industrial gas turbine. “The brief was to make this battery provide these essential grid services as well as, or better than, the existing gas turbine,” Boyd said. The project first required extensive modelling and tuning of the battery’s capabilities. Before construction began, a significant level of effort went into the modelling of the technology and into its responses to the constantly changing needs of the network. Working with Hitachi Energy, the project team used this modelling to inform how the BESS control system was configured. The control software allows the battery to function as a virtual synchronous machine, responding in a similar way to a traditional generator to help stabilise the network when conditions change. But the way it adds power to the network is of vital importance. Because they don’t have rotating parts, batteries don’t provide physical inertia. Instead, the virtual synchronous machine imitates the stabilising behaviour of a large, spinning generator. Engineers had to optimise this inertial response, enabling the battery – which is actually a collection of 192 individual battery racks – to inject power rapidly to correct the frequency. It had to respond rapidly enough to stabilise the system without creating instability in the other generators connected to the network. This required detailed power system modelling as part of the connection process to understand how the BESS would respond under different network conditions. That same modelling enabled engineers to analyse different operating scenarios and identify relevant control settings long before the battery was ever connected to the network. Getting those settings right was critical. “If the settings weren’t properly tuned, there was a risk of introducing instability into the network,” Hillebrand said. New technology, 40-year-old network While the modelling broke new ground, integrating the battery into a power station approaching 40 years old brought new challenges. Engineers had to repurpose an existing connection point, modifying a 132 kV switchyard and its electrical protection systems. The ageing infrastructure came with its own, unique problems. “With infrastructure that has been modified and upgraded over many years, it was important to verify the existing equipment and connections against the drawings,” Hillebrand said. The engineering team painstakingly verified existing equipment and connections, collaborating closely with the substation’s owner, Power and Water Corporation. “You really need to go through an as-building process to make sure everything functions the way that you expect it to,” he said. All of this happened within a live network, as the station continued to supply electricity to the Darwin-Katherine network. Modifying the battery connection point required temporarily disconnecting one of the station’s auxiliary power supplies, leaving just a single transformer operational. “We made sure that we had backups of backups for critical station power,” Hillebrand said. Lessons for the future Commissioning confirmed the accuracy of the modelling. The subsequent unexpected generator trip demonstrated the battery’s ability to stabilise the network in place of traditional gas-fired spinning reserve capacity. Beyond its considerable fuel savings – a primary driver for the battery technology – the battery now helps manage demand peaks by avoiding unnecessary turbine starts. Territory Generation is already applying the experience to future projects. “One of our biggest learnings was that the modelling time and effort is absolutely imperative. We are focusing on making sure that we’ve got the modelling side of things well understood.” Celebrate the outstanding projects driving the construction pipeline with the Engineers Australia Excellence Awards. artigo.texto: XPeng's IRON Robot Solid-State Battery Rolls Off in Small-Batch Production, Scale Manufacturing Targeted by Year-End On October 28, at the 2026 Embodied Intelligence Robot Conference and Embodied Intelligence Main Forum hosted by the China Society of Automotive Engineers, Gu Jie, vice president of XPeng Group, revealed that the solid-state battery used in its IRON robot has completed small-batch production and rolled off the line, and the overall robot project is in the sprint phase before SOP (standard operating procedure). Gu Jie made the remarks while speaking at the forum. SOP is typically seen as the key milestone marking a product's transition from engineering validation to volume manufacturing, and the statement signals that the IRON robot's core power component has already cleared the mass-production stage ahead of the rest. XPeng Robotics is regarded as one of the group's most important business segments outside of new energy vehicles, and its pace of progress has clearly accelerated recently. On September 22, XPeng Group held its first robot supply chain partner conference, drawing leading suppliers of core components including actuators, dexterous hands, sensors and AI chips. XPeng Robotics has completed supply chain factory audits and designated core components, further solidifying mass-production readiness. Under the established plan, the IRON robot will enter large-scale production by the end of 2026 and officially go on sale and begin deliveries in 2027. The solid-state battery is the core selling point that sets the IRON robot apart from similar products. XPeng Group announced at its 2025 Tech Day that its new-generation humanoid robot IRON would be the industry's first to use an all-solid-state battery. In February this year, the group disclosed related technical progress: all-weather road testing had concluded, the battery pack's volume utilization had risen to 78%, 23 percentage points higher than conventional liquid battery packs, while weight was reduced by 35%. On the battery self-development front, XPeng Group Chairman He Xiaopeng said in September that the group has invested in three battery cell companies and that all its batteries will be made in-house starting in 2026. This arrangement provides a common foundation for the power solutions of both the robot and vehicle businesses. In terms of application scenarios, the IRON robot is slated to enter XPeng stores and commercial settings worldwide starting in 2027, taking on service functions such as sales assistance and product presentations, forming a closed loop of "mass production—delivery—scenario deployment." In the secondary market, XPeng-W (09868.HK) rose HK$1.18 (approximately $0.15) that day, a gain of 3.347%. For XPeng Group, the significance of the solid-state battery's small-batch rollout extends beyond the robot itself. Humanoid robots have far higher requirements than passenger cars for battery energy density, safety and lightweighting. If this technology path is validated on robots, it could in the future feed back into the company's vehicle products. However, the journey from "small-batch rollout" to "large-scale production and delivery" still requires clearing two hurdles: yield ramp-up and cost control. Whether the end-2026 mass-production target can be met on schedule will be a key observation point for testing the company's execution.

artigo.texto: China's NIO taps EVE Energy, Gotion High-tech to make its in-house large cylindrical cells, with small-volume output due by year-end NIO's multi-year push into in-house batteries has finally produced tangible progress. According to Jipian Lab, the large cylindrical cells independently designed by NIO have been confirmed for contract manufacturing by EVE Energy (300014.SZ) and Gotion High-tech (002074.SZ), with small-volume output due by the end of the year. At the same time, NIO continues to use CATL (300750.SZ) batteries in models under its Firefly and Onvo brands, and cooperation between the two sides has not cooled despite the in-house push. The significance of this news goes beyond one automaker's supply chain choices. It means that after Geely, Li Auto and Leapmotor, another vehicle manufacturer has extended its reach into the core segment of power batteries, and the supplier-dominated structure of the power battery industry is gradually being pried open by automakers' own R&D. NIO did not start late on in-house cell development. The company launched the business in 2021, planned a battery plant with 100 GWh of annual capacity, and internally set a 2024 target for installing self-developed cells in vehicles in 2022. But buffeted by business volatility, the effort stalled for a time. The 46105 large cylindrical cell unveiled at NIO Day 2023, originally intended for the 120 kWh battery pack in the NIO ET9, ultimately did not materialize, and the production version of the ET9 switched to CATL cells. The turning point came in the second half of last year. As sales recovered and its financial position improved, NIO restarted the in-house battery business. In February this year, NIO Battery Technology (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. was established, deepening its R&D footprint. A NIO representative previously told media that the company is accelerating R&D on solid-state battery technology and expects to achieve large-scale application after 2027. For now, NIO's battery strategy works both ends: near-term deployment of large cylindrical cells and a medium- to long-term bet on solid-state batteries. Compared with Li Auto's approach, NIO is not yet able to significantly reduce its reliance on outside suppliers. Li Auto announced in September that within the year it will switch all models except the L9 to its own batteries, but the cells are developed by Li Auto itself and contract-manufactured by Sunwoda (300207.SZ) and CALB (3931.HK), and the company does not yet have cell production capacity of its own. Leapmotor, meanwhile, has already put its in-house cell line into production, with first-phase capacity sufficient to meet the needs of 500,000 to 600,000 vehicles. The only company that has truly achieved fully in-house battery development and production is BYD (002594.SZ), which built its business on batteries. Most automakers' in-house battery operations are still in their early stages, either lacking cell production capacity or unable to cover all model demand with their own batteries, ultimately still relying on suppliers as a backstop. For NIO, in-house batteries carry an additional test. As one of the few companies in the industry committed to battery swapping, NIO needs batteries from different suppliers, with varying capacities and specifications, to circulate efficiently through its swap network while balancing differences in performance and density. This year NIO also announced a partnership with Geely in charging and swapping, and how Geely-family swap-capable models will be integrated into NIO's swap network once launched will likewise test its operational capabilities. That means NIO is taking on more risk than brands without battery swapping. At the industry level, automakers' in-house batteries are unlikely to threaten battery suppliers' room to survive in the short term, but the bargaining landscape is already changing. With battery R&D and production capabilities in hand, automakers gain more initiative in negotiations with suppliers and find it easier to secure capacity when supply is tight. That in turn forces battery makers to speed up technology iteration and improve product competitiveness. Still, developing and producing power batteries in-house requires enormous investment, and without economies of scale it is hard to generate clear economic benefits, making it a burden for automakers instead. The more likely path for the industry is this: a handful of automakers that have already achieved results will continue in-house development, while more companies fall back to a model of jointly defining products with suppliers, with automakers leading product definition and deeply participating in battery pack and cell design while core technology still comes from battery suppliers. Worth noting is that as NIO advances in-house batteries, the downstream race to build charging infrastructure for power batteries is also heating up. BYD, Geely, Chery and Li Auto have successively announced plans to build megawatt-level fast-charging stations, and battery maker Sunwoda has also proposed building 10,000 megawatt-level fast-charging stations by the end of 2027 together with industrial capital, automakers and charging operators. Vehicle-side charging rates have been pushed from 5C to 10C, 12C and even 15C, while charging piles remain mostly below 250 kW. Data from the China Charging Alliance shows that as of August 2026, charging piles below 120 kW accounted for 67.8% and those between 120 and 250 kW for 22.5%, with the two combined making up more than 90%. The gap between vehicle-side capability and charging infrastructure means large-scale application of ultra-fast charging will still take time. For NIO, whether its in-house cells can be smoothly integrated into the swap system and keep the network efficient and safe across batteries from different suppliers will be a harder challenge than building a set of reliable cells.
