artigo.texto: Strengthening the Foundation for Mass Production: Lead Intelligent’s Warm Isostatic Pressing Machine Accelerates Solid-State Battery Industrialization By PR Newswire WUXI, China, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Solid-state batteries are at a critical stage of transition from pilot production to large-scale manufacturing. To address key challenges in densification and solid-solid interface contact, Lead Intelligent has developed a horizontal warm isostatic pressing machine that delivers uniform three-dimensional pressure of up to 600 MPa across a wide temperature range from room temperature (RT) to 150°C. The machine achieves temperature control accuracy of ±2°C and pressure control accuracy of ±2%. Integrating automatic loading and unloading with precise, coordinated temperature and pressure control, the machine can increase cell density to over 95%, accelerating the industrialization of solid-state batteries. As solid-state batteries move toward mass production, two major challenges remain: high impedance caused by insufficient solid-solid interface contact, and the limitations of conventional unidirectional pressing, including uneven density and pronounced edge effects. Based on Pascal’s principle, isostatic pressing applies isotropic pressurization within a sealed chamber to achieve multidimensional material compaction and densification. It is a key processing route for addressing solid-solid interface contact challenges in solid-state batteries. For the practical requirements of large-scale solid-state battery manufacturing, warm isostatic pressing offers an effective balance between densification performance, production efficiency, and manufacturing cost, making it a highly cost-effective option for mass production. As construction of solid-state battery capacity accelerates, warm isostatic pressing machines are becoming core incremental machines for battery manufacturers’ next-generation solid-state production lines. Core Technology: Precise Temperature-Pressure Coordination for High-Precision Process Control Building on its R&D system, Lead Intelligent’s horizontal warm isostatic pressing machine overcomes the “black box” limitations of traditional warm isostatic pressing process by enabling real-time monitoring of temperature and pressure inside the chamber. The machine upgrades from conventional unidirectional pressing to precise temperature-pressure coordination to promote closer contact between electrodes and electrolytes, making it well suited for solid-state battery mass production. - Pressure system: It delivers uniform three-dimensional pressure of up to 600 MPa, with pressure control accuracy ≤±2%. Automatic pressure compensation and emergency depressurization functions keep pressure fluctuations within ±2% during a 30-minute pressure holding period, ensuring process stability and repeatability. - Temperature system: The working temperatures can reach up to 150°C, and can be adjusted within a wide operating range from room temperature (RT) to 150°C, with temperature control accuracy of ±2°C. The initial heating time to 150°C takes no more than three hours, balancing process adaptability with mass production cycle-time requirements. - Chamber specifications: The working chamber inner diameter is ≥400 mm, the effective length is ≥4,000 mm, and the volume is around 500 L. It accommodates batch processing of workpieces in various sizes and meets the capacity requirements of GWh-scale production lines. Designed for Mass Production: Comprehensive Optimization for Large-Scale Manufacturing For GWh-scale manufacturing, warm isostatic pressing machines must do more than meet core process specifications. They shall also coordinate with whole line cycle time, logistics systems, and upstream and downstream processes. To meet these requirements, Lead Intelligent has optimized machine structure, automatic operation, and safety systems in parallel. Horizontal Design for Continuous Production Lines The horizontal working chamber and automatic loading and unloading design significantly reduce factory height requirements while seamlessly integrating with automatic logistics systems to meet the needs of continuous production and material transfer between upstream and downstream processes, adapting to takt-based operation on large-scale production lines. Electrodes and solid electrolytes can be stacked and assembled before being loaded into the chamber for pressing and densification, simplifying process flow. Full-process Automation to Minimize Manual Intervention The machine enables unmanned operation throughout cell pretreatment and material box circulation. It integrates four key functions: cell hot air preheating, cold air drying and cooling, automatic fixture loading and unloading, and material box automatic circulation. The machine covers the entire workflow including loading, pretreatment, isostatic pressing and unloading, minimizing manual intervention and improving production efficiency and process consistency within each batch. At the foundational level, the machine is equipped with dual pressure and temperature monitoring for the chamber, together with pipeline pressure-relief ports to safeguard machine operation. artigo.texto: A Rivian owner facing repeated outages in Santa Barbara, California, is considering using the truck as a backup power source instead of paying for a conventional home battery install. After getting storage quotes above $20,000, they asked other electric vehicle owners whether a Rivian could handle a small set of essentials when the power cuts out. Here's what to know On Reddit, the owner wrote that their "power goes out several times a year" and said solar battery quotes "keep coming in over $20k." Because the need was limited to one built-in fridge, some lights, and a few small appliances, a cheaper backup option for essentials rather than a whole-home system was seen as the best option. Commenters outlined a range of ways to do that, from simple extension-cord use to generator interlocks, manual transfer switches, and portable batteries that sit between the truck and the home's circuits. One commenter said, "The Rivian inverter has a max of 1500 W," adding that they had relied on extension cords for a freezer and refrigerator during outages. For households dealing with repeated blackouts, adding battery storage is one of the most effective ways to protect a home during outages, lower energy costs, and gain more energy independence. Homeowners comparing options can explore EnergySage for home battery storage choices and competitive installation estimates, and EnergySage has teamed up with electrification brand Qmerit to help homeowners get the best price on home battery storage solutions. More background Cost was a major theme in the thread, especially the difference between installed whole-home battery systems and pieced-together alternatives. The original poster said they had started "to give up" on waiting for bidirectional charging and had seen estimates suggesting a future charger setup could cost about $8,000, which still felt expensive compared with a large portable power bank. A number of replies focused on using a power station as the go-between for the truck and the house. In that setup, the Rivian charges the portable battery, which then feeds a home through a transfer switch or inlet. One commenter said a setup like that can work if household use stays under roughly 1,200 watts while the Rivian charges the buffer battery at about 1,400 watts. The same commenter said they use load shedding for server and network equipment, which "saves me 7kwh a day if i do that." What can be done? Even without official vehicle-to-home capability, some Rivian owners said they have already assembled outage backups around their trucks. That kind of workaround can provide basic backup without the cost of a five-figure installation. It can keep food cold, lights on, and critical devices running while reducing dependence on the grid. The original poster indicated in the thread that they were going to go with the Pecron F5000 system after getting a recommendation from a thread visitor. For readers who want something smaller and less expensive than a whole-home system, Pila is another company offering strong battery backup options. Pila's plug-and-play batteries are priced at a fraction of what a whole-home backup system would cost, which aligns with the thread's focus on lower-cost resilience. Where can I learn more? How to keep essentials powered during an outage is a common topic of discussion. • During an outage, EVs kept the grid operating and proved emergency backup can scale. • GM's push to power homes in blackouts has run into steep install-cost concerns. • More homeowners are installing backup batteries without paying upfront costs through financing. artigo.texto: Delectrik Wins 120 MWh Flow Battery Project in Gujarat ⚡ Quick Read - What happened: Gurugram-based Delectrik Systems secured a 120 MWh utility-scale vanadium flow battery project in Gujarat via a GIPCL tender with Bondada Engineering, while Amazon and Tata Motors partnered to deploy 3,000 e-trucks across India. - Why it matters: These developments signal significant scaling of advanced energy storage systems and medium-to-heavy commercial vehicle electrification for Indian EPCs and developers. - Watch: Execution milestones for the GIPCL and NTPC flow battery projects, alongside the rollout pace of Tata’s electric trucks across national freight corridors. Background and Context India’s fast-evolving energy landscape is witnessing a convergence of grid-scale storage advancements and commercial fleet electrification. As renewable energy penetration deepens across the country, grid operators and developers are increasingly looking at diverse battery energy storage system (BESS) technologies to manage intermittency. Simultaneously, the logistics and e-commerce sectors are scaling up zero-emission transportation to cut emissions beyond last-mile deliveries. Recent industry updates highlight major strides in vanadium flow battery deployments, large-scale electric truck deployments, and emerging grid infrastructure pressures driven by the EV charging boom. Key Details Gurugram-based Delectrik Systems Private Limited has won a major utility-scale flow battery project with a capacity of 120 MWh in Gujarat. The contract was awarded in the latest round of the BESS tender issued by Gujarat Industries Power Company Limited (GIPCL), with Bondada Engineering Limited participating as an associate. This marks Delectrik’s second utility-scale project for the year, following its ongoing 100 MWh flow battery project for NTPC Renewable Energy Limited. In the e-mobility space, Amazon and Tata Motors have joined forces to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon’s Indian transportation network, extending fleet electrification into inter-city freight corridors. Furthermore, global developments such as CATL’s launch of the 9 MWh TENER+ energy storage system and TENER Sodium system in Australia offer engineering lessons for high-density storage solutions, while a GlobalData report underscores the growing grid pressures caused by public DC fast-charging hubs. What This Means for EPCs and Developers For EPC contractors and renewable energy developers in India, the deployment of alternative storage chemistries like vanadium flow batteries opens up robust engineering, procurement, and construction opportunities outside standard lithium-ion applications. Flow batteries offer distinct advantages for long-duration energy storage (LDES), making them critical assets for upcoming utility-scale tenders. Meanwhile, the aggressive scaling of heavy-duty electric commercial vehicles by corporate giants like Amazon and Tata Motors highlights the need for robust commercial charging infrastructure, presenting lucrative execution avenues for infrastructure developers. What Happens Next Industry stakeholders will closely monitor the execution of Delectrik’s 120 MWh GIPCL project alongside its ongoing NTPC assignment. Additionally, power planners will need to address the rising grid pressures highlighted by rapid DC fast-charger adoption by implementing advanced demand-side management and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) frameworks. As India’s renewable energy sector continues to expand rapidly, the integration of innovative storage technologies and large-scale e-mobility infrastructure remains pivotal to grid stability and clean energy transition goals.

artigo.texto: Insight and analysis on the data center space from industry thought leaders. Rethinking the Blind-Mate Connection PBMC technology helps liquid-cooled servers deliver higher flow in less space while better accommodating alignment variation during installation and service. Much of the conversation around liquid cooling focuses on the system itself. However, higher cooling demands are also changing expectations for the individual components within it. One such component is the connection point between IT equipment and the cooling infrastructure. For server and rack designers, that connection now must do more than simply link two sides of a liquid loop. It must support greater coolant flow, fit within increasingly constrained server-tray space, and accommodate alignment variations that come with real-world installation and removal. Those requirements have helped drive the development of a newer approach to the traditional blind-mate connection: the pivoting blind-mate coupling (PBMC). PBMC technology was developed through collaboration within the Open Compute Project ecosystem and reflects a broader industry effort to address the changing needs of high-performance liquid-cooled systems. Parker Hannifin’s BQC Series is one example of this newer coupling architecture. Why the Connection Needed to Change The development of the PBMC started with a practical set of system-level requirements. Newer rack and server architectures called for greater flow through the connection while reducing the space the coupling occupied in the server tray. The connection also needed more self-alignment capability between the two sides as equipment was inserted and removed. Solving one of those problems can make another more difficult. Increasing flow can push designers toward larger flow paths. Server designers, meanwhile, are trying to preserve as much usable tray space as possible. And because a blind-mate connection is made during installation rather than being manually aligned by a technician, the coupling must also account for the possibility that the plug and socket may not align perfectly every time. PBMC technology was developed to address those requirements as part of the same connection design. Accounting for Real-World Misalignment Blind-mate couplings already solve an important problem in liquid-cooled server systems: they allow a connection to be made as equipment is installed from the front (cold-aisle) side of the system. That matters for more than convenience. The rear (hot-aisle) side of a server rack can contain manifolds, connections, and other equipment operating in a high-temperature environment. Installation and removal from the cold aisle can reduce the need for personnel to reach into the hot aisle to handle connections at the rear of the rack. The tradeoff is that a blind-mate connection does not have a technician guiding the two coupling halves together. Server trays, racks, and manifolds are also not always positioned with perfect precision. Small differences in component location can add up by the time the two sides of the connection meet. A pivoting blind-mate design provides more self-alignment capability as the two sides of the connection come together. Rather than depending as heavily on near-perfect alignment between the two halves, the connection can accommodate a greater degree of positional variation during mating. For system designers, that can reduce the sensitivity of the connection to the normal dimensional variation present throughout the surrounding equipment. That does not mean PBMCs replace every traditional blind-mate connection. They are particularly relevant in server-tray and blade-system applications where self-alignment capability, higher flow, and limited available space all have to be considered together. More Flow Without Giving Up Server-Tray Space Flow performance was another major factor behind the PBMC’s development. As cooling requirements increase, the connection cannot become an unnecessary restriction within the loop. It needs to support the required coolant flow while keeping pressure losses through the connection under control. Simply making every component larger, however, is not an ideal answer. Space inside the server tray is limited, and cooling hardware competes for room with the computing equipment it is meant to support. The length and overall footprint of the coupling therefore become part of the system-design conversation. PBMC designs address that challenge by combining a larger flow path with a compact overall package. The objective is straightforward: support higher flow without requiring designers to give more of the tray to the connection itself. Designing for High-Flow Conditions Higher flow also creates challenges less visible than the connection size. One is seal retention. O-rings and other seals must remain securely positioned as fluid travels through the connection. Under demanding flow and pressure conditions, a poorly retained seal can be pulled from its groove and carried downstream with the system fluid. This condition, often referred to as seal washout, can compromise the connection and create problems elsewhere in the cooling loop. For that reason, seal retention becomes an important design consideration as coupling flow requirements increase. Retention features can help keep seals properly positioned under demanding operating conditions rather than treating them as an afterthought to flow performance. Part of a Broader Shift in Liquid-Cooling Design The value of PBMC technology is not tied to any one feature. Its development reflects how closely connected the requirements within modern liquid-cooling systems have become. Flow affects component size. Component size affects available tray space. Blind mating affects alignment requirements. Higher flow introduces its own mechanical considerations. artigo.texto: Segundo o Departamento Provincial de Proteção Florestal de Quang Ngai , a província possui atualmente cerca de 826.000 hectares de floresta. Especialistas estimam que a área florestal da província absorve e armazena cerca de 2 milhões de toneladas de carbono anualmente, o equivalente a aproximadamente 2 milhões de créditos de carbono. Quang Ngai se prepara para entrar no mercado de créditos de carbono. Com sua vasta área florestal e alta taxa de cobertura florestal, a província de Quang Ngai está implementando soluções abrangentes para o manejo e proteção florestal sustentável e se preparando para participar do mercado de créditos de carbono. No âmbito do Programa de Redução de Emissões para as regiões Centro-Sul e Planalto Central, sob a iniciativa LEAF, prevê-se que Quang Ngai receba aproximadamente 1,13 milhão de créditos de carbono. Além de se preparar para explorar a receita proveniente do carbono florestal, a província está implementando efetivamente a política de pagamento por serviços ambientais florestais. Até o final de outubro de 2026, mais de 400 bilhões de VND haviam sido pagos a proprietários de florestas, comunidades e famílias. Segundo o Sr. Nguyen Van Nam, chefe do Departamento de Proteção Florestal da província de Quang Ngai, para explorar o valor econômico do carbono florestal, é necessário completar o arcabouço legal, coletar dados, desenvolver projetos e mobilizar recursos. Este processo deve cumprir integralmente as etapas de registro, medição, avaliação, verificação, emissão e comercialização de créditos de carbono, garantindo a distribuição dos benefícios conforme estipulado. Quando os requisitos técnicos e legais forem atendidos, a receita proveniente dos créditos de carbono proporcionará financiamento adicional para a proteção e o desenvolvimento florestal, incentivando os proprietários florestais e as comunidades locais a manterem um compromisso de longo prazo com a floresta. Para aumentar o valor dos recursos florestais, a província de Quang Ngai está se concentrando em concluir o banco de dados e realizar o inventário florestal. O Departamento Provincial de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente está conduzindo com urgência o inventário e os levantamentos florestais, conforme diretrizes do Ministério da Agricultura e Meio Ambiente e do Comitê Popular Provincial, com previsão de divulgação dos resultados em 2027. A província também está colaborando com o Instituto de Ciências Florestais do Vietnã para desenvolver projetos-piloto de carbono florestal como base para uma implementação mais ampla. Segundo o Sr. Do Tam Hien, Vice-Presidente do Comitê Popular da Província de Quang Ngai, o desenvolvimento de créditos de carbono florestal contribui para alcançar as metas de crescimento verde, reduzir as emissões de gases de efeito estufa e aumentar o valor econômico das florestas. Uma vez que os projetos sejam reconhecidos com créditos de carbono, a receita proveniente do carbono pode complementar o financiamento para a proteção e o desenvolvimento florestal, criando um incentivo para que os proprietários florestais e as populações locais mantenham o compromisso com a silvicultura a longo prazo.

artigo.texto: Monsson announces the launch of Eskilstuna Power Reserve, its first investment in a battery energy storage facility in Sweden. The project includes a battery energy storage system (BESS) with a capacity of 60 MWh and a power rating of 30 MW, designed for a two-hour discharge duration. Commissioning activities began in September 2026, with commercial operation scheduled for November 2026. Eskilstuna Power Reserve is designed to provide flexibility in power system operation and contribute to grid stability in Sweden’s SE3 bidding zone. The system can switch between charging and discharging in less than three seconds, enabling a rapid response to variations in electricity generation and consumption. The project uses Monsson’s proprietary technology and reflects the company’s experience in developing, engineering and deploying utility-scale energy storage facilities. Its implementation marks the expansion of Monsson’s presence in the Nordic market and the growth of its energy storage activities. “Eskilstuna Power Reserve represents an important step in Monsson’s expansion into the Nordic market. Through this 30 MW / 60 MWh project, we are bringing our energy storage technology and expertise to Sweden, with the aim of contributing to grid flexibility and stability. Commissioning activities are finished, and commercial operation is scheduled for November 2026. Our team in Sweden, together with our colleagues in Romania, is ready to provide these flexibility services both locally and across Europe,” said Sebastian Enache, Head of Strategy & M&A at Monsson. At the launch event on 22 October, held in Eskilstuna under the theme “Storing Energy, Powering Generations”, the attendees included representatives of Sweden’s energy industry, grid operators, authorities and the business community. The programme featured presentations on the project’s technology and business model, discussions with the Monsson team and guided tours of the facility ahead of commercial operation. “By developing Eskilstuna Power Reserve, Monsson is expanding its portfolio of storage solutions designed to support energy systems with a growing share of renewable generation in Europe. The project provides a foundation for the company’s continued development in the Nordic region, where flexibility and efficient energy management are important components of energy infrastructure,” said Joanna Lillequist, CEO of Monsson Energy AB. Daniel Ioniță, Ambassador of Romania to Sweden, said: “This facility is Romanian expertise at work in Sweden: designed, built and operated by Romanian professionals, with technology developed at home and applied here. With over 95% of its components manufactured in EU member states, it is also a good example of how European strategic autonomy is built in practice. It strengthens Sweden’s energy transition and the security of the regional power system, and it shows that Romania is competitive on the European energy market.” “Eskilstuna has long been a city with an ambitious energy agenda, with goals to become truly fossil-free and climate positive by 2045. This important investment provides a new capability for Eskilstuna and Strängnäs. Batteries can provide multiple benefits for the national and local grid, and we see this as the beginning of a long-term partnership. At ESEM, we are eager to innovate together to realise the potential, for example through our new local flexibility market. We are excited and glad that a project of this kind has found its place here,” said Daniel Lindekrans Henriksson, Energy Strategist, Eskilstuna Municipality.

artigo.texto: Sungrow has announced plans to partner with ENGIE and Elecnor to advance the 150MW/300MWh Hazelwood battery energy storage system (BESS) located in Victoria, Australia. Sungrow Australia, a Sungrow subsidiary, will provide the technology, while Elecnor will act as the balance-of-plant (BOP) contractor. Discover B2B Marketing That Performs Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms. The BESS is set to enter commercial operations in 2028. The project plans to use 66 units of Sungrow’s ST5015-UX BESS from its PowerTitan 2.0 series. It will also use 33 SC6900UD-MV power conversion system (PCS) inverters and the company’s EMS3000 smart controller. The new system is designed for utility-scale deployment and will offer high energy density, liquid-cooled thermal management, advanced battery monitoring, and power conversion features to support long-term reliability and safety. Hazelwood BESS 2 will use grid-forming technology designed to help maintain voltage and frequency stability and respond quickly to changes in network conditions. The project partners also expect these capabilities to support the integration of variable renewable generation as its share of electricity supply increases. The system aims to provide flexible energy resources for Victoria and the National Electricity Market (NEM) by storing electricity during periods of low demand and delivering it when needed. Hazelwood BESS 2 represents further development in large-scale battery storage initiatives in Australia, highlighting the involvement of international suppliers such as Sungrow in the country’s move towards an evolving energy system. Sungrow Australia managing director Thomas Hou said: “The Hazelwood BESS 2 represents an important step in advancing grid-forming energy storage in Australia. “Through our collaboration with ENGIE, we aim to bring advanced energy storage technology to support grid stability and enable greater integration of renewable energy. “We look forward to contributing our expertise and supporting the continued development of a more resilient energy system in Victoria.” In August 2026, Sungrow was chosen by Verano Energy to supply a 152MW/606MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) for the Observatorio project in Chile.

artigo.texto: Resumo - Aneel aprovou na terça o edital do primeiro leilão de baterias do Brasil - Garantias de proposta e fiel cumprimento recuaram quase 40% - Investimento de referência caiu de R$ 9,8 mi para R$ 6 mi por MW - Certame atraiu cadastro recorde de mais de 296 GW de empreendimentos - Disputas marcadas para 2 e 4 de dezembro com preços-teto distintos - Base pagante virou 'usuários de reserva de capacidade' no texto A Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) aprovou, na terça-feira, o edital do primeiro leilão de baterias do Brasil. Na versão final, a agência incluiu mudanças para ampliar a concorrência entre as empresas e ajustou as regras sobre os custos dos contratos. Entre as principais alterações, a Aneel reduziu em cerca de 40% as garantias de proposta e de fiel cumprimento. Além disso, a agência diminuiu o investimento de referência das baterias de R$ 9,8 milhões para R$ 6 milhões por megawatt (MW). Outra mudança importante envolve a participação das empresas. A partir de agora, companhias do mesmo grupo econômico poderão formar consórcios, uma demanda recorrente do setor. O leilão também representa um avanço para a segurança energética do país, especialmente diante do crescimento das fontes renováveis. Nesse cenário, a disputa já desperta o interesse de investidores e fabricantes nacionais e estrangeiros. Cadastro recorde e barreira a ‘aventureiros’ Segundo a Aneel, o leilão atraiu um volume recorde de projetos cadastrados, que ultrapassa 296 gigawatts (GW). Com as novas regras, a expectativa é ampliar ainda mais a concorrência entre os participantes. Apesar das flexibilizações, a agência manteve exigências para avaliar a capacidade financeira das empresas. O objetivo é evitar a participação de investidores sem condições de cumprir os contratos. No caso de consórcios formados por companhias do mesmo grupo econômico, apenas a controladora precisará comprovar o patrimônio líquido mínimo. Dessa forma, a Aneel busca evitar a dupla contagem de patrimônio, problema identificado no leilão de térmicas realizado em março. Além disso, o edital estabelece regras específicas para projetos ligados a fundos de investimento em participações (FIP). Nesses casos, as empresas deverão identificar os cotistas com participação indireta superior a 5%. Segundo a agência, a medida busca identificar os investidores com exposição econômica relevante nos projetos vencedores. Preços-teto e datas das disputas A Aneel também definiu os preços máximos para as duas disputas previstas em dezembro. No primeiro leilão, marcado para 2 de dezembro, o preço-teto será de R$ 1,76 milhão por MW ao ano. Nesse caso, as empresas deverão cumprir exigências de conteúdo nacional. Já o segundo certame ocorrerá em 4 de dezembro, sem a obrigação de nacionalização. Por isso, o preço máximo será menor, de R$ 1,58 milhão por MW ao ano. Quem paga a conta ainda divide o setor Apesar dos avanços no edital, a divisão dos custos do leilão continua entre os principais pontos de discussão no setor elétrico. A questão, inclusive, pode acabar na Justiça. Para tentar reduzir as divergências, a Aneel retirou do documento as referências diretas aos geradores de energia como responsáveis pelos pagamentos. Em substituição, a agência adotou o termo “usuários de reserva de capacidade”. No entanto, a mudança de redação não altera as regras atuais. Segundo a Aneel, os geradores continuam responsáveis pelos custos, conforme determina a legislação. Enquanto isso, representantes do setor buscam apoio no Congresso para modificar a lei antes dos leilões de dezembro. A proposta pretende mudar a responsabilidade pelo pagamento das baterias destinadas ao sistema elétrico. Caso o Congresso aprove a alteração, a Aneel terá de reavaliar os efeitos da nova legislação sobre os contratos, conforme explicou Gentil Nogueira, relator do processo. Na véspera da aprovação do edital, Nogueira reconheceu o interesse do setor em modificar a legislação. Entretanto, ressaltou que qualquer mudança exigirá uma nova discussão na agência. “É lógico, há o interesse legítimo na modificação legislativa, a gente compreende essa posição. Mas de qualquer forma, havendo a modificação legislativa, qualquer texto que fosse colocado traria invariavelmente a discussão para a Aneel sobre os efeitos sobre esse contrato”, afirmou.

artigo.texto: ANEEL has approved the final rules for Brazil’s large-scale battery storage auctions EPE registered 6,091 projects with close to 300 GW capacity across the two auctions in August 2026 Winning projects will secure 15-year contracts starting from August 2028 Brazil’s energy regulator, the National Electric Energy Agency (ANEEL), has approved the final rules for the country’s first large-scale battery energy storage auctions scheduled to be held on December 2 and 4, 2026. The auctions will procure power availability from standalone battery energy storage systems (BESS) with contracts starting from August 1, 2028, and running for 15 years. The first auction, under Tender Notice No. 05/2026, requires equipment to meet domestic content criteria and minimum technical requirements dubbed National Storage category. Tender Notice No. 06/2026, under the Storage category, covers eligible projects for the second auction without the same domestic content requirement. Successful projects must be able to deliver their contracted maximum power for four hours/cycle, for up to two cycles a day, and a maximum of 366 cycles a year. The systems must also be capable of recharging fully within six hours. Both the auctions will contract power availability in MWs. Payments will be based on fixed annual revenue, paid in 12 monthly installments. The amount may be reduced depending on operational performance. ANEEL has also lowered the reference investment cost used to calculate financial guarantees, from BRL 9.8 million/MW to BRL 6 million/MW. The agency said this would reduce entry barriers and encourage competition. These plans follow the Ministry of Mines and Energy launching a public consultation for the auctions as part of the 2026 Reserve Capacity Auction (LRCAP)—Storage in November 2025 as part of Brazil’s efforts to secure grid stability and affordable tariffs (see Brazil Announces Country’s Maiden Battery Storage Systems Auction). In August 2026, the Energy Research Office (EPE) completed the registration process for projects interested in participating in the LRCAP auctions. It registered a total of 6,091 projects representing 296.8 GW of power capacity. Brazil’s solar energy association, ABSOLAR, has reportedly proposed a storage target of at least 8 GW by 2030 to be able to take advantage of renewable energy expansion and prepare the grid for the energy transition.

artigo.texto: Mercedes-Benz's decision to develop its own batteries in-house is already paying big dividends, after the German brand announced that it has developed a pioneering new battery chemistry that will herald cheaper, faster-to-charge batteries that offer 30 per cent more range. Joining the ranks of Tesla, Volkswagen, Ford and Toyota, as well as leading EV giant BYD, Mercedes only opened its substantial eCampus back in 2024 and it was scientists working at the new R&D hub who were behind the new manganese-rich battery tech. No timescale was revealed for when the new Lithium-Manganese-Oxide battery (LMO) or the even more energy-packed Lithium-Nickel-Manganese-Oxide (LNMO) unitwill be rolled out, but the new lithium iron phosphate (LFP)-replacing tech is expected to be introduced within the next two years, ahead of Benz's own solid-state batteries that will launch towards the end of this decade. Read more - 'We won't be left wanting': Solid-state battery-powered cars with a potential 1500km of range likely for Australia - Major battery breakthrough confirmed - The Australian electric car battery breakthrough: Aussie smarts commercialise new battery that could result in a big change for the EVs we drive such as the Tesla Model Y, BYD Seal and more New batteries are greener and more sustainable The new batteries were unwrapped at the premium German brand's 140 Years of Innovation celebrations, where Mercedes scientists said that as well as being superior to the current LFP batteries available in cars like the new Mercedes CLA, its new LMO/LNMO pave the way for a greener, more sustainable future. That's because the manganese-rich chemistries are less reliant on cobalt, with the LNMO completely free of the in-demand element. Cobalt remains problematic for the car industry, with more than three-quarters of it sourced from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) from mines that are known to use unsafe working conditions and environmentally damaging extraction practices. The challenge for Benz, explained the scientists and battery engineers, was to attempt to replicate the same high energy density of its current LFP battery technology without cobalt. New batteries to beat BYD's LFP cells First to launch in the "near future" is the LMO tech, which blends its chemistry with Nickel-Manganese-Cobalt (NMC) oxide to maintain its energy density, but the big gains will come later with the completely cobalt-free LNMO tech, which costs less to produce than equivalent LFP cells. Crucially, when scaled up to the same size and weight of the equivalent LFP batteries, which have been popularised by BYD, the new tech offers far faster charging and, at least 30 per cent more range. Capable of working with far higher voltages, the new LMO batteries are also said to be safer than existing cells. Mercedes engineers wouldn't be drawn on figures, but if applied to the current 58kWh LFP battery that powers the Mercedes CLA, the new battery will raise the range of the base model from 447km to more than 580km with higher charging rates, potentially above 400kW (+200kW) for a sub-10-minute 10 to 80 per cent top-up. The same power packs are also tolerant of fast DC charging, retaining as much as 80 per cent of their original capacity after more than 1500 charge cycles, in research carried out on non-Benz batteries. Full technical details have not been revealed on either the LMO or LNMO batteries, nor exact timings of when they will be rolled out, but it's thought both will be replacements for the current LFP chemistry, rather than the brand's flagship NMC cells. The latter will then be superseded by the firm's most advanced solid-state batteries that are currently being developed in partnership with US-based Factorial and Taiwan's ProLogium for an introduction around 2029. When questioned by CarsGuide, Mercedes insiders said if the German brand was beaten to market in the race to introduce solid-state batteries, or other more advanced chemistries, by the likes of China's CATL it would favour the off-the-shelf solution, so long as it offered the "best price for the customer". Originally, many analysts had written off LMO and LNMO batteries as 'transitional chemistries' but, the prolonged delay in introducing solid-state and the high costs and ethical issues concerning sourcing cobalt have now seen CATL and Japan's Toyota also investing heavily in manganese-rich alternatives that will rival Benz's tech. Opened back in 2024 as part of a €14 billion ($A22b) investment in R&D, the new eCampus is a 10,000-square-metre facility that consists of three labs that are designed to fast-track new battery innovation with the ultimate aim of slashing the cost of a high-voltage battery by 30 per cent in the near future. The facility, located within Benz's Stuttgart R&D hub, is one giant building that enables scientists to develop the chemistry, build prototype cells to torture-test, and then evolve the concept, before scaling it up for full mass production.

artigo.texto: A Portaria nº 3.199, divulgada nesta quinta-feira (29/10) pelo Ministério da Fazenda, estabelece o calendário de implementação do MRV de gases de efeito estufa no Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE). A norma escalona a adesão dos segmentos regulados até 2031 e começa a exigir medição anual de carbono equivalente das grandes empresas. O dever de MRV alcança operadores cujas emissões somem 10 mil tCO2e anuais ou mais. Após 2030, empresas com volume superior a 25 mil tCO2e precisarão cumprir as exigências do Plano Nacional de Alocação. O marco legal do SBCE é a Lei 15.042/2024. O ingresso dos segmentos ocorrerá em três fases. Em 2027, a etapa inicial abrange alumínio, cimento, vidro, papel e celulose, siderurgia integrada, extração de bauxita e de minério de ferro, química e petróleo e gás natural. Até 2029, entram cerâmica, bebidas e alimentos, mineração de outras substâncias, siderurgia semi-integrada, ramos químicos adicionais, eletricidade e refino de petróleo. Até 2031, a vez é dos transportes ferroviário, aquaviário e rodoviário. Cada fase terá quatro anos de preparação: no primeiro, elabora-se o plano de monitoramento; nos dois seguintes, as emissões são acompanhadas; no último, os dados são reunidos para o Plano Nacional de Alocação. Nesta etapa inicial, não há exigência de relatórios imediatos, teto de emissões nem despesas. Segundo a Fazenda, o limite global e a distribuição de Cotas Brasileiras de Emissões serão definidos no Plano Nacional de Alocação, valendo desde 2030 e com 100% de gratuidade no início. Para 2026, a pasta planeja criar a Câmara de Assuntos Regulatórios com os setores da primeira fase e promover consultas sobre as regras dos programas de MRV e de compensação de emissões. No começo de 2027, o governo prevê treinamentos setoriais.

artigo.texto: At 7x24 Exchange, AI Data Center Growth Confronts New Realities of Power, Grid Reliability and Community Trust SAN ANTONIO, Texas — The data center industry's accelerating transition toward artificial intelligence is challenging some of its longest-standing assumptions about infrastructure design, operational reliability and relationships with the outside world. That was the overriding message Monday, October 26, as the 7x24 Exchange Fall 2026 Conference opened its technical program in San Antonio under the theme The Intersection of AI & Traditional Data Centers. Across a series of presentations spanning agentic AI, power system engineering, grid reliability and community engagement, speakers described an industry confronting challenges that extend well beyond higher rack densities and greater demand for electricity. AI workloads are changing how power must be delivered and managed. Large data center campuses are becoming consequential participants in grid operations rather than simply customers of electric utilities. And developers are finding that technical and economic arguments alone may no longer be enough to secure acceptance in communities where they intend to build. Opening the proceedings, 7x24 Exchange Chairman Bob Cassiliano identified community opposition as a challenge that has overtaken several of the industry's other longstanding concerns. "Last year it was artificial intelligence, sustainability, the labor shortage," Cassiliano said. "Although these challenges remain, they have been superseded by community opposition to data centers." Cassiliano pointed to mounting concerns over electricity prices, water consumption, noise, land use and property values, along with the increasingly political character of efforts to restrict development. He suggested that industry organizations develop a more coordinated strategy for engaging governors and senior state officials, complementing ongoing outreach to local communities. The opening also included an announcement that 7x24 Exchange would contribute $40,000 to American Red Cross disaster relief efforts supporting communities affected by wildfires, hurricanes and flooding across the United States. Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Infrastructure Design The morning keynote, delivered by AI futurist and former Google DeepMind executive Steve Brown, placed the industry's infrastructure expansion within a larger transition from conversational AI tools toward autonomous agents capable of executing complex work. "We're using data centers to turn energy into intelligence," Brown told attendees, describing the physical infrastructure required to support an increasingly AI-driven economy. Brown argued that growing demand for AI inference and autonomous agents could sustain the industry's expansion even as questions persist about the financial sustainability of massive infrastructure investments. "There may be a financial bubble, there may be a debt bubble, but I do not believe there is a demand bubble," he said. Of particular relevance to data center operators, Brown described how agentic computing introduces different workload characteristics from conventional chatbot interactions. Rather than responding to a single prompt, AI agents may execute repeated cycles of reasoning, tool use, database access and task completion over hours or days. Depending on their complexity, he suggested, agents could consume hundreds or thousands of times more tokens than conventional chatbot interactions. The implications extend to hardware architecture. Agentic applications move between GPU-intensive reasoning and CPU-based operations, increasing the importance of heterogeneous computing environments with both CPU/GPU and CPU-only infrastructure. Brown also emphasized persistent memory, low-latency interconnects and secure execution environments as requirements for increasingly autonomous systems. Those changes, he suggested, will demand new ways of evaluating AI infrastructure efficiency. Rather than emphasizing tokens generated per second, Brown proposed measuring useful tasks or economic outcomes relative to energy consumption. The shift, in his view, points toward a future in which data center productivity is judged less by raw computational output than by the useful work that computing delivers. Google and Cummins Examine the Electrical Consequences of AI Loads The next presentation moved from AI's computational requirements to the electrical systems needed to support them. In a joint session on AI load dynamics, Google power systems engineer Ashish Upreti and Cummins technical advisor Rich Scroggins detailed the challenges created by rapid, synchronized changes in power demand from AI computing equipment. Unlike conventional data center workloads, AI training can produce repeated swings between high-power computation and comparatively low-power states as processors complete calculations, exchange information and begin subsequent operations. These fluctuations can occur over milliseconds or seconds, creating distinct challenges for generation equipment, power electronics, UPS systems and electrical distribution infrastructure. The speakers outlined a layered approach to mitigating those fluctuations. Software-level controls can limit how quickly computing loads increase or decrease, although slowing workload transitions can affect computational efficiency. Supercapacitors can address extremely short-duration power spikes, while battery energy storage systems are better suited to absorbing fluctuations occurring over several seconds. The distinction matters because repetitive power swings can create operating conditions that conventional generator acceptance testing does not fully capture. Scroggins explained that a generator may successfully handle an individual load step but behave differently when similar changes occur repeatedly, particularly when the next transition arrives before the governor or voltage regulator has fully recovered. artigo.texto: Springdale residents hold public hearing to oppose proposed data center Residents from Springdale and nearby municipalities gathered at a public hearing to urge Allegheny County officials to deny a developer's application for a proposed data center on the site of the old Cheswick Power Station. Marty Garrigan of Springdale Township said, "Stand up, speak up to save our community and that community in the down river and up river." Cathy Majer, a Springdale Borough resident, shared her perspective on the site's history. "It was filthy. It was loud. When those towers came down a couple years ago, everyone was happy. And shortly after that, we find out that a data center and a hyperscale data center want to go in there," she said. Springdale Borough has already approved Allegheny DC's initial application. The county had 97 questions on the application. During the public hearing, county officials questioned the developer, whose representative described the inquiries as routine and emphasized the project's potential benefits, including jobs, tax revenue and community improvements. "There's always somebody that doesn't want something," said Anna Skipper-Jewart, counsel for Allegheny DC. "But if it's done right, it can be a good neighbor." Looking for more news in your area | Subscribe to the WTAE YouTube Channel Residents raised concerns about the daily testing of the facility's 124 backup generators. "At 124 generators, that means at least five generators will be tested every day. Did you ever hear one generator of that size?" Majer said. Skipper-Jewart explained adjustments made to address community feedback. "We originally had them on the roof, and that is a little bit more typical for a project like this. But what we heard was, OK, we're in a valley here, so maybe let's see if we can move them to the ground. So we've made that adjustment. And with that, we have made the adjustment to have them double stacked," she said. Another concern involved road access blocking St. Mark's Cemetery. Al Wegler, the cemetery's caretaker, expressed satisfaction with the developer's accommodations. "They're going to have a parking lot area for us. We were told that we don't have to worry about snow removal. That will be taken care of by them. So, as far as we're concerned, they're doing a lot to us," he said. The county has 90 days to decide whether to accept, accept with conditions, or deny the developer's application. Download the WTAE app to stay connected with breaking news. artigo.texto: Kota Kinabalu: Sabah is a net carbon sink but has eight of Malaysia’s 10 poorest districts, highlighting the need to ensure that carbon-market investments translate into tangible economic benefits for local communities. Sabah Government Climate Advisor Datuk Darrel Webber said the State had abundant natural resources, including forests, mangroves and oil palm, as well as its own laws, yet poverty remained a concern. “We have forests, mangroves, palm oil and our law, yet many of our people are poor. This is the part I am not proud of,” he said at the recent Sustainable Action Conference 4.0, themed “Sustainability as the New Economic Advantage”, organised by Control Union Malaysia. Webber said Sabah’s status as a net carbon sink presented an opportunity to attract investment and develop a low-carbon economy, provided the benefits were shared more widely. “I do not think there are many jurisdictions in the world that can call themselves a net carbon sink,” he said, noting that Sabah calculated its greenhouse gas inventory in 2024, making it one of the first to do so. He cautioned that carbon markets must not allow the State to supply raw materials while others capture most of the economic value. “If a carbon market only makes money at the top, we repeat an old story. Sabah would supply the raw materials while others take the value,” he said. Carbon, he added, should serve as a driver of broader economic development rather than an opportunity that benefits only a handful of people. “Buyers around the world increasingly ask for low carbon goods, and they want proof. A carbon market gives us the rules, the records and the proof they ask for. Sabah can be the place where goods are made, not only where they are grown. I would like to see two doors open for investors,” he said. The first opportunity, he said, was for companies based in Sabah or sourcing products from the State to invest in insetting initiatives that reduce carbon emissions across their supply chains. “They invest in Sabah and the value of their investment stays in Sabah,” he said. The second was to attract businesses seeking to participate in the low-carbon economy by establishing operations in Sabah and using carbon credits generated in the State as part of their journey towards net zero. Webber said he wanted to see more middle- and downstream activities established locally, particularly the processing and manufacturing of products derived from agriculture and timber. “Because Sabah takes in more carbon than it gives out, we have room to grow without losing our low carbon standing,” he said. He said the success of carbon projects and investments should be assessed by how much value remained in Sabah, how much reached lower-income communities and how much new capacity was developed locally. Webber said Sabah accounted for 22 per cent of Malaysia’s land area, while 36 per cent of the country’s carbon sequestration capacity came from the State. Sabah also had 60 per cent of Malaysia’s mangroves, he said. He cited Sabah’s history of forest conservation initiatives, including the Infapro Rainforest Project, which began in 1992 and used nature-based approaches to address climate change. More recently, the Kuamut Rainforest Conservation Project became Malaysia’s first certified nature-based carbon project, he said. Webber also highlighted Sabah’s record in forest certification, saying the State had the world’s longest certified tropical rainforest under the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) in 1997. Sabah was also Malaysia’s largest palm oil-producing region and, consequently, probably its largest producer of certified sustainable palm oil, he said. He added that Sabah was the only Malaysian region committed to certifying all its palm oil by 2030 according to the highest and most credible international sustainability standards. artigo.texto: Quang Ngai busca maneiras de gerar receita a partir de créditos de carbono florestal. Com aproximadamente 826.000 hectares de floresta, Quang Ngai está acelerando o inventário, completando a coleta de dados e implementando projetos-piloto de crédito de carbono, visando criar recursos financeiros adicionais para a gestão, proteção e desenvolvimento sustentável das florestas. A cada ano, as florestas absorvem aproximadamente 2 milhões de toneladas de carbono. Quang Ngai possui atualmente cerca de 826.000 hectares de floresta, incluindo aproximadamente 604.000 hectares de floresta natural e cerca de 222.000 hectares de floresta plantada. Este é um recurso importante para a província, que permite o desenvolvimento de pesquisas para reduzir as emissões de gases de efeito estufa e aumentar a capacidade de sequestro e armazenamento de carbono. Segundo o Instituto de Ciências Florestais do Vietnã, as atividades potenciais incluem a proteção de florestas naturais, a limitação do desmatamento e da degradação florestal, a restauração de florestas degradadas, a melhoria da qualidade das florestas plantadas, a conversão de florestas de pequena escala em florestas de grande escala e a extensão do ciclo de negócios florestais. Além disso, o manejo florestal sustentável, o desenvolvimento de árvores dispersas e os modelos agroflorestais também contribuem para a melhoria da qualidade das florestas e o aumento da capacidade de sequestro de carbono. Segundo o Sr. Nguyen Van Nam, chefe do Departamento de Proteção Florestal da Província de Quang Ngai, com base em cálculos orientados pelo Departamento de Silvicultura e Proteção Florestal, as florestas da província absorvem e armazenam aproximadamente 2 milhões de toneladas de carbono anualmente, o equivalente a cerca de 2 milhões de créditos. Atualmente, Quang Ngai está implementando o Programa de Redução de Emissões para as regiões Centro-Sul e Planalto Central, no âmbito da iniciativa LEAF, que deverá receber aproximadamente 1,13 milhão de créditos de carbono. No entanto, a quantidade estimada de carbono absorvido e armazenado não equivale necessariamente ao número de créditos reconhecidos e negociáveis. Para gerar receita, os programas e projetos devem atender aos padrões exigidos para cálculo, medição, relato, avaliação e verificação de resultados. Segundo o Departamento Provincial de Proteção Florestal, Quang Ngai está implementando atividades para reduzir as emissões em conjunto com o manejo e a proteção florestal sustentável, a prevenção de incêndios florestais, a limitação da degradação e a melhoria da qualidade das florestas plantadas. Ao mesmo tempo, a província está coordenando o desenvolvimento de projetos-piloto de carbono florestal de acordo com padrões nacionais ou internacionais, com foco tanto em florestas naturais quanto em florestas plantadas. Você também pode gostar Os resultados dos projetos devem ser avaliados, analisados, verificados e submetidos à autoridade competente para consideração, reconhecimento e emissão de créditos antes de participarem na negociação no mercado de carbono. A implementação dessas atividades visa tanto proteger os recursos florestais quanto criar uma base para mobilizar recursos financeiros de programas, organizações e empresas para participar de atividades de redução de emissões. Programa piloto de créditos de carbono: preparando fluxos de receita a partir das florestas. Para implementar projetos de crédito de carbono, Quang Ngai está se concentrando em concluir o banco de dados sobre a área, o estado atual e as características de cada tipo de floresta. O Departamento Provincial de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente está atualmente realizando um levantamento e inventário florestal, conforme orientação do Ministério da Agricultura e Meio Ambiente e do Comitê Popular Provincial. Os resultados do inventário devem ser publicados em 2027. Segundo o Sr. Nguyen Van Nam, os dados de inventário ajudam a determinar os estoques de carbono, monitorar as mudanças nos recursos florestais e avaliar a viabilidade da implementação de projetos em cada área. Também servem como base para a seleção de métodos de cálculo adequados às características de cada tipo de floresta. Paralelamente ao trabalho de inventário, Quang Ngai está coordenando com o Instituto de Ciências Florestais do Vietnã o desenvolvimento de projetos-piloto de carbono florestal na Dak To Forestry Company Limited, na Kon Ray Forestry Company Limited e no Conselho de Gestão Florestal de Proteção de Dak Ha. Essas áreas foram selecionadas com base no tamanho da área florestal, na extensão da floresta e na diversidade de tipos e condições florestais. Essas características incluem florestas latifoliadas perenes, florestas de coníferas e florestas plantadas; e condições florestais que variam de ricas, médias a pobres e severamente degradadas. Essas características facilitam a avaliação da aplicabilidade dos métodos de determinação de carbono em diferentes condições florestais. Segundo o Departamento Provincial de Proteção Florestal de Quang Ngai, os resultados do projeto piloto serão utilizados para pesquisar, selecionar métodos e desenvolver projetos de carbono florestal adequados às condições locais. artigo.texto: Pakistan is reportedly planning a major investment in lithium-ion battery manufacturing, with military-owned Margalla Heavy Industries Limited (MHIL) said to have signed a $2.25 billion agreement with Chinese partners and local investors to establish a battery plant in Rawalpindi. The proposed facility is expected to have an annual production capacity exceeding 1,000 megawatts (MW), with initial output projected at 200–300 MW. However, the project’s production timeline depends on the government’s approval of a dedicated battery manufacturing policy. According to the reported plan, commercial production could begin within six to eight months after the policy receives government approval. Hamad Ali Mansoor, chief executive of the Engineering Development Board (EDB), reportedly said the factory building was ready, and machinery had been installed. The Chinese and Pakistani investors signed the agreement in July, although their identities have not been publicly disclosed. Battery Policy Approval Remains Key Hurdle The proposed investment comes as Pakistan seeks to reduce its dependence on imported batteries and expand domestic manufacturing for electric vehicles (EVs), solar power systems and large-scale electricity storage. The government’s National Lithium-Ion Battery Manufacturing Policy 2026–2031 aims to support local production, attract investment and develop an export-oriented battery industry. However, the policy was still awaiting approval in the latest reports. Approval of the policy is expected to be a key step towards starting commercial operations at the proposed plant. Read More: Pakistan Govt Borrows Net Rs. 373.97 Billion in a Week Battery Demand Could Reach 100,000 MW by 2030 The Engineering Development Board estimates that Pakistan’s demand for battery energy storage systems could reach 100,000 MW by June 2030 if economic growth reaches 5% or more. Demand could reach around 80,000 MW if growth remains below 3%. According to the reported estimates, meeting the projected demand could require four to five large battery manufacturing plants, each costing approximately $1 billion to $1.25 billion. Grid stabilisation alone could require 3,000–5,000 MW of battery storage capacity, highlighting the potential role of energy storage in supporting Pakistan’s electricity infrastructure. The proposed Rawalpindi facility is expected to manufacture lithium-ion batteries for applications including electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Domestic production could help reduce reliance on imported battery technology, create industrial employment and support Pakistan’s transition towards cleaner energy. However, the project’s final production schedule remains dependent on government approval of the battery manufacturing policy.

artigo.texto: Mercedes-Benz's decision to develop its own batteries in-house is already paying big dividends, after the German brand announced that it has developed a pioneering new battery chemistry that will herald cheaper, faster-to-charge batteries that offer 30 per cent more range. Joining the ranks of Tesla, Volkswagen, Ford and Toyota, as well as leading EV giant BYD, Mercedes only opened its substantial eCampus back in 2024 and it was scientists working at the new R&D hub who were behind the new manganese-rich battery tech. No timescale was revealed for when the new Lithium-Manganese-Oxide battery (LMO) or the even more energy-packed Lithium-Nickel-Manganese-Oxide (LNMO) unitwill be rolled out, but the new lithium iron phosphate (LFP)-replacing tech is expected to be introduced within the next two years, ahead of Benz's own solid-state batteries that will launch towards the end of this decade. Read more - 'We won't be left wanting': Solid-state battery-powered cars with a potential 1500km of range likely for Australia - Major battery breakthrough confirmed - The Australian electric car battery breakthrough: Aussie smarts commercialise new battery that could result in a big change for the EVs we drive such as the Tesla Model Y, BYD Seal and more New batteries are greener and more sustainable The new batteries were unwrapped at the premium German brand's 140 Years of Innovation celebrations, where Mercedes scientists said that as well as being superior to the current LFP batteries available in cars like the new Mercedes CLA, its new LMO/LNMO pave the way for a greener, more sustainable future. That's because the manganese-rich chemistries are less reliant on cobalt, with the LNMO completely free of the in-demand element. Cobalt remains problematic for the car industry, with more than three-quarters of it sourced from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) from mines that are known to use unsafe working conditions and environmentally damaging extraction practices. The challenge for Benz, explained the scientists and battery engineers, was to attempt to replicate the same high energy density of its current LFP battery technology without cobalt. New batteries to beat BYD's LFP cells First to launch in the "near future" is the LMO tech, which blends its chemistry with Nickel-Manganese-Cobalt (NMC) oxide to maintain its energy density, but the big gains will come later with the completely cobalt-free LNMO tech, which costs less to produce than equivalent LFP cells. Crucially, when scaled up to the same size and weight of the equivalent LFP batteries, which have been popularised by BYD, the new tech offers far faster charging and, at least 30 per cent more range. Capable of working with far higher voltages, the new LMO batteries are also said to be safer than existing cells. Mercedes engineers wouldn't be drawn on figures, but if applied to the current 58kWh LFP battery that powers the Mercedes CLA, the new battery will raise the range of the base model from 447km to more than 580km with higher charging rates, potentially above 400kW (+200kW) for a sub-10-minute 10 to 80 per cent top-up. The same power packs are also tolerant of fast DC charging, retaining as much as 80 per cent of their original capacity after more than 1500 charge cycles, in research carried out on non-Benz batteries. Full technical details have not been revealed on either the LMO or LNMO batteries, nor exact timings of when they will be rolled out, but it's thought both will be replacements for the current LFP chemistry, rather than the brand's flagship NMC cells. The latter will then be superseded by the firm's most advanced solid-state batteries that are currently being developed in partnership with US-based Factorial and Taiwan's ProLogium for an introduction around 2029. When questioned by CarsGuide, Mercedes insiders said if the German brand was beaten to market in the race to introduce solid-state batteries, or other more advanced chemistries, by the likes of China's CATL it would favour the off-the-shelf solution, so long as it offered the "best price for the customer". Originally, many analysts had written off LMO and LNMO batteries as 'transitional chemistries' but, the prolonged delay in introducing solid-state and the high costs and ethical issues concerning sourcing cobalt have now seen CATL and Japan's Toyota also investing heavily in manganese-rich alternatives that will rival Benz's tech. Opened back in 2024 as part of a €14 billion ($A22b) investment in R&D, the new eCampus is a 10,000-square-metre facility that consists of three labs that are designed to fast-track new battery innovation with the ultimate aim of slashing the cost of a high-voltage battery by 30 per cent in the near future. The facility, located within Benz's Stuttgart R&D hub, is one giant building that enables scientists to develop the chemistry, build prototype cells to torture-test, and then evolve the concept, before scaling it up for full mass production.

artigo.texto: OpenAI’s $20 billion planned data center development in Effingham County may have put southeast Georgia on the data center map. Cities in Bulloch, Bryan, Effingham and Liberty counties are receiving data center development inquiries – some for the first time. And, at the same time, a wave of data center moratoriums is now washing over southeast Georgia as local governments scramble to be proactive rather than reactive to the state’s data center boom. While Georgia has been a nationwide leader for developing the tech facilities for at least a year, southeast Georgian leaders predicted the region’s water and energy infrastructure would be a barrier to development. Much of southeast Georgia lies zones cited as most at risk for saltwater intrusion into the Floridan aquifer. The risk of severe storms and hurricanes along the coast also leaves power grids vulnerable. However, technology like closed-loop cooling systems, which require less water, and a major Georgia Power infrastructure expansion, mean a region that was once seemingly unfit for data centers, will now house one of the largest in the country. OpenAI announced its 1,400-acre Effingham County data center campus in July, which is expected to use 3.2 Gigawatts of electricity at full build-out. Since then, advocacy has picked up for local officials to establish stronger safeguards to guide their own data center destinies. Some say the region – and Georgia as a whole – needs to move beyond a patchwork of local responses and establish clear rules before developers come knocking. “Data centers are not going away,” said David Bennett, chairman of the Bulloch County Board of Commissioners, which was one of the first counties to establish a data center moratorium. “This is something that you’re going to have to regulate and make work within your community. Otherwise, they’re going to take advantage of you.” Step 1: Moratorium Community members across coastal Georgia are pushing their elected officials to adopt moratoriums on data center development, regardless of whether they’ve received inquiries or proposals. They argue it puts a pause on any potential development and gives communities a chance to research and develop ordinances or zoning guidelines. “You can’t outright ban data centers because of state and federal laws,” Damon Mullis, the Ogeechee Riverkeeper, said to Bulloch County’s Board of Commissioners in April. “But, you can prepare. You can create guidelines, limitations, consequences for noncompliance.” While Bulloch was the first, Liberty County and the city of Pembroke in Bryan County have since followed suit. Liberty County Commissioners voted unanimously to adopt a 120-day moratorium, beginning Oct. 15. The Liberty County Development Authority confirmed recently that it’s received inquiries since Effingham and Wayne County data center projects were announced; though, none have been presented to county commission boards. The City of Pembroke adopted a 180-day data center moratorium in the first week of October. Pembroke Mayor Tiffany Ziegler said while the city hasn’t received any inquiries, she wanted to ensure its code addressed data center development clearly. Ziegler said she personally doesn’t support data centers within Pembroke’s city limits, mainly due to infrastructure limitations and a lack of support from the community. “At the same time, we need to be careful and precise with the wording of any ordinance,” she wrote. “My priority is clear, specific language that defines what is permitted, what is prohibited, and what requirements apply.” Bulloch County has even taken its moratorium period a step further, extending it beyond its original 90 days and forming a committee made up of people from the community and nominated by commissioners, to provide input as Bulloch County drafts an ordinance for data centers. The committee held its first meeting in early October. Bennett said the county will extend its data center moratorium beyond the first of the year if extra time is needed to form an ordinance. “There is no rush,” Bennett said. “The goal is to come out of this with a solid zoning policy that protects the people of the county while also providing some benefit to them.” Jeffrey Beauvais, the north coast advocate for coastal nonprofit One Hundred Miles, said his organization is encouraging more local governments to formally involve its citizens in the process through opportunities like advisory boards. “There are a lot of good staff who are doing good work, but it remains sort of behind the scenes,” he said. “I think it gives people a lot more confidence in whatever law a county or city ultimately writes up if they feel they've been meaningfully involved in the process or they know someone who is meaningfully involved.” Step 2: What’s in an ordinance Nonprofits like the Ogeechee Riverkeeper created data center ordinance templates for communities to consider. They encourage communities to require a Special Use Permit for data centers, forcing developers to go through the public process and requiring a council vote in public. This is what Statesboro’s Planning and Zoning team opted to do when it finalized its data center ordinance in June, after nearly a year of researching the tech facilities. “We were not keen on having a by-right allowance for them,” Statesboro Planning and Zoning Director Justin Williams said. “That’s how you end up with a lot of them in your community, and you end up with problems.” Writing data centers into an ordinance as a permitted use is also how developers and elected officials avoid the public eye as seen in Effingham County, where OpenAI’s massive project moved forward without a public hearing or any type of vote. Cities and counties also are being urged to prohibit non-disclosure agreements during the proposal and development process. artigo.texto: Illumion, a University of Cambridge spinout developing advanced battery imaging technology, has raised £1.7 million in funding. Illumion is commercialising charge photometry, a novel battery imaging technology that acts like a window into working batteries. Its first product, illumionONE, allows researchers to observe how individual battery particles behave during charge and discharge, providing insights that are difficult to capture with conventional testing methods. The company is also developing illumionX, a next-generation platform designed to help industrial battery teams translate those insights into faster development cycles and better quality-control decisions. Foresight Group provided follow-on investment alongside ZEISS Ventures, Cambridge Enterprise Ventures, Parkwalk, Cambridge Angels and YourVC. The funding round will support Illumion’s continued commercial development, product roadmap, and engagement with customers and partners across the battery ecosystem. “This funding marks an important next step for Illumion as we translate world-class research into practical tools that accelerate battery innovation and development,” said Christoph Schnedermann, co-founder and CEO of Illumion. “Charge photometry gives researchers and engineers a new way to understand how battery materials behave in real time, and we are excited to continue developing our technology with the support of Foresight, ZEISS Ventures and our existing investors.” Andrew Bloxam, partner at Foresight Group, commented: “Illumion has developed a differentiated technology platform addressing an important challenge within battery research and industrial development. “Since Foresight’s initial investment, the team has made encouraging technical and commercial progress, and the involvement of ZEISS Ventures underlines the strategic relevance of the company’s imaging technology. We are pleased to continue supporting Christoph and the wider team through this next phase of development.” Budget: Founders’ Relief a ‘shot of adrenaline’ for entrepreneurs Julian Schroth, investment manager at ZEISS Ventures, added: “Battery technology is a key area of innovation, and advanced imaging tools can help researchers and manufacturers gain deeper insights into battery behaviour during development and testing. “Illumion’s has developed a differentiated approach to battery imaging, and we look forward to supporting the company as it advances its platform and engages with customers across the battery value chain.” Mills & Reeve advised Illumion on this funding round. The team was led by corporate partner and Head of VC Investments Zickie Lim, who commented: “This investment is an exciting example of the cutting-edge innovation emerging from the UK’s university spinout ecosystem. We were thrilled to support Illumion on this vital funding round which will enable the company to advance its pioneering battery imaging technology and enter its next phase of commercial growth.” Foresight first invested in Illumion in 2024 through the Foresight Technology EIS and VCT funds. Since then, Foresight has supported the Company through active Board engagement, strategic guidance, investor introductions and support for non-dilutive funding applications, including Illumion’s successful Innovate UK Growth Catalyst grant. artigo.texto: Growing power demand from hyperscale data centers has put the energy sector in the spotlight. Once seen as stable, income-generating assets, energy and utility stocks are attracting investors as data centers scramble to secure power. Growing demand is boosting regulated utilities in fast-growing regions, including companies like Southern Company (SO -1.22%). Meanwhile, independent power producers benefit more from growing electricity prices, and companies like Constellation Energy (CEG -0.35%) are locking in long-term power purchase agreements with hyperscalers. Here's why these two energy stocks look like no-brainer buys for investors with $3,000 to invest. Southern Company is seeing strong data center growth in its service regions Southern Company is a diversified energy holding company that owns regulated utilities like Georgia Power Company and Alabama Power Company, natural gas infrastructure (including gas distribution and pipelines), and wholesale power through Southern Power. The company is seeing robust growth across its service regions, notably Georgia Power and Alabama Power. It's secured approval (from the EPA) for 10 gigawatts of new power generation resources, including natural gas units, combustion turbines, solar facilities, and grid-scale battery storage. SO Southern Company NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 10/28/26 The company has locked in large-load contracts with data center customers, and these long-term agreements cover 100% of the incremental cost of serving them. Georgia Power entered into a 25-year 3.2-GW contract for OpenAI's campus in Effingham County, Georgia. The company has also partnered with Alphabet to add 96 MW of capacity to the grid through nuclear plant uprates. Southern Company is also seeing strong demand for its on-site power generation systems through its subsidiary, PowerSecure, and for wholesale power generation through its subsidiary, Southern Power, which operates natural gas turbines. For investors seeking exposure to growing electricity demand from AI data centers, Southern Company is an appealing utility in a fast-growing region for serving data centers. That, coupled with its 3.3% dividend yield, makes it an attractive stock for more conservative investors seeking stable exposure to AI's growing energy needs. Constellation Energy has locked in numerous long-term power deals with hyperscalers For more aggressive investors seeking greater exposure to the growing power crunch, Constellation Energy stands out. As a merchant power producer, Constellation owns power generation assets and sells electricity into the market at prevailing prices. When prices surge, Constellation benefits. But if demand wanes and prices fall, Constellation feels that pain too. To meet growing demand, Constellation is expanding capacity through new projects, uprates and upgrades, and acquisitions. The company has signed deals with numerous major companies, including Microsoft, Meta Platforms, Walmart, Amazon, and Alphabet. CEG Constellation Energy NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 10/28/26 Under Constellation's 20-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Microsoft, the company will add 835 MW of new power capacity, including the restart of Three Mile Island Unit 1, which will be renamed the Crane Clean Energy Center. With Alphabet, Constellation will add 890 MW of capacity through nuclear uprates across 11 reactors at 6 nuclear sites. While Constellation benefits from rising electricity prices, it is taking steps to reduce the volatility of price swings that accompany demand booms and busts. By signing long-term PPAs with hyperscalers, the company locks in a large portion of its energy in multidecade deals that provide predictable cash flows. If you want more upside exposure to AI's growing energy demand and can stomach the volatility, Constellation Energy, down 34% over the past year, looks like another solid energy stock to buy to capitalize on this boom.
