artigo.texto: It’s now taken for granted that data centers across the U.S. are driving up electricity prices. As many Americans have soured on the energy-consuming facilities powering digital life and the AI boom, the issue has become central to the midterm elections. Ad after political ad targets data centers, with many stating as fact that electricity prices have gone up as a result. “No one asked for that data center to be built here, and no one here is getting a damn thing from it except higher electric bills,” one ad in Ohio, paid for by Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown, says. Another ad in Texas, from Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico, alleges that his Republican opponent’s support for data centers led to “skyrocketing utility bills.” Tens of millions of dollars have been spent airing ads that make claims about data centers and electricity prices this cycle, with heavy spending on races in states such as Ohio, Texas, Pennsylvania and Michigan, according to the ad-tracking service AdImpact. Recent surveys have found that a majority of Americans would not support a nearby data center, making opposition to the facilities a rare area of bipartisan agreement. The top reason to oppose data centers, according to one poll, is rising electricity prices. At the same time, Department of Energy Secretary Chris Wright has repeatedly claimed that data centers have beneficial effects on electricity prices. “The actual record of data centers coming on is they almost always are accompanied by a multiyear freeze in electricity prices. So, in real terms, a gradual decline in the cost of electricity,” he said on Sept. 17 at an event hosted by the conservative news outlet the Daily Caller. “These are a massive force to reduce the price of electricity and stop the price rises.” Wright is correct that in principle, data centers could bring down prices. According to some analyses, that’s even happened in some places. But he fails to mention data, including from his own agency, that show that the opposite is also happening for many Americans. At least for the PJM Interconnection, the nation’s largest grid operator serving more than 65 million people in the Midwest and mid-Atlantic, prices have likely gone up as a result of data centers. A July report from the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, one of the DOE’s federal labs, and the economic consulting firm the Brattle Group, found that increased demand, or load growth, including from large data centers, contributed to “significant” price increases in the PJM region in 2025. Still, the report makes the point that most of the observed price increases in the past few years are not due to data centers — and that overall, at least until 2025, increased load growth was associated with lower retail electricity prices. Data centers have contributed to, but aren’t the only reason for, price increases in Ohio and other states in the Midwest. In Texas, where prices have risen only modestly, it is not entirely clear, experts told us, but large price increases would not be expected to occur in the same way in part because the state is rapidly deploying new low-cost wind and solar power. As we’ll explain, whether data centers raise prices depends on multiple factors. It’s not a given that prices will rise if a data center moves in, but the risk is real — and price increases have already occurred in some places. “Data centers can put either upward or downward pressure on electricity prices,” Jacquelyn Pless, an energy economist at the University of Toronto, told us. “It depends on how much it costs to serve the new demand, whether utilities can use existing infrastructure more efficiently, and who ultimately pays for any required investments.” “Secretary Wright has been clear that energy subtraction policies, not data centers, have been responsible for rising electricity prices and that when states encourage energy addition policies, growing electricity demand (including with data centers) drives down electricity costs for American families,” DOE spokesperson Ben Dietderich told us, placing blame on closures of coal and natural gas plants and renewable portfolio standards, policies that require a minimum amount of clean energy. DOE also cited examples of data center agreements that have led to rate freezes, which appear on a White House webpage from July touting President Donald Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge. We’ll share what experts think of the pledge. What the Data Show If many Americans think that all of or even the bulk of their recent electricity price increases are due to data centers, that is a misconception. “To date, except for in the PJM market, load growth and data centers in particular as a sub-sector of load growth, have not been a principal driver of price increases in electric markets around the country,” Douglas J. Arent, a global fellow at the Columbia University Center on Global Energy Policy, told us. According to the July LBNL report, national average retail electricity prices have risen 29% between 2019 and 2025, but that figure falls to just 3% when adjusted for inflation. The reason for price increases varies, but Arent said the main drivers are fuel price increases, especially for natural gas, and the cost of replacing and updating grid infrastructure. Much of the U.S. grid is old and due for improvement, just as equipment and labor costs have soared with inflation, supply chain constraints and Trump’s tariffs. “The politics has certainly grown much larger than the data and the facts on this one,” Arent said. The LBNL report notes that at the state level, increased demand, in part from data centers, is associated with a decline in electricity prices in recent years, and that residential customers “may have benefited from load growth from 2019 to 2025 in some states.” At least through 2024, North Dakota, New Mexico and Nebraska each significantly grew their load while reducing inflation-adjusted prices. A estratégia prevê aproveitar o potencial de geração de energia renovável do país para atrair empresas de tecnologia, ampliar a infraestrutura de processamento de dados e reduzir a dependência de soluções estrangeiras. Energia renovável para atrair data centers Durante o discurso, Lula destacou a capacidade energética brasileira como diferencial para receber centros de dados, estruturas fundamentais para serviços de computação em nuvem e sistemas de inteligência artificial. “Temos que aproveitar o potencial energético de um país que talvez seja o que tenha mais capacidade de energia renovável para trazer os datacenters necessários para acumular dados no Brasil.” O plano de governo prevê contrapartidas para empresas que instalarem data centers no país, incluindo capacidade computacional destinada ao mercado brasileiro. Também estabelece investimentos em supercomputadores nacionais e expansão dos serviços de nuvem. A instalação dessas estruturas deverá considerar eficiência energética, uso progressivo de fontes 100% renováveis e impactos sobre o abastecimento de água, o sistema elétrico e as comunidades locais. Governo prevê desenvolvimento de IA brasileira Outra proposta é desenvolver sistemas nacionais de inteligência artificial para diminuir a dependência de tecnologias dos Estados Unidos e da China. Para isso, o presidente defendeu ampliar o ensino de disciplinas ligadas à ciência e à tecnologia. “Queremos ensinar mais matemática, mais engenharia porque não quero ficar dependendo de inteligência artificial chinesa e americana. Quero criar uma brasileira”, afirmou. O plano prevê modelos de linguagem em português e em outras línguas, além de uma plataforma nacional de dados para treinamento e avaliação desses sistemas. Também propõe fortalecer instituições públicas de pesquisa, incentivar empresas brasileiras de hardware e software de alto desempenho e aproximar universidades e setor produtivo. Entre as áreas que poderão receber aplicações de IA estão o agronegócio, a saúde e os serviços financeiros. Regulamentação das big techs Lula também defendeu regulamentar as grandes empresas de tecnologia, relacionando a proposta à influência das plataformas digitais durante o processo eleitoral. “Vamos ter que regulá-las. Não é possível que a gente não tenha consciência de que um crime no mundo digital tem que ser tratado igual a um crime da vida real”, declarou. artigo.texto: Data center concerns continue in Amherst County despite no active project AMHERST COUNTY, Va. (WSET) — No data center project is currently moving forward in Amherst County, but the possibility of one has already sparked debate. “I don’t want one of these stupid things in my backyard any more than I want one in my neighbor’s backyard,” Amherst County resident Kevin Wittman said. Data centers have been a growing concern in Amherst County for months. “It’s going to affect our ecosystems,” neighbor Teresa Almond said. Almond says she loves the beauty of the James River and worries a data center could use too much water and harm the environment. With speculation about possible sites, some residents worry a project could be closer than they think. “I think there’s a data center planned here or on the other side across the road,” resident Sky Pacot said. Pacot has concerns about the water usage and noise associated with data centers. However, he says he appreciates the board’s open communication throughout the process. While some residents have raised concerns about a potential application, county leaders say there is no application currently under consideration. “We have no applications to discuss,” Board of Supervisors member Chris Adams said. The possibility of a data center is enough to bring concerned neighbors to county meetings and make their opinions known. In August, the Board of Supervisors voted to require special use permits for future data centers. That gives the county more control over proposed projects and gives neighbors a chance to weigh in. “To apply, you have to submit a noise study. You have to evaluate that. You would have to show a concept plan showing setbacks, meeting the criteria set forth in the ordinance,” Director of Community Development Tyler Creasy said. Adams was one of two supervisors who voted against the ordinance. He said data centers can meet existing zoning rules while still bringing economic benefits to Amherst County. “I want to make sure that that process is done right. But at the same time, I want to make things more fiscally beneficial for the taxpayers, the ones that are carrying the tax burden day in and day out of this county,” Adams said. The possibility of a data center also came up the same day the board voted to require special use permits. ABC13 asked Adams, “Did you have any idea about that application?” “Absolutely not. No, that was a complete surprise to everyone of us that evening,” Adams said. The application was deemed incomplete, meaning it could not move forward without a special exception. No completed application has been submitted, but that doesn’t mean the conversation about data centers has ended. “I obviously don’t want to do anything that’s harmful to our county, to our natural resources or anything that can harm our citizens,” Adams said. “I don’t know how many more times we have to keep showing up and tell those who are working for us in public office we do not want it,” Wittman said.

artigo.texto: Why Nickel-Zinc Batteries Fit In-Rack Storage for AI As AI changes the power demands placed on the rack, the role of in-rack energy storage is evolving beyond traditional backup. October 29, 2026 AI is changing the power demands placed on the rack. However, higher power densities are only part of the story. The workloads themselves are increasingly dynamic, creating rapid and repeated changes in demand that the surrounding power infrastructure must be prepared to support. High-density AI infrastructure can bring thousands of GPUs online in parallel, moving together between compute and communication-intensive tasks. Those synchronized shifts can create fluctuations in power demand on millisecond timescales, extending beyond individual servers and racks to place additional stress on upstream power infrastructure. At the same time, the growing concentration of high-value GPU and xPU infrastructure makes consistent power delivery increasingly important to system utilization and performance. For in-rack energy storage, this introduces an important shift. Providing backup when primary power is interrupted remains essential, but increasingly dynamic AI workloads are creating another requirement alongside it: the ability to respond to rapid changes in power demand. As those requirements converge at the rack, the characteristics of the underlying energy storage technology become increasingly important. The Tradeoff AI Is Bringing Into Focus Rack-level backup is already well established, particularly among hyperscalers. Traditional Battery Backup Units (BBUs) are designed primarily to provide the runtime needed when primary power is interrupted. At the other end of the spectrum, capacitor-based systems can respond effectively to extremely short, high-frequency power events, but offer limited energy duration and scalability. AI is bringing the space between those applications into sharper focus. As rack power densities rise and workloads become more dynamic, energy storage is increasingly being evaluated against a wider range of requirements. Runtime still matters, but so does power density, response capability, cycle performance, footprint, safety, sustainability and compatibility with evolving rack architectures. The challenge is not simply finding a technology that responds faster or stores more energy. It is determining which combination of characteristics best supports the application, whether the requirement is established backup, dynamic power response or different capabilities across different portions of the infrastructure. That is where nickel-zinc (NiZn) presents an interesting opportunity. Why Nickel-Zinc Fits the AI Era Nickel-zinc battery technology combines high power capability with usable energy storage, a balance that becomes particularly valuable as more power is concentrated within space-constrained rack environments. Its high-rate charge and discharge capability also allows the technology to respond quickly and repeatedly in short-duration, high-power applications. Those characteristics make NiZn relevant across a broader range of in-rack energy storage requirements. Usable energy remains important for backup applications, while high-rate performance creates opportunities for battery-based energy storage to support rapidly changing AI power demands. As energy storage moves closer to high-density compute infrastructure, however, performance cannot be considered in isolation. The proximity of batteries to increasingly valuable servers, networking equipment and cooling infrastructure makes safety an important consideration in both chemistry selection and system architecture. Nickel-zinc uses a nonflammable, aqueous electrolyte and is incapable of thermal runaway in UL 9540A cell-level testing. These characteristics can provide greater flexibility as operators evaluate how to integrate energy storage safely into increasingly power-dense environments. That flexibility is even more relevant as codes, standards and site requirements place greater emphasis on thermal runaway, fire propagation and system-level safety. NFPA 855 and IFC Section 1207 are among the industry requirements addressing these considerations, while ZincFive’s existing data center battery systems comply with multiple industry-recognized safety standards. Sustainability is another part of the equation. Nickel-zinc uses abundant, highly recyclable materials and delivers 25–50% lower lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions than lead-acid or lithium-ion alternatives. As AI infrastructure continues to scale, the material lifecycle and environmental impact of the technologies supporting that growth warrant consideration alongside performance and safety. One Chemistry Does Not Mean One Architecture The ability of nickel-zinc to address a broader range of power requirements does not mean every application should be served by the same product. ZincFive is extending its high-rate NiZn technology from the UPS layer into the rack with its NiZn In-Rack Power Solutions, comprising two dedicated solutions designed for different applications. The ZincFive Battery Backup Units (BBU) are being developed for established rack-level backup, applying NiZn’s high power capability, safety and high-rate performance where immediate power is needed following an interruption to the primary source. The ZincFive AI Dynamic Power Modules (DPM), meanwhile, are designed to support the highly dynamic power demands of AI workloads, including transient mitigation, pulse power support and other dynamic power applications. Developing dedicated solutions for these applications gives OEMs, hyperscalers and data center operators greater flexibility to match power capabilities to their specific workloads and architectures. Depending on the environment, that could mean traditional backup, dynamic power support or a combination of solutions across different portions of the infrastructure. artigo.texto: Eólicas miram data centers para ampliar demanda em meio a cortes de geração Dirigentes defendem novas usinas e reforços na transmissão; compensação financeira por restrições passadas mantém em aberto o desafio de aproveitar a energia disponível O setor eólico brasileiro aposta na chegada de data centers para impulsionar investimentos e destravar a demanda, enquanto parques já instalados enfrentam restrições para produzir energia. A aparente contradição foi tratada na 17ª edição do Brazil Windpower, em São Paulo, que expôs o desafio dessa estratégia: coordenar a expansão das usinas, das redes e do consumo para que novos empreendimentos encontrem espaço em um sistema que já precisa limitar a geração. A presidente executiva da Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica (Abeeólica), Elbia Gannoum, afirmou que o curtailment, como são conhecidos os cortes de geração, permanece sem solução operacional, apesar do avanço na regulamentação das compensações às empresas. A Portaria Normativa nº 140, publicada pelo Ministério de Minas e Energia em julho, tem alcance delimitado. Ela disciplina a compensação por cortes ocorridos entre setembro de 2023 e novembro de 2025, classificados como decorrentes de confiabilidade elétrica ou indisponibilidade externa. A adesão exige a assinatura de um termo de compromisso que inclui a renúncia a disputas sobre compensações por restrições ocorridas até a data estabelecida. O tratamento dessas perdas, entretanto, deixa em aberto as condições físicas que levam às restrições. Segundo o ONS (Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico), os cortes são uma medida técnica necessária para preservar a segurança do sistema quando a geração disponível não pode ser integralmente aproveitada. A produção eólica e solar varia ao longo do tempo e nem sempre coincide com os momentos de maior consumo. Essa distinção limita o alcance de uma solução centrada apenas na construção de linhas. Em diagnóstico sobre o curtailment, o ONS aponta que, mesmo com a eliminação de restrições de transmissão, podem continuar ocorrendo cortes quando a oferta supera a demanda em determinados horários. A expansão das redes resolve parte do problema; o equilíbrio entre produção e consumo exige outras respostas. É nesse contexto que os data centers aparecem na agenda da indústria. Elbia defendeu atenção à infraestrutura de transmissão necessária para receber essas novas cargas e aproveitar o interesse de grandes consumidores pelo Brasil. A dirigente também apontou a retomada da indústria eólica nacional como uma das prioridades do setor. João Galamba, assessor sênior do Conselho Global de Energia Eólica (GWEC), defendeu que a instalação de data centers seja acompanhada de nova geração limpa. Na avaliação dele, o desafio brasileiro está na capacidade de entregar essa energia, o que passa pela infraestrutura das redes e pelo enfrentamento do curtailment. A proposta abre uma frente de negócios para geradores e fabricantes, mas seu efeito sobre os cortes depende de como os projetos forem implantados. À luz do diagnóstico do ONS, o aumento do consumo pode ajudar a absorver excedentes; a construção simultânea de novas usinas exige avaliar onde e quando essa energia será produzida e consumida. O anúncio de uma nova carga, isoladamente, não permite medir o alívio que ela proporcionará às restrições existentes. A distribuição dos impactos dos cortes também continua em discussão regulatória. Em outubro, a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) aprovou regras para organizar a ordem das restrições e compartilhar seus efeitos entre diferentes fontes. A aplicação definitiva foi prevista para 18 meses após a publicação da resolução, com uma etapa anterior de simulação dos resultados. No horizonte internacional, Elbia citou o objetivo de elevar a eletrificação do consumo mundial de energia a 35% até 2035. A meta integra a campanha Electrify Now, liderada pela Global Renewables Alliance com apoio do GWEC, e busca ampliar o uso de eletricidade em transportes, processos industriais e outras atividades hoje atendidas por combustíveis fósseis. Trata-se de uma agenda defendida pelas organizações, cuja concretização depende de decisões de governos, empresas e consumidores. Entre os fabricantes, Roberto Veiga, vice-presidente da Goldwind no Brasil, apresentou o investimento em capacidade industrial em Camaçari, na Bahia, como demonstração do interesse da companhia pelo mercado brasileiro e pelo fortalecimento da cadeia nacional. A produção local também tem uma função comercial. Ao anunciar a aquisição da fábrica da GE em Camaçari, em 2024, a Goldwind destacou que o atendimento aos critérios de nacionalização do BNDES facilitaria o acesso dos clientes ao financiamento de longo prazo para a compra dos equipamentos.

artigo.texto: Laying out his vision of a modern, booming New Mexico economy, state Sen. Michael Padilla, D, touted a bill in the 2025 legislative session that he said would incentivize “the construction and installation of microgrids in underserved communities across New Mexico.” Crucially, he added, the development of microgrids for projects like subdivisions or data centers would align “with our environmental goals by facilitating the use of clean energy technologies and reducing greenhouse gases.” As electricity demand spikes across the U.S. and rolling blackouts plague regional grids, hospitals, universities, small towns, low-income communities and tribes have turned to microgrids for resilient, self-sourced energy powered by solar or wind. By all accounts, Senate Bill 418 appeared to facilitate just that. Padilla’s initial bill failed, but after some tense, eleventh-hour negotiations, a pared down version passed as an amendment to a broader grid modernization measure. No microgrid in particular was mentioned during the vote. Only in hindsight did it become clear that the amendment was tailor-made for industry, including the construction of what was to become one of the most controversial A.I. data centers in the West — Project Jupiter, a sprawling 1,400-acre campus slated for southern New Mexico. “I feel really hoodwinked in some ways,” House Rep. Kristina Ortez, D, told High Country News. In the final throes of the session, Sen. Padilla added the amendment, which Ortez, one of HB 93’s co-authors, believed would benefit local hospitals, schools, and fire departments. It wasn’t until months later, when Project Jupiter sparked local opposition, that the realization washed over her: “Oh, my God, this is what that amendment allowed to happen.” WHEN PADILLA DESCRIBED his bill in a committee meeting, he did so beside Jennifer Bradfute, a lobbyist for Borderplex Digital Assets, one of Project Jupiter’s developers, who he introduced as an “energy expert.” Bradfute said she was working on large digital infrastructure projects in the Borderplex region, which includes Las Cruces and Santa Teresa, New Mexico, El Paso, Texas, and Ciudad Juárez in Mexico, as well as in central New Mexico near Isleta Pueblo. “Our development is focused on solar power generation,” Bradfute said. “The flexibility of using microgrids that could be developed sooner than some of what our public utilities can provide would also provide power solutions for some of our Native American areas throughout the state that have not been able to be served by our public utilities so far.” Later, in a follow-up hearing, she emphasized the bill was needed “so we can have sufficient legal certainty to invest $5 billion and create 1,000 jobs.” Though the microgrid bill had early support, it ultimately died due to environmental concerns. However, just as New Mexico’s 60-day legislative session was wrapping up, another Democrat, House Rep. Nathan Small, held an eleventh-hour meeting in his chambers to try and push through certain language from the microgrid bill in the form of an amendment to House Bill 93. This bill aimed to modernize New Mexico’s electrical grid, and the amendment sought to permit the generation and distribution of self-sourced power, allowing “qualified” microgrids to produce 20 megawatts or more of energy — enough to power a small city. The amendment also stated that unless a microgrid sought to sell energy to a public utility company, it would not be regulated by state authorities. The negotiations in Small’s chambers led to an added provision saying that all microgrids had to conform to the Energy Transition Act, or ETA, , which would require all of the energy they generate and sell to be from net-zero carbon resources by 2045. Later that day, Padilla brought the amendment to the state Senate with a brief introduction. Paper copies of the language were then handed out, and senators were still reading it when a voice vote was called to add the amendment to the bill. Minutes later, the entire measure passed the Senate. The following day, the House concurred, and the amended bill was approved. The bill has now opened the door for Project Jupiter and other major industrial development — huge projects that differ markedly from what the microgrid amendment once seemed to promise. “Since that legislation has passed,” Padilla said in an interview with HCN in late October, “You have Castileon in Rio Rancho,” he said. “You have Pacific Fusion in my district up in Mesa del Sol. So our state really did get really ignited economically.” Near a subdivision in Rio Rancho, Castileon Corp. is building Project Ranger, a 1,000-acre hypersonic missile manufacturing facility that could lead to dangerous chemical fires, according to reporting in Wired magazine. Pacific Fusion has broken ground on a $1 billion research and manufacturing campus near Albuquerque to build modular nuclear fusion power plants for nuclear weapons research. Both projects purport to create hundreds of local jobs. PROJECT JUPITER’S MICROGRID AIMS to generate about the same amount of energy as New Mexico’s largest public utility company, PNM. That’s enough to power half a million homes and more than 100 times the amendment’s 20-megawatt minimum — all from one microgrid powered by fuel cells converting natural gas into electricity. Project Jupiter’s next hurdle is an air quality permit from the New Mexico Environment Department, or NMED. After NMED posed questions “concerning the accuracy of emissions testing” in the permit application, two Project Jupiter developers, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Yucca Growth Infrastructure, said they would reduce projected emissions by 35%, from 8.8 million tons to 5.7 million tons per year. “NMED’s staff asked hard technical questions, and they pushed us to address the concerns raised by the public,” said Mahesh Thiagarajan, executive vice president and head of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, in a statement. artigo.texto: Data center ou centro de distribuição de dados é um espaço projetado para abrigar diversos computadores, chamados de servidores, com funções variadas, como processamento, armazenamento e distribuição de dados. Sevidores são dispositivos em uma rede, responsáveis por gerenciar recursos de rede, com a capacidade de armazenar arquivos e aplicativos que são fornecidos a vários usuários ou dispositivos de uma vez só. Felipe Pameira, Desenvolvedor Web do Brasil Escola, explica que a principal função do data center é "garantir que informações, sistemas e serviços digitais estejam disponíveis, sejam processados com eficiência e possam ser acessados de maneira segura pelos usuários". Leia também: Folha divulga Ranking Universitário 2026 Tópicos desta notícia - 1 - Quem são os usuários de um data center? - 2 - Data centers no Brasil - 3 - Importância de data centers Quem são os usuários de um data center? Os data centers, atualmente, são utilizados de forma direta ou indireta por qualquer pessoa que utilize internet ou serviços digitais. "Por exemplo, quando uma pessoa acessa um aplicativo no celular dela, a empresa dona do aplicativo precisa ter um data center ou alugar data centers para que a informação daquele aplicativo seja carregada no celular do usuário", explica o desenvolvedor. Os usuários, mesmo sem esse conhecimento, recebem informações enviadas de um data center. Já bancos, hospitais, universidades, indústrias, empresas de comércio eletrônico, operadoras de telecomunicações, redes sociais, órgãos públicos e grandes plataformas de tecnologia utilizam os recursos do data center de forma direta para distribuir seus serviços. Data centers no Brasil Atualmente, o mercado brasileiro de data center está com ocupação de 96% dos data centers, de forma que novos clientes terão somente 4% disponíveis, estimado para manter assim até 2030, mesmo com a criação de novos projetos. A expectativa é que o mercado de data center no Brasil deva dobrar até 2030, atraindo investimentos bilionários, devido à demanda de novos centros. Segundo o Relatório de Mercado Data Center Brasil, realizado pela JLL, o estoque de data center cresceu mais de seis vezes desde 2012. Sendo a região de São Paulo, Barueri e Campinas a com a maior quantidade de datas ceters no país. Com o investimento em novas estruturas, é esperado que novos centros de processamento de dados surjam como alternativa; um deles é o de Fortaleza. Importância de data centers Felipe explica que os data centers se tornaram uma das infraestruturas mais importantes da economia digital, já que sustentam o funcionamento de algumas empresas e instituições, além de viabilizar o desenvolvimento de novas tecnologias. O desenvolvedor divide a importância dos data centers em três frentes: tecnológica, econômica e ambiental. A instalação de novos centros de processamento de dados atrai investimentos expressivos, movimenta a área da construção civil e sustenta o funcionamento de sistemas de informações disponíveis. Apesar disso, no quesito ambiental, essas construções enfrentam desafios significativos, como o consumo de água para o resfriamento dos servidores em funcionamento e o alto gasto de energia elétrica, tanto para alimentar os equipamentos quanto para manter a temperatura adequada. "Por isso, a expansão do setor exige planejamento para evitar pressões excessivas sobre a infraestrutura energética e os recursos hídricos das regiões onde essas instalações são construídas. Nesse contexto, cresce a busca por data centers mais eficientes, com equipamentos que realizam mais processamento utilizando menos energia, sistemas avançados de refrigeração e maior participação de fontes renováveis no fornecimento elétrico", afirma. artigo.texto: In a special meeting Thursday afternoon, Chatham County leaders voted unanimously to change a zoning ordinance so that language about data centers could be added. Leaders say this is an important step for the county in setting clear language that addresses data centers. The county board also voted to schedule a public hearing to address them. Other WRAL Top Stories The moratoriums are being put in place amid a wave of public backlash over data centers, particularly larger centers primarily focused on powering artificial intelligence infrastructure and tools. In February, Chatham County adopted a temporary moratorium on data centers. Chatham County residents, along with the nonprofit Haw River Assembly, said on Wednesday that they are pushing for a statewide moratorium on building data centers. "Small governments need time to put in regulations to protect from some of the harms these massive data centers can bring," said Amanda Robertson, chair of the Chatham County Board of Commissioners. The current moratorium is not stopping plans for a data center near Moncure. The county was sued by a property owner over its moratorium, and a Superior Court judge recently ruled in favor of the property owner. The developer, Eco TIP West, plans to build a 750-megawatt data center at the Triangle Innovation Point West business park. In April, it sued the county, saying its project was already in progress when county commissioners approved the moratorium and therefore should have been exempted. Despite the lawsuit, Chatham County has continued to develop regulations to address these new and intensive land uses—to protect Chatham County residents and the environment. A public hearing is set for Nov. 30 to consider any changes in development standards for data centers.

artigo.texto: Recurrent Energy, a subsidiary of Canadian Solar Inc., has completed the sale of two standalone battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in France to BW ESS, a global energy storage owner and operator. The transaction covers a combined capacity of 200 MW / 800 MWh and marks BW ESS’s entry into the French energy storage market. The deal also highlights Recurrent Energy’s growing presence in the battery storage sector and its ability to develop and monetize large-scale energy storage projects. The two projects included in the transaction are Baixas and Coquainvilliers, each with a capacity of 100 MW / 400 MWh. Baixas is located in the Pyrénées-Orientales department in southern France, while Coquainvilliers is situated in the Calvados department in northern France. Together, the projects are expected to provide 200 MW of power capacity and 800 MWh of energy storage to support the French electricity system. Both projects have secured advanced transmission-level grid connection positions and have been developed based on favourable grid conditions. According to the companies, the projects are expected to face very limited network constraints, which could support their integration into the electricity network and enable them to provide flexibility services to the power system. Recurrent Energy originated and developed both projects, undertaking key development activities, including securing land, advancing grid connections, obtaining permits and managing engagement with local stakeholders. The company will continue to oversee the projects through the remaining development stages, using its technical capabilities and understanding of the French energy market. Following the completion of the remaining development milestones, BW ESS will take responsibility for delivering the projects through construction and into commercial operation. The company plans to own and operate both battery storage facilities over the long term. This arrangement will allow Recurrent Energy to continue contributing its development expertise while BW ESS expands its portfolio of operational energy storage assets. For BW ESS, the acquisition represents its first transaction with Recurrent Energy and provides an immediate 200 MW / 800 MWh platform in France. The company stated that the projects would establish a foundation for developing a larger energy storage portfolio in the country as it expands its global operations. Erik Strømsø, CEO and Co-Founder of BW ESS, said the acquisition was an important milestone in the company’s international expansion. He highlighted France’s growing requirement for electricity system flexibility, particularly as weather-sensitive demand and changes in the generation mix create more variable power supply and demand conditions. He also noted that battery storage could complement France’s nuclear-based electricity generation by providing rapid-response flexibility, absorbing surplus electricity and making low-carbon power available when required. Dylan Marx, CEO of Recurrent Energy, said the transaction demonstrated the company’s ability to develop high-quality BESS projects and create value while remaining involved throughout their development. He added that the projects would support grid stability, balance electricity supply and demand, and facilitate the integration of renewable energy into France’s electricity system once operational. The transaction strengthens both companies’ positions in the European energy storage market, while adding 800 MWh of planned battery storage capacity to France’s developing electricity flexibility infrastructure. artigo.texto: Evergy executive answers questions about data centers after email to customers LEE’S SUMMIT, Mo. (KCTV) - Evergy says it has turned down data centers that couldn’t meet its requirements for large electricity customers. The company sent an email to customers on Monday about its rules for data centers. KCTV5 asked local data center opponents for their follow-up questions that the email did not address in detail, then took those questions to Chuck Caisley, Evergy’s chief consumer officer. Caisley said the email was sent to dispel misunderstanding that has developed as concerns about data centers have grown locally and nationally. “There’s a lot of information floating around online, but a lot of it isn’t accurate,” Caisley said. “It’s from different parts of the country and just projected here. We wanted to answer some of the key questions we knew our customers had.” Questions for Evergy Evergy says it can’t simply refuse to serve data centers, unless those needs would jeopardize what other customers need. “We’re not an advocate for or against data centers,” Caisley said. “That’s not our job. Our job is to protect our existing customers and make sure that if data centers come to our area, they don’t jeopardize our reliability and they don’t negatively impact rates.” He frequently used the term “existing customers” but later clarified that he means all customers, current or future, who do not fit into the special “large load” category of large data centers. Asked whether Evergy has said no to anyone, Caisley said yes. “We’ve probably said no to dozens of data centers that just couldn’t meet the requirements that we’ve set out,” Caisley said. Asked what happens if other customers need more power during peak periods or due to growth in other sectors, Caisley said: “We can turn down or turn off to make sure that there’s still enough generation for our existing customers.” The rules apply to new facilities using 75 megawatts or more, and to existing customers who expand by that much. Asked if there are any other facilities in Evergy’s service area that require that amount of energy, he said not yet. “Panasonic is getting close, but no, right now data centers are an exclusive club over 75 megawatts,” Caisley said. Rates, collateral and who is covered Caisley said large load customers pay a premium over other large customers. He described how that money is used. “That money is put together in a pool and used to reduce future rate increases for our other customers,” Caisley said. In testimony at an Oct. 8, 2025, Kansas Corporation Commission hearing, KCC staff witness Justin Grady estimated large load customers would pay 7% to 10% more than existing industrial customers. The estimate is cited in the commission’s Nov. 6, 2025, order approving the Evergy plan. Caisley described the premium another way. He said large load customers pay about 20% more than other “similarly situated customers.” Additionally, large load customers pay for equipment built just to serve them. Their contracts also include early exit penalties and collateral. Asked what happens if the business goes bankrupt, Caisley emphasized that customers must post collateral in one of several forms. “They have to post either a letter of credit or cash or in some cases we have a parental company guarantee if they’re a big enough company,” Caisley said, citing parent companies like Meta or Google in some cases. Some of the rules stem from Missouri Senate Bill 4, passed in 2025. It requires the Missouri Public Service Commission to adopt large load rates that reflect those customers’ share of costs and keep other customers from paying unjust or unreasonable costs. The law applies to the investor-owned utilities the commission regulates. The Kansas rules came through a different process. Evergy applied to the Kansas Corporation Commission in February 2025 for approval of a Large Load Power Service rate plan. The commission approved a unanimous settlement on Nov. 6, 2025. The KCC says it does not regulate municipal utilities or electric cooperatives. Caisley said Evergy’s large load customer rules have been in place for months. He said every hyperscale data center in Evergy’s service area has to follow the rules because all of those data centers came about after the rules went into effect. Copyright 2026 KCTV. Released Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Reports related to this article: Written by Danny Levin, Deputy Editor for IIR News Intelligence (Sugar Land, Texas) Summary Elon Musk says Tesla's Megapack battery energy-storage systems are nearly sold out through 2027. Demand for Tesla's Megapacks During Tesla's recent third-quarter earnings conference call, chief executive officer Elon Musk said the company's Megapack battery-energy storage systems are nearly sold out through 2027. "Energy demand is very strong," Musk said in the October 21 call. "We are actually almost sold out of all Megapacks for 2027, and we are ramping production as quickly as possible to meet demand. We also expect gross margins on that to increase meaningfully." Industrial Info Resources data show more than $30 billion worth of active and planned projects that are using, or considering using, Tesla's Megapack battery-energy storage system (BESS) units. Tesla's energy generation and storage business, its highest-margin hardware business line, recorded a 33.1% gross margin in the third quarter--an increase from 20.4% in the previous quarter. The company deployed 13.7 gigawatt-hours of energy storage, indicating its second-best quarterly performance. Also in the call, Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja said the margin improvement is mainly due to tariff refunds and warranty adjustments. Tesla recently began producing its Megapack 3 batteries at its facility in Brookshire, Texas. Megapack 3 is the company's third-generation utility-scale system, which features lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells. In order to support future assembly of Megapack 3s, Tesla earlier this year signed a deal with LG Energy Solution to source $4.3 billion worth of LFP cells. View the related project report here. artigo.texto: Rooftop solar energy systems, paired with battery energy storage, are one of the most effective ways to bring down household energy bills. A typical installation saves many hundreds of pounds each year, the precise amount varying according to capacity, configuration and location. “With the Warm Homes Loan Scheme now in place, more homes can go solar next year than ever before, taking control of their energy and insulating themselves from high energy bills” said Chris Hewett, Chief Executive of Solar Energy UK. “Critically, it will ensure that households across society can overcome any financial barriers, making sure that the benefits are felt where they are most needed. We are already expecting the annual record for smaller-scale solar systems to be broken within a few weeks. I have every confidence that the scheme will help deliver yet another record next year, over and above the 300,000 we expect to see this year. That in turn means employing more people, cutting energy bills and fuel poverty, delivering economic growth and cutting dependence on increasingly expensive natural gas. The Warm Homes Loan Scheme was first trumpeted in the Labour’s 2024 manifesto, as part of the Warm Homes Plan. It is comparable to a Scottish Government programme that formerly offered interest-free loans for home solar installations, which had a significant impact on fuel poverty. Rather than being provided directly by the state, the loans will be made available across the UK via a series of partners, including Solar Energy UK members Sunsave and E.ON (via Homeserve). Interest rates will be cut by up to 5 percent on the rate that would otherwise apply, saving customers hundreds of pounds a year and ensuring that savings exceed repayments. Loans for solar panels will be capped at up to £15,000, enough to secure an array substantially larger than the household average. The same cap will apply for battery energy storage, again plentiful. “Two further aspects of the scheme are also very welcome” added Gemma Grimes, Solar Energy UK’s Director of Policy and Delivery. “All home energy upgrades, barring connections to heat networks, will be conducted by installers certified by the standards body MCS, with whom we work closely. This will help secure and maintain consumer confidence. Grants for heat pumps will also remain, under the government’s Boiler Upgrade Scheme (and Home Energy Scotland in Scotland), further reducing the cost of installations.” For additional information:

artigo.texto: O Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias (BESS) na subestação de 110 kV de Uong Bi, com capacidade de 5 MW/10 MWh, desempenha um papel estratégico na otimização do fornecimento e regulação de energia na região. Este é um dos principais projetos de uma série de iniciativas iniciadas em junho de 2026, com a Northern Power Construction Project Management Board (Northern Power Corporation) como investidora. O projeto do Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias (BESS, na sigla em inglês) na subestação de 110 kV de Uong Bi foi energizado. Para garantir a estabilidade e melhorar a capacidade operacional do sistema de energia, a Quang Ninh Power Company, em coordenação com as unidades relevantes, está realizando os testes de aceitação, os testes de aceitação técnica e a energização do projeto de instalação do Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias (BESS) na subestação de 110kV de Uong Bi. A entrada em operação do sistema BESS na subestação de 110 kV de Uong Bi visa complementar as soluções de armazenamento e regulação de energia para a rede elétrica regional. O sistema é capaz de armazenar eletricidade quando necessário e retomar a geração de energia na rede nos momentos oportunos, ajudando assim a reduzir a pressão sobre a carga durante os horários de pico, aumentando a flexibilidade operacional e a confiabilidade do fornecimento de energia. Essa tecnologia contribui para a melhoria da utilização eficiente de fontes de energia renováveis, atendendo às necessidades de eletricidade para o desenvolvimento socioeconômico . Anteriormente, a Quang Ninh Power Company realizou testes de aceitação e energizou dois sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) nas subestações de 110 kV de Gieng Day e de 110 kV de Trang Bach. O sistema em Gieng Day tem capacidade de 10 MW e capacidade de armazenamento de 20 MWh; o sistema em Trang Bach tem capacidade de 5 MW e capacidade de armazenamento de 10 MWh. Com a energização do sistema BESS na subestação de 110 kV de Uong Bi, todos os três sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, parte da fase inicial implementada pela Northern Power Corporation na cidade, entraram em operação. Isso contribui para melhorar a eficiência da infraestrutura da rede elétrica existente e garantir um fornecimento de energia seguro e estável.

artigo.texto: O governo terá de definir exatamente o que é um serviço de data center para colocar o Redata em funcionamento. A tarefa parece simples, mas envolve uma questão que pode decidir quem terá ou não acesso aos benefícios do novo regime: a Nomenclatura Brasileira de Serviços (NBS), tabela oficial usada pelo país para classificar serviços, está em sua versão de 2018, anterior à explosão da inteligência artificial e à transformação do mercado de infraestrutura computacional. Sete dias depois da sanção da lei que instituiu o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Center (Redata), representantes do Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC) e da Receita Federal realizaram, em 22 de setembro, a primeira reunião do novo Comitê Gestor da NBS. O colegiado foi criado justamente para receber, analisar e propor alterações nessa classificação. Seu regimento, aprovado naquela reunião, só foi publicado no Diário Oficial da União nesta quinta-feira, 29 de outubro. A proximidade das datas chama atenção, mas não há até agora documento público demonstrando que o Redata tenha sido discutido no encontro. O Capital Digital procurou a ata e as propostas analisadas pelo Comitê, mas esses documentos não foram localizados nas páginas públicas consultadas. A importância da NBS para o Redata está na própria estrutura do regime. Para conceder tratamento tributário diferenciado à infraestrutura digital, o governo precisa transformar conceitos como data center, computação em nuvem, processamento de alto desempenho e serviços associados à inteligência artificial em classificações objetivas. Em termos simples, a NBS funciona como um catálogo oficial dos serviços existentes na economia. Em vez de o governo falar genericamente em “computação em nuvem”, por exemplo, a nomenclatura permite identificar a atividade por código e descrição. Essa classificação pode ser usada em políticas públicas, tributação, comércio exterior e estatísticas. Isso não significa que os novos serviços digitais estejam necessariamente fora da classificação atual. Categorias mais amplas podem comportar parte dessas atividades. A questão é saber se os códigos e descrições existentes são suficientemente precisos para uma política tributária criada especificamente para incentivar a instalação de infraestrutura de data centers no Brasil. É aí que entra o Comitê Gestor criado neste ano pelo MDIC e pelo Ministério da Fazenda. Formado por representantes da Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Industrial, Inovação, Comércio e Serviços e da Receita Federal, ele poderá receber e avaliar propostas de mudança tanto da NBS quanto de suas notas explicativas. Empresas, associações e órgãos públicos podem propor alterações. Os pedidos admitidos devem ter uma versão pública divulgada durante 30 dias para manifestações de terceiros antes da análise definitiva. O Capital Digital examinou a planilha disponibilizada pelo MDIC para divulgar essas propostas. O arquivo está vazio. Portanto, pelo instrumento oficial de transparência, não aparece até agora qualquer proposta pública para criar ou modificar classificações relacionadas a data centers, nuvem, inteligência artificial ou processamento de alto desempenho. Isso não significa que inexistam discussões internas. O regimento permite propostas originadas no próprio governo e estabelece prioridade para iniciativas apresentadas de ofício pelos integrantes do Comitê e por órgãos públicos. Por isso, a ata da primeira reunião tornou-se um documento relevante para saber se alguma adequação relacionada ao Redata já começou a ser discutida. A questão ganha peso porque a classificação dos serviços não interessa apenas ao novo regime dos data centers. A reforma tributária também exige maior precisão na identificação das diferentes modalidades de serviços para implantação da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS) e do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS). Na prática, MDIC e Receita passam a ocupar uma posição estratégica. Enquanto o governo incentiva investimentos bilionários em data centers e infraestrutura de inteligência artificial, os dois órgãos administram justamente o instrumento que pode ajudar a estabelecer quais atividades serão enquadradas nas novas políticas tributárias. A diferença pode ser grande. Um data center moderno não vende apenas espaço para servidores. Pode oferecer armazenamento, processamento, computação em nuvem, capacidade computacional, treinamento e inferência de modelos de IA e outros serviços agregados. A forma como o governo enquadrar essas atividades poderá influenciar quais receitas serão consideradas serviços abrangidos pelo regime. A regulamentação do Redata terá, portanto, de responder uma questão central: quais códigos e descrições serão utilizados para enquadrar os serviços beneficiados? O governo poderá usar as categorias já existentes ou concluir que precisa atualizá-las. O novo Comitê Gestor oferece justamente o caminho institucional para fazer essa revisão. Por enquanto, sabe-se que sua primeira reunião ocorreu uma semana depois da sanção do Redata e que não há propostas de alteração submetidas à consulta pública na planilha oficial do MDIC. O que ainda não se sabe é se a adequação da classificação dos serviços de data center, nuvem e inteligência artificial já começou a ser discutida internamente. Antes de o benefício tributário chegar aos data centers, portanto, há uma decisão menos visível, mas importante: definir com precisão quais serviços da nova economia digital estarão dentro do Redata.

artigo.texto: VAN BUREN -- Data center companies interested in Van Buren will now need to meet strict planning reviews and application regulations. Van Buren City Council members voted unanimously Monday to approve an ordinance amending the zoning chapter of its municipal code to better regulate data centers. Wally Bailey, planning director, said the city has yet to see a data center express interest in building there but that doesn't mean it will not happen in the future. Some of the requirements in the new regulations include having companies building the data center acquire a third-party noise study, a plan to mitigate any increase in noise above what considered a noise disturbance and having the building be set back 1,000 feet from any zoning district that permits residential uses. Bailey said the amended municipal code will require any possible data centers to provide the city information on what their impact might be and if they will require any additional utility connections. He noted some centers require gas lines in order to power turbines. "We wanted to get something on the books to get started and have something so we wouldn't be caught having someone walk in wanting to do something and we don't have anything," Bailey said. Councilwoman Tonia Fry said she was appreciative of the work by Bailey and other city officials in helping the city get ahead of any possible issues. Bailey said he took into account what some other counties across the state were doing when creating the ordinance but also had to factor in how much manpower the city could put forward to regulations. Some counties have very extensive regulations which would require the city to hire more people in order to enforce the regulations, Bailey said. Under the city's ordinance, developers of data centers will be required to submit various plans about the project for approval, Bailey said. He said this will include presenting site plans, landscaping plans and other documents to the city's Planning Commission. Bailey said this will allow residents to come in and voice their concerns about the plans and those concerns addressed by the developer. "It won't just be somebody walking in and coming up to the window and saying I want a permit for a $1 billion data center," he said. "It will be a much more involved process than that." Bailey said if disagreements are had about the permitting process, the review of these types of data centers can be brought before the City Council. Overall, Bailey said he wants as much review of the process as much as possible to protect the city and its residents from having a data center where it is not wanted. Councilman Kody Morris expressed concerns regarding data centers being a permitted use in the city's Industrial-2 zoning under the new ordinance. Morris said he wondered if the centers should not require a conditional-use permit to be built in the city rather than permitted. He said other uses that require a permit in industrial zoning include retail buildings, offices, banks, libraries, churches, homeless shelters and gun ranges. "To me, having a data center is a hot topic right now and if you are going to make a school or a church go through that then surely we can make a billion-dollar company go through that," Morris said. Bailey said, while the use may not require a conditional use permit, building a data center in the city still requires submitting documents for a plan review that would serve the same purpose. Many of the uses that require a conditional-use permit in industrial zoning bring more residential traffic than the industrial traffic that may not blend well with it, Bailey said. Bailey said on top of the ordinance passed Monday, he would not be surprised if the issue of data centers was addressed by the state legislature. "Because so many cities are passing laws that are all a little bit different, I wouldn't be a bit surprised if something doesn't come up in the next legislative session or the next one, fine tuning what cities can do or not do," Bailey said. artigo.texto: A equipe técnica opera os equipamentos em preparação para a energização das subestações. Com o crescente desenvolvimento de fontes de energia distribuída e energias renováveis, o sistema elétrico impõe maiores exigências em relação ao equilíbrio entre oferta e demanda, à regulação de energia e à operação flexível. Portanto, a tecnologia de armazenamento de energia é considerada uma das soluções tecnológicas importantes para atender a essas exigências. O Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias (BESS) implantado em subestações de 110 kV possui uma configuração de potência e capacidade de armazenamento de 5 MW/10 MWh e 10 MW/20 MWh, juntamente com um Sistema de Conversão de Energia (PCS), um Sistema de Gerenciamento de Energia (EMS), um Sistema de Gerenciamento de Baterias (BMS), um sistema de proteção e um sistema SCADA integrados de forma síncrona. Diferentemente dos sistemas tradicionais de transmissão e distribuição de energia, o BESS (Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias) tem a capacidade de armazenar energia elétrica e devolvê-la ao sistema quando necessário. O sistema pode absorver energia no momento apropriado e devolvê-la à rede de acordo com a demanda operacional, contribuindo assim para uma melhor gestão do sistema elétrico. A entrada em operação do sistema BESS nos distritos de Lap Thach, Ba Thien, Bac Viet Tri, Phu Ninh, Dong Xuan, Ninh Dan, Cam Khe e Thuy Van não só adiciona um novo tipo de equipamento tecnológico à rede elétrica, como também contribui para promover a aplicação de tecnologia digital , automação e soluções de armazenamento de energia na gestão operacional. Este resultado também abre uma nova abordagem na gestão da operação da rede elétrica, visando utilizar eficazmente as soluções de armazenamento de energia e atender aos requisitos de uma operação de sistemas de energia cada vez mais flexíveis e confiáveis. Oficiais e funcionários de diversas unidades inspecionam o sistema de armazenamento de energia por baterias (BESS). Como unidade designada para gerenciar e operar o sistema, a tarefa definida para a Phu Tho High Voltage Power Grid Enterprise é organizar a gestão e a operação de acordo com as responsabilidades atribuídas, cumprindo os procedimentos técnicos e os requisitos de segurança para novos equipamentos. Diferentemente dos equipamentos elétricos tradicionais, os sistemas BESS combinam tecnologia de baterias, eletrônica de potência, controle automático e monitoramento de dados, exigindo que os operadores abordem o equipamento de forma holística, com um conhecimento profundo tanto dos estados elétricos quanto tecnológicos. A implantação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) em 8 subestações também exige um aprimoramento gradual da capacidade da equipe em acessar novas tecnologias. Esse processo não só serve à gestão dos sistemas recém-comissionados, como também contribui para a aquisição de experiência prática, acompanhando a tendência de desenvolvimento da rede elétrica rumo à modernização, automação e maior aplicação de tecnologia digital. Thuy Linh - Quang Dao (Empresa de Rede Elétrica de Alta Tensão de Phu Tho)

artigo.texto: Stand-alone battery energy storage systems can respond rapidly to grid and market requirements without being tied to a specific generation asset. Through merchant applications, storage can capture multiple value opportunities while supporting the balancing, flexibility, and resilience needs of a power system with a growing share of variable renewable energy. The three-project structure combines targeted project sizes with a shared delivery approach. With two 5MWh systems and one 10MWh system, the portfolio is designed to provide adaptable storage capacity across different merchant use cases and market conditions. The projects are built on the Jinko Tera liquid-cooled energy storage system (5.01MWh). Tuned for merchant trading, the system captures peak-valley spreads with a tested 94.1% conversion efficiency and low-power standby modes, while its grid-forming capability and fast response enable it to flexibly meet grid-balancing and regulation demands, providing a robust hardware foundation for the portfolio's multi-scenario participation in spot and ancillary-services markets. Roberto Murgioni, General Manager of Jinko ESS Europe, said, “We are very pleased to build on our collaboration through this three-project portfolio. This portfolio shows how stand-alone BESS can provide targeted flexibility across projects of different sizes. We look forward to supporting their long-term success with reliable technology, operational expertise and close partnership.”

artigo.texto: CATL hit another milestone in its solid-state battery development, advancing to 20 Ah cells. The world’s leading battery maker aims to begin small-scale production in 2027. CATL continues advancing solid-state EV batteries CATL remains the leading global EV battery manufacturer by a wide margin. According to SNE Research, CATL held a commanding 39.9% share of the global EV battery market through the first half of 2026. To stay ahead, the company is advancing several new battery chemistries, including solid-state and sodium-ion, promising to be safer, more efficient, and lower cost than traditional lithium-ion batteries. When investors asked about the progress of its solid-state battery program on Tuesday, CATL said it continues to invest heavily in all-solid-state batteries and expects to begin small-scale production in 2027. As it has stated before, output is expected to be limited at first as it scales up to mass production around 2030. Speaking at the Summer Davos Forum in June, CATL chairman and CEO Robin Zeng said that, on a scale of one to nine, all-solid-state batteries have only reached level four. All-solid-state batteries differ from semi-solid-state batteries in that they require a solid electrolyte to conduct lithium ions, rather than a liquid. The company uses a sulfide-based solid electrolyte system, which offers high ionic conductivity and deformability, but maintaining stable contact between solid components remains a hurdle. CATL said its sulfide-based batteries have now entered 20 Ah trial production as it aims to achieve an energy density of 500 Wh/kg. Trial production in 2027, reaching mass market in 2030 CATL’s 2027 timeline to begin small-scale production aligns with other automakers and battery manufacturers racing to introduce all-solid-state EV batteries. Toyota, which has been promising solid-state batteries for nearly a decade now, aims to launch the first all-solid-state battery-powered EV in 2027 or 2028. Using Sumitomo Metal Mining’s proprietary powder synthesis technology, Toyota claimed to have developed a “highly durable cathode material” for all-solid-state batteries last October. Toyota revealed a prototype last year, claiming it can deliver 745 miles (1,200 km) of range and charge in under 10 minutes. However, like CATL, Toyota expects production to be limited and will not reach the mass market until closer to the end of the decade. Samsung SDI, on the other hand, aims to begin mass production of its SolidStack all-solid-state batteries in the second half of 2027. BYD, which ranks second in global EV battery sales behind CATL, also plans to launch its first solid-state battery-powered vehicle in 2027. In an exclusive interview with Carwow.es last month, executive vice president Stella Li said BYD is in “the leading position” on solid-state batteries and will “prove that” next year. BYD’s battery division, FinDreams, aims to begin producing sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries in limited batches in 2027, ramping up to mass production by 2030. Electrek’s Take While solid-state batteries are often hailed the “holy grail” of battery tech, they are only one part of the equation. Top comment by AutoMotive Toyota is not to be trusted as their press briefings are misinformation over facts for the past 10 years. CATL has legitimacy and timeline is a maybe. Mass produced for ev is a huge under taking before applications for small electronics tools lawn mowers motorcycles. They need to crawl before they walk. CATL, BYD, and others continue advancing lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion batteries, which will ultimately create more efficient, lower-cost options that offer various performance needs. BYD’s second-generation Blade LFP batteries already deliver over 1,000 km (621 miles) of CLTC range. What’s next? One thing is certain: New battery chemistries and evolving tech will only continue making EVs more efficient, unlocking longer driving ranges, faster charging speeds, and better performance. artigo.texto: Entre janeiro de 2023 e junho de 2026, a Anthropic destinou US$ 19,2 bilhões à aquisição de capacidade computacional e infraestrutura de IA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL Anthropic prevê gastos de US$ 1 trilhão com chips e data centers até 2045 Por Redação A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do assistente de inteligência artificial Claude, poderá desembolsar cerca de US$ 1 trilhão (R$ 5,33 trilhões) em chips e infraestrutura de processamento de dados até 2045. A estimativa consta de informações financeiras divulgadas pela companhia em meio ao processo de abertura de capital nos Estados Unidos e evidencia a dimensão dos investimentos necessários para sustentar o avanço da inteligência artificial (IA). Segundo os dados apresentados, a empresa acumulava, até junho de 2026, compromissos de aproximadamente US$ 587 bilhões com infraestrutura tecnológica. Nos quatro meses seguintes, foram acrescentados US$ 266 bilhões em contratos novos e revisados. A companhia também prevê gastos adicionais com equipamentos da AMD e chips desenvolvidos pelo Google. Entre os principais fornecedores estão gigantes da tecnologia como Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Nvidia e Broadcom. O maior contrato individual envolve a Broadcom, com US$ 161 bilhões destinados ao fornecimento de semicondutores e infraestrutura. Também se destacam os acordos de US$ 114,5 bilhões com o Google, US$ 110 bilhões com a Amazon e US$ 45 bilhões com a Microsoft. A Anthropic ainda possui um contrato de US$ 120,5 bilhões para acessar processadores gráficos da Nvidia por meio da SpaceX, empresa de Elon Musk. Com a entrega integral da capacidade contratada, prevista para dezembro, o custo mensal poderá alcançar US$ 3,1 bilhões. O volume projetado representa uma expansão expressiva em relação aos investimentos já realizados pela companhia. Entre janeiro de 2023 e junho de 2026, a Anthropic destinou US$ 19,2 bilhões à aquisição de capacidade computacional e infraestrutura de IA. No mesmo período, a receita acumulada chegou a US$ 21,3 bilhões, dos quais US$ 16,3 bilhões foram registrados somente no primeiro semestre de 2026. O resultado representa crescimento de 1.300% na comparação anual. Apesar da expansão do faturamento, os compromissos bilionários ampliam os desafios financeiros da empresa. A sustentabilidade dos investimentos dependerá da manutenção do crescimento das receitas e da capacidade de competir com a OpenAI e outras desenvolvedoras de modelos de inteligência artificial. A divulgação dos números ocorre em meio aos preparativos para a estreia da Anthropic na bolsa de valores. A companhia, fundada em 2021, foi avaliada em US$ 965 bilhões em uma rodada de financiamento realizada em maio de 2026.

(JHVEPhoto / iStock) Reading Time: 2minutes The U.S. Department of Energy announced a $5.1 billion loan to Alliant Energy on Wednesday, including $1.6 billion for Wisconsin Power and Light, Wisconsin’s third-largest electrical utility. Alliant spokesperson Cindy Tomlinson told Wisconsin Watch that the loan may support the construction of a natural gas storage facility in Rock County and a pair of battery storage facilities — one in southwestern Wisconsin and another near Sheboygan — among other possibilities. All three still require approval from the Wisconsin Public Service Commission. The loan itself doesn’t name those projects, and Tomlinson noted that the federal dollars could also support efforts to restart or repurpose shuttered power plants or build new natural gas plants. The company estimates Wisconsin ratepayers will save $400 million over the life of the loan. “To the extent that tax dollars are used to help pay for projects that are approved,” Wisconsin Citizens Utility Board Executive Director Tom Content wrote in an email, “that should lower the overall cost over 20-40 years.” The deal dates back to the final days of the Biden administration, when the Department of Energy’s Loan Programs Office focused on shoring up clean energy projects that otherwise struggled to get bank loans. The office mulled cancelling existing clean energy loans after President Trump’s return to the White House in January 2025, Bloomberg reported. The new loan language doesn’t explicitly bar spending on renewable energy infrastructure. It instead allows the utility to direct funding to “energy infrastructure and related projects that increase energy supply or enhance grid reliability, including but not limited to nuclear, coal, oil, natural gas, geothermal or hydropower power generation facilities.” “The Energy Department is delivering on President Trump’s promise to lower electricity costs and unleash the full potential of American energy,” U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said in a statement. artigo.texto: Nova bateria da GAC promete mais de 1.000 km de rodagem em carros elétricos Tecnologia em desenvolvimento alcança densidade energética superior a 400 Wh/kg e tem previsão de estrear em modelos da marca de luxo Hyper ainda em 2026 O Grupo GAC anunciou nesta quarta-feira (28) o avanço no desenvolvimento de suas baterias de estado sólido, migrando a tecnologia da fase de pesquisas para a linha de produção-piloto em sua matriz em Guangzhou, na China. O componente alcançou uma densidade energética superior a 400 Wh/kg, índice projetado para viabilizar veículos 100% elétricos com autonomia superior a 1.000 km com uma única carga. A tecnologia substitui o eletrólito líquido convencional das baterias íon-lítio por um composto sólido, permitindo o uso de ânodos de lítio metálico e a construção de estruturas mais compactas. A promessa da montadora chinesa é aplicar a inovação em modelos comerciais da Hyper, sua divisão premium de veículos elétricos, ainda em 2026. Processo e redução de custos Além dos ganhos em alcance e estabilidade térmica, a fabricante desenvolveu um método de produção que combina eletrodos secos, transferência de eletrólito fino e fusão de interface diretamente no local de montagem, garantindo um contato ideal sem a necessidade de etapas complexas de colagem. Segundo estimativas da própria empresa, a consolidação desse processo fabril em larga escala pode reduzir em 15% os investimentos em equipamentos, cortar em 40% a área necessária para as instalações industriais e diminuir em mais de 35% os custos de produção das baterias. O movimento da GAC ocorre em meio a uma corrida da indústria automotiva global por maior eficiência energética e alcance na mobilidade elétrica. Recentemente, a BMW também deu início à produção em série de suas baterias Gen6 na planta de Shenyang, na China, apostando na tecnologia cell-to-pack para elevar a densidade de energia em mais de 20% e a autonomia em até 30% em sua futura linha de veículos Neue Klasse. Estratégia de eletrificação O projeto de baterias de estado sólido é desenvolvido pelo GAC Group desde 2014 e é tratado pela companhia como um pilar central para a próxima geração de automóveis elétricos. A transição para o estado sólido é vista por especialistas como a solução definitiva para mitigar a ansiedade por autonomia e acelerar o tempo de recarga nos modelos eletrificados de alta capacidade, duas das maiores preocupações dos clientes e possíveis compradores de automóveis na atualidade.

artigo.texto: Aneel aprova editais de dois leilões de sistemas de baterias para dezembro Certames terão contratos de 15 anos, com início do suprimento em agosto de 2028; preços-teto serão de R$ 1,76 milhão e R$ 1,58 milhão por megawatt ao ano A Aneel (Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica) aprovou, por unanimidade, nesta terça-feira (27), os editais dos dois leilões de reserva de capacidade destinados à contratação de novos sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias. As disputas estão previstas para 2 e 4 de dezembro, com início do suprimento em 1º de agosto de 2028 e contratos de 15 anos. O primeiro certame, denominado Armazenamento Nacional, será destinado a projetos que atendam aos requisitos mínimos de conteúdo nacional do sistema de credenciamento de fornecedores do BNDES. O segundo será realizado na modalidade Armazenamento, sem a mesma exigência de nacionalização. Os preços-teto, definidos pelo Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME), serão de R$ 1,76 milhão por megawatt (MW) ao ano para o produto com conteúdo nacional e de R$ 1,58 milhão por MW ao ano para o outro certame. Os processos foram relatados pelo diretor Gentil Nogueira de Sá Júnior. A contratação remunerará a disponibilidade de potência das baterias para atender aos comandos do ONS (Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico). Os empreendimentos receberão uma receita fixa anual, paga em 12 parcelas mensais, sujeita a reduções conforme o desempenho operacional. A remuneração será devida independentemente do acionamento dos sistemas, observadas as obrigações contratuais. Os projetos deverão oferecer disponibilidade mínima de 30 MW e sustentar a potência máxima por quatro horas a cada ciclo completo. As regras preveem até dois ciclos diários, respeitado o limite de 366 ciclos anuais, e recarga completa em até seis horas. A eficiência total mínima exigida será de 85%. Os sistemas também deverão atender aos requisitos de conexão, incluindo a funcionalidade de formação de rede, conhecida como grid forming. A verificação pelo ONS ocorrerá durante o processo de integração das instalações ao sistema elétrico, como condição para a entrada em operação em teste e comercial. O custo da contratação será rateado exclusivamente entre os geradores de energia, conforme a legislação citada nos votos. O relator classificou o custeio como o tema mais controverso dos certames e registrou que a discussão em andamento no Congresso não afasta a obrigação da agência de cumprir a regra vigente. Entre as mudanças após as consultas públicas, a Aneel reduziu de R$ 9,8 milhões/MW para R$ 6 milhões por MW as garantias financeiras das exigências patrimoniais. A garantia de proposta será de R$ 60 mil por MW de disponibilidade máxima ofertável. Já a garantia de fiel cumprimento e o patrimônio líquido mínimo serão, cada um, de R$ 600 mil por MW vinculado ao lance. Os editais também permitirão consórcios entre empresas do mesmo grupo econômico, com regras para evitar a dupla contagem de patrimônio, e explicitarão a possibilidade de participação de concessionárias de transmissão, observadas as obrigações das concessões. Após apontamento da equipe técnica do Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU), a comprovação patrimonial deverá considerar os compromissos assumidos conjuntamente nos dois leilões. A agência manteve o risco de conexão com os empreendedores e rejeitou a prorrogação automática do início do suprimento por atrasos nas instalações de acesso. Também preservou o limite anual de 2,5% de indisponibilidade programada, equivalente a aproximadamente 219 horas, incluindo intervenções para recompor a capacidade das baterias ao longo do contrato.

artigo.texto: NIPSCO to deliver $57.5M in savings to electric customers from data center development The average residential electric customer is expected to receive approximately $90 total, or about $5 per month for 18 months. (WPTA) - NiSource Inc. announced Wednesday that it’ll deliver $57.5 million in savings to its existing electric customers generated through data center development. Subject to regulatory approval, the average residential electric customer is expected to receive a monthly bill credit of approximately $5 for 18 months, beginning approximately 30 days after approval. The credit is an expansion of the value being driven through the NiSource GenCo model and is an early example of how the region’s growth can create meaningful benefits for existing NIPSCO electric customers. The new credit builds on $1.75 billion in customer credits expected from previously announced agreements with Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft. Under those agreements, large-load customers will fund the infrastructure needed to serve them, while a portion of the revenues generated through their contracts will be returned directly to existing NIPSCO electric customers. Electric customers can expect the first of these credits to begin in the first quarter of 2027 and ramp up over time. “When our region grows, our customers share in the benefits,” said Vince Parisi, NIPSCO President and Chief Operating Officer. “Putting the value from data center development directly back on customers’ bills is one more way we’re turning growth into real savings for families across northern Indiana.” Visit NIPSCO.com to learn more about NIPSCO’s efforts to support customer affordability.
