artigo.texto: Newswise — The Department of Energy’s (DOE) Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is helping lead a national consortium focused on quickly moving energy storage innovations from the lab to U.S manufacturing. Called the Battery Manufacturing (BattMan) Accelerator, the consortium combines the power of four national laboratories, leading universities and industry partners to address critical barriers in scaling up new battery technologies. The accelerator will focus on lowering manufacturing costs, shortening development timelines, and strengthening U.S. manufacturing leadership in advanced energy storage solutions for the electric grid, data centers, electric mobility and national security. “The BattMan Accelerator is exactly the kind of coordinated national effort that turns scientific breakthroughs into economic and energy security advantages,” said Chins Chinnasamy, consortium lead for ORNL. “With our combination of expertise in Super Intelligence (SI)-driven smart manufacturing, real-time defect detection, and advanced electrode processing, ORNL is in a unique position to reduce commercialization risks for the American battery industry.” BattMan will also strengthen the critical mineral supply by advancing battery materials made from more abundant domestic elements. The BattMan Accelerator is led by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and includes Argonne National Laboratory and National Laboratory of the Rockies, as well as founding university partners including the University of Washington, Binghamton University, University of Alabama, Arizona State University, and University of Michigan-Dearborn. The accelerator is actively establishing collaborations with companies across the battery and materials manufacturing sector. The laboratories will work closely with these university partners and industry to test and validate manufacturing processes at increasing scales and toward commercially viable production. In the long term, the consortium aims to develop self-optimizing manufacturing systems using real-time data, automated feedback and digital twins that link virtual and real systems to safely model ways to improve performance. BattMan will build on the autonomous laboratory concept by advancing autonomous pilot lines. These integrate sensing, process monitoring and intelligent control systems to improve product quality and reduce variability in the manufacturing process. Pilot scale demonstration proves manufacturing readiness, speeding scale-up and reducing commercialization costs. The accelerator is actively establishing collaborations with companies within the battery and materials manufacturing sector. Scaling up discovery to manufacturing ORNL researchers constantly collaborate with industry partners in the manufacturing and energy storage sectors. Its BattMan research will take place in the Battery Manufacturing Facility (BMF), the country’s largest open-access battery manufacturing research and development center. Ruhul Amin, who leads electrode materials optimization for BattMan at ORNL, said companies work with ORNL battery experts at the BMF to incorporate and test new materials and designs in batteries made onsite with modular, reconfigurable commercial equipment. All battery manufacturing steps are incorporated into a coordinated, data-connected workflow. As part of BattMan, BMF will vertically integrate a smart test bed that incorporates advanced sensing, real-time monitoring, and data analysis. This modular system will enable both wet and dry electrode manufacturing approaches. In collaboration with NLR, which will focus on advanced characterization and SI‑driven quality control, ORNL will complement this work by developing a digital twin to further optimize and refine process performance. The outcome will be an SI-based manufacturing platform capable of detecting production irregularities as they occur and autonomously adjusting parameters to prevent defects. “If these electrodes are not produced correctly, that material is wasted —including critical materials like lithium and cobalt,” Chinnasamy said. “Up to 40 percent can end up as scrap. Working jointly with battery manufacturers, ORNL will design first-of-its-kind electrode manufacturing equipment that identifies even the smallest errors and corrects them in real time.” The goal is to reduce scrap to less than 5 percent, which will also reduce costs related to construction and supply chain bottlenecks, Chinnasamy said. The system will be adaptable for manufacturing any type of energy storage system. This could include conventional lithium-ion batteries used in vehicles, drones, electronics and grid energy storage batteries. But the system could also apply to solid state, flow batteries or next-generation chemistries. Research and industry partners will help make sure that the technology can bridge from lab to commercial scale with a variety of materials, autonomous synthesis and characterization, and high-throughput automation. Universities will also contribute to processing and integration capabilities and develop workforce training on the new processes and technologies. Parans Paranthaman will lead battery industry collaboration in BattMan for ORNL. SI plays key role in future of battery manufacturing SI has the potential to speed up discovery of new materials, improve efficiency of laboratory processes and support predictive, cost-effective design. In manufacturing specifically, SI could be helpful in more precisely identifying the source of contamination or other errors that might arise as batteries are produced on a bustling factory floor. BattMan is currently forming industry partnerships in battery and battery materials manufacturing. Institutions and companies interested in participating can visit www.pnnl.gov/battman. artigo.texto: HPE's Quantum Computing Bet: A Multi-Vendor Path to the Data Center Key Highlights - HPE’s collaboration with QuEra targets future on-premises integration of neutral-atom quantum systems with HPE Cray supercomputers. - HPE is working across competing quantum architectures to avoid committing its infrastructure strategy to a single processor technology. - Quantum installations have architecture-specific facility requirements, ranging from cryogenic cooling to precision lasers, vacuum systems, vibration isolation and environmental controls. - Specialized classical processors will handle time-critical quantum control and error correction, while HPC systems support broader hybrid computing workloads. - Existing demonstrations establish integration feasibility, but commercially scalable fault-tolerant systems and viable deployment economics remain unproven. Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is approaching quantum computing as an infrastructure integration challenge rather than a race to develop its own quantum processor. The company is positioning its HPE Cray supercomputing platforms as a foundation for bringing quantum systems into established high-performance computing (HPC) and data center environments. HPE's September 22 collaboration announcement with neutral-atom quantum computing developer QuEra Computing expands a relationship dating to 2025. The companies aim to integrate future fault-tolerant quantum systems with on-premises HPE Cray infrastructure, enabling quantum processors and conventional supercomputers to operate within coordinated computing environments. The effort builds on HPE's June expansion of collaborations with eight quantum technology companies, spanning competing processor architectures along with quantum control systems, error-correction technologies and software interoperability. For data center operators, the implications extend well beyond adding another type of computing accelerator. Depending on the architecture, quantum systems can require extreme cryogenic cooling, precision lasers, vacuum equipment, vibration isolation and specialized environmental controls. They also depend on classical computing resources for measurement processing, system control and increasingly demanding error-correction workloads. Integrating those requirements with existing HPC infrastructure presents challenges that could prove as consequential to commercial deployment as advances in quantum processors themselves. HPE's strategy is to provide the classical computing infrastructure surrounding those emerging technologies without committing to a single quantum architecture. Research installations have already demonstrated that quantum processors can operate alongside conventional supercomputing resources. The more consequential question is whether HPE and its partners can turn those early integrations into reliable, repeatable and commercially supportable fault-tolerant systems. QuEra Deal Targets On-Premises Quantum Integration Under the expanded collaboration, HPE and QuEra intend to develop integrated testbeds, software interoperability, hybrid algorithms and performance benchmarks to support future quantum deployments alongside HPE Cray supercomputing infrastructure. The work is intended to address the practical requirements of coordinating quantum processors with the classical computing systems that prepare workloads, process results and support quantum error correction. QuEra Chief Commercial Officer Yuval Boger, who previously discussed the development of hybrid quantum-classical infrastructure on the DCF Show, emphasized that integrating quantum hardware into an HPC environment presents different engineering challenges than providing access through the cloud. Boger said, “HPE's deep experience in supercomputing gives organizations the benefit of working with a partner who can solve that problem at the scale they need.” The collaboration envisions deploying future fault-tolerant quantum hardware at customer facilities rather than requiring organizations to rely exclusively on cloud-based quantum computing services. That option could appeal to national laboratories, defense organizations, pharmaceutical researchers and other institutions managing classified information, proprietary intellectual property or data subject to sovereignty requirements. QuEra's neutral-atom architecture uses individual atoms as qubits, manipulating them with lasers and electromagnetic controls. Unlike superconducting quantum processors, which generally require dilution refrigerators operating at temperatures measured in millikelvin, neutral-atom systems can operate without extreme cryogenic refrigeration. They still require specialized laser systems, vacuum equipment, precision optics and environmental controls, presenting facility requirements substantially different from those of conventional servers. On-premises quantum-HPC integration is already being tested. In Japan, the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST) operates QuEra's 260-physical-qubit Gemini neutral-atom computer as part of its ABCI-Q research platform, which also incorporates an NVIDIA H100-based AI supercomputer. An October 26 case study published by QuEra describes Gemini operating in a separate building approximately 350 meters from the main GPU installation, mounted on vibration-isolation equipment and connected through a software-defined network. The installation demonstrates how specialized quantum hardware can be incorporated into a broader computing environment without occupying the same physical space as conventional HPC resources. The broader ABCI-Q testbed also highlights an important distinction: loosely coupled, batch-oriented quantum-classical workflows are feasible today, while future fault-tolerant systems will require tighter, lower-latency coordination between quantum processors and their classical control infrastructure. artigo.texto: Xcel Energy announced the arrival of battery units at its Blue Lake battery storage site in Minnesota, part of what the utility says will soon be the largest battery portfolio in the region. The Blue Lake project is part of a broader plan to diversify power resources in the state. Together with two planned projects in Becker, Minnesota, Xcel Energy expects to operate more than 735 megawatts (MW) of battery energy storage in Minnesota by the end of 2027, creating the largest battery portfolio in the Upper Midwest. “For more than a century, energy companies have generated electricity when customers need it and delivered it almost immediately. Battery storage changes what’s possible. It allows us to store energy and dispatch it when it’s needed most, giving us a powerful new tool to maintain reliability, support growing energy needs and make the most of the diverse resources that power our system,” said Bria Shea, president of Xcel Energy–Minnesota, North Dakota and South Dakota. Xcel Energy argues the evolution of energy storage systems over the years means they can be deployed more broadly at existing energy sites such as Blue Lake, allowing the utility to leverage existing infrastructure while integrating new technologies. The Blue Lake batteries will store energy generated across Xcel Energy’s Upper Midwest system, including energy from wind, solar, nuclear, and natural gas resources. The 135.5 MW battery energy storage facility will include 132 battery units capable of storing energy and delivering electricity for up to four hours. “The Blue Lake project demonstrates how battery storage is becoming an increasingly important part of grid operations,” said Justin Meagher, Xcel Energy battery storage project manager. “These systems can respond quickly to changing conditions, store energy when it’s available and provide electricity when customer demand is high. That flexibility helps us operate the electric system more efficiently while continuing to deliver reliable service to customers.” The Blue Lake Battery Energy Storage System is expected to begin serving customers in 2027. Energy storage deployment is set for another record in 2026. According to BloombergNEF’s latest outlook, 188 gigawatts (GW) or 535 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of energy storage projects will be installed, 62% of which are installed in China, the United States, and Australia. The U.S. is set to deploy 30% more energy storage capacity over the next 10 years than expected just six months ago, BloombergNEF forecasts, predicting cumulative domestic deployments of 213.9 GW by 2030 and 434.4 GW by 2036. Global deployments could eclipse 3,098 GW/11,106 GWh in 2036, roughly 10 times today’s totals.

artigo.texto: BW ESS has acquired a portfolio of two battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in France from Recurrent Energy, a subsidiary of Canadian Solar, with a combined capacity of 200 MW of power and 800 MWh of energy storage. The transaction, announced on October 29, 2026, marks BW ESS's entry into the French market, which becomes the seventh country in which the company operates. Both projects are at an advanced stage of development and have secured grid connection positions on the electricity transmission network. However, they must complete the remaining development procedures before construction can begin. Under the agreement, Recurrent Energy will continue leading the development of the facilities until they reach ready-to-build status, after which BW ESS will take responsibility for construction and subsequent commercial operations. Two projects with 100 MW and 400 MWh each The acquired portfolio consists of two standalone battery storage facilities located in different regions of France. The first project, Baixas, is located in the Pyrénées-Orientales department in southern France and will have 100 MW of power and 400 MWh of energy storage capacity. The second, Coquainvilliers, is located in the Calvados department in Normandy and will also provide 100 MW of power and 400 MWh of storage capacity. Together, the two facilities will deliver 200 MW and 800 MWh, equivalent to four hours of discharge at full rated power. According to Recurrent Energy, both projects have advanced transmission grid connection positions and have been developed at locations where grid constraints are expected to be limited. The company has so far been responsible for securing land, progressing grid connection procedures, managing permits and maintaining relationships with local authorities and communities. Both projects will be developed as standalone battery energy storage systems, meaning they will not be directly connected to a specific renewable power generation facility. Recurrent Energy to continue development as BW ESS takes over construction Although the portfolio sale has been announced, Recurrent Energy will remain involved throughout the next development phase. The Canadian Solar subsidiary will be responsible for completing the remaining procedures and preparing the assets for construction. Once they reach that stage, BW ESS will take responsibility for construction, commissioning and operation, with plans to retain long-term ownership of the facilities. The transaction represents the first agreement between the two companies. BW ESS has not disclosed the financial value of the acquisition or a specific timeline for construction or commercial operation. According to figures provided in its announcement, the company currently has an international storage portfolio comprising more than 540 MWh of operational battery capacity and approximately 12 GWh under construction or in pre-construction. Its activities span the United Kingdom, Australia, Italy, Germany, Spain, Sweden and, following this transaction, France. The 800 MWh portfolio will support flexibility in France's electricity system The acquired facilities are designed to help manage imbalances between electricity generation and consumption. Battery energy storage systems can absorb electricity during periods of greater availability and discharge it back into the grid when demand increases or generation conditions change. They can also provide rapid-response services and contribute to electricity frequency stability. According to the companies, the Baixas and Coquainvilliers projects are intended to address flexibility requirements in the French electricity system and support the integration of renewable generation. Erik Strømsø, CEO and co-founder of BW ESS, explained that the acquisition establishes an initial platform of 200 MW and 800 MWh in France, from which the company intends to expand its domestic portfolio. Meanwhile, Dylan Marx, CEO of Recurrent Energy, noted that the transaction forms part of the company's strategy to develop BESS projects while remaining involved in the stages preceding commercial operations. The sale allows Recurrent Energy to transfer ownership of two projects developed in France while retaining technical and development responsibilities until they reach ready-to-build status. With this acquisition, BW ESS adds 800 MWh of planned battery storage capacity to its French project portfolio. However, this capacity is not yet installed or operational, and its deployment remains subject to the completion of development procedures and construction.

artigo.texto: Shunning AI data centers will cost the US far more than embracing them. Just look at the UK. See more of our coverage in your search results. I get it. I really do. Data centers are noisy. They are ugly. They can push up electricity prices for customers like you and me, an important point to which I’ll return. They are also being built by big tech companies that have squandered public trust. They promised us that social media would connect the world. Instead, it harmed our kids and denuded our attention spans. But even with all these concerns, I believe that the decisions in the coming months on data center build-out are among the most consequential in history. I also believe that the right policy, give or take a few caveats, is simple: build, baby, build. To see my reasoning, come to the nation of my birth. The UK. Terrific place. Big Ben. Impressive universities like Oxford and Cambridge. The nation that incubated the Industrial Revolution. What’s not to like? Well, about 25 years ago, the Brits took a decision. We decided to prioritize the environment over construction, nice views over vital infrastructure, tangible local concerns over the distant abstraction of the national interest. You can probably understand the motive if you’ve ever read “The Lord of the Rings.” We wanted to be The Shire, that picturesque idyll of trees, lovely pubs, and hobbits. In many ways, The Shire was J.R.R. Tolkien’s paean to the England he adored and wished to protect. But you know the old saying about how the road to hell is paved with good intentions? The cumulative effect of these policies has turned the UK not into The Shire but into something more like Mirkwood: cold, poor and increasingly lacking in beauty. The logic is simple. If you fail to build infrastructure, the local environment may look terrific except for the fact that, over time, you can’t afford to look at it very much. They call it a cost of living crisis, but it’s really a building crisis. When you keep adding new environmental and other requirements to any project, you create a viper’s nest of vested interests that block, stymie and delay. This is why obtaining permission for a project in the UK is now more difficult than building it. The planning application for the Lower Thames Crossing ran to nearly 360,000 pages and cost almost $400 million, more than twice what Norway paid to actually build the world’s longest road tunnel. All told, more than $1.6 billion was spent before a spade went into the ground. Such stories abound in Britain. The do-gooders wanted to preserve local wildlife, a lovely sentiment. What happened in practice is that $133 million was loaded onto the cost of a tunnel to protect bats from a rail line. The do-gooders wanted to burnish their green credentials, and ended up exporting emissions to other nations whose products they bought while their own industries were hollowed out. Was this hypocrisy or treason? Get opinions and commentary from our columnists Subscribe to our daily Post Opinion newsletter! Thanks for signing up! The UK is not unlike California without Silicon Valley: all the gridlock, none of the growth to pay for it. And it makes me want to cry. I see a nation of vast potential being slowly strangled by what we might call Shire syndrome. Entrepreneurs, business leaders and blue-collar workers don’t lack talent but are increasingly priced out of global markets. Old people struggle to heat their homes. Living standards have been stagnant for more than 20 years. With this warning in mind, let us circle back to America, a nation with so much going for it. Again, I get the concerns about data centers but it’s worth stating that a moratorium in the US would not stop AI development. It would merely export it to the Gulf, China and beyond. And this would make American infrastructure vulnerable to cyberattack, the military vulnerable to foreign dominance and US companies vulnerable to competition. When Trump says, “Whoever wins AI, wins,” he’s not kidding. But let us also acknowledge that AI supremacy, while a vital strategic interest, also requires a wise approach. Without enough reliable baseload power, new data centers will strain the system. Tech firms should be required to secure direct power sources, whether gas turbines, nuclear restarts or dedicated connections, rather than leaning solely on the grid. Households shouldn’t pay for upgrades that serve AI companies. One also notes the “circular funding” of the big AI companies, where chip companies are guaranteeing loans for the firms that buy their chips. They tell us it’s all above board but it smells fishy. What’s imperative is that if the AI boom turns to bust, shareholders should pick up the bill, not taxpayers. Americans are sick of socialism for the superrich, rugged capitalism for everyone else. I acknowledge that this analysis will seem to some readers overly parochial. What about an AI-induced jobs apocalypse? What about existential risk? Shouldn’t humanity pause to contemplate and contain these dangers? To be clear, I worry about these things as much as the next prepper, but in the absence of an enforceable global accord, what’s the alternative to the US trying to stay ahead? And this takes us back to The Shire — for there’s a part of the story that hobbits never knew. The Shire was not peaceful because it was idyllic. It was peaceful because, beyond its borders, the Rangers kept watch. Rugged, unthanked and mostly unseen, they held back the dark forces so that hobbits could tend their gardens and squabble over fence lines. The Shire’s tranquility depended utterly on strength somewhere else. In the age of AI, nobody is keeping watch on America’s behalf. You are the City upon a Hill, the soldier on the wall, the only thing standing between the free world and a future dominated by the Chinese Communist Party, a totalitarian clique which regards AI as a route to global supremacy and whose true nature has been revealed not just by the Tiananmen Sq

artigo.texto: Data centers podem quase dobrar consumo de energia até 2030; onde o Brasil entra nessa disputa Estudo aponta matriz elétrica renovável como vantagem para atrair infraestrutura de IA, mas avanço depende de investimentos e conexões à rede O consumo mundial de eletricidade dos data centers pode quase dobrar até 2030, impulsionado pela expansão da inteligência artificial. A demanda deve passar de 485 terawatts-hora (TWh) em 2025 para 950 TWh ao fim da década, segundo projeção da Agência Internacional de Energia (AIE). A corrida por abastecimento abre uma oportunidade para o Brasil: usar sua matriz elétrica majoritariamente renovável para atrair empresas e investimentos em infraestrutura digital. Essa é uma das conclusões do relatório 10 Energy Megatrends, produzido pelo Energy Summit em parceria com a Deloitte, com lançamento nesta quarta-feira, 28. O estudo reúne dez tendências para o setor energético e aponta a disponibilidade de eletricidade confiável e de baixa emissão como um fator cada vez mais relevante na escolha dos locais que receberão novos centros de processamento de dados. Os data centers abrigam servidores que armazenam informações e executam serviços digitais, da computação em nuvem ao treinamento e funcionamento de modelos de inteligência artificial. Além de alimentar os equipamentos, a eletricidade mantém os sistemas de refrigeração necessários para evitar o superaquecimento das instalações. Com o avanço da IA, a capacidade de fornecer energia de forma contínua ganha peso nas decisões de investimento. Segundo o relatório, a espera por conexão à rede elétrica pode chegar a cinco a sete anos em mercados dos Estados Unidos e da Europa. As dificuldades estimulam empresas de tecnologia a buscar contratos de longo prazo e fontes de geração dedicadas ao abastecimento de suas operações. Para o Brasil, o estudo identifica três vantagens: uma matriz elétrica com participação de renováveis superior a 85%, a capacidade das hidrelétricas de ajustar a produção e a interligação entre diferentes regiões pelo Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). A combinação pode favorecer a instalação de centros de processamento interessados em conciliar disponibilidade de energia e menores emissões. O potencial, porém, depende de infraestrutura. O relatório aponta a necessidade de acelerar a conexão de grandes consumidores, ampliar investimentos no sistema elétrico e dar previsibilidade regulatória aos projetos. A existência de geração renovável, por si só, não garante que a energia esteja disponível no local e no prazo exigidos pelas empresas. Há também uma exigência crescente quanto à origem da eletricidade. Segundo o estudo, empresas passam a buscar o abastecimento por fontes livres de carbono em cada hora de operação, elevando o padrão em relação à compensação do consumo por certificados anuais. Nesse modelo, importa assegurar o fornecimento mesmo quando não há sol ou quando a produção eólica diminui. A disputa cria oportunidades para geradoras e empresas de infraestrutura, além dos próprios operadores de data centers. Contratos de fornecimento de longo prazo, subestações dedicadas e sistemas de resfriamento mais eficientes passam a integrar os projetos de expansão digital. O relatório cita a Scala Data Centers como exemplo brasileiro dessa integração. No Campus Tamboré, em São Paulo, a empresa combina infraestrutura elétrica dedicada, fornecimento renovável e soluções de refrigeração para atender instalações com elevada demanda de processamento. A relação entre energia e inteligência artificial também funciona no sentido inverso. O estudo aponta que algoritmos podem melhorar as previsões de geração solar e eólica, antecipar condições de operação e ajudar a equilibrar oferta e consumo. Para o Brasil, a oportunidade envolve tanto abastecer a expansão da economia digital quanto aplicar a tecnologia para melhorar a eficiência de seu próprio sistema elétrico.

artigo.texto: Newswise — RICHLAND, Wash. — The Department of Energy’s Pacific Northwest National Laboratory is leading a new national consortium to accelerate the transition of energy storage innovations from discovery to domestic manufacturing. Called the Battery Manufacturing (BattMan) Accelerator, the consortium will address critical barriers in scaling new battery technologies. The accelerator will focus on lowering manufacturing costs, speeding up development from the lab to commercial scale and boosting U.S. leadership in energy storage manufacturing. “Breakthroughs in battery science must be matched by our ability to manufacture them at scale. BattMan brings together the tools, data and partnerships needed to design manufacturable solutions from the start and accelerate their transition into industry,” said Jie Xiao, Battelle Fellow at PNNL with a joint appointment as Boeing Martin Professor of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Washington in Seattle. BattMan will also support critical mineral supply chains to help the nation reduce dependence on foreign sources for battery materials. The BattMan Accelerator includes Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Argonne National Laboratory and the National Laboratory of the Rockies along with founding university partners including the University of Washington, Binghamton University, the University of Alabama, Arizona State University, and the University of Michigan-Dearborn. The accelerator is actively establishing collaborations with companies within the battery and materials manufacturing sector. “Advancing the next generation of battery technologies requires more than scientific discovery alone,” said Angela Becker-Dippmann, an associate laboratory director at PNNL. “It requires an integrated approach to manufacturing, data and scale-up. BattMan brings together the national laboratories, universities and industry partners needed to accelerate innovation and strengthen America’s leadership in energy storage manufacturing.” Bridging discovery and manufacturing Scientific research is often driven by untangling mysteries behind observed physical processes. When studying batteries, scientists investigate how a new battery material might behave under a range of different conditions or how to modify materials for better performance. And while fundamental research has led to critical innovations in long-lasting, more affordable batteries, some research efforts don’t always prioritize manufacturing issues like processability, repeatability, cost and scale-up risks, Xiao said. “With BattMan, we’ll encourage our research partners to think: If this is a breakthrough and could work outside a lab setting, then what can we do to lower the manufacturing cost through innovations?” Xiao said. PNNL, with industry and university partners, recently published a paper outlining a variety of different research topics that are both important on a purely scientific level and could help the battery manufacturing industry lower costs and increase efficiency. The paper highlighted how Super Intelligence could be critical to battery manufacturing. “SI-driven methods that use processing and manufacturing data have the potential to speed up discovery of new materials, improve efficiency of laboratory processes and support predictive, cost-effective design,” Xiao said. In manufacturing specifically, SI could identify sources of contamination with greater precision, detect subtle process variations, or mitigate potential manufacturing risks in real time as batteries are produced on a bustling factory floor. What’s more, SI could also help industry identify market trends and act on them, Xiao said. BattMan will enhance battery innovation and manufacturing by applying real data captured by the consortium, digital tools and especially SI, she added. “Incorporating SI into both research and manufacturing allows us to move from trial and error to predictive design,” said Stanley Whittingham, distinguished professor of chemistry at Binghamton University in New York and a 2019 Nobel Prize laureate recognized for the development of lithium-ion batteries. “This capability is key to accelerating innovation while ensuring technologies can be produced reliably and affordably at scale.” Scientific goals of BattMan’s manufacturing In the near term, BattMan will implement high-throughput experimentation, automated synthesis and characterization, along with digital manufacturing tools to improve data quality, reproducibility and process consistency across partner institutions. Over the long term, the initiative seeks to develop self-optimizing manufacturing systems using real-time data, digital twins and closed-loop control. BattMan will build on the autonomous laboratory concept by advancing autonomous pilot lines, aiming to cut scale-up time and costs, speed commercialization and strengthen domestic supply chains. “Ultimately, we want to become a go-to source for the domestic energy storage industry, where research can be translated for broad energy storage manufacturing,” Xiao said. BattMan is now in the process of forming industry partnerships in battery and battery materials manufacturing. For institutions and companies interested in participating, click here. Supported by DOE’s Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Technologies Office within the Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation Office, the BattMan Accelerator integrates SI, materials science and advanced manufacturing into a coordinated, data-driven innovation ecosystem.

artigo.texto: Oficial: Baic confirma chegada ao Brasil e terá linha de montagem local Exclusivo: Baic confirma chegada ao Brasil e terá linha de montagem local. Crédito: Marcus Celestino A BAIC apresentou oficialmente ao mercado brasileiro o inédito BAIC Arcfox T1, crossover elétrico que chega para disputar espaço no acirrado segmento de modelos compactos de emissão zero. Revelado ao público durante o Festival Interlagos, o veículo desembarca para combater diretamente concorrentes de peso, como BYD Dolphin, Dolphin Mini, Geely EX2, GAC Aion UT e MG4 Urban. As entregas oficiais no território nacional começam em novembro de 2026. Para embalar sua estreia, a fabricante aposta em uma rede inicial estruturada com 50 concessionárias e em uma agressiva política de preços. O modelo é comercializado em duas configurações: a opção de entrada PRO, que conta com preço promocional de lançamento de R$ 129.900 (condição válida até 31 de dezembro de 2026 ou enquanto durarem os estoques), e a versão topo de linha MAX, tabelada em R$ 139.900. O Arcfox T1 destaca-se logo de início pelo porte. No total, são 4,33 metros de comprimento, 1,86 m de largura, 1,57 m de altura e um generoso entre-eixos de 2,77 metros — medida vista em veículos maiores e que garante excelente espaço interno. Visualmente, o utilitário ostenta o design característico da marca chinesa. Na dianteira, os faróis afilados são interligados por uma barra de LED transversal. As rodas podem ser de 17 ou 18 polegadas, variando conforme a versão. As maçanetas são semirrecolhíveis e a pintura pode receber acabamento bicolor. O catálogo de cores inclui as opções Branco Polar, Prata Aurora, Prata Elétrico e Cinza Eclipse, enquanto a cabine exibe duas combinações bicolores: Cinza Champagne e Preto Noir. Leia também - Fipe dos clássicos: como funcionará novo índice de referência de preços - Projeto brasileiro, nova picape Volkswagen Tukan também será produzida no exterior - Bolsonarista perde aposta e entrega Porsche de R$ 1,5 milhão a eleitor de Lula Cabine espaçosa e lista de equipamentos O aproveitamento interno é um dos pontos fortes do crossover. O porta-malas tem capacidade para 459 litros, podendo ser ampliado para até 1.352 litros com o rebatimento do banco traseiro. Na opção MAX, o teto panorâmico amplia a sensação de espaço a bordo. O painel de instrumentos digital em LCD de 8,8 polegadas atua em conjunto com a central multimídia flutuante de 15,6 polegadas sensível ao toque. O sistema oferece espelhamento via Apple CarPlay e Easy Link, além de comandos de voz em inglês e interface multilíngue com suporte ao português. Em relação a acabamento, o painel e as laterais possuem revestimento de toque macio, mantendo o plástico rígido em áreas pontuais das portas. O Arcfox T1 traz ainda um recurso peculiar de série: a inclinação total dos bancos dianteiros, permitindo que os assentos formem uma superfície plana para momentos de descanso — quase que uma cama. Além disso, o assento do motorista conta com ajustes elétricos e aquecimento em ambas as versões. A configuração MAX acrescenta ventilação, regulagem elétrica e memória para o passageiro dianteiro, tampa do porta-malas com acionamento elétrico e retrovisores externos com rebatimento automático no travamento do veículo. Motor elétrico de 96 cv e tecnologia V2L Sob o capô, o Arcfox T1 traz um propulsor elétrico síncrono de ímã permanente instalado no eixo dianteiro. O conjunto adota a tecnologia de enrolamento de fio plano (Hairpin), que, segundo a marca, proporciona ganho de força e maior eficiência energética. O sistema entrega 96 cv de potência e 17,9 kgfm de torque. A aceleração de 0 a 100 km/h é feita em 12,4 segundos, com velocidade máxima limitada eletronicamente acima de 140 km/h. A alimentação fica a cargo de uma bateria de fosfato de ferro-lítio (LFP) com 42,3 kWh de capacidade. A autonomia declarada pelo Programa Brasileiro de Etiquetagem Veicular (PBEV) do Inmetro é de 283 km. Para a recarga, o modelo aceita corrente alternada (CA) de até 6,6 kW (com carga completa em menos de 8 horas) e suporte a carregamento rápido em corrente contínua (CC) de até 89 kW, permitindo elevar o nível da bateria de 30% a 80% em cerca de 25 minutos. O veículo dispõe ainda das funções bidirecionais V2L (Vehicle-to-Load) e V2V (Vehicle-to-Vehicle), possibilitando alimentar dispositivos externos ou transferir energia para outros automóveis. Outro recurso curioso do modelo é o sistema EZT, uma assistência para manobras em baixa velocidade que atua autonomamente nos freios para reduzir o raio de giro em até 30 cm, facilitando o esterçamento em vagas apertadas. O modelo traz também de série câmera de visão panorâmica de 540° — que une imagens 360° ao redor da carroceria a uma projeção de 180° do chassi transparente —, sensores de estacionamento dianteiros e traseiros e assistente de partida em rampa. Segurança e pacote ADAS na versão MAX O pacote completo de assistências à condução (ADAS), contudo, é exclusivo da versão topo de linha MAX — estratégia adotada pela BAIC para manter a opção de entrada PRO com preço mais competitivo, a exemplo do que ocorre com o rival Geely EX2. Ainda assim, ambas as configurações saem de fábrica equipadas com freios a disco nas quatro rodas, freio de estacionamento eletrônico (EPB) com função Auto Hold e seis airbags (frontais, laterais e de cortina). A variante MAX adiciona: - Frenagem autônoma de emergência (AEB) - Alerta de colisão frontal (FCW) - Piloto automático adaptativo com função Stop-and-Go (ACC) - Assistente integrado de cruzeiro (ICA) - Assistente de tráfego congestionado (TJA) - Alerta de colisão de pedestres (PCW) - Alerta de saída de faixa (LDW) - Assistente de estacionamento automático (APA para vagas paralelas, perpendiculares e saída) - Assistente para vias estreitas e manobra em marcha a ré com memorização de trajeto Rede de pós-venda e planos para o Brasil Para estruturar sua operação no país, a BAIC implementou uma rede de pós-venda que promete 97% de disponibilidade d

artigo.texto: BW ESS, the global energy storage owner-operator, has acquired two utility scale standalone battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in France from Recurrent Energy, a global developer, owner, and operator of solar and energy storage assets. The acquisition marks BW ESS’ entry into France, its seventh market globally. The projects, each with a capacity of 100 MW/400 MWh, are located in the regions of Calvados and Eastern Pyrenees. Both projects, which are in advanced development, are expected to play an important role in supporting the flexibility, reliability, and resilience of the French power system as the country continues to integrate higher levels of renewable energy. The acquisition represents a significant step in the continued expansion of BW ESS’ international energy storage platform. The company brings extensive experience from its existing markets and deep expertise across development, construction, optimisation, and long-term asset ownership. France is an increasingly important market for battery energy storage, underpinned by the country’s growing need for flexible capacity, system balancing, and grid stability. As renewable generation continues to expand, large scale BESS assets are expected to become increasingly critical in helping to manage supply and demand, reduce system constraints, and support the efficient operation of the electricity network. The two projects are also expected to benefit from their standalone configuration and strategic positioning within the French power system. As battery storage assets, they will be able to provide rapid-response flexibility services, store electricity when supply is abundant, and discharge when it is most needed. This capability helps improve system efficiency and supports the broader energy transition. Erik Strømsø, CEO and Co-Founder of BW ESS, commented: “Entering France is a significant milestone for BW ESS and a natural next step in the expansion of our global energy storage platform. These acquisitions give us an immediate 200 MW/800 MWh platform in the country and provide a strong foundation for building a sizeable French portfolio. France has a strong nuclear base, but it also has a growing need for flexibility as weather-sensitive demand and an evolving generation mix create more variable system conditions. Batteries can complement France’s nuclear backbone by adding the rapid-response flexibility needed to balance the system, absorb surplus power, and make low-carbon generation available when it is most valuable. We are excited to work with Recurrent Energy through the next phase and to apply BW ESS’ long-term owner-operator expertise as we bring these assets into construction and operation.” Dylan Marx, CEO of Recurrent Energy, added: “This transaction with BW ESS showcases our ability to create value through the delivery of high-quality BESS projects, while remaining closely involved in their development through to commercial operation. It is a strong testament to the BESS platform we have built in France and our ability to continue scaling it.” BW ESS intends to own and operate the assets over the long term, applying its experience across construction, optimisation, and asset management to support their successful delivery and long-term performance. Recurrent Energy will continue to lead the projects through the remaining development phase until they are ready-to-build, drawing on its local market knowledge, technical capabilities, and experience in delivering renewable energy and storage projects. artigo.texto: [DigitalToday reporter Jae-won Choi] China's CATL, the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker, is accelerating development of next-generation solid-state batteries. It has entered the stage of trial production of 20 ampere-hour (Ah) battery cells. It aims to start limited production in 2027. Electrek reported on Oct. 28, local time, that CATL said in a recent response to investor questions, "We are continuously investing in solid-state battery research and development and plan to begin limited production next year." CATL is developing solid-state batteries using sulphide-based solid electrolytes. It is currently conducting trial production of 20Ah cells. It has set a target of achieving an energy density of 500 watt-hours per kilogram (Wh/kg). Solid-state batteries replace the liquid electrolyte in existing lithium-ion batteries with a solid. They are drawing attention as next-generation batteries because they can improve energy density and safety, but technical challenges remain for mass production. The sulphide-based electrolyte adopted by CATL has the advantage of high ionic conductivity and good processability. On the other hand, it is difficult to maintain stable contact between the electrode and electrolyte during charging and discharging. As a result, even if it has entered the trial production stage, additional verification is needed on durability and safety, production yield and price competitiveness before applying it to actual electric vehicles. CATL expects initial production volume to be limited. It sees the timing of full-scale mass production as around 2030. CATL Chairman and CEO Robin Zeng (로빈 젱) said at the Summer Davos Forum in June that he assessed the maturity of solid-state battery technology at stage 4 out of 9. That means technical completeness for mass production is not yet sufficient. Competition in the global battery industry is also intensifying. Toyota aims to launch electric vehicles equipped with solid-state batteries in 2027 to 2028. Samsung SDI is pushing to mass-produce solid-state batteries in the second half of 2027 and is considering humanoid robots as an initial commercialisation target. BYD also plans to start limited production of sulphide-based solid-state batteries in 2027 and expand production scale by 2030. CATL, meanwhile, maintained its No. 1 position in the global EV battery market with a 39.4 percent share from January to August this year. Attention is focused on whether CATL, which leads the conventional battery market, can also secure competitiveness in solid-state batteries.

artigo.texto: Two Brokerages Slash CATL Targets as Battery Margins Erode Published on 10/29/2026 at 17:31 | Editorial boerse-global.de JPMorgan cut its rating on CATL's Hong Kong-listed shares from "Overweight" to "Neutral" on October 20, according to media reports, and trimmed its price target to HK$500 from HK$725. The bank pointed to a faster-than-expected deterioration in profitability across the battery sector. Its stance on CATL's A-shares was left untouched at "Overweight." Two days later, UOB Kay Hian took an even sharper knife to its own target, reducing it by 40.7% to HK$400. The brokerage cited the company's disappointing quarterly results and a lag in passing higher taxes through to customers. It also lowered its net profit forecasts for 2026 through 2028 by 5%, 10% and 16% respectively — an adjustment that reaches well beyond the current fiscal year. Revenue gallops, profit crawls The downgrades landed roughly a week after CATL reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of RMB 165.221 billion, up 58.58% year on year. Net profit attributable to shareholders came in at RMB 21.246 billion, a gain of 14.54% over the prior-year period but a decline of 5.77% from the second quarter. Reuters noted that both profit and revenue growth fell short of analyst expectations, with earnings expanding at their slowest pace in nearly two years. That gap between top-line expansion and bottom-line momentum is the crux of the bear case. Whether new projects can close it is the crux of the bull case. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Australia: interest, not yet investment CATL aims to convert Australian interest in sodium-ion batteries into concrete project investments, Bloomberg reported, citing the company's regional head. For investors, that represents an opening rather than a secured business win — the decisive question is whether interest translates into actual investment decisions. Technological promise alone does not answer what economic contribution new projects might make. The company has been stacking up agreements that show the various routes it intends to pursue. On October 22, CATL and BAIC Group signed a strategic cooperation deal covering vehicles with battery-swap technology, battery supply and swap networks, with a target of one million vehicles. The scope stretches beyond battery deliveries: in the optimistic scenario, vehicles, supply and infrastructure interlock. What matters for investors is whether the partners actually execute — a target figure is not the same as delivered cars. Heavy trucks offer another concrete angle. CATL presented its Tianxing II battery solution on October 20 and announced an expansion of its Qiji swap system, with initial agreements covering 13,000 units according to company statements. By the end of 2026, CATL plans 900 battery-swap stations for heavy trucks in China. A joint venture is signed; a profit contribution is not Some initiatives carry more binding force than others. An investment interest is not a founded joint venture, and an agreed target volume says nothing about actual progress or later earnings contribution. Those distinctions deserve to be preserved in any assessment. On October 19, CATL and Chery Automobile established the joint venture CATL Chery (Wuhu) New Energy Technology, with registered capital of CNY 1 billion — CATL holding 51% and Chery 49%. The entity exists. A profit contribution cannot yet be derived from it. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. The bear scenario is straightforward: activities expand while profit keeps growing markedly slower than revenue. The latest quarterly comparison makes that risk relevant without cementing it as a trend. What would change the picture The immediate catalyst would be tangible progress on Australian project investments. A longer-dated marker is the small-series production of solid-state batteries in 2027, which CATL said on Tuesday it expects, as told to investors. That, too, remains an expectation rather than a completed production start. Both themes pose the same demand to investors: technological and commercial prospects must harden into deliverable execution. Ad CATL Stock: New Analysis - 29 October Fresh CATL information released. What's the impact for investors? Our latest independent report examines recent figures and market trends.

artigo.texto: OTTAWA, Kan. — KSHB 41 reporter Lily O’Shea Becker covers Franklin and Douglas counties in Kansas. Share your story idea with Lily. — With a national focus on the Kansas midterm election, national pro-data center political action committees (PAC) are filtering funds and messaging into the Sunflower State. On Wednesday, NBC News reported pro-data center super PAC Building the Future is spending more than $1.5 million to support Sen. Ty Masterson, the Republican candidate in the Kansas governor race. Defend U.S., a super PAC out of Virginia, is sending mailers to households in Ottawa, Kansas, as residents vote on a citizen-led proposed ordinance to ban data centers in town for 10 years. “If you take a trip up and down I-35, you’ll see it big as day," Ottawa resident Michael Lewis said. "They have those 50-foot billboards out there.” Lewis is talking about multiple billboards along Interstate 35 that read "VOTE NO On the Data Center Question." A group of Ottawa and Franklin County residents formed a coalition known as Ottawa United Inc. amid a proposed 300-acre data center development on the south side of town. The group rallied this summer to gain enough signatures on an initiative petition to put a data center question on the November ballot. In a lawsuit filed in August, Lewis and Ottawa resident Kim Conard alleged the city ignored the petition. On Oct. 20, a judge ruled in favor of Lewis, Conard and Ottawa United. City residents are now voting on whether to put a ban on data center development in Ottawa for 10 years. Now, Ottawa United is fighting something bigger. It's unclear who funded the billboards along I-35. Super PAC Defend U.S. is listed as the sender of multiple mailers Lewis received at his home. Jessica Christopher, a Franklin County Ottawa United member, says she's received multiple calls and texts in-favor of data center development in Ottawa. “We can’t outspend," Christopher said. "We don’t have billboards on every corner, and out of town, we aren’t sending out mailers; we’re door knocking.” Christopher lives near Proximity Park, where the city and developer Lightfield Energy were planning a data center development. She wrote the proposed data center ordinance for Ottawa United. "At the end of the day, this is Ottawa, this isn’t what happens nationwide; this is what happens in our backyard," she said. It's an issue Christopher says is non-partisan. It's evident along East Logan Street. While neighbors across the street from one another sport yard signs for candidates from across the aisle, both residents also have Ottawa United's "Vote Yes" sign placed in their lawns. “It’s showing the resolve in our community, that in the face of outside spending, that we’re still united, we’re still Ottawa, we’re still Ottawa United," Lewis said. KSHB 41 News reached out to Masterson with questions and for a statement in response to NBC News' Wednesday report. A response was not issued by the time of this publication. Ty Masterson is a pay-to-play politician, and out-of-state tech companies are spending millions to buy him the governorship. No one spends that kind of money without expecting something in return, and Masterson will pay them back with a data center in every cornfield while everyday Kansans foot the bill. As governor, I'll end the corruption, put real guardrails on data centers, and answer to the people of Kansas, not special interests. —

artigo.texto: Powersafe, Huawei e Zipp Energia apresentam no evento Imersão Indústria FIEMG 2026, em Belo Horizonte, um modelo integrado de armazenamento de energia. A tecnologia permite que indústrias economizem energia e mantenam operações críticas funcionais durante apagões, com um caso de sucesso na empresa Rivelli Alimentos. De olho na crescente demanda da indústria e da agroindústria por soluções capazes de reduzir os custos com eletricidade e garantir maior segurança no fornecimento, a Powersafe, empresa brasileira especializada em soluções de armazenamento de energia, participa, em parceria com a Huawei Digital Power e a Zipp Energia, da 9ª edição do Imersão Indústria, promovido pela Federação das Indústrias do Estado de Minas Gerais (FIEMG), nos dias 29 e 30 de outubro, em Belo Horizonte. As três empresas apresentam soluções integradas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS, na sigla em inglês), que permitem às indústrias gerenciar o consumo de eletricidade, reduzir despesas nos horários de maior tarifa e manter operações críticas em funcionamento durante interrupções no fornecimento da rede elétrica. - Economia estimada de 50% na conta de luz para a indústria. - Tecnologia garante até 27 horas de energia durante apagões. - Primeiro sistema homologado pela Cemig para cliente privado em MG. - Integração com energia solar e geradores a diesel. - Evento ocorre em Belo Horizonte (MG) em outubro de 2026. A proposta é mostrar ao setor produtivo que a adoção de baterias industriais envolve não apenas o fornecimento dos equipamentos, mas também estudos de viabilidade econômica, dimensionamento, engenharia, integração com outras fontes de energia, homologação junto às distribuidoras e acompanhamento técnico da operação. Caso de Sucesso na Indústria de Alimentos Um dos exemplos apresentados será o projeto recentemente colocado em operação na unidade de produção de matrizes da Rivelli Alimentos, em Carmo do Cajuru (MG). A instalação reúne um sistema de baterias de 1,29 megawatt-hora (MWh), tecnologia Huawei, uma usina solar de 378 quilowatts-pico (kWp) e integração com a rede elétrica e um gerador a diesel. Segundo as empresas responsáveis, trata-se do primeiro sistema BESS instalado para um cliente privado em Minas Gerais com homologação integral pela Cemig Distribuição. O projeto tem potencial estimado de reduzir em cerca de 50% os custos com energia elétrica da unidade, além de assegurar maior autonomia para atividades essenciais. Engenharia Integrada e Eficiência Energética "Os sistemas de armazenamento estão abrindo uma nova frente de eficiência energética para a indústria brasileira. Mais do que instalar baterias, é necessário entender o perfil de consumo e as necessidades de cada operação para desenvolver uma solução que combine economia, confiabilidade e retorno financeiro. Minas Gerais já tem exemplos concretos dessa aplicação", afirma André Ribeiro, gerente de Renováveis da Powersafe. Na parceria apresentada durante o evento, a Huawei Digital Power fornece a tecnologia de armazenamento, incluindo os sistemas inteligentes da linha LUNA2000, com baterias de lítio-ferro-fosfato (LFP). A Zipp Energia atua no desenvolvimento dos projetos, estudos de viabilidade, obras, subestações e integração dos sistemas. Já a Powersafe responde pelo fornecimento das soluções, engenharia aplicada, testes, comissionamento e suporte pós-venda. O modelo permite atender empresas com diferentes perfis de consumo e necessidades operacionais, especialmente aquelas que enfrentam custos elevados no horário de ponta, ultrapassagem de demanda contratada ou riscos associados à interrupção de processos produtivos. Aplicações Práticas da Tecnologia BESS Entre as aplicações estão o peak shaving, que reduz os picos de demanda elétrica; o load shifting, que permite utilizar energia armazenada nos períodos de tarifas mais elevadas; o gerenciamento de energia reativa e o fornecimento de energia de reserva em situações de emergência. No caso da Rivelli, a continuidade do fornecimento é especialmente importante porque a ventilação e o controle das condições ambientais dos aviários dependem de eletricidade. Em situações críticas, o sistema foi projetado para oferecer aproximadamente dez horas de autonomia, podendo chegar a 27 horas com o desligamento de cargas não essenciais. O armazenamento precisa ser pensado de acordo com a realidade de cada indústria. A engenharia é fundamental para integrar baterias, geração solar, rede elétrica e sistemas de emergência, garantindo que todos esses recursos funcionem de maneira coordenada e segura, explica Arthur Pena, da Zipp Energia. Mercado de Baterias em Expansão A participação das empresas no Imersão Indústria ocorre em um momento de avanço do armazenamento de energia no Brasil, impulsionado pela evolução regulatória, pelo crescimento da geração renovável e pela necessidade de maior flexibilidade e segurança no sistema elétrico. O setor também acompanha a preparação dos primeiros leilões federais de reserva de capacidade voltados ao armazenamento em baterias, previstos para dezembro de 2026. Embora os certames sejam direcionados a projetos de maior escala, a discussão amplia a visibilidade das tecnologias de armazenamento e suas aplicações em diferentes segmentos econômicos. Em Minas Gerais, a presença expressiva da geração solar e a concentração de atividades industriais e agroindustriais criam oportunidades para sistemas capazes de integrar geração própria, gestão do consumo e continuidade operacional. Para a Powersafe, a tendência é que os projetos de baterias ganhem participação crescente nas decisões de investimento das empresas, principalmente em segmentos nos quais a energia elétrica representa uma parcela relevante dos custos ou sua interrupção pode provocar perdas de produção. artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia 29 de outubro de 2026, às 12:11 O lucro líquido da BYD avançou 28% no terceiro trimestre, impulsionado pelo forte desempenho nas exportações. A maior vendedora de veículos elétricos do mundo acelera a expansão internacional para compensar a desaceleração da demanda na China, seu principal mercado. A montadora sediada em Shenzhen informou nesta quinta-feira, 29, que o lucro líquido somou 10,02 bilhões de yuans (US$ 1,50 bilhão), acima dos 7,82 bilhões de yuans registrados um ano antes. A receita aumentou 14%, para 221,49 bilhões de yuans. Apesar do avanço, os números ficaram abaixo das expectativas do mercado. Analistas ouvidos pela Visible Alpha estimavam lucro líquido de 11,10 bilhões de yuans, com receita de 240,83 bilhões de yuans no período. No acumulado de janeiro a setembro, o lucro líquido caiu 4,2%, para 22,34 bilhões de yuans, enquanto a receita ficou praticamente estável em 566,30 bilhões de yuans, informou a empresa. Os resultados evidenciam os desafios enfrentados pelas montadoras chinesas no maior mercado automotivo do mundo. Com a competição doméstica mais intensa e as vendas perdendo fôlego, a BYD – como outras rivais locais – busca no exterior uma nova frente de crescimento. As vendas internacionais continuaram a sustentar o desempenho no trimestre, representando mais de 40% do total. A BYD exportou mais de 550.700 veículos de “nova energia” (categoria que inclui elétricos puros e híbridos plug-in), mais que o dobro do volume de um ano antes. Já as vendas totais cresceram em ritmo bem menor, de 19%, para 1,3 milhão de unidades. Analistas avaliam que a expansão internacional se tornará ainda mais decisiva se a demanda na China continuar enfraquecendo. O fôlego no exterior, porém, dependerá da capacidade da empresa de contornar barreiras comerciais crescentes e avançar na produção local em mercados estratégicos. No curto prazo, a BYD parece bem posicionada. A nova fábrica na Hungria deve iniciar a produção em breve, reforçando a base industrial da companhia na Europa em um momento em que a União Europeia busca restringir importações de híbridos produzidos na China. Na China, há sinais favoráveis: a demanda por modelos com recarga ultrarrápida segue firme, e as entregas podem ganhar tração nos próximos meses com a redução das restrições de oferta de baterias, segundo analistas da Bernstein. artigo.texto: *Conteúdo oferecido pela Aurora Energy Research Por:* Julia Alves Stehmman e Rodrigo Longo A seis semanas do primeiro leilão de baterias do país, ainda não está definido quem vai pagar a conta. Dependendo da regra, o custo para uma mesma tecnologia pode variar de R$0 a mais de R$18/MWh. 1. Por que existe um leilão de capacidade e o que é o Ercap Até 2021, o Brasil tinha um sistema essencialmente hidrotérmico, com flexibilidade garantida pelos reservatórios. Desde então, solar e eólica cresceram rapidamente e, em 2026, já superam um terço da eletricidade gerada no país. São fontes baratas, mas não despacháveis. Com isso, o pico de consumo líquido passou para o início da noite, entre 18h e 20h, quando a geração solar desaparece. Para atender a essa ponta, o sistema precisa de usinas que o operador possa acionar quando necessário, como térmicas, hidrelétricas com reservatório e armazenamento. O paradoxo é que as renováveis derrubaram o preço da energia na maior parte do dia. Uma usina que só opera nas poucas horas críticas, como uma térmica a gás de ciclo aberto, não consegue cobrir seus custos fixos apenas vendendo energia. Sem uma receita adicional por capacidade, não há como investir nesse tipo de usina, embora o sistema dependa dela. É o chamado missing money. O leilão de reserva de capacidade foi criado para resolver esse problema. Em vez de remunerar a energia gerada, ele paga pela disponibilidade, por meio de uma receita fixa. Essa receita é financiada pelo Encargo de Potência para Reserva de Capacidade (Ercap), que cobre investimento, operação e manutenção, impostos e margem dos projetos. Nos leilões de térmicas, como o de março de 2026, o custo do Ercap é repassado para os consumidores finais. Os leilões de baterias, marcados para dezembro, mudam essa lógica em dois pontos. O primeiro é a Conta de Potência para Reserva de Capacidade (Concap). Diferentemente de uma térmica de ponta, a bateria também gera valor no mercado de energia, porque carrega ao meio-dia, quando a energia é barata, e descarrega à noite, quando é cara. Essa receita de arbitragem não fica com o desenvolvedor: ela vai para a Concap e reduz o encargo pago pelo sistema. O segundo ponto é quem paga, tema da próxima seção. 2. As maneiras de alocar o Ercap das baterias Para o pagamento do encargo das baterias, a Lei 15.269/2025 adotou uma lógica distinta da aplicada às térmicas: atribuiu o custeio exclusivamente aos agentes de geração e delegou à Aneel a definição da metodologia de rateio. A justificativa é que a necessidade de capacidade firme decorre da expansão das fontes renováveis intermitentes, e por isso esse custo não deveria ser repassado às tarifas. A regra, porém, ainda não está fechada. Atualmente há quatro alternativas principais de rateio em discussão, ao mesmo tempo: As quatro frentes correm em calendários diferentes, junto a outras propostas. A CP 37, que decide entre os critérios de flexibilidade e de potência, recebe contribuições até 6 de novembro, e a decisão final pode adotar um dos dois critérios ou uma combinação deles. No Congresso, o PL 3,716 teve urgência aprovada em 13 de outubro, mas ainda não tem relator. Tudo converge para os leilões de 2 e 4 de dezembro, com início de suprimento em 1º de agosto de 2028. 3. Quanto cada tecnologia pagaria em cada cenário Nas projeções da Aurora Energy Research, o Brasil ainda precisa contratar cerca de 14 GW de capacidade firme até 2030, ou seja, potência confiável e despachável, além do que já foi contratado no leilão de março, para atender ao crescimento da demanda de pico. O leilão de dezembro é, portanto, apenas o primeiro de uma série. O MME já definiu um calendário com um leilão de reserva de capacidade por ano, no segundo semestre de 2027, 2028 e 2029, com o armazenamento em baterias entre as tecnologias elegíveis. Assumindo uma receita fixa de aproximadamente R$1450/kW-ano para remunerar um projeto de BESS ao longo de 15 anos de contrato e uma receita de arbitragem no valor de R$ 280/kW-ano que volta ao sistema pelo Concap. O Ercap líquido, que efetivamente precisa ser rateado, fica em torno de R$1170/kW-ano, em torno de R$2,3 bilhões em 2028 para a alocação de 2GW no próximo leilão. A partir desses valores e da alocação de leilões de capacidade futuros, calculamos quanto as renováveis pagariam em cada cenário de alocação de custos do Ercap. a) Parâmetros de flexibilidade e de entrega de potência por tecnologia Para calcular quanto cada tecnologia pagaria, é preciso definir os dois critérios de rateio em discussão: a flexibilidade operativa e a contribuição para o atendimento da demanda no horário de ponta, representada pelos fatores de de-rating (confiabilidade de entrega em horários de demanda pico). A proposta da Aneel gradua o encargo em quatro patamares: inflexível (P1) paga 100%, flexibilidade baixa (P2) paga 75%, alta (P3) paga 50% e muito alta (P4) paga 25%. Eólicas e solares ficam no patamar menos flexível. Ainda não existe métrica consolidada de flexibilidade no setor, então a classificação por tecnologia é uma aproximação. O ONS propõe, no lugar da flexibilidade, um índice de contribuição de potência na janela crítica em que o leilão contrata potência (ICP-JC). O coeficiente de cada gerador seria 1 − 0,75 × ICP-JC, com piso de 25%, e a base de cobrança continuaria sendo a energia gerada no mês. No nosso exercício, o ICP-JC é aproximado pelo montante que a tecnologia gera em horários críticos com base no histórico dos últimos quatro anos. b) Custos para renováveis em cada cenário de rateio Com as regras definidas, calculamos quanto solar e eólica pagariam por MWh gerado no cenário Aurora Central, em 2035. O custo total das baterias é o mesmo em todos os casos. O que muda é como ele é dividido. - Rateio simples ou consumidores pagam. O valor é o mesmo, cerca de R$ 11,3/MWh, porque o total gerado é praticamente igual ao total consumido. Só muda quem paga: - No rateio simples, pagam os geradores. artigo.texto: Brooks Town Council met Oct. 19 and approved changes to its zoning ordinance, following a series of committee-led workshops to refresh and retrofit language. “The major change to the ordinance here, besides some technical things here and there, the biggest thing was that a prohibition against data centers and cryptocurrency miners was added,” Mayor Dan Langford said. While data centers are said to need utility connections like sewer, water, and electricity, which Brooks cannot support, town officials stated intention to protect the town. Data centers are now prohibited in zoning districts of residential and agricultural, town residential, town mixed-use, institutional, and light assembly manufacturing. Within the ordinance, a data center is defined as “a centralized physical facility or building used to house computer systems, servers, and related IT equipment for storing, processing, and distributing digital information, including crypto currency activities.” The town is among several Georgia municipalities to enact a ban against data centers including neighboring jurisdictions like Fayetteville and Palmetto. “We added a size limitation for buildings,” Town Manager Maurice Ungaro said. “We have 25,000 square feet [structure] limitation.” “In other words, we have a direct prohibition against these sorts of facilities in the town… and we have an indirect way of banning those… the indirect method is the building size limitation,” Mayor Langford said. According to county officials, Fayette County is not attracting any more data centers. Fayette County Development Authority President and CEO Niki Vanderslice spoke at a Brooks Town Council meeting earlier this year indicating the town is incapable of supporting infrastructural demands for a hypothetical data center. The visit reportedly was held in response to residents’ concerns about neighboring developments in communities like Fayetteville and Tyrone and requested by Ungaro. Additionally, 27 other changes were made to the ordinance regarding punctuation, hyphenation, capitalization, and grammatical errors. For related stories and to find a link to zoning ordinance updates, visit www.fayette-news.net. In other news, council adopted a resolution to recognize “Support Your Local Chamber of Commerce Day.”

artigo.texto: SÃO PAULO, 28 Out (Reuters) - O primeiro leilão de baterias do Brasil teve edital aprovado com mudanças para permitir maior competitividade entre as empresas participantes, além de uma redação mais genérica sobre a base pagadora dos custos da contratação, conforme deliberado pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) na terça-feira. Os valores das garantias de proposta e de fiel cumprimento caíram quase 40%, acompanhando a atualização do investimento de referência para as baterias, que passou de R$9,8 milhões para R$6 milhões por megawatt (MW). Também foi aceita a possibilidade de formação de consórcios entre empresas do mesmo grupo econômico, ponto que vinha sendo pleiteado por empresas interessadas. O certame de baterias tem sido amplamente aguardado pelo setor elétrico, uma vez que ampliará o leque de recursos de segurança energética do Brasil em meio ao forte crescimento das fontes renováveis de energia, e já tem mobilizado diversos investidores, incluindo fabricantes estrangeiras e nacionais do segmento. As mudanças no edital devem ajudar a ampliar a disputa no certame inédito, que atraiu cadastramento recorde de mais de 296 gigawatts (GW) de empreendimentos, segundo a agência reguladora. Mas a Aneel manteve exigências para comprovação da capacidade financeira dos empreendedores, visando evitar a participação de "aventureiros" no leilão. Para consórcios de empresas do mesmo grupo econômico, por exemplo, a comprovação do patrimônio líquido mínimo será feita apenas por meio da controladora, de forma a evitar distorções de dupla contagem de patrimônio, como a que teria ocorrido no leilão de térmicas realizado em março. No caso de fundos de investimento em participações (FIP) com projetos participantes do leilão, deverão ser identificados os cotistas cuja participação indireta seja superior a 5%. A ideia, segundo a Aneel, é exigir a identificação dos investidores que tenham exposição econômica relevante nos projetos vencedores. Os preços-teto do leilão foram fixados em R$1,76 milhão por MW ao ano para a disputa de baterias com conteúdo nacional, marcada para 2 de dezembro, e de R$1,58 milhão por MW ao ano para a concorrência de 4 de dezembro, que não tem exigência de nacionalização. Já com relação à discussão sobre os pagadores do custo associado ao leilão, tema que ameaça causar uma judicialização, a Aneel retirou do edital referências expressas aos geradores de energia como base pagante, substituindo pela expressão "usuários de reserva de capacidade". No entanto, o regulador ressaltou que isso não muda o entendimento atual de quem são os pagadores -- os geradores, conforme definido em lei --, e nem prepara o edital para uma eventual mudança da legislação. Os geradores de energia estão se mobilizando no Congresso para conseguir mudar, antes do leilão em dezembro, o trecho de uma lei que imputa a eles os custos da contratação das baterias para o setor elétrico brasileiro. Caso isso ocorra, a Aneel irá rediscutir os contratos associados ao leilão, afirmou o relator do processo, Gentil Nogueira. "É lógico, há o interesse legítimo na modificação legislativa, a gente compreende essa posição. Mas de qualquer forma, havendo a modificação legislativa, qualquer texto que fosse colocado traria invariavelmente a discussão para a Aneel sobre os efeitos sobre esse contrato", destacou Nogueira, na véspera. (Por Letícia Fucuchima; edição de Roberto Samora)

artigo.texto: Until this week, League City’s former development code did not specifically identify data centers as a distinct use category, meaning a developer could potentially build a data center in League City by right. City officials recently changed the development code to give the city more authority over whether a data center could be built in League City. “There’s been a national discussion about data centers,” Mayor Nick Long said. “In doing some research about our own standards for data centers, [we] noticed that we really didn’t have anything that would prevent somebody from building a data center by right in certain pieces of property across League City.” How it works League City City Council voted unanimously at its Oct. 27 meeting to amend the city’s unified development code to require developers to secure a special use permit, which has to be approved by council, to build a data center in League City. The city’s Planning and Zoning Commission voted unanimously at an earlier meeting on Oct. 19 to recommend the council adopt the changes, according to city documents. After voting to approve the amendment, council voted 7-1 to approve the ordinance’s first and final reading, meaning council would not need to vote a second time at a Nov. 17 meeting to pass the ordinance. Updating the code would allow the city to review proposals to build data centers in League City on a case-by-case basis in a public setting, Long said. The discussion Council member Tom Crews cast the sole vote against adopting the changes on first and final reading, noting he wanted the city to add clearer regulatory language to address a potential data center’s impact on the community, such as water use or noise impact, before the second reading. However, some council members disagreed with Crews’ suggestion and said creating too clear standards would amount to having a “checklist” for developers to satisfy in order to move a project forward. “There is a high potential for change in what a data center is and how it operates,” council member Chad Tressler said at the meeting. “Trying to preplan around that change would be problematic.” In other news The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, which regulates the state's air quality, water quality and waste management, has shut down its electronic filing portal for certain environmental permit applications, an agency spokesperson confirmed Oct. 22, according to previous reporting by Community Impact. The shutdown comes after watchdog groups said the agency violated an order from Gov. Greg Abbott by processing nearly three dozen permit applications for data center projects.

artigo.texto: DRESDEN, Tenn. — Dresden’s Planning Commission voted Thursday to recommend new zoning regulations for data centers. The ordinance hopes to establish restrictions on where data centers could be built and how they would operate if one were to come to the city. The proposed ordinance will now go before the Dresden City Commission for a vote on the first Monday in December at the Dresden Municipal Complex. Planning Commission Chairman Tommy Moore told WPSD-TV the importance of the ordinance. “We have no regulations about data centers, and we still don’t,” Moore said. “Now we’ve made a recommendation to actually adopt these ordinances, that will give some regulation to them.” More specifically, Moore said the proposed regulations would restrict where data centers could be built, establish requirements for their distance from homes, and limit noise to 60 decibels at the nearest property line. Moore also told WPSD the ordinance includes provisions intended to protect city taxpayers from expenses associated with a potential data center. “They’re responsible for most of the expenses that deal with it, if not all of them,” Moore said. “We have made sure that it’s not going to cost the city any money.” However, before Thursday’s vote, several residents raised concerns during public comment about the potential effects of data centers on the community. Jessica Ward, a local farmer who lives outside Dresden’s city limits, said she worries about what a future development could mean for the environment and her children. “We have a local farm, and I have heard all different things about these data centers that truly worry me for our future,” Ward said. In a statement to reporters, the Tennessee Valley Authority said it has established a separate electricity rate for data centers. The rate includes additional charges intended to prevent the costs of serving those facilities from being passed on to other electricity customers.
