artigo.texto: Proposed data center in Pine Island will undergo a new environmental review due to settlement A proposed data center in Pine Island will undergo a new state environmental review as part of a lawsuit settlement. Announced Wednesday, the settlement dismisses a lawsuit by the Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy (MCEA) against Google and Ryan Companies’ proposed data center in Pine Island. Under the agreement, the MCEA will dismiss the lawsuit, and Google and Ryan Companies will complete a new Environmental Assessment Worksheet (EAW) and submit it to the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency (MPCA). The MPCA will conduct a broad analysis of how the proposed data center would affect multiple environmental and community concerns, including water and energy impacts, as well as noise and light pollution. After the study concludes, Google and Ryan Companies have agreed to develop a plan to mitigate those effects, according to the MCEA. Residents, government agencies, and other Minnesotans will then have 60 days to comment on the project. “For too long, AI data center proposals in Minnesota have been shrouded in secrecy,” Kathryn Hoffman, CEO of the MCEA, said in a statement. “This settlement brings transparency, democracy, and proper oversight back into the process, and provides Pine Island residents with critical information about how this proposal stands to impact their community and our shared natural resources. Going forward, we will continue to monitor the process and review the information as it’s released.” MCEA filed the lawsuit last October, arguing that the original environmental review of the proposal lacked the specificity and analysis required by law to accurately evaluate the project’s potential environmental impacts. Peter Fitzgerald, senior vice president of Real Estate Development at Ryan Companies, provided the following statement: “Ryan Companies is pleased that the lawsuit has been settled. Over the last three years, Ryan has built lasting relationships with the Pine Island community to deliver clear community benefits alongside a project that meets and exceeds the state’s highest standards. “The settlement confirms that previous City approvals remain valid, and we welcome the additional review by the MPCA. We believe this is a best-in-class project that has the potential to become the national standard for responsible data center development. In addition to the commitments made to the community and school, the project is investing in Minnesota’s grid with the historic clean energy investment. We are also limiting water use through the closed-loop system, which protects our water resources. We are now adding enhanced review and municipal protections with this agreement.” Luke Hellier, the public affairs manager for Google, also provided a statement: “Google is pleased to reach a constructive resolution that allows Project Skyway to move forward in Pine Island. The goal has always been to build world-class infrastructure while serving as a responsible neighbor and resource steward. This agreement ensures the project meets robust environmental standards while delivering local economic benefits. Google appreciates the collaborative work with Ryan Companies, the Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy, and the City of Pine Island to secure a sustainable path forward.”

artigo.texto: Coordenador da organização cobra análise dos impactos acumulados na região A empresa capixaba Line Solution anunciou a instalação de um data center com investimento previsto de R$ 7,4 bilhões em Baixo Guandu, no noroeste do Estado. O prefeito Lastênio Cardoso (MDB), que reassume o cargo nesta terça-feira (27) após afastamento determinado pela Justiça Eleitoral, afirmou que a água necessária ao empreendimento viria de uma represa no Rio Doce. Ele disse ter articulado a apresentação do projeto ao governo estadual, mas não soube informar se foram apresentados estudos de impacto ambiental. A expectativa de transformar o município com a instalação de um data center contrasta com as preocupações sobre a pressão adicional nos recursos hídricos da região. Enquanto o prefeito Lastênio Cardoso fala em geração de empregos e no aumento da arrecadação municipal, Merci Fardin, coordenador do Observatório Capixaba da Água e do Meio Ambiente, aponta a necessidade de avaliar os impactos do empreendimento em conjunto com os de outros projetos previstos para a região. O Projeto Rubi, apresentado ao Executivo pela Line Solution, prevê a implantação de um data center voltado ao processamento de dados e à inteligência artificial, além de condomínios logístico e industrial. O complexo ocupará uma área de aproximadamente 566 hectares, e a previsão divulgada pela empresa é iniciar as operações em 2031. O projeto ainda está nas fases de desenvolvimento, licenciamento e captação de recursos. O prefeito Lastênio Cardoso afirmou que o município reúne condições estratégicas para receber a estrutura, especialmente pela disponibilidade de água e energia. “O data center precisa de muita água e a água que nós temos aqui é a represa, no Rio Doce. Precisa de energia e já tem a energia ali do lado”, disse, em referência à Usina Hidrelétrica de Mascarenhas, localizada no Rio Doce, em Baixo Guandu. A usina foi vendida pela portuguesa EDP à VH GSEO UK Holdings Limited, subsidiária da gestora britânica de investimentos Victory Hill, em uma operação concluída em dezembro de 2022. O prefeito relatou que participou da articulação política para apresentar o projeto ao governo estadual, incluindo reuniões com secretários, o ex-governador Renato Casagrande e o vice e atual governador Ricardo Ferraço (MDB). Segundo ele, essa etapa já foi cumprida, e o avanço agora depende do empreendedor e do grupo responsável pela implantação. “Eu apenas fiz a minha parte pra ajudar politicamente”, afirmou. Questionado sobre a apresentação de estudos de impacto ambiental, Lastênio direcionou a pergunta ao empresário Mário Rodrigues, fundador e CEO da Line Solution, alegando que ele poderia fornecer informações mais precisas sobre essa etapa. Apesar de não detalhar o estágio dos estudos ambientais, o prefeito demonstrou confiança nos efeitos econômicos do empreendimento. “Eu acho que isso acontecendo transforma o nosso município, entendeu? É outro patamar, em termos de porte, em termos de emprego”, afirmou, comparando a expectativa em torno do data center à transformação que atribui à construção e à inauguração da Usina Hidrelétrica de Mascarenhas, em 1974. “Esse data center, pra nós, vai ser 100 vezes mais do que aquilo”, afirmou. A empresa estima a criação de até 550 vagas de trabalho, sendo 500 durante as obras e 50 na operação. Também projeta uma arrecadação anual de R$ 50 milhões a R$ 60 milhões em Imposto Sobre Serviços (ISS), considerando uma alíquota de 5% sobre a receita bruta. Os valores são projeções apresentadas pela própria companhia, e não receitas ou empregos já concretizados. Para Merci Fardin, a discussão que trata da instalação do complexo não pode se limitar à disponibilidade de recursos naturais nas proximidades do terreno. É necessário considerar a pressão acrescentada por diferentes empreendimentos e seus efeitos conjuntos sobre a água e as atividades econômicas existentes. O coordenador da organização chamou atenção para o risco de novos projetos serem avaliados isoladamente, sem que se considere o conjunto das intervenções previstas para a região. “Se você coloca mais um projeto, tem uma tendência de aumento do uso dos recursos hídricos, contando com os outros projetos que estão anunciados ali”, observou. Ele ressalta que o planejamento precisa levar em conta os efeitos acumulados sobre os recursos naturais provocados na expansão de diferentes atividades econômicas no Norte do Estado e defendeu que a análise do data center considere os demais empreendimentos que poderão disputar recursos e demandar infraestrutura. A preocupação é relevante diante das características do Projeto Rubi. De acordo com as informações divulgadas pela Line Solution, o data center terá capacidade computacional inicial de 100 megawatts (MW). A estrutura vai ser voltada ao processamento de grandes volumes de dados, atividade que exige fornecimento contínuo de energia e sistemas de controle térmico para manter os equipamentos em funcionamento. Apesar de empresa afirmar que utilizará um sistema fechado de resfriamento, com reutilização contínua da água e reposição mensal estimada em volume equivalente ao consumo de três casas populares, essa projeção precisa ser analisada à luz dos dados técnicos do projeto, incluindo a fonte de abastecimento, a demanda efetiva e as condições de disponibilidade hídrica do território. Ainda não há, nas informações divulgadas sobre o empreendimento, detalhamento suficiente para confirmar qual manancial vai ser utilizado para abastecer o complexo, qual volume será solicitado ou se já foi protocolado pedido de outorga para captação de água. A identificação da fonte é essencial para determinar quais órgãos são responsáveis pela autorização de uso. O Rio Doce é um curso d’água de domínio federal, enquanto a competência sobre outros mananciais depende do enquadramento de cada corpo hídrico. artigo.texto: Read the battery storage moratorium, meeting starts at 7pm in the town hall From the Town of Amity, TOWN OF AMITY RESIDENTS: There will be a 2027 budget hearing on November 2, 2026, at 7:00 pm at the town hall. This is the same date and time for the proposed local law to impose a Moratorium on Large Battery Energy Storage Systems and a local law to Repeal and Replace the Local Law for Solar Energy System Regulation. TOWN OF AMITY Proposed Local Law No. 2 of the Year 2026 A Local Law to Impose a Moratorium on Large Battery Energy Storage Systems Be it enacted by the Town Board of the Town of Amity as follows: Section Title. This Local Law shall be known as the “Moratorium on Large Battery Energy Storage Systems.” Section 20 Authority and Intent; Findings; Purpose. ao Authority and Intent. This Local Law is intended to be consistent with and is adopted pursuant to the laws of the State of New York, including but not limited to the following authorities: New York State Constitution Article IX, N2(c)(ii)(10); Municipal Home Rule Law Sl 0; Statute of Local Governments S 10. bo Findings of Fact. The Town Board makes the following Findings of Fact relating to this Local Law: l . Amity is a community that takes great pride in and assigns great value to its rural residential character, small-town atmosphere, fine agricultural lands, Genesee River access, trails, and cultural, recreational, scenic and other natural resources. - Preservation of the Town’s irreplaceable recreational and scenic sites, high-quality agricultural land, air quality and water quality, and priceless and unique character, is of significant value to the inhabitants of the Town and to the people who visit the Town. - The Town’s rich natural environment is a valuable asset that creates a sense of identity and well-being for residents of the area. Preserving and protecting the scenic, recreational, other natural resources and aesthetics of the Town is important for both a healthy environment and vibrant economy. - As renewable power sources like wind and solar provide a larger portion of New York’s electricity, energy storage systems will allow clean energy to be available when and where it is most needed and better use existing resources more efficiently and with fewer emissions. New York State has adopted policy and law to promote the installation of energy storage systems to be integrated into solar and wind energy projects and in critical locations within the electrical distribution and transmission grid. - The Town supports the use of energy storage systems with appropriate regulations to promote and preserve the health, safety and welfare of the Town and its citizens. - Large Battery Energy Storage Systems are battery energy storage systems that are usually integrated with Solar Energy System Facilities or connected directly into the electrical distribution or transmission grid. - While battery energy storage systems are regulated by the New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code, the Town does not currently have regulations for the siting and installation of Large Battery Energy Storage Systems and the Town Planning Board has begun reviewing various possible regulations to address these uses. - Allowing the activities prohibited by Section 4 (Moratorium and Prohibitions) of this Local Law without first obtaining more education and information may impair the existing character of the Town, because by their nature, such activities may have the potential to produce a combination of negative impacts upon the environment and people living in or in proximity to the communities in which they are located. Negative impacts suggested to be associated with those activities include, without limitation, noise, emergency response and fire fighting considerations, damage to roadways, damage to and loss of agricultural lands and soils, damage to and loss of open space, natural areas, and scenic views, decreased recreational opportunities, and loss of tourism. During the effectiveness of this Local Law, the Town Board can study and draft revisions to the Existing Solar Energy System Facilities law and regulations for Large Battery Energy Storage Systems, and study the activities prohibited by Section 4 of this Local Law and determine whether to amend the Town Battery energy storage laws. c. Purpose. The purpose of this Local Law is to enable the Town to stay any and all of the activities prohibited by Section 4 of this Local Law, and all Town-level approvals relating to those activities for a period of twelve (12) months in order to provide the Town time to study the impacts, effects, and to consider amendments to the Town ‘s Large Battery storage laws to appropriately address the same within the confines of New York State law. The Town Board believes that a twelve-month moratorium after the effective date of this Local Law, coupled with the mechanism for Land Use Permits After Appeal, as are available under Section 8.3 of the Town’s Land Use Law (Local Law No. I of 2017) , will achieve an appropriate balancing of interests between the need to safeguard the character and other resources of the Town and the health, safety and general welfare of its residents, and the rights of individual property owners or businesses desiring to conduct such activities during that period. artigo.texto: FIMER has launched its next-generation PVS990 series of utility-scale central inverters and battery energy storage system (BESS) power conversion systems (PCS) at the Renewable Energy India (REI) Expo 2026, held from October 22 to 24 at India Expo Mart, Greater Noida. The newly launched PVS990-2000 is a 2 MW central inverter designed for utility-scale solar power plants and energy storage applications. The platform offers power ratings ranging from 2,000 kVA to 8,000 kVA, with a scalable architecture aimed at supporting multi-megawatt installations while improving system efficiency and reducing installation time. Technical Features The inverter features a DC input voltage of up to 1,500 V, grid-support capabilities, including power quality management and fault ride-through (FRT), and protection systems on both the DC and AC sides. It also supports SCADA-based industrial data communication and is designed to operate without a separate chiller installation. "The PVS990 is the result of FIMER's continued investment in R&D, shaped by the evolving needs and feedback of our customers across the global utility-scale market. We have brought together decades of power-electronics expertise, advanced engineering and real-world project insights to create a platform that is distinctive in its scalability, performance and grid-support capabilities. With the PVS990, we are redefining what customers can expect from utility-scale solar and storage systems," said KN Sreevatsa, Group Co-CEO, FIMER. Alongside the launch, FIMER showcased its portfolio of solar and storage solutions for residential, commercial and industrial (C&I), and utility-scale applications at Hall 16, Booth A90. Its residential portfolio included the PowerUNO single-phase hybrid inverter and PowerTRIO three-phase hybrid inverter series under its Power Platform. For the C&I segment, the company showcased its PVS-100/120-TL inverter range, now available under the Make in India initiative, alongside its PVM-75/125-TL series. The latter is designed for modular C&I applications and supports AC-coupled battery storage systems. 415kW Utility-Scale String Inverter FIMER also displayed its PVM-415, a 415 kW utility-scale string inverter. The company highlighted its inverter solutions for retrofitting older solar power plants, aimed at helping plant operators improve system performance, reliability and operational efficiency by upgrading existing inverter infrastructure. FIMER's portfolio draws on technologies developed across its manufacturing facilities in Italy and India, reflecting its presence in the Indian and global renewable energy markets.

artigo.texto: Rodan Installing 50-MWh Battery Storage Behind Meter at Ontario Cement Plant An Ontario cement supplier will install 50-MWh in on-site energy storage capacity that promises to be the biggest behind-the-meter battery project in Canada so far. St. Marys Cement is working with Rodan Energy Solutions which will install the battery storage system at the cement production site in Bowmanville, Ontario. Rodan will develop, own and operate the system which it hopes to put into commercial operation by May 2028. The cement supplier will utilize the batteries to reduce peak electricity demand and gain some long-term energy savings without a prohibitive upfront capital investment cost. “Our Bowmanville plant has been part of the community since 1968, and we have continued to invest in its long-term performance. This project brings together energy cost management, operational resilience and our sustainability roadmap in a practical way,” Jorge Wagner, CEO of St. Marys Cement parent company Votorantim Cimentos, said in a statement. “By helping us reduce demand on the grid during periods of peak system demand while supporting reliable plant operations, the project reflects Sustainable Legacy, one of the values of Our VC Way, and our commitment to creating lasting value for our operations and communities,” Wagner added. The St. Marys project will be Votorantim Cimentos’ first behind-the-meter battery storage project in North America. The battery system will be synchronized with the grid but also capable of powering the cement plant during periods of high provincial electricity demand, helping offset the need for on-site generation such as diesel power which would raise greenhouse gas emissions. Votorantim would compensate Rodan Energy through its own savings from both energy use and grid services. Rodan will optimize the system through its FlexOps energy management platform. “This agreement is a demonstration of what behind-the-meter BESS can deliver for large industrial energy users – real economic savings, a lower emissions footprint, and energy security they control,” Rodan Energy Solutions CEO Paul Grod said. “We are actively building a North American portfolio of projects like this one, and we are looking for the right C&I partners, financiers, battery manufacturers, and EPCs to grow with us.” Rodan currently manages about 1,500 MW of distributed energy resources throughout North American electricity markets. Commercial and industrial customers increasingly are seeking on-site battery storage to handle frequency regulation, on-site power and transient load challenges. St. Marys Cement has operated a plant in Ontario dating back 114 years. Its current facility’s capacity exceeds five million metric tons of cement production annually. Globally, the cement industry emits close to 2.5 billion metric tons in greenhouse gases annually, accounting for about 6% of total industrial emissions around the world. artigo.texto: Trending A handful of companies and a handful of U.S. states - including Ohio - could account for most of the increased electricity demands from the rapid growth of artificial intelligence that could drive up electric power prices, according to a new study by Ohio State University. Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle and Apple will consume 75% of the increased demand for electricity to power data centers, the study said. "The rapid emergence of generative artificial intelligence and large-scale data analytics has driven a sharp expansion of computational demand," the study said. Companies tend to build clusters of data centers in areas with strong energy availability, a mature electric grid and fiber-optic infrastructure, favorable climatic conditions and supportive policy environment, the study said. "In North America, clusters are concentrated in regions such as Virginia, Texas, Ohio, and North Carolina, which coincide with established hyperscale infrastructure, large electricity markets, and documented policy support for data-center development," the Ohio State study said. In areas where clusters are located, there will be an increase in demand for electricity. "Fewer than 10 regions account for nearly two-thirds of total projected demand, indicating a strong concentration of infrastructure in a limited number of states and countries. Oregon, Virginia, Iowa, Ohio and Ireland emerge as dominant hubs," according to the study. Combined annual data center electricity consumption worldwide could increase from about 118 terawatt-hours in 2024 to between 239 and 295 terawatt-hours by 2030, the study concluded. A key question raised by the study is who will pay for the increased power supply required for data centers. "For households, farms and businesses, the implications depend partly on whether data center customers cover the infrastructure costs associated with their demand," Ohio State professor Ani L. Katchova, said in a statement. If not, consumers and businesses could face higher electric rates, she said. However, the boom in data centers is also expected to produce a huge windfall in tax revenues. A study by Bain and Company estimated that the expansion in artificial intelligence could produce nearly $2 trillion a year in revenues by 2030, "equivalent to the combined GDP of the world's 10 largest emerging economies." The Ohio-based Buckeye Institute, a non-profit group, has opposed any moratoriums on new data centers in Ohio, saying that the best choice is to make sure the companies pay for any additional costs. "While Ohio policymakers should not dismiss legitimate public concerns about data centers, they should reject moratoriums on their construction," said Aswin Prabhakar, an economic research analyst at The Buckeye Institute. "A better approach would increase transparency, require data center developers to bear the risks and costs of their projects, ensure they pay all their local property taxes, and ensure government regulations address real problems while creating a fair process for project approval." Tax revenue isn't everything, says a group called Conserve Ohio that has tried to ban construction of large data centers in the state. "Rushing to replace human workers with AI," is a downside for society, one of the leaders of Conserve Ohio, Andrew Gula, told The Center Square. Another is large corporations paving over large swaths of land, Gula said. Data centers are "dragging us away from renewable energy sources," Gula added. "Essentially my whole life climate change has been talked about," Gula said. "Now it's all out the window and we're just putting gas turbines everywhere. No thought for the future, only focus is on AI and the narrative that China is gunning for us."

artigo.texto: The U.S. data center boom is emerging as a key issue in political advertising on social media in the home stretch of the midterm campaign season, a Pew Research Center analysis finds. Spending on political ads mentioning data centers has increased exponentially in the run-up to the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. Over a period of 90 days from Jul. 27 to Oct. 24, advertisers on Facebook and Instagram spent almost $12 million on ads that mention data centers in the context of social issues, elections or politics. (In this analysis, we refer to these ads as “political ads.”) As recently as January, pro-data center sentiment was slightly more common in this advertising than anti-data center sentiment. Among political ads mentioning data centers, 42% were supportive of them while 31% were critical. The remainder did not take a clear stance. But since the beginning of this year, ads that mention data centers have grown increasingly critical. So far in October, 57% of these ads have expressed opposition to data centers, while just 3% have been clearly in favor of them. This Pew Research Center analysis looks at U.S. political ads on Facebook and Instagram that discuss data centers. Why did we do this? Pew Research Center does research to help the public, media and decision-makers understand important topics. This research builds on our recent work about data centers and artificial intelligence. Facebook and Instagram advertising data comes from the Meta Ad Library API. The Ad Library is maintained by Meta and includes every advertisement about politics, elections or social issues appearing on Meta platforms worldwide. For simplicity, we use “political ads” throughout this post to refer to these ads. For this analysis, we identified every ad in the Ad Library that mentioned data centers in its text or audio and ran on Facebook or Instagram in the United States from Jan. 1 to Oct. 24, 2026. Most of the ads we identified (87%) ran on both platforms. For each ad, we collected its text, the states in which it ran and how much was spent to run it. Meta provides ad spending data as a range, so we used the midpoint of each ad spend range when calculating total spending. We then used GPT-5.6 Luna to determine if each ad: Is critical of data centers, supportive of data centers or does not take a clear stance on them Mentions topics in a data center context, including large corporations, energy use, water use, the environment, jobs and taxation Whether the ad promotes a particular candidate for office, and if so whether that candidate is a Republican or Democrat Across all of these categories, the model achieved an average F1 score of 0.88 and 95% accuracy on a validation dataset of 300 ads coded by trained human coders. See the full model prompt we used to classify these ads. We also used several other data sources to complement this analysis. These include historical data on total political ad spending from the Meta Ad Library Report as of Oct. 24; the number of competitive House, Senate and gubernatorial races in each state, according to the Cook Political Report on Oct. 24; and the number of current and planned data centers in each state based on Data Center Map estimates on Oct. 27. What issues are discussed in ads about data centers? Facebook and Instagram ads that criticize data centers often mention corporate interests % of __ U.S. political ads on Facebook and Instagram mentioning data centers that discuss their impacts on … Source: Analysis of 13,956 ads about social issues, elections or politics that mentioned data centers and ran in the U.S. on Facebook or Instagram from July 27 to Oct. 24, 2026. PEW RESEARCH CENTER Share this chart Facebook and Instagram ads that criticize data centers often mention corporate interests % of __ U.S. political ads on Facebook and Instagram mentioning data centers that discuss their impacts on … Source: Analysis of 13,956 ads about social issues, elections or politics that mentioned data centers and ran in the U.S. on Facebook or Instagram from July 27 to Oct. 24, 2026. PEW RESEARCH CENTER Some common themes emerge in political ads on Facebook and Instagram that mention data centers: Large corporations and their involvement in data center development (mentioned in 30% of all political ads about data centers) Data centers’ energy use (24%) Environmental effects of data centers and the water required to run them (17% and 15%, respectively) Certain themes are more common in ads that are critical of data centers than in ads that support them. For example, nearly half of ads that oppose data centers discuss the corporate interests behind them, like the tech industry or utility companies. That is roughly double the share of pro-data center ads that mention these interests. Meanwhile, ads that support data centers disproportionately discuss their impact on jobs. Who pays for ads about data centers? A majority (61%) of recent spending on Facebook and Instagram political ads about data centers has been on ads that don’t promote specific candidates for office. These ads are typically paid for by advocacy groups. More than half of these ads (56%) express opposition to data centers, but 13% are supportive – a much larger share than among campaign ads. The remaining 39% of recent spending has been for ads that support specific candidates. Of the campaign ads in our analysis period, 72% promote Democratic candidates and 15% promote Republican candidates, while the remainder are for independent candidates or those whose party affiliation could not be determined. A majority of these campaign ads are critical of data centers, and this holds true across party lines. Pro-data center ads are rare for both parties, occurring in less than 1% of campaign ads overall. In other words, Democratic candidates are more likely than Republicans to post political ads about data centers.But when they do talk about data centers, Democratic and Republican candidates are similarly critical of them. artigo.texto: On October 27, Brazil's National Electric Energy Agency (ANEEL) unanimously approved the tender documents for two battery storage capacity reserve auctions, to be held on December 2 and 4. They will be Brazil's first centralized procurement of battery energy storage. A day earlier, the Brazilian Photovoltaic Solar Energy Association (ABSOLAR) submitted its 2027–2030 energy agenda to the re-elected Lula government, proposing 8 GW of utility-scale storage by 2030 and an annual, technology-neutral capacity auction mechanism, with the two December auctions as its starting point. SMM believes the first auctions matter mainly because they will set price and contract benchmarks for utility-scale storage in Brazil, while near-term equipment demand depends on the procurement volume ultimately announced by the Ministry of Mines and Energy (MME). Because the domestic-content auction takes priority and the open auction fills the remainder, imported systems will still need to cover whatever local capacity cannot supply. Chinese storage suppliers will enter the market through two routes: local partnerships and the open auction. Two Auctions: Domestic Content First, Open Auction Fills the Gap Both auctions procure reserve capacity from new electrochemical storage projects connected to Brazil's National Interconnected System (SIN). The December 2 "National Storage" auction is limited to projects that meet the minimum local-content requirements of the Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) and has priority in meeting the procurement demand set by the MME. The December 4 "Storage" auction has no equipment-origin requirement. The MME has set ceiling prices of R$1.76 million/MW per year and R$1.58 million/MW per year, respectively, putting the domestic-content auction about 11.4% higher. Winning projects will sign 15-year contracts and begin supplying capacity on August 1, 2028. They will receive a fixed annual payment for available capacity, paid in 12 monthly installments regardless of dispatch, with deductions for underperformance. Each project must be at least 30 MW, sustain maximum output for four hours, run no more than two cycles a day and 366 cycles a year, fully recharge within six hours, achieve round-trip efficiency of at least 85%, and provide grid-forming capability. Projects connecting at critical grid nodes receive a locational bonus in the bidding. Over 6,000 Projects Registered, Far Exceeding Any Likely Procurement Volume According to Brazil's Energy Research Office (EPE), more than 6,000 projects totaling 296.9 GW registered for the two auctions. The MME has yet to announce the procurement volume. The Brazilian Association of Energy Storage Solutions (ABSAE) estimates Brazil's 2028 power shortfall at about 4.5 GW, putting registered capacity at roughly 66 times that gap. Registration did not require environmental licenses, so the bar was low and registered capacity should not be read as effective supply. ANEEL has set the bid bond at R$60,000/MW, and both the performance bond and the minimum net-worth requirement at R$600,000/MW. Developers bear grid-connection risk, and delays in connection facilities will not automatically postpone the supply start date. Financial strength, grid access, and equipment delivery capability will be the main filters for projects. Local-Content Threshold: Domestic Capacity Cannot Cover All Demand In the first phase, which runs through the end of 2027, BNDES divides a storage system into eight components, four of which are classed as strategic. A qualifying system must combine at least three components, including at least one strategic component, and reach a national-content index of at least 15% by value. BNDES has so far accredited BYD, Gotion High-Tech, Moura, TBEA, Trina Storage, SecPower, WEG, and You.On as storage system suppliers. Supply capacity remains the main constraint. ABSAE's early-July survey put expected domestic capacity under existing localization routes at about 12 GWh, or roughly 3 GW. If the 2028 shortfall of 4.5 GW were met entirely with four-hour batteries, storage demand would be about 18 GWh, so domestic capacity could cover only about two-thirds. The remainder would still have to come from imported systems in the open auction. The cost gap is equally pronounced. Based on SMM research, initial quotes for localized systems were 40%–50% higher than for fully imported systems, although they have since eased. On a 15-year contract basis, and with BNDES financing and low-cost Climate Fund loans, a localized system can approach the project returns of an imported one if its premium is held to around 25%. The domestic-content auction's ceiling price is only about 11.4% above the open auction's, well below the equipment premium. Because capacity revenue must cover the full cost of equipment, construction, grid connection, and financing, whether domestic-content projects can win within the ceiling price depends largely on how much of the equipment premium low-cost financing can offset. Unresolved Issues: Procurement Volume and Cost Allocation The biggest uncertainties are the procurement volume and who pays. The MME has not yet published demand for either auction. Under current rules, capacity procurement costs are allocated entirely to generators, an arrangement ANEEL kept in its latest review. Some generators argue that this conflicts with technology neutrality and had earlier called for the auctions to be postponed, while a bill in Congress proposes shifting the cost to electricity consumers. ABSOLAR's agenda again calls for the relevant rules to be amended. ABSOLAR's Agenda: An 8 GW Target, Annual Auctions, and Battery Tax Cuts ABSOLAR's agenda comprises three commitments. Bateria Brasil (Battery Brazil) proposes 8 GW of utility-scale storage by 2030, annual technology-neutral capacity auctions, and cutting battery taxes to the level applied to renewables. artigo.texto: LG Energy Solution powers up battery manufacturing with North American expansion LG Energy Solution is hitting the gas on its competitiveness with its 46-series cylindrical battery cells, backed by a robust supply chain for fast-tracked market expansion to leverage its elite global production network. The LG Energy Solution Michigan-Lansing battery plantLG ENERGY SOLUTION LG Energy Solution is hitting the gas on its competitiveness with its 46-series cylindrical battery cells, backed by a robust supply chain for fast-tracked market expansion to leverage its elite global production network. On Oct. 1, the battery maker signed a memorandum of understanding with indiGOtech, a promising U.S. electric commercial vehicle startup. Under the agreement, the two firms will integrate LG Energy Solution’s cells for the automaker’s next-generation EVs. The partnership is expected to secure a stable supply chain for advanced battery technologies for upcoming commercial EVs, while expanding the Korean company’s 46-series supply references across North America to strengthen its market position. IndiGOtech is expanding its business horizons by integrating charging infrastructure and digital mobility services with its vehicles under a Transportation-as-a-Service business model. Driven by the broader electrification wave, the e-commerce boom and advances in battery technology, the EV market continues to build momentum. According to Global Market Insights, the global electric van market valued at roughly $16.3 billion in 2024 is forecast to surge to about $65.6 billion by 2034, registering a compound annual growth rate of 15.5 percent. The company aims to broaden plans to secure new global orders for 46-series cells by strengthening domestic manufacturing and opening a production facility in Queen Creek, Arizona. LG Energy Solution is accelerating its overall order intake, backed by a differentiated product lineup including 46-series and high-voltage midnickel cells. The company also seamlessly bridges Energy Storage Systems (ESS) and EV batteries through strategic rebalancing. In August, the company celebrated the full launch of its Lansing, Michigan, plant and finalized a quintuple production hub network of ESSs across North America. Designed as a versatile complex, the Lansing plant will manufacture both lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries for ESS and nickel manganese cobalt cells for batteries, achieving a total annual production capacity of over 35 gigawatt-hours. Beginning with pouch-type cell production for ESS this year, the company will kick off mass production of prismatic LFP batteries and anchor the North American supply chain in the EV business by supplying Toyota. With the Lansing plant operational, LG Energy Solution has completed its five-site North American ESS production network comprising sites in Lansing and Holland in Michigan, NextStar Energy in Ontario, L-H Battery Company in Ohio with Honda and Ultium Cells in Tennessee with GM, providing the operational agility to support EV and ESS lines in response to shifting market demand. artigo.texto: ACME Solar Holdings is seeing early returns from its battery energy storage business, with partially commissioned projects and short-term peak-power contracts beginning to contribute to revenue. Encouraged by the progress, the company has raised its battery energy storage system (BESS) commissioning target for FY27 to more than 12 GWh from the earlier 10 GWh. It has also doubled its BESS capacity target for 2030 to 50 GWh from 25 GWh, while raising its renewable energy capacity ambition to 15 GW from 10 GW. The change in strategy reflects the growing role of battery storage in ACME's business. Rather than waiting for an entire solar-plus-storage project to become operational, the company is commissioning batteries wherever grid connectivity is available and looking to generate revenue from them through peak-power sales. The Early Positive Signs ACME had commissioned around 5.2 GWh of BESS capacity by the end of the first half of FY27, meeting its initial target of 5 GWh. Around 1.9 GW of its contracted projects have also been partially commissioned. On the solar side, 1.7 GW of modules have been delivered to project sites, of which 1.1 GW has been installed. The company said 200 MWp of the installed capacity had already been charged, with the remaining modules expected to be charged by November-December 2026. The early commissioning of batteries is beginning to translate into commercial activity. ACME said it had secured more than ₹1,600 crore in revenue through short-term contracts for partial sale of its FY27 capacity. It has also locked in more than ₹1,500 crore for partial sale of FY28 capacity. During the quarter, the company sold 324 million units through short-term peak-power contracts. This growing contribution from storage operations has coincided with a sharp rise in quarterly earnings. ACME reported revenue of ₹1,007 crore in Q2 FY27, up 67.5% year-on-year, while EBITDA increased 63.6% to ₹874 crore. Net profit rose 133.5% to ₹269 crore. For ACME, the attraction of BESS is not just the additional capacity it brings to the portfolio, but the opportunity to start earning from projects earlier. Management made this shift in priorities clear during the earnings call, saying the company would focus on the quality of earnings and returns rather than simply chasing capacity additions. “Megawatts matter. But the measure we would ourselves to earnings growth and the quality of these earnings,” management said. Under Control BESS Prices The company is also trying to keep storage project costs under control by installing batteries at locations where the required grid infrastructure is already in place. This avoids fresh spending on transformers and AC infrastructure, which would otherwise be needed for greenfield installations. ACME said its capitalised BESS cost was currently between ₹90 lakh and ₹1 crore per MWh. Using existing infrastructure saves around ₹20 lakh per MWh, according to management. “We have been able to do between ₹90 lakh to ₹1 crore kind of a number for the CapEx which we have capitalised on our books,” management said. The company expects battery costs to remain stable or decline, although the outlook will depend on raw material prices and other supply-side factors. Another part of the strategy is to use available solar power to charge batteries. At some project locations, the battery is ready to operate even though the associated solar capacity is not fully commissioned. ACME is using the available generation to charge the batteries and sell power when demand is higher. The company also sees an opportunity in using curtailed solar power for battery charging and subsequent merchant sales. This could help it make use of electricity that would otherwise go unutilised, while improving battery utilisation and cash flows. Peak-power demand strengthens the case for BESS ACME's expansion plans are also riding on what management sees as a change in the way electricity is being procured in India. States are increasingly looking for power during peak-demand hours, creating an opportunity for storage-backed renewable projects. “Everybody is short on peak power, and nobody wants to be dependent on the weather patterns to assess their demand,” management said during the call. The company pointed to 50 GWh of peak-power tenders rolled out by September 2027 and more than 20 GW of upcoming tenders across solar-plus-storage and other configurations. It also expects 200-250 GWh of short-term peak-power contracts to come up in the near to medium term. ACME recently signed an additional 400 MW PPA with NTPC, taking its contracted portfolio to around 92% of the total 8,370 MW. It has also contracted around 19 GWh of BESS equipment from suppliers including CATL, Ganfeng and Trina. Execution will determine whether the higher targets are achievable The bigger challenge now is to turn the expanded pipeline into operational capacity. Transmission connectivity delays continue to affect project timelines, although ACME is trying to limit the impact by prioritising battery installations at locations where grid infrastructure is already available. Management is targeting around 1.5 GW of capacity commissioning in FY27, while acknowledging that some projects could spill over by a quarter depending on commissioning timelines. For FY28, the company expects to add around 2.5-3 GW. The expansion will also require substantial capital. ACME said it had incurred approximately ₹6,500 crore in capital expenditure during the first half of FY27 and expects spending in the second half to be similar or higher. Its weighted average cost of debt for fully operational projects stood at around 8.4%. Management said approximately 65% of operational borrowings came from institutions such as PFC and REC, which it believes provides some protection against frequent interest-rate changes. artigo.texto: Rodan Energy vai desenvolver o maior sistema de armazenamento de baterias atrás do medidor do Canadá na St. Marys Cement A Rodan Energy Solutions Inc. e a St. Marys Cement Inc. (Canadá), subsidiária da Votorantim Cimentos North America, anunciaram um acordo de longo prazo em 27 de outubro de 2026, segundo comunicado à imprensa da empresa. O acordo abrange o desenvolvimento, a propriedade e a otimização de um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias de 50 megawatts-hora atrás do medidor na instalação da St. Marys Cement em Bowmanville, Ontário, que as empresas descrevem como a maior instalação de BESS atrás do medidor do Canadá até hoje. Pelo arranjo, a Rodan Energy vai desenvolver, possuir e operar o ativo e fornecer otimização energética contínua por meio de sua plataforma FlexOps. A Rodan assume o capital de desenvolvimento e o risco operacional, enquanto a St. Marys Cement recebe uma solução energética de longo prazo totalmente gerenciada, sem desembolso de capital inicial. O sistema de baterias foi projetado para permitir que a fábrica reduza sua demanda da rede durante os períodos de pico de consumo de eletricidade, mantendo as operações essenciais. Ele também permitirá o carregamento em períodos de menor demanda para uso nos períodos de pico elevado, reduzindo a demanda da rede quando a intensidade de carbono da eletricidade pode ser maior. Para a Votorantim Cimentos North America, o projeto marca um passo em uma estratégia mais ampla de melhoria do desempenho energético, da resiliência operacional e da sustentabilidade. A fábrica de Bowmanville opera desde 1968, e a empresa tem continuado a investir na instalação e na comunidade do entorno. O projeto apoia o roteiro de sustentabilidade da VCNA, incluindo o compromisso de concreto net-zero até 2050 e metas intermediárias para 2030. Paul Grod, presidente e CEO da Rodan Energy Solutions, indicou que o acordo demonstra o que o armazenamento atrás do medidor pode entregar a grandes consumidores industriais de energia, citando economia financeira, menor pegada de emissões e segurança energética sob controle do cliente. Ele observou que o desempenho da Rodan está diretamente vinculado aos resultados para seu cliente e que a empresa está construindo um portfólio norte-americano de projetos semelhantes, enquanto busca parceiros comerciais e industriais, financiadores, fabricantes de baterias e empresas de engenharia, aquisições e construção. Jorge Wagner, presidente e CEO da Votorantim Cimentos North America, disse que a fábrica de Bowmanville faz parte da comunidade desde 1968 e que a empresa tem continuado a investir em seu desempenho de longo prazo. Ele descreveu o projeto como uma combinação prática de gestão de custos de energia, resiliência operacional e o roteiro de sustentabilidade, refletindo o valor Legado Sustentável do VC Way da empresa e seu compromisso com valor duradouro para as operações e as comunidades. Ele acrescentou que a Rodan traz capacidade técnica, compromisso de longo prazo e profundidade operacional ao longo da vida do ativo. Base para Novos Projetos Como primeiro projeto desse tipo da VCNA, a instalação de Bowmanville cria uma base para avaliar oportunidades semelhantes em outras operações da VCNA. As empresas afirmam que ele demonstra como a infraestrutura energética direcionada pode apoiar a produção confiável, a eficiência de custos e o avanço rumo aos compromissos de sustentabilidade. Escala da Plataforma FlexOps O projeto da St. Marys funciona na plataforma de otimização FlexOps da Rodan, que atualmente gerencia mais de 1.500 MW de recursos energéticos distribuídos em toda a América do Norte, incluindo carga interrompível, geração e sistemas de armazenamento de baterias conectados à rede e atrás do medidor. A Rodan afirma que o portfólio está crescendo rapidamente para atender à demanda do mercado de eletricidade norte-americano. A Rodan está expandindo seu portfólio de BESS atrás do medidor e convida a parcerias de consumidores comerciais e industriais de energia que buscam soluções de custo e resiliência de longo prazo, bem como de fabricantes de baterias, empresas de EPC, investidores e instituições financeiras. A empresa também está em discussões ativas com hyperscalers, operadores de data centers de grande porte, consumidores industriais e comerciais, frotas de veículos elétricos e concessionárias para as quais o armazenamento atrás do medidor é uma solução cada vez mais prática para a demanda de energia, as restrições da rede e os compromissos de energia limpa. A Rodan Energy Solutions se descreve como uma empresa líder norte-americana de otimização de rede e serviços de energia, cuja plataforma FlexOps gerencia mais de 1.500 MW de recursos energéticos distribuídos para produtores de energia, concessionárias e grandes consumidores de energia. A Votorantim Cimentos North America faz parte da Votorantim Cimentos, descrita como uma das maiores empresas de materiais de construção e soluções sustentáveis do mundo. Na América do Norte, a VCNA fornece cimento, concreto, agregados e materiais de construção relacionados. Com sede em Toronto, Ontário, Canadá, a VCNA tem mais de 130 unidades na América do Norte e opera sob as marcas St Marys Cement, Canada Building Materials, Prairie Materials, Superior Materials e United Materials. Este relatório fornece uma análise aprofundada do mercado de cimento no Canadá, cobrindo tamanho de mercado, crescimento, demanda, oferta, fluxos comerciais, preços, cenário competitivo e previsões até 2035. O estudo é projetado para fabricantes, distribuidores, importadores, exportadores, investidores, equipes de compras, consultores e equipes de estratégia que precisam de uma visão consistente e orientada por dados da dinâmica do mercado e de uma definição analítica transparente do escopo do produto. artigo.texto: DNV, the independent energy expert and assurance provider, has acted as technical advisor during a technical due diligence (TDD) process for financing of a €50 million portfolio of three standalone battery energy storage systems (BESS) being developed by the independent energy storage provider and infrastructure developer, Return Energy, in the Spanish province of Bizkaia. The projects, located in Güeñes, Barakaldo, and Lezama, will provide a combined power capacity of 55 MW and storage capacity of 220 MWh. The portfolio is, to date, the largest standalone battery storage portfolio in Spain to reach financial close. As technical advisor, DNV provided an independent assessment of the project design, technology selection, contracts, and key technical risks, together with recommendations to mitigate those risks and support the financing process. Spain’s electricity system is expected to require substantial growth in energy storage capacity as the share of variable renewable generation increases. BESS can help balance differences between electricity production and demand, support grid stability, and provide additional flexibility to the power system. The projects form part of Return Energy’s wider pipeline in the Basque Country, which exceeds 1400 MWh of energy storage capacity and 352.6 MW of power capacity. Brice Le Gallo, Vice-President and Regional Director for Southern Europe, MEA & LATAM, Energy Systems at DNV, commented: “Energy storage is becoming an increasingly important part of Spain’s power system as renewable generation grows. DNV’s Energy Transition Outlook for Spain shows that a more electrified, renewables-based energy system will require substantially more storage to provide flexibility and support grid stability. Projects reaching financial close are an important part of moving energy storage development from planning into deployment. Our role is to provide an independent view of the technology, design, and technical risks so that the parties involved can make investment decisions with greater confidence.” Steve Sceery, Country Head for Return Energy in Spain, added: “DNV has been a key partner to help us complete the financing for this landmark transaction in Spain. They brought to bear their full technical expertise on what is a new asset class here in Spain which was instrumental in ensuring a swift and successful transaction. We valued both their knowledge and agility in this process.” Carlos Albero, Market Manager for Iberia, concluded: “DNV combines experience from established battery storage markets including the US, the UK, the Nordics, and Chile with its local energy expertise in Spain. Our work on the Bizkaia portfolio reflects the growing role of independent technical assessment as standalone storage moves from an emerging segment towards wider deployment in the Spanish market.” Spain’s National Energy and Climate Plan foresees a substantial expansion of storage capacity by 2030: 22.5 GW, including 12.5 related to BESS. With deployment still at an early stage, projects now reaching financing and construction will help determine how quickly storage can scale alongside renewable generation. The issue also explores topics such as offshore wind foundations, solar maintenance, training the new workforce, inspection & maintenance, and more! With insights from experts such as Everllence, BW Ideol, EM&I, Watson Farley & Williams, and many more, make sure to check out this issue now.

artigo.texto: Embrapii supera mil projetos de IA; interesse estrangeiro cresce No ABES Summit, Finep detalha mudanças no financiamento à inovação e ApexBrasil relata procura de fundos chineses por data centers. A Empresa Brasileira de Pesquisa e Inovação Industrial (Embrapii) já apoiou mais de mil projetos que utilizam IA, como tecnologia principal ou incorporada a processos e produtos. Somente em 2025, foram iniciadas 255 iniciativas nessa área, ante cerca de 35 em 2020. Os números foram apresentados por Túlio Oliveira, líder de Programas Prioritários da instituição, durante o ABES Summit 2026, realizado nesta terça-feira, 27 de outubro, em São Paulo. Desde o início de suas operações, em 2014, a Embrapii acumula mais de 4,5 mil projetos de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação, envolvendo aproximadamente 3 mil empresas. Segundo Oliveira, entre 20% e 25% dessas iniciativas incorporam IA, seja no desenvolvimento de soluções específicas, seja em aplicações como manutenção preditiva, eficiência energética e otimização de processos industriais. “Está evoluindo, tem se tornado cada vez mais nativo”, afirmou o executivo, ao comentar o aumento das propostas que já incluem IA desde sua concepção. O avanço da demanda por recursos foi discutido no painel “Financiar a reinvenção: onde está o capital para inovar e competir na nova economia”, que reuniu representantes da Embrapii, Finep, ApexBrasil e ABGi Brasil. A moderação foi de Jamile Sabatini Marques, diretora de Inovação e Fomento da Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Software (ABES). Embrapii pode financiar até 90% dos projetos de pequenas empresas O modelo da Embrapii combina recursos da instituição, das empresas e dos centros de pesquisa credenciados para apoiar o desenvolvimento de tecnologias. A atuação concentra-se principalmente nos níveis intermediários de maturidade tecnológica, que incluem provas de conceito, validações e protótipos. Para grandes empresas, a participação da Embrapii pode alcançar um terço dos recursos necessários, enquanto as unidades de pesquisa normalmente contribuem com parcelas entre 15% e 20%. Nas companhias com faturamento anual de até R$ 90 milhões, o aporte da instituição pode chegar a 50%. No caso de micro e pequenas empresas, a combinação com recursos do Sebrae permite atingir percentuais de apoio de 80% a 90%, conforme as características e condições de cada projeto. Oliveira explicou que as empresas podem procurar diretamente as unidades credenciadas, sem depender da publicação de editais específicos. O modelo busca compartilhar riscos tecnológicos e financeiros durante as etapas de desenvolvimento. Finep adapta crédito e subvenção aos ciclos de inovação O gerente do Departamento de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação da Finep, Luiz Sergio Utino, apresentou mudanças nos mecanismos de financiamento para atender empresas que desenvolvem tecnologias em ciclos mais curtos. Entre as medidas estão a ampliação da rede de agentes financeiros responsáveis pelo crédito descentralizado e a revisão dos procedimentos de enquadramento e análise das operações diretas. Segundo Utino, o crédito descentralizado atende empresas com faturamento inferior a R$ 90 milhões, em projetos financiados de até R$ 30 milhões. As operações diretas da Finep são destinadas a projetos de maior porte, sujeitos aos critérios financeiros e técnicos da instituição. Outra mudança envolve as chamadas de subvenção econômica. Em determinadas linhas, a agência passou a adotar fluxo contínuo, permitindo a apresentação e avaliação de propostas ao longo do período de inscrições, sem concentrar todas as análises em uma única etapa. O formato também possibilita a reapresentação de projetos não aprovados, desde que observadas as regras de cada chamada. Utino reconheceu que a Finep ainda precisa aprimorar procedimentos para acompanhar a velocidade do desenvolvimento tecnológico. “A gente está atento, e sabemos que precisa melhorar”, afirmou. ApexBrasil identifica interesse de fundos estrangeiros em IA Além do financiamento público, a atração de capital privado foi abordada por Sérgio Rossi, especialista em investimentos estrangeiros da ApexBrasil. Segundo ele, o Brasil concentra aproximadamente metade dos investimentos de venture capital realizados na América Latina e reúne entre 200 e 250 fundos desse segmento. A agência atua na aproximação de startups brasileiras com investidores internacionais, incluindo fundos de corporate venture capital (CVC), modalidade em que grandes empresas investem em negócios tecnológicos para atender a objetivos estratégicos. Rossi informou que uma iniciativa desenvolvida pela ApexBrasil para estimular esse mercado já contribuiu para atrair mais de US$ 1 bilhão em investimentos ao país desde sua criação. Nos últimos dois anos, a procura internacional passou a incluir com maior frequência projetos relacionados à IA. Segundo o executivo, investidores que anteriormente concentravam suas consultas em transição energética e hidrogênio passaram a buscar empresas que desenvolvem modelos e aplicações da tecnologia. “Praticamente todos falam ‘eu quero entender o que o Brasil tem de IA’”, relatou Rossi, ao descrever as conversas com fundos internacionais. A demanda também alcança a infraestrutura computacional. A agência recebeu recentemente uma delegação com pelo menos dez fundos chineses interessados em oportunidades no segmento de data centers. Rossi relacionou essa procura à disponibilidade de energia renovável no Brasil e às perspectivas associadas ao Redata. Acesso aos recursos exige planejamento das empresas Marina Loures, diretora de Inovação e Transformação Digital da ABGi Brasil, apontou a dificuldade de identificar os instrumentos disponíveis como um dos obstáculos enfrentados por empresas que ainda não utilizam mecanismos de fomento. Segundo ela, a variedade de linhas de crédito, incentivos fiscais e chamadas de subvenção exige que as organizações conheçam as condições de cada modalidade antes de apresentar propostas. artigo.texto: Massive new data centers are the physical foundation for tech companies’ hopes and dreams for AI. But the rush to expand warehouses full of energy-hungry servers has also kicked up fights across the world over their impact on power grids, utility bills, nearby communities, and the environment. From audacious plans to launch data centers into space to the latest legal battles over pollution, The Verge has the biggest news and reporting surrounding data centers. - Highway robbers are targeting trucks carrying data center components. NBC News reports that accelerated data center construction across the country is creating new opportunities for heists that involve phishing, corporate identity theft, and car-ramming. Truckloads of costly equipment like servers, fiber-optic cables, computer memory chips, copper wires and bitcoin mining machines crisscrossing America’s highways have become prime targets for organized criminal groups looking for big payoffs, according to law enforcement and industry experts. - Data center backlash is uniting America If there’s one issue that seems to activate all kinds of voters in 2026, it’s data centers. The rapid buildout of these massive server storage facilities — and the infrastructure construction and expenses that come with them — has sparked local opposition in communities across the country and become a major issue in many congressional and gubernatorial campaigns. At the same time, tech money has been pouring into many of these races. Leading the Future, a super PAC backed by venture capitalist Marc Andreessen and OpenAI President Greg Brockman, has already spent $45 million in a year. And Public First Action, an Anthropic-backed group that says it supports AI safeguards, says it’s raised $80 million. Both have funded Democratic and Republican-aligned groups. Other super PACs see an opportunity to push for stricter AI policies, like the recently created Tomorrow Together, which launched $4 million in ads for battleground House races, with messages about data center development and AI safety. Read Article > - Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom As it prepares to go public, Anthropic’s S-1 filing makes generative AI’s methane dependency glaringly obvious. In documents filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission Monday, Anthropic acknowledges that data centers are becoming increasingly reliant on “natural gas” — the fossil fuel industry’s marketing term for what is primarily methane — leaving the company’s AI data center buildout vulnerable to rising fuel costs and existing supply chain constraints. And in a possible catch-22, Anthropic admits that rising global temperatures — a symptom of burning fossil fuels — will increase the company’s operating costs. Read Article > - It’s a good time to sell gray paint. The New York Times reports that data centers are “painting gray concrete and gray steel with more gray,” leading to an unexpected boom for paint manufacturers. Gravel producers and wiring companies are also enjoying an uptick, “creating a long tail of unlikely winners.” Gray Paint Has Never Had It as Good as in the A.I. Boom [The New York Times] - Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI. New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand — with gas turbines or renewable energy — will determine just how dirty things will get. So far, though, things are looking grim. Here are a few recent articles about the projects: - KGUN 9: Marana approves data center regulations amid community pushback - The Salt Lake Tribune: A woman was arrested while protesting data centers at a Utah County meeting. Here’s how it unfolded. - The Texas Tribune: Greg Abbott raked in $9 million from data center-related donors as he called for regulations - Wisconsin Public Radio: Milwaukee joins list of Wisconsin cities putting a pause on data center projects - Trump says paying communities a “dividend” could make data centers more popular. Continuing to push the widely unpopular data center projects, Trump said in a Truth Social post that some of them “have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck.” His plan sounds lot like Meta’s approach on the Hyperion project in Louisiana, where Mark Zuckerberg has touted $50,000 bonus checks for teachers despite a secretive approval process residents didn’t know much about. - Texas is still permitting data centers despite a supposed statewide moratorium. Governor Greg Abbott announced a permitting pause for data centers in September. But state agencies are still processing permits, according to an analysis of public records by advocacy groups Public Citizen and FracTracker. The governor’s office, however, denies approving any data center-related permits. - The fossil fuel comeback is here The US is building more fossil fuel infrastructure than it has in a decade while renewable energy growth slows down, a new report shows. Electricity demand is also climbing faster than it has in more than a decade with more data centers, factories, and electric vehicles plugging into the grid. Despite those growing demands, the Trump administration has sought to hobble the wind and solar industries in favor of fossil fuels. https://tiinside.com.br/27/10/2026/gaisp.resumo: O Grupo de Acompanhamento da Implantação das Soluções para os Problemas de Interferência (GAISPI), coordenado pela Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel), aprovou, nesta terça-feira (27), propostas apresentadas pela Entidade Administradora da Faixa (EAF) que somam R$ 1,66 bilhão em investimentos para novas políticas públicas. Os projetos preveem a distribuição de conversores de TV 3.0 a famílias de baixa renda e a implantação de um data center voltado ao processamento de dados e aplicações de inteligência artificial (IA) para o Governo Federal. As iniciativas poderão ser financiadas com recursos remanescentes do leilão do 5G, resultado das economias obtidas na execução dos compromissos previstos no edital. As propostas seguem agora para análise e deliberação do Conselho Diretor da Anatel. Os estudos apresentados pela EAF identificaram uma disponibilidade estimada de R$ 1,69 bilhão para projetos adicionais, após a reserva de aproximadamente R$ 2 bilhões para assegurar a conclusão das obrigações originais do edital do 5G, incluindo uma margem de segurança de 10%. Para o conselheiro da Anatel e presidente do GAISPI, Edson Holanda, os resultados demonstram a importância da eficiência na gestão dos recursos e do aprimoramento dos mecanismos de acompanhamento e fiscalização. “A atuação eficiente das entidades executoras, aliada ao aperfeiçoamento contínuo dos mecanismos de acompanhamento e fiscalização pelo GAISPI, tem permitido otimizar a aplicação dos recursos do leilão do 5G e gerar economias importantes. Esses resultados abrem a possibilidade de ampliar os benefícios para a sociedade, com novas políticas públicas, sem comprometer as obrigações originalmente previstas. É uma demonstração de que uma governança sólida, com planejamento, transparência e controle, pode transformar eficiência na gestão em mais entregas para a população”, destaca Holanda. TV 3.0 para famílias de baixa renda A proposta de distribuição de conversores de TV 3.0 prevê investimento estimado de R$ 1,28 bilhão para atender aproximadamente 910 mil famílias nos municípios de São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro e no Distrito Federal, com prioridade para beneficiários do Bolsa Família inscritos no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico). O objetivo é permitir que famílias de baixa renda também tenham acesso à nova geração da televisão aberta brasileira, que oferecerá avanços na qualidade de imagem e som, além de novos recursos de interatividade e integração com serviços digitais. O estudo desenvolvido pela EAF considera investimento total de R$ 1.280.690.000, com custo médio estimado de R$ 1.407,36 por família. O orçamento contempla a aquisição dos equipamentos, logística, distribuição, comunicação, atendimento à população, tecnologia e demais despesas operacionais necessárias à execução do programa. A implementação está prevista para ocorrer em até 24 meses, de forma escalonada, com início pelo município de São Paulo, como projeto-piloto. A estratégia permitirá avaliar os resultados e aperfeiçoar os procedimentos antes da ampliação para as demais localidades. A iniciativa aproveita a experiência acumulada na distribuição gratuita de equipamentos de recepção de televisão digital no Brasil, incluindo a atuação da EAF na execução do programa Brasil Antenado. Data center para inteligência artificial e serviços públicos O GAISPI também aprovou a proposta de implantação de um data center de alta capacidade, com investimento estimado de R$ 375 milhões, destinado a atender órgãos e instituições federais, especialmente em aplicações de inteligência artificial, processamento de dados sensíveis e hospedagem de serviços governamentais críticos. O projeto prevê uma infraestrutura pública de processamento de dados, com titularidade da União e operação pela Telebras. A EAF ficará responsável pela implantação, seguindo modelo semelhante ao adotado na Rede Privativa de Comunicação da Administração Pública Federal. O cenário técnico de referência contempla uma área de aproximadamente 5 mil metros quadrados e dois módulos de infraestrutura. O primeiro será dedicado a aplicações de inteligência artificial, com 20 racks, seis servidores equipados com um total de 48 unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs), além de servidores e sistemas de armazenamento de alta capacidade. O segundo módulo será destinado a serviços tradicionais de tecnologia da informação e colocalização de equipamentos. A infraestrutura também contará com sistemas redundantes de energia e conectividade, além de soluções de resfriamento adequadas às exigências de processamento de alto desempenho. O prazo estimado para implantação é de 12 meses, condicionado à disponibilidade de energia, aos licenciamentos e aos prazos de fornecimento e integração dos equipamentos. A iniciativa busca ampliar a autonomia tecnológica do país e fortalecer a capacidade do Estado brasileiro de desenvolver, hospedar e operar aplicações estratégicas de inteligência artificial e serviços digitais em infraestrutura nacional. Eficiência e novos investimentos As propostas representam uma nova etapa na aplicação dos recursos associados aos compromissos do leilão do 5G. Além da execução dos projetos originalmente previstos, as economias identificadas permitem avaliar investimentos adicionais em iniciativas de interesse público. A implementação dos dois projetos dependerá da aprovação do Conselho Diretor da Anatel e do cumprimento dos procedimentos técnicos e regulatórios aplicáveis, preservando os recursos necessários à conclusão das obrigações originais do edital. A EAF seguirá responsável pelos detalhamentos técnicos, operacionais e financeiros necessários à eventual execução das iniciativas, conforme as diretrizes estabelecidas pelo GAISPI e pela Anatel.
